In the Middle Country, bathing at an interval of less than half a month, and the absence of a proper occasion and so forth—these two are the factors.

Nahānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on bathing is concluded.

8. Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Training Rule on Discoloring

368. Aṭṭhame paṭiladdhanavacīvarenāti ettha pubbe akatakappaṃ katipāhaṃ nivāsanatthāya tāvakālikavasena laddhampi saṅgayhatīti vadanti.

368. In the eighth [training rule], regarding the phrase `paṭiladdhanavacīvarena`, they say that even a robe that was previously unmarked, acquired temporarily for the purpose of wearing for a few days, is included.

369. “Navaṃ nāma akatakappa”nti sāmaññato vuttattā aññena bhikkhunā kappabinduṃ datvā paribhuttaṃ cīvaraṃ, tena vā, tato labhitvā aññena vā kenaci dinnampi katakappameva navaṃ nāma na hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Nivāsetuṃ vā pārupituṃ vā”ti vuttattā aṃsabaddhakāsāvampi pārupitabbato kappaṃ kātabbanti vadanti. Cammakāranīlaṃ nāma cammaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ kātuṃ yojiyamānaṃ nīlaṃ. Pakatinīlamevāti keci. Yathāvuttacīvarassa akatakappatā, anaṭṭhacīvarāditā, nivāsanāditāti tīṇi aṅgāni.

369. Because it is generally stated, '“New” means unmarked,' it should be understood that a robe used by another monk after he has applied the kappa-mark—or a robe given by that monk himself, or one received from him and given by someone else—is considered to have been marked and is not called 'new.' Because it is stated, '...to wear as an under-robe or to wear as an upper-robe,' they say that even a shoulder-cloth, since it is to be worn, must be marked. 'Tanner's blue' (`cammakāranīlaṃ`) means the blue that is applied to make leather blue. Some say it is simply natural blue. The three factors are: the aforesaid robe's being unmarked, its not being a lost robe, etc., and its being worn, etc.

Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on discoloring is concluded.

9. Vikappanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Training Rule on Designation

374. Navame [V 2.0043] yenāti yena saddhiṃ, yassa santiketi attho. Sāmaṃ vikappitassa apaccuddhāro, vikappanupagacīvaratā, avissāsena paribhogoti tīṇi aṅgāni.

374. In the ninth [training rule], `yena` means 'with whom,' that is, 'in whose presence.' The three factors are: not revoking a robe designated by oneself, the robe being one that is subject to designation, and using it without permission.

Vikappanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on designation is concluded.

10. Cīvaraapanidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Training Rule on Hiding a Robe

378. Dasame [M 2.0045] pāḷiyaṃ antamaso hasāpekkhopīti api-saddena atheyyacittaṃ kodhena dukkhāpetukāmaṃ, avaṇṇaṃ pakāsetukāmañca saṅgayhati. Teneva “tivedana”nti vuttaṃ. Upasampannassa pattādīnaṃ apanidhānaṃ, vihesetukāmatādīti dve aṅgāni.

378. In the tenth [training rule], regarding the Pāli phrase `antamaso hasāpekkhopi`, by the word `api` is included an act done without a thievish mind, but with the wish to cause suffering out of anger or the wish to proclaim faults. For that very reason, it is called `tivedana`. The two factors are: the hiding of the bowl, etc., of an ordained monk, and the desire to harass, etc.

Cīvaraapanidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on hiding a robe is concluded.

Niṭṭhito surāpānavaggo chaṭṭho.

The sixth chapter, the Surāpāna Vagga, is concluded.

7. Sappāṇakavaggo

7. The Chapter on Living Beings

1. Sañciccapāṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Training Rule on Intentionally [Killing] a Living Being

382. Sattamassa paṭhame usuṃ saraṃ asati khipatīti issāso. Na hettha kiñci jīvitaṃ nāma visuṃ tiṭṭhatīti sambandho. Tattha pāṇeti satte. Appamattena vattaṃ kātabbanti yathā pāṇakānaṃ vihesāpi na hoti, evaṃ sallakkhetvā otāpanasammajjanādivattaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva.

382. In the first [training rule] of the seventh [chapter]: An `issāso` (archer) is so called because `usuṃ saraṃ asati khipati` (he shoots an arrow). The connection is this: Herein, no so-called 'life' exists separately. Therein, `pāṇe` refers to beings. 'Duty should be done with heedfulness' means that having considered how even harassment of small creatures might not occur, one should perform duties such as sunning things and sweeping. The rest is as has been said.

Sañciccapāṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on intentionally [killing] a living being is concluded.

2. Sappāṇakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Living Beings

387. Dutiye [V 2.0044] udakasaṇṭhānakappadeseti kaddamapāsāṇādibhūmiyaṃ. Tatthāti āsitte kappiyaudake. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva.

387. In the second [training rule], 'a place suitable for the establishment of water' means ground with mud, stones, and so on. 'There' means in permissible water that has been poured. The rest is just as has been said.

Sappāṇakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning living beings is concluded.

3. Ukkoṭanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Reopening a Case

392. Tatiye “tassa bhikkhuno santikaṃ gantvā”ti vuttattā yassa adhikaraṇaṃ saṅghakammena nihataṃ, tassa sammukhe eva ukkoṭentassa pācittiyaṃ. Parammukhe pana dukkaṭameva.

392. In the third [training rule], because it is stated, 'having gone into the presence of that bhikkhu,' a pācittiya offense is incurred for one who reopens the case only in the presence of the bhikkhu whose legal issue was settled by a formal act of the Saṅgha. In his absence, however, it is only a dukkaṭa offense.

395. “Dhammakamme [M 2.0046] adhammakammasaññī ukkoṭeti, anāpattī”ti vuttattā anādariyatādi viya ukkoṭanaṃ sayaṃ akusalaṃ na hoti, dhammakammasaññāya, pana vimatiyā ca ukkoṭaneneva akusalaṃ hoti. Yathādhammaṃ nihatatā, jānanā, ukkoṭanāti tīṇi aṅgāni.

395. Because it is said, 'If one reopens a case, perceiving a lawful formal act as an unlawful one, there is no offense,' the act of reopening is not in itself unwholesome, unlike disrespect and so on. However, it becomes unwholesome by the very act of reopening with the perception that it is a lawful formal act or with doubt. The three factors are: the state of having been settled according to the Dhamma, knowing this, and the act of reopening.

Ukkoṭanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning reopening a case is concluded.

4. Duṭṭhullasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning a Grave Offense

399. Catutthe āpattiṃ āpajjatiyevāti dhuranikkhepapakkhe vuttaṃ. Vatthupuggaloti āpannapuggalo. Chādetukāmatāya hi sati eva avassaṃ aññassa ārocanaṃ vuttaṃ, vatthupuggalassa ca ārocanā nāma na hotīti paṭicchādanamevāti adhippāyo. Koṭi chinnā hotīti chādessāmīti dhuranikkhepe satipi puggalaparamparāya gacchantī āpattikoṭi chijjati.

399. In the fourth [training rule], the statement 'he certainly incurs an offense' is said in the case of abandoning the burden. 'The person of the case' means the person who has committed the offense. For, only when there is a desire to conceal is it said that one must necessarily inform another, and informing the person of the case is not called 'informing'; therefore, it is precisely concealment—this is the meaning. 'The limit is cut' means that even when there is an abandoning of the burden with the thought, 'I will conceal it,' the limit of the offense, proceeding through a succession of persons, is cut off.

400. “Anupasampannassa sukkavissaṭṭhi ca kāyasaṃsaggo cāti ayaṃ duṭṭhullaajjhācāro nāmā”ti idaṃ duṭṭhullārocanasikkhāpadaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “anupasampannassa…pe… ādito pañca sikkhāpadāni duṭṭhullo nāma ajjhācāro, sesāni aduṭṭhullo. Sukkavissaṭṭhikāyasaṃsaggaduṭṭhullaattakāmā panassa ajjhācāro nāmā”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 82) iminā vacanena virujjhatīti vīmaṃsitabbaṃ. Puggalapemena chādayato cettha “aññe garahissantī”ti bhayavasena chādanakkhaṇe [V 2.0045] paṭighova uppajjatīti “dukkhavedana”nti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Upasampannassa duṭṭhullāpattijānanaṃ, paṭicchādetukāmatāya dhuranikkhepoti dve aṅgāni.

400. “For one who is not fully ordained, both emission of semen and physical contact are called grave misconduct.” This statement, in the commentary on the training rule concerning the disclosure of grave offenses, should be examined as it contradicts the following passage: “For one not fully ordained… the first five training rules are called grave misconduct; the rest are not grave. However, for him, emission of semen, physical contact, and grave misconduct for the sake of personal desire are called misconduct.” Herein, for one who conceals an offense out of personal affection, it should be understood that at the moment of concealment, aversion arises out of fear—thinking, “Others will criticize”—and thus it is called a “painful feeling.” For a fully ordained person, there are two factors: knowing of a grave offense, and, with the desire to conceal it, abandoning the task.

Duṭṭhullasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning a grave offense is concluded.

5. Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning One Less Than Twenty Years Old

402. Pañcame rūpasippanti heraññikasippaṃ. Gabbhe sayitakālena saddhiṃ vīsatimaṃ vassaṃ paripuṇṇamassāti gabbhavīso.

402. In the fifth [rule], ‘craft of forms’ means the craft of a silversmith. ‘Gabbhavīso’ refers to one for whom the twentieth year is complete, including the time spent lying in the womb.

404. Nikkhamanīyapuṇṇamāsīti [M 2.0047] sāvaṇamāsassa puṇṇamiyā āsāḷhīpuṇṇamiyā anantarapuṇṇamī. Pāṭipadadivaseti pacchimikāya vassūpanāyikāya. Dvādasa māse mātu kucchismiṃ vasitvā mahāpavāraṇāya jātaṃ upasampādentīti attho. “Tiṃsa rattindivo māso, dvādasamāsiko saṃvaccharo”ti (a. ni. 3.71; 8.43; vibha. 1023) vacanato “cattāro māsā parihāyantī”ti vuttaṃ. Vassaṃ ukkaḍḍhantīti vassaṃ uddhaṃ kaḍḍhanti, “ekamāsaṃ adhikamāso”ti chaḍḍetvā vassaṃ upagacchantīti attho. Tasmā tatiyo tatiyo saṃvaccharo terasamāsiko hoti. Te dve māse gahetvāti nikkhamanīyapuṇṇamāsato yāva jātadivasabhūtā mahāpavāraṇā. Tāva ye dve māsā anāgatā, tesaṃ atthāya adhikamāsato laddhe dve māse gahetvā. Tenāha “yo pavāretvā vīsativasso bhavissatī”tiādi. “Nikkaṅkhā hutvā”ti idaṃ aṭṭhārasannaṃ vassānaṃ ekaadhikamāse gahetvā tato vīsatiyā vassesupi cātuddasīatthāya catunnaṃ māsānaṃ parihāpanena sabbadā paripuṇṇavīsativassataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Pavāretvā vīsativasso bhavissatīti mahāpavāraṇādivase atikkante gabbhavassena saha vīsativasso bhavissatīti attho. Tasmāti yasmā gabbhamāsāpi gaṇanūpagā honti, tasmā. Ekavīsativassoti jātiyā vīsativassaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

404. ‘The Nikkhamanīya full moon’ refers to the full moon of the month of Sāvaṇa, which is the full moon immediately following the full moon of Āsāḷha. ‘On the first day of the fortnight’ means on the day of undertaking the later rains-residence. The meaning is this: they ordain one who, after staying in the mother's womb for twelve months, was born on the day of the Great Pavāraṇā. Because it is said, “Thirty days and nights make a month, twelve months make a year,” it is stated, “four months are deficient.” ‘They draw up the rains-residence’ means they pull the rains-residence forward; the meaning is that they enter the rains-residence after setting aside one month as an ‘extra month.’ Therefore, every third year has thirteen months. ‘Taking those two months’ means taking the two months obtained from the extra month for the sake of the two months that have not yet arrived in the period from the Nikkhamanīya full moon until the Great Pavāraṇā, which is the birthday. For that reason, he said the words beginning with, “who, after the Pavāraṇā, will be twenty years old.” The phrase ‘being free from doubt’ was stated with reference to always ensuring a full twenty years by taking the six extra months over eighteen years, and then, for the twenty years, reducing four months for the sake of the cātuddasī days. ‘After the Pavāraṇā, he will be twenty years old’ means that when the day of the Great Pavāraṇā has passed, he will be twenty years old, including the year in the womb. This is because the months in the womb are also included in the count. ‘Twenty-one years old’ is said with reference to being twenty years from birth.

406. Aññaṃ upasampādetīti upajjhāyo, ācariyo vā hutvā upasampādeti. Sopīti upasampādentopi anupasampanno. Ūnavīsativassatā, taṃ ñatvā upajjhāyena hutvā upasampādananti dve aṅgāni.

406. ‘Ordains another’ means that, being a preceptor or a teacher, he ordains another. ‘Even he’ means that even the one ordaining is not fully ordained. The two factors are: the state of being less than twenty years old, and, knowing this, the act of ordaining while being a preceptor.

Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning one less than twenty years old is concluded.

6. Theyyasatthasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning the Thief-Caravan

409. Chaṭṭhe [V 2.0046] theyyasatthabhāvo, ñatvā saṃvidhānaṃ, avisaṅketena gamananti tīṇi aṅgāni.

409. In the sixth [training rule], there are three factors: the state of being a thief-caravan, knowing the arrangement, and going without missing the appointment.

Theyyasatthasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning the thief-caravan is concluded.

412. Sattamaṃ vuttanayameva.

412. The seventh [training rule] is in the same manner as has been stated.

8. Ariṭṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Ariṭṭha

417. Aṭṭhame [M 2.0048] antarāyanti antarā vemajjhe eti āgacchatīti antarāyo, diṭṭhadhammikādianattho. Ānantariyadhammāti anantare bhave phalanibbattane niyuttā cetanādidhammāti attho. “Na saggassā”ti idaṃ bhikkhunidūsanakammassa ānantariyattābhāvato vuttaṃ. Ariyasāvikāsu, pana kalyāṇaputhujjanabhūtāya ca balakkārena dūsentassa ānantariyasaasameva. Mokkhantarāyikatā pana lolāyapi pakatattabhikkhuniyā dūsakassa tasmiṃ attabhāve magguppattiyā abhāvato vuttā.

417. In the eighth [training rule], ‘antarāya’ (obstacle) is so called because it comes (`eti`) or arrives (`āgacchati`) in between (`antarā vemajjhe`); it is a harm in this present life and so on. The meaning of ‘ānantariya-dhammā’ is: dhammas such as volition that are engaged in producing a result in the immediately following existence. The phrase, “not for heaven,” is stated because the act of corrupting a bhikkhunī does not have the nature of an ānantariya act. However, for one who corrupts by force a noble female disciple or a virtuous worldling woman, it is indeed similar to an ānantariya act. But the quality of being an obstacle to liberation is stated because the path does not arise in that very existence for one who corrupts a bhikkhunī of normal virtue, even if she is fickle.

Tasmiṃ attabhāve anivattanakā ahetukaakiriyanatthikadiṭṭhiyova niyatamicchādiṭṭhidhammā. Paṇḍakādīnaṃ gahaṇaṃ nidassanamattaṃ. Sabbāpi duhetukāhetukapaṭisandhiyo vipākantarāyikāva duhetukānampi maggānuppattito.

In that existence, the non-retrogessing dhammas of fixed wrong view are the views of causelessness, inefficacy of action, and nihilism. The inclusion of eunuchs and so on is merely an illustration. All rebirth-linkings with two roots or without roots are indeed obstacles to the result, because even for those with two roots, the path does not arise.

Ayanti ariṭṭho. Rasena rasanti anavajjena paccayaparibhuñjanarasena pañcakāmaguṇapaabhogarasaṃ samānetvā. Upanento viyāti ghaṭento viya, so eva vā pāṭho.

‘Ayaṃ’ means: this Ariṭṭha. ‘Rasena rasaṃ’ means: having equated the taste of enjoying the five strands of sensual pleasure with the taste of the blameless consumption of requisites. ‘Upanento viya’ means: like striving (`ghaṭento viya`); or alternatively, that (`ghaṭento`) is the reading itself.

Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamāti ettha aṭṭhi eva nimmaṃsatāya kaṅkalanti ca vuccati. Palibhañjanaṭṭhenāti avassaṃ patanaṭṭhena. Adhikuṭṭanaṭṭhenāti ati viya kuṭṭanaṭṭhena. Pāḷiyaṃ “tathāhaṃ bhagavatā…pe… nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti idaṃ vatthuanurūpato vuttaṃ. Evaṃ pana aggahetvā aññenapi ākārena yaṃ kiñci bhagavatā vuttaṃ viparītato gahetvā parehi vuttepi amuñcitvā voharantassāpi vuttanayānusārena tadanuguṇaṃ samanubhāsanakammavācaṃ yojetvā āpattiyā āropetuṃ, āpattiyā adassanādīsu tīsu yaṃ kiñci abhirucitaṃ nimittaṃ katvā ukkhepanīyakammaṃ [V 2.0047] kātuñca labbhati. Samanubhāsanaṃ akatvāpi “māyasmā evaṃ avacā”ti bhikkhūhi vuttamatte laddhiyā appaṭinissajjanapaccayāya dukkaṭāpattiyāpi ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kātumpi vaṭṭatevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Dhammakammatā, samanubhāsanāya appaṭinissajjananti dve aṅgāni.

Here, in ‘aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā,’ a bone itself, due to being fleshless, is also called a ‘kaṅkala’ (skeleton). ‘Palibhañjanaṭṭhena’ means: by the meaning of inevitably causing a fall. ‘Adhikuṭṭanaṭṭhena’ means: by the meaning of being something to be excessively minced. In the Pāḷi, this phrase, “Thus I… by the Blessed One… is not able to be an obstacle,” is stated in accordance with the story of Ariṭṭha. However, for a bhikkhu who, not grasping it thus but in some other manner, grasps in a contrary way whatever was said by the Blessed One, and speaks without relinquishing that view even when told by others, it is allowable, in accordance with the stated method, to apply a formal act of admonition suitable for him and to charge him with an offense. Furthermore, it is allowable to perform an act of suspension, having made the grounds for it any preferred reason among the three, such as not seeing the offense. It should be understood that even without performing a formal admonition, merely upon being told by the bhikkhus, “Venerable, do not speak thus,” it is indeed permissible to perform an act of suspension for the dukkaṭa offense conditioned by not relinquishing the view. The two factors are: the fact that it is a valid formal act, and the non-relinquishing of the view upon admonition.

Ariṭṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning Ariṭṭha is concluded.

9. Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Association with a Suspended Bhikkhu

424. Navame [M 2.0049] “ukkhitto anosārito”ti vuttattā ariṭṭhassa ukkhepanīyakammaṃ katanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

424. In the ninth training rule, because it is said, “suspended, not reinstated,” it should be understood that it is indeed proper to perform the act of suspension on Ariṭṭha.

425. Pāḷiyaṃ “ekacchanne”ti sāmaññato vuttattā nānūpacārepi ekacchanne nipajjane paṇṇattiṃ ajānantassa arahatopi ukkhittānuvattakānampi pācittiyameva. Akatānudhammatā, ñatvā sambhogādikaraṇanti dve aṅgāni.

425. In the Pāḷi, because it is stated generally “under one roof,” even if not in close proximity, for lying down under one roof, it is indeed a pācittiya offense even for an Arahant who does not know the regulation, and also for the followers of the suspended one. The two factors are: the state of not having been reinstated, and knowingly performing association and so on.

Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Association with a Suspended Monk is concluded.

10. Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Kaṇṭaka

428. Dasame pireti sambodhanatthe nipātapadaṃ. Sesaṃ anantarasikkhāpadadvaye vuttanayameva.

428. In the tenth training rule, the word `pire` is a particle in the sense of addressing. The remainder is in the same manner as stated in the two immediately preceding training rules.

Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Kaṇṭaka is concluded.

Niṭṭhito sappāṇakavaggo sattamo.

The seventh chapter, the Sappāṇaka Vagga, is concluded.

8. Sahadhammikavaggo

8. The Sahadhammika Vagga

1. Sahadhammikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning a Fellow Monk

434. Aṭṭhamavaggassa [V 2.0048] paṭhame upasampannassa paññattena vacanaṃ, asikkhitukāmassa lesena evaṃ vacananti dve aṅgāni.

434. In the first training rule of the eighth chapter, the two factors are: speaking to a fully ordained person about what has been laid down, and speaking thus with a pretext, being one who does not wish to train.

Sahadhammikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning a Fellow Monk is concluded.

2. Vilekhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Disparagement

438. Dutiye alajjitāti alajjitāya. Evaṃ sesesupi. Sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjatītiādi bhikkhubhikkhunīnaññeva vuttaṃ alajjilakkhaṇaṃ, sāmaṇerādīnaṃ, pana gahaṭṭhānañca sādhāraṇavasena yathāsakaṃ sikkhāpadavītikkamanapaṭigūhanādito veditabbaṃ. Lajjilakkhaṇepi eseva nayo. Kiñcāpi [M 2.0050] kukkucce uppannepi madditvā karonto, kappiye akappiyasaññitāya karontopi taṅkhaṇikāya alajjitāya evaṃ karonti. Tathāpi kukkuccādibhede visuṃ gahitāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

438. In the second training rule, `alajjitā` means ‘due to shamelessness.’ This is also the case for the remaining terms. The characteristic of a shameless person, stated as “one intentionally commits an offense,” and so on, is spoken of only for bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs. However, for novices and so on, and for householders, it should be understood in a general sense from their respective transgression and concealment of training rules, and so on. This same method applies to the characteristic of a scrupulous person. Although one may act by suppressing remorse even when it has arisen, or one may act in what is allowable with the perception that it is unallowable, they do so with a momentary shamelessness. Nevertheless, it should be understood that in the distinctions of remorse and so on, these are taken separately.

Vajjiputtakā dasavatthudīpakā. Parūpahāraaññāṇakaṅkhāparavitāraṇādivādāti ettha arahattaṃ paṭijānantānaṃ kuhakānaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ disvā “mārakāyikā devatā asuciṃ upasaṃharantī”tigāhino parūpahāravādā nāma. Arahato sabbesaṃ itthipurisādīnaṃ nāmādiajānane aññāṇaṃ, tattha sanniṭṭhānabhāvena kaṅkhā, parato sutvā nāmādijānanena paravitāraṇo atthītivādino aññāṇavādā, kaṅkhāvādā, paravitāraṇavādā ca tesaṃ, mahāsaṅghikādīnañca vibhāgo kathāvatthuppakaraṇe vutto.

The Vajjiputtakas are the expounders of the ten points. In the phrase `parūpahāra-aññāṇa-kaṅkhā-paravitāraṇādi-vādā`, those who, upon seeing the seminal emission of deceivers claiming Arahantship, hold the view that “deities of Māra’s host bring about the impurity,” are called `parūpahāravādā` (holders of the view of external influence). Those who hold the view that an Arahant has ignorance in not knowing the names and so on of all men, women, etc.; that there is doubt therein due to an absence of certainty; and that there is investigation of others because of knowing names and so on after hearing from another, are the `aññāṇavādā` (holders of the view of ignorance), `kaṅkhāvādā` (holders of the view of doubt), and `paravitāraṇavādā` (holders of the view of investigating others). The classification of them, and of the Mahāsaṅghikas and others, is stated in the Kathāvatthuppakaraṇa.

Cattāro maggā ca phalāni cāti ettha ca-kārena abhiññāpaṭisambhidāpi saṅgahitāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kecīti pariyattidharā dhammakathikā. Puna kecīti paṭipattidharā paṃsukūlikattherā. Itare panātiādīsu ayaṃ adhippāyo – dhammakathikattherā pana paṃsukūlikattherehi ābhataṃ suttaṃ sutvā –

Here, in the phrase “the four paths and the fruits,” it should be understood that by the particle `ca`, the higher knowledges and analytical insights are also included. `Keci` (some) refers to the Dhamma-preachers who are masters of the scriptural learning. Again, `keci` refers to the rag-robe-wearing elders who are masters of the practice. In the phrase `itare pana` (but the others) and so on, this is the intended meaning: the Dhamma-preaching elders, having heard the sutta brought by the rag-robe-wearing elders—

“Yāva [V 2.0049] tiṭṭhanti suttantā, vinayo yāva dippati;

Tāva dakkhanti ālokaṃ, sūriye abbhuṭṭhite yathā.

“As long as the suttantas stand, and as long as the Vinaya shines, so long will they see the light, just as when the sun has risen.

“Suttantesu asantesu, pamuṭṭhe vinayamhi ca;

Tamo bhavissati loke, sūriye atthaṅgate yathā.

“When the suttantas are no more, and when the Vinaya is forgotten, darkness will be in the world, just as when the sun has set.

“Suttante rakkhite sante, paṭipatti hoti rakkhitā;

Paṭipattiyaṃ ṭhito dhīro, yogakkhemā na dhaṃsatī”ti. (a. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.130) –

“When the suttanta is protected, the practice is protected; the wise one, established in the practice, does not fall away from security from the bonds.”

Idaṃ suttaṃ āharitvā attanova vādaṃ patiṭṭhapentā pārājikānāpajjanavasena ṭhitā paṭipattisaṅgahitā pariyattiyeva mūlanti āhaṃsūti. Tenāha “sace pañca bhikkhū cattāri pārājikāni rakkhaṇakā…pe… sāsanaṃ vuḍḍhiṃ viruḷhiṃ gamayissantī”ti. Etena ca parikkhīṇe kāle lajjigaṇaṃ alabhantena vinayadharena alajjinopi pakatatte saṅgahetvā tehi saha dhammāmisasambhogaṃ saṃvāsaṃ karontena bahū kulaputte upasampādetvā sāsanaṃ [M 2.0051] paggahetuṃ vaṭṭatīti idaṃ sijjhatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Garahitukāmatā, upasampannassa santike sikkhāpadavivaṇṇananti dve aṅgāni.

Having brought this sutta and establishing their own view, they said: “The scriptural learning itself is the root; those who abide by way of not committing a pārājika offense are included in the practice.” Therefore, it was said: “If five bhikkhus are guardians of the four pārājikas… they will lead the Sāsana to growth and increase.” And by this, it should be understood that this is accomplished: in a time of decline, it is proper for a Vinaya master who cannot find a group of scrupulous monks to uphold the Sāsana by gathering even shameless monks who are of normal status (i.e., have not committed a pārājika), having communion in Dhamma and material things and living together with them, and giving the full ordination to many sons of good family. The two factors are: the desire to censure, and disparaging the training rule in the presence of a fully ordained person.

Vilekhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Disparagement is concluded.

3. Mohanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Feigning Ignorance

444. Tatiye pāḷiyaṃ ko pana vādo bhiyyoti tehi aññehi bhikkhūhi diṭṭhadvattivārato bhiyyo pana vitthārena uddisiyamāne pātimokkhe nisinnapubbatā atthi ce, tattha kimeva vattabbaṃ, āpattimokkho natthi evāti adhippāyo. Tañca yathādhammo kāretabboti tanti kāraṇatthe upayogavacanaṃ, tāyāti attho. Yathā dhammo ca vinayo ca ṭhito, tathā tāya āpattiyā kāretabboti vuttaṃ hoti. Mohāropanaṃ, tikkhattuṃ sutabhāvo, mohetukāmassa mohananti tīṇi aṅgāni.

444. In the third training rule, in the Pāḷi, as for the phrase 'what more is there to say?': if he has previously sat through the Pātimokkha being recited in greater detail by those other monks, more than the two or three times he has been present, what then is there to be said? The meaning is this: there is no release from the offense. In the phrase 'And he should be dealt with according to the Dhamma,' the word 'taṃ' is a term in the accusative case used in the instrumental sense; the meaning is 'by that.' It is meant that he should be dealt with for that offense in such a way as the Dhamma and the Vinaya are established. Imposing feigned ignorance, the state of having heard it three times, and the feigning of ignorance by one who wishes to feign ignorance—these are the three factors.

Mohanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on feigning ignorance is concluded.

4. Pahārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Striking

451. Catutthe [V 2.0050] pāḷiyaṃ kāyapaṭibaddhena vāti ettha pāsāṇādinissaggiyapahāropi saṅgahito.

451. In the fourth training rule, in the Pāḷi, in the phrase 'or with something connected to the body,' a blow by throwing something, such as a stone, is also included.

452. Rattacittoti kāyasaṃsaggarāgena vuttaṃ. Methunarāgena pana pahārato purisādīsu dukkaṭameva. Mokkhādhippāyena daṇḍakoṭiyā sappādiṃ ghaṭṭetvā maṇḍūkādiṃ mocentassapi anāpatti eva. Kupitatā, upasampannassa na mokkhādhippāyena pahāroti dve aṅgāni.

452. The phrase 'with a lustful mind' is said with reference to lust for bodily contact. However, for a monk who strikes with sexual lust, and for one who strikes men and so on, there is only a dukkaṭa offense. For one who, with the intention to free, strikes a snake or the like with the tip of a staff and thereby frees a frog or the like, there is no offense. The state of being angry, and striking a fully ordained person not with the intention to free—these are the two factors.

Pahārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on striking is concluded.

5. Talasattikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Threatening Gesture

457. Pañcame [M 2.0052] na paharitukāmatāya dinnattā dukkaṭanti ettha kimidaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, pahārapaccayā, udāhu uggiraṇapaccayāti? Uggiraṇapaccayāva, na pahārapaccayā. Na hi paharitukāmatāya asati tappaccayā kāci āpatti yuttā, uggiraṇassa pana attano sabhāvena asaṇṭhitattā tappaccayā pācittiyaṃ na jātaṃ, asuddhacittena katapayogattā ca ettha anāpatti na yuttāti dukkaṭaṃ vuttanti gahetabbaṃ.

457. In the fifth training rule, regarding the statement 'Because it was delivered without the intention to strike, it is a dukkaṭa,' a question arises: does this dukkaṭa offense arise from the cause of striking, or from the cause of brandishing? It arises only from the cause of brandishing, not from the cause of striking. Indeed, when there is no intention to strike, no offense due to that cause is proper. However, because the brandishing itself was not stable by its own nature, a pācittiya offense did not arise. And because the effort was made with an impure mind, it is not proper that there be no offense in this case. Therefore, a dukkaṭa is stated. Thus it should be understood.

458. Pubbeti anantarasikkhāpade. Sesaṃ anantarasadisameva.

458. As for 'pubbe,' it refers to the immediately preceding training rule. The remainder is just the same as in the immediately preceding one.

Talasattikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on a threatening gesture is concluded.

6. Amūlakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Groundless Accusation

459. Chaṭṭhe “attaparittāṇaṃ karontā”ti idaṃ na ca veramūlikā anuddhaṃsanāti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Anuddhaṃsanakkhaṇe pana kopacittameva uppajjati. Teneva “dukkhavedana”nti vuttaṃ. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva.

459. In the sixth training rule, this phrase 'acting for self-protection' is stated in order to show that this is not a disparagement rooted in enmity. However, at the moment of disparagement, only a mind of anger arises. For that very reason, 'a painful feeling' was stated. The remainder is in the manner already stated.

Amūlakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on a groundless accusation is concluded.

7. Kukkuccuppādanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Causing Remorse

464. Sattame [V 2.0051] upasampannassa aphāsukāmatā, kukkuccuppādananti dve aṅgāni.

464. In the seventh training rule: the desire for the discomfort of one who is fully ordained, and the causing of remorse; these are the two factors.

Kukkuccuppādanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on causing remorse is concluded.

8. Upassutisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Eavesdropping

471. Aṭṭhame suyyatīti suti, vacanaṃ. Tassā samīpaṃ upassuti. Suyyati etthāti sutīti evañhi atthe gayhamāne savanaṭṭhānasamīpe aññasmiṃ assavanaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhatīti āpajjati. Aṭṭhakathāyañca upassuti-saddasseva atthaṃ dassetuṃ “yattha ṭhatvā”tiādi vuttaṃ, na suti-saddamattassa.

471. In the eighth training rule: Because it is heard (suyyati), it is suti (hearing); this is the word. Nearness to that is upassuti. Indeed, when the meaning is taken thus: 'it is heard here (suyyati ettha), therefore it is suti,' it follows that one stands in another place of non-hearing near a place of hearing. And in the commentary, to show the meaning of the very word upassuti, 'where standing,' etc., was said, not to show the meaning of the mere word suti.

473. Ekaparicchedānīti [M 2.0053] kadāci akiriyato, kadāci kiriyato samuṭṭhānasāmaññena vuttaṃ. Upasampannena codanādhippāyo, savananti dve aṅgāni.

473. The phrase 'by one definition' (ekaparicchedena) is said with a commonality of origin, sometimes from non-action, sometimes from action. The intention to accuse regarding a fully ordained one, and listening; these are the two factors.

Upassutisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on eavesdropping is concluded.

9. Khiyyanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Disparagement

474. Navame dhammakammatā, jānanaṃ, chandaṃ datvā khiyyananti tīṇi aṅgāni.

474. In the ninth training rule: the state of being a formal act in accordance with the Dhamma, knowing, and disparaging after having given consent; these are the three factors.

Khiyyanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on disparagement is concluded.

10. Pakkamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Departing

481. Dasame vinicchayakathāya dhammikatā, taṃ ñatvā kammato paṭṭhāya ekasīmaṭṭhassa samānasaṃvāsikassa hatthapāsavijahananti dve aṅgāni.

481. In the tenth training rule: the lawfulness of the discussion for decision, and, knowing that, from the formal act onwards, the abandoning of the hand's reach of a co-resident who is within the same boundary; these are the two factors.

Pakkamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on departing is concluded.

11. Dubbalasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

11. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Invalidation

484. Ekādasame [V 2.0052] upasampannassa dhammena laddhasammutitā, saṅghena saddhiṃ cīvaraṃ datvā khiyyitukāmatāya khiyyananti dve aṅgāni.

484. In the eleventh training rule: the authorization for the fully ordained one having been obtained in accordance with the Dhamma, and disparaging with the desire to disparage after having given a robe together with the Sangha; these are the two factors.

Dubbalasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on invalidation is concluded.

489. Dvādasamaṃ vuttanayameva.

489. The twelfth training rule is of the same method as has been stated.

Niṭṭhito sahadhammikavaggo aṭṭhamo.

Concluded is the eighth Sahadhammikavagga (Chapter on Comrades in the Dhamma).

9. Rājavaggo

9. The Chapter on Kings

1. Antepurasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Inner Quarters

499. Navamavaggassa [M 2.0054] paṭhame pāḷiyaṃ saṃsuddhagahaṇikoti ettha gahaṇīti gabbhāsayasaññito mātu kucchippadeso, purisantarasukkāsamphuṭṭhatāya saṃsuddhagahaṇiko. Abhisittakhattiyatā, ubhinnampi sayanigharato anikkhantatā, appaṭisaṃviditassa indakhīlātikkamoti tīṇi aṅgāni.

499. In the first training rule of the ninth chapter, regarding the phrase 'saṃsuddhagahaṇiko': 'gahaṇī' is the region of the mother's belly designated as the womb. One is 'saṃsuddhagahaṇiko' because of not being touched by the semen of another man. The state of being an anointed Khattiya, the non-departure of both the king and queen from the bedchamber, and the crossing of the threshold by one who has not been announced; these are the three factors.

Antepurasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on the inner quarters is concluded.

2. Ratanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Valuables

506. Dutiye āvasathassāti ettha antoārāme vā hotu aññattha vā, yattha katthaci attano vasanaṭṭhānaṃ āvasatho nāma. Chandenapi bhayenapīti vaḍḍhakiādīsu chandena, rājavallabhesu bhayena. Ākiṇṇamanussepi jāte…pe… āsaṅkantīti tasmiṃ nimmanussaṭṭhāne pacchā ākiṇṇamanusse jātepi visaritvā gamanakāle aññassa adiṭṭhattā tameva bhikkhuṃ āsaṅkanti. Patirūpaṃ nāma kappiyabhaṇḍe sayaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ gahetvā akappiyabhaṇḍe patirūpānaṃ upāsakādīnaṃ [V 2.0053] dassetvā cetiyādipuññe niyojanaṃ vā dāpetvā nirapekkhagamanaṃ vā. Samādapetvāti yācitvā. Parasantakatā, vissāsaggāhapaṃsukūlasaññānaṃ abhāvo, ananuññātakāraṇā uggahaṇādi cāti tīṇi aṅgāni.

506. In the second training rule, regarding the phrase āvasathassa: whether it is inside a monastery or in another place, one's own place of residence anywhere whatsoever is called a dwelling (āvasatha). As for chandenāpi bhayenāpi (out of desire or fear): with carpenters and so on, it is out of affection; with royal favorites, it is out of fear. As for ākiṇṇamanussepi jāte... āsaṅkanti (even if it becomes crowded with people... they suspect): even if that uninhabited place later becomes crowded with people, because at the time of departure, having forgotten, he does not see others, they suspect that very bhikkhu. What is called 'suitable' (patirūpaṃ) is: regarding allowable items, taking them oneself with the perception of it being refuse-cloth; regarding unallowable items, having them given to suitable lay devotees and so on, or departing without concern. As for samādapetvā: it means having applied (yojetvā). The state of being another's property; the absence of the perception of taking with familiarity and the perception of it as refuse-cloth; and taking, etc., without a permitted reason—these are the three factors.

Ratanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Valuables is concluded.

3. Vikālagāmappavisanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Training Rule on Entering a Village at an Improper Time

508. Tatiye pāḷiyaṃ bhayakathanti rājacorādibhayaṃ vā rogāmanussadubbhikkhakantārādibhayaṃ vā ārabbha pavattaṃ. Visikhākathanti suniviṭṭhādivīthikathaṃ. Kumbhaṭṭhānakathanti udakatitthakathaṃ, kumbhadāsīkathaṃ vā. Pubbapetakathanti atītañātikathaṃ. Nānattakathanti vuttāhi, vakkhamānāhi ca vimuttaṃ nānāsabhāvaṃ [M 2.0055] niratthakakathaṃ. Lokakkhāyikanti “ayaṃ loko kena nimmito”tiādinā lokasabhāvakkhānavasena pavattanakathā. Evaṃ samuddakkhāyikā veditabbā. Iti bhavo iti abhavoti yaṃ vā taṃ vā niratthakakāraṇaṃ vatvā pavattitakathā itibhavābhavakathā. Ettha ca bhavo sassataṃ, vuḍḍhi, kāmasukhañcāti tividho, abhavo tabbiparītavasena. Iti imāya chabbidhāya itibhavābhavakathāya saddhiṃ dvattiṃsatiracchānakathā nāma honti. Atha vā pāḷiyaṃ sarūpato anāgatāpi araññapabbatanadīdīpakathā iti-saddena saṅgahetvā dvattiṃsatiracchānakathāti vuccanti. Iti vāti ettha iti-saddo pakāratthe. Vā-saddo vikappatthe. Tasmā evaṃ pakāraṃ ito aññaṃ vā tādisaṃ niratthakakathaṃ kathetīti attho gahetabbo.

508. In the third training rule, in the Pāḷi, 'talk of fear' (bhayakathā) is talk that arises concerning fear of kings, thieves, etc., or fear of disease, non-humans, famine, difficult journeys, etc. 'Talk of streets' (visikhākathā) is talk of roads, such as 'it is well-established'. 'Talk of water-pot stands' (kumbhaṭṭhānakathā) is talk of watering places, or talk of female slaves carrying water pots. 'Talk of the long-departed' (pubbapetakathā) is talk of deceased relatives. 'Various talk' (nānattakathā) is meaningless talk of various kinds, which is separate from what has been said and what will be said. 'Talk about the world' (lokakkhāyikā) is talk that arises by way of explaining the nature of the world, such as, "By whom was this world created?". Similarly, 'talk about the ocean' (samuddakkhāyikā) should be understood. Talk that arises from stating some meaningless reason or other, such as, "Thus there is becoming," "Thus there is annihilation," is 'talk of becoming and non-becoming' (itibhavābhavakathā). Herein, 'becoming' (bhava) is threefold: eternalism, growth, and sensual pleasure; 'non-becoming' (abhava) is the opposite of these. Thus, together with these six kinds of talk on becoming and non-becoming, there are thirty-two kinds of base talk (tiracchānakathā). Alternatively, although talk of forests, mountains, rivers, and islands is not explicitly mentioned in the Pāḷi, it is included by the word 'iti', and thus they are called the thirty-two kinds of base talk. Here, in the phrase iti vā, the word 'iti' is in the sense of 'type', and the word 'vā' is in the sense of 'alternative'. Therefore, the meaning should be taken as: "one speaks this kind of talk, or other such meaningless talk different from what has been mentioned".

512. Ussāhaṃ paṭippassambhetvā vihāraṃ gacchantāti ettha gāmūpacārato bahi nikkhante antarārāmādīnamupacāraṃ paviṭṭhe sandhāya vuttaṃ. Gāmūpacārabbhantare pana paṭipassaddhussāhānampi puna tameva vā aññaṃ vā gāmaṃ pavisitukāmatāya sati āpucchanakiccaṃ natthi. “Kulaghare vā…pe… gantabba”nti idaṃ pana purebhattaṃ paviṭṭhānaṃ vikāle sañjāte vikāle gāmappavesassa āpucchitabbatāya vuttaṃ. Adinnādāne vuttanayenāti dutiyaleḍḍupātaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

512. Here, the phrase 'having pacified one's exertion and going to the monastery' is said in reference to those who, having gone out beyond the village precincts, have entered the precincts of an intermediate monastery and so on. However, for those whose exertion is pacified within the village precincts, if there is a desire to re-enter that same village or another village, there is no duty to ask leave. This statement, 'One should go to a family's house...', is said because for those who entered in the forenoon, when the improper time arrives, permission must be asked for entering the village. The phrase 'in the way stated in the Adinnādāna (rule on taking what is not given)' is said in reference to the second clod's fall.

515. Antarārāmantiādīsūti ettha ussavadivasādīsu manussehi gāme padakkhiṇaṃ kārentaṃ jinabimbādiṃ pūjetukāmehi vā rogavūpasamādiyatthaṃ manussehi yācitehi vā bhikkhūhi suppaṭicchannādividhiṃ akatvāpi vīthimajjheneva gāmaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti vadanti, taṃ na [V 2.0054] gahetabbaṃ anāpattivāre avuttattā, “maggā anokkamitvā…pe… pācittiya”nti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. vikālagāmappavesanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) paṭikkhittattā ca. Vesāliṃ anupariyāyitvā parittaṃ karontenāpi ānandattherena suppaṭicchannatādiṃ akopenteneva, apaññatte vā sikkhāpade katanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Keci pana “antarārāmādigāmantare ṭhitehi garuṭṭhānīyānaṃ paccuggamanānuggamanādivasena gāmavīthiṃ otarituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti, tampi antaragharaṃ pavisantaṃ pati kātuṃ na vaṭṭati eva. Antarārāmādikappiyabhūmiṃ pana uddissa gacchantaṃ pati kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti khāyati, vīmaṃsitabbaṃ. Santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchanā[M 2.0056], ananuññātakāraṇā vikāle gāmappavesoti dve aṅgāni.

515. Here, regarding 'intermediate monastery', etc.: some say that on festival days and so on, when requested by people who wish to worship a Buddha image, etc., that is being made to circumambulate the village, or when requested by people for the purpose of pacifying illness, etc., it is allowable for bhikkhus to circumambulate the village right through the middle of the street, even without performing the procedure of being well-covered, etc. That statement should not be accepted, because it is not stated in the section on non-offenses, and because it is rejected by the text, 'Without descending from the road... it is a Pācittiya offense'. It should be understood that even when the Elder Ānanda recited the protective verses while going around Vesālī, it was done without violating the rule of being well-covered, etc., or it was done before that training rule was laid down. But some say: 'It is allowable for those staying in an intermediate monastery, etc., between villages to descend to the village street by way of going to meet or to see off venerable bhikkhus.' Even that is not allowable with respect to entering within the houses. However, it seems allowable to do so with respect to going towards an allowable area such as an intermediate monastery; this should be investigated. Not asking a bhikkhu who is present, and entering a village at an improper time without a permitted reason—these are the two factors.

Vikālagāmappavisanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on Entering a Village at an Improper Time is concluded.

4. Sūcigharasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning a Needle-Case

520. Catutthe pāḷiyaṃ vāsijaṭeti vāsidaṇḍake. Aṭṭhimayādisūcigharatā, karaṇakārāpanādivasena attano paṭilābhoti dve aṅgāni.

520. In the fourth training rule, in the Pāḷi, the term 'vāsijaṭa' means in the handle of an adze. The two factors are: the state of being a needle-case made of bone and so forth, and the acquisition of it for oneself by means of making it, causing it to be made, and so forth.

Sūcigharasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning a Needle-Case is concluded.

5. Mañcapīṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Beds and Benches

521. Pañcame pāḷiyaṃ āsayato, bhikkhave, moghapuriso veditabboti hīnajjhāsayavasena ayaṃ tucchapurisoti ñātabbo, hīnāya paccaye lolatāya puggalassa tucchatā ñātabbāti adhippāyo. Imasmiṃ sikkhāpade, ito paresu ca pañcasu attanā kārāpitassa paṭilābhe eva pācittiyaṃ. Paribhoge panassa, aññesañca dukkaṭameva. Pamāṇātikkantamañcapīṭhatā, attano karaṇakārāpanavasena paṭilābhoti dve aṅgāni.

521. In the fifth training rule, in the Pāḷi, the phrase 'O monks, a foolish person is to be known by his inclination' means this person is to be known as a vain person by means of his base disposition. The intention is that the vanity of a person is to be known by his greediness for an inferior requisite. In this training rule, and also in the five subsequent ones, a pācittiya offense is incurred only upon the acquisition of that which was caused to be made by oneself. In its use, however, for oneself and for others, there is only a dukkaṭa offense. The two factors are: the state of a bed or bench exceeding the prescribed measure, and the acquisition of it for oneself by means of making it or causing it to be made.

Mañcapīṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Beds and Benches is concluded.

6. Tūlonaddhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Stuffed Mattresses

526. Chaṭṭhe [V 2.0055] poṭakitūlanti tiṇagacchajātikānaṃ tūlaṃ. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva.

526. In the sixth training rule, the term 'poṭakitūla' refers to the floss from species of grass, shrubs, or trees. The remainder is just as has been stated.

Tūlonaddhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Stuffed Mattresses is concluded.

7. Nisīdanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning the Sitting-Cloth

531-536. Sattame [M 2.0057] nisīdanassa pamāṇātikkantatā, attano karaṇādinā paṭilābhoti dve aṅgāni.

In the seventh training rule, the two factors are: the state of the sitting-cloth exceeding the prescribed measure, and the acquisition of it for oneself by means of making it and so forth.

Nisīdanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning the Sitting-Cloth is concluded.

537-547. Iminā nayena aṭṭhamanavamadasamesupi aṅgāni veditabbāni. Sesaṃ sabbattha suviññeyyamevāti.

By this method, the factors are to be understood in the eighth, ninth, and tenth training rules as well. The remainder is easy to understand.

Niṭṭhito rājavaggo navamo.

The ninth, the Royal Chapter, is concluded.

Khuddakavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The method for the commentary on the minor training rules is concluded.

6. Pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ

6. The Section on Offenses to be Confessed

1. Paṭhamapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the First Training Rule Concerning Offenses to be Confessed

553. Pāṭidesanīyesu [M 2.0058][V 2.0056] paṭhame paṭidesetabbākāradassananti evaṃ āpattiṃ navakassa santike desetabbākāradassanaṃ. Iminā lakkhaṇena sambahulānaṃ āpattīnampi vuḍḍhassa santike ca desetabbākāro sakkā viññātunti. Tatrāyaṃ nayo – “gārayhe, āvuso, dhamme āpajjiṃ asappāye pāṭidesanīye”ti evaṃ sambahulāsu. Vuḍḍhassa pana santike “gārayhaṃ, bhante, dhammaṃ…pe… gārayhe, bhante, dhamme”ti yojanā veditabbā. Tattha asappāyanti saggamokkhantarāyakaranti attho. Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā antaraghare ṭhitāya hatthato sahatthā yāvakālikaggahaṇaṃ, ajjhoharaṇanti dve aṅgāni.

553. Among the rules on offenses to be confessed, in the first, the phrase 'showing the manner in which it should be confessed' means showing the manner of confessing the offense in the presence of a junior monk. By this characteristic, it is possible to understand the manner of confessing multiple offenses, and the manner of confessing in the presence of a senior monk. In this regard, this is the method: 'Friend, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable, confessable offense.' Thus, the application for multiple offenses is to be understood. In the presence of a senior monk, however, the application is to be understood as: 'Venerable sir, a blameworthy state... Venerable sir, blameworthy states...'. Therein, 'unsuitable' means that which creates an obstacle to heaven and liberation; this is the meaning. The two factors are: the taking of a yāvakālika item with one's own hand from the hand of an unrelated bhikkhunī standing within a house, and the act of swallowing it.

Paṭhamapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the First Training Rule Concerning Offenses to be Confessed is concluded.

558. Dutiye paripuṇṇūpasampannāya ananuññātākārena vosāsanā, anivāretvā bhojanajjhohāroti dve aṅgāni.

558. In the second training rule, the two factors are: instructing a fully ordained bhikkhunī in an unauthorized manner, and swallowing food without having been prevented.

563. Tatiye sekkhasammatatā, gharūpacāre animantitatā, gilānassa aniccabhattādiṃ gahetvā bhuñjananti tīṇi aṅgāni.

563. In the third training rule, the two factors are: the state of not being invited into the precincts of a household designated as a family of trainees (sekha), and the eating, by one who is not ill, after having accepted occasional food and so forth.

570. Catutthe sāsaṅkāraññasenāsanatā, ananuññātaṃ yāvakālikaṃ appaṭisaṃviditaṃ ajjhārāme paṭiggahetvā agilānassa ajjhoharaṇanti dve aṅgāni. Sesaṃ uttānameva.

570. In the fourth training rule, the two factors are: the state of being a forest dwelling that is deemed dangerous, and for one who is not ill, the swallowing of a yāvakālika item that was received inside the monastery, it being unannounced and unpermitted. The remainder is self-evident.

Pāṭidesanīyavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The method for the commentary on the offenses to be confessed is concluded.

7. Sekhiyakaṇḍaṃ

7. The Sekhiya Section

1. Parimaṇḍalavaggavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Parimaṇḍala Chapter

576. Sekhiyesu [M 2.0059][V 2.0057] yasmā vattakkhandhake (cūḷava. 356 ādayo) vuttavattānipi sikkhitabbattā sekhiyāneva, tasmā pārājikādīsu viyettha pāḷiyaṃ paricchedo na kato. Cārittanayadassanatthañca “yo pana bhikkhu olambento nivāseyya, dukkaṭa”nti avatvā “sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti sabbattha pāḷi āropitā. Padabhājane pana “āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti vuttattā sabbattha anādariyakaraṇe dukkaṭaṃ veditabbaṃ.

576. In the Sekhiyas, because the duties taught in the Vattakkhandhaka are to be trained in, they are indeed Sekhiyas. Therefore, unlike in the Pārājika and other sections, a classification is not made here in the Pāḷi. And to show the method of proper conduct, instead of saying, 'Whatever bhikkhu should wear his lower robe hanging down, there is a dukkaṭa offense,' the Pāḷi 'Training is to be undertaken' is applied in all cases. However, in the Padabhājana, because it is said, 'There is an offense of dukkaṭa,' it should be understood that in all cases, there is a dukkaṭa offense for acting with disrespect.

Aṭṭhaṅgulamattanti matta-saddena tato kiñci adhikaṃ, ūnampi saṅgaṇhāti. Teneva nisinnassa caturaṅgulamattampi vuttaṃ. Na hi nisinnassa caturaṅgulappamāṇaṃ, ṭhitassa aṭṭhaṅgulamevāti sakkā niyametuṃ ūnādhikattasambhavato. Tasmā yathā sāruppaṃ hoti evaṃ aṭṭhaṅgulānusārena nivāsanaññeva adhippetanti gahetabbaṃ. Teneva vakkhati “yo pana bhikkhu sukkhajaṅgho vā”tiādi. Kurundiyaṃ “ajānantassa anāpattī”ti ādaraṃ katvā uggaṇhantassāpi ajānanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tenāpi nirantaraṃ nivāsanapārupanavattaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ, asikkhito anādariyameva. Parimaṇḍalaggahaṇena ukkhipitvā nivāsanampi paṭikkhittanti āha “ukkhipitvā vā otāretvā vā”ti.

Regarding 'aṭṭhaṅgulamattaṃ' (a measure of eight finger-breadths): by the word 'matta' (measure), it includes something slightly more or less than that. For that very reason, even a measure of four finger-breadths is stated for one who is seated. Indeed, it is not possible to determine that for a seated person the measure is four finger-breadths and for a standing person it is only eight finger-breadths, because of the possibility of it being less or more. Therefore, it should be understood that what is intended is simply the wearing of the lower robe in a suitable manner, in accordance with the eight finger-breadths. For that very reason, it will be said, 'Whatever bhikkhu has thin shins...' and so on. In the Kurundī, the statement 'for one who does not know, there is no offense' is said in reference to the non-knowing of even one who is learning with respect. Even that one must constantly train in the duty of wearing the lower robe and donning the upper robe; for one who does not train, it is simply disrespect. By the inclusion of the term 'parimaṇḍala', even wearing the robe by lifting it up is prohibited; therefore, he said, 'whether having lifted it up or having lowered it down.'

Sacittakanti vatthuvijānanacittena sacittakaṃ. Sāratthadīpaniyaṃ pana upatissattheravādanayena lokavajjattaṃ gahetvā “vatthuvijānanacittena, paṇṇattivijānanacittena ca sacittaka”nti (sārattha. ṭī. sekhiyakaṇḍa 3.576) vuttaṃ. Tattha ca vatthuvijānanaṃ visuṃ na vattabbaṃ. Paṇṇattivijānanena tassāpi antogadhabhāvato idaṃ vatthuṃ evaṃ vītikkamantassa āpattīti vijānanto hi paṇṇattiṃ vijānātīti vuccati. Upatissattheravāde cettha paṇṇattiṃ ajānitvā aparimaṇḍalanivāsanādivatthumeva [V 2.0058] jānantassa paṇṇattivītikkamānādariyābhāvā sabbasekhiyesu anāpatti eva abhimatā, tañca na yuttaṃ kosambakkhandhake (mahāva. 451 ādayo) vaccakuṭiyaṃ udakāvasesaṃ ṭhapentassa paṇṇattivijānanābhāvepi āpattiyā vuttattā. Vuttañhi tattha “tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno hoti [M 2.0060]…pe… so aparena samayena tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi hotī”tiādi (mahāva. 451). Aṭṭhakathāyañcassa “tvaṃ ettha āpattibhāvaṃ na jānāsīti, āma na jānāmīti. Hotu āvuso, ettha āpattīti, sace hoti, desessāmīti. Sace pana te, āvuso, asañcicca asatiyā kataṃ, natthi āpattīti. So tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi ahosī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 451) vuttaṃ, tathā “adhammavādīti ukkhittānuvattakesu aññataro”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 457-458) ca vuttaṃ. Khandhakavattānañhi sekhiyattā tattha vutto nayo imesaṃ, idha vutto ca tesaṃ sādhāraṇova hotīti. Teneva “asañcicca asatiyā kataṃ, natthi āpattī”ti evaṃ idha vutto āpattinayo tatthāpi dassito. Tasmā phussadevattheravāde eva ṭhatvā vatthuvijānanacitteneva sabbasekhiyāni sacittakāni, na paṇṇattivijānanacittena. Bhiyyokamyatāyasūpabyañjanapaṭicchādanaujjhānasaññīti dve sikkhāpadāni lokavajjāni akusalacittāni, sesāni paṇṇattivajjāni, ticittāni, tivedanāni cāti gahaṇameva yuttataraṃ dissati. Tenevettha “asañciccāti purato vā pacchato vā olambetvā nivāsessāmīti evaṃ asañciccā”tiādinā vatthuajānanavaseneva anāpattivaṇṇanā katā, na paṇṇattivijānanacittavasena.

As for 'sacittaka', it is defined by a mind that knows the object. In the Sāratthadīpanī, however, following the view of Elder Upatissa and taking it as a worldly fault, it is said: 'It is sacittaka by a mind that knows the object and by a mind that knows the regulation.' In that statement, the knowing of the object should not be stated separately, because by the knowing of the regulation, that knowing of the object is also included within it. Indeed, one who knows, 'For a bhikkhu transgressing this object in this way, there is an offense,' is said to know the regulation. In the view of Elder Upatissa, for one who does not know the regulation but only knows the object—such as the act of wearing the lower robe unevenly—a non-offense is intended in all the Sekhiyas, due to the absence of transgression of or disrespect for the regulation. But that is not correct, because in the Kosambakkhandhaka, an offense is stated for one who leaves remaining water in a latrine, even in the absence of knowing the regulation. For it is said there: 'At that time, a certain bhikkhu had committed an offense... later, he came to hold the view that there was no offense in that offense,' and so on. And in its commentary it is said: 'When asked, "Do you not know that there is an offense in this?" he replied, "Yes, I do not know." When told, "Friend, let it be, there is an offense in this," he said, "If there is, I will confess it." When it was said, "But friend, if it was done by you unintentionally, through a lapse of mindfulness, there is no offense," he came to hold the view that there was no offense in that offense.' Likewise, it is also said: '"One with a wrong teaching" means one of the followers of the suspended bhikkhu.' Indeed, because the duties of the Khandhakas are Sekhiyas, the method taught there is common to these Sekhiya rules, and the method taught here is common to those Khandhaka duties. For that very reason, the principle of offense taught here—'If done unintentionally, through a lapse of mindfulness, there is no offense'—is also shown there. Therefore, standing only in the view of Elder Phussadeva, all Sekhiyas are 'sacittaka' only by a mind that knows the object, not by a mind that knows the regulation. The understanding that the two training rules—that concerning covering curry and condiments and that concerning reproachful perception—are worldly faults (lokavajja) with unwholesome minds, while the remaining rules are faults by regulation (paṇṇattivajja) with three kinds of mind and three kinds of feeling, appears more suitable. For that very reason, here the explanation of non-offense is made only by way of not knowing the object—as in the passage beginning, '"Unintentionally" means not intending thus: "I will wear it hanging down in front or behind"'—and not by way of a mind that knows the regulation.

Apica “yassa sacittakapakkhe cittaṃ akusalameva hoti, taṃ lokavajja”nti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanā) iminā lakkhaṇavacanenāpi cetaṃ sijjhati. Vatthuvijānanacittavaseneva hettha “sacittakapakkhe”ti vuttaṃ. Itarathā paṇṇattivijānanacittavasena sabbasikkhāpadānampi sacittakapakkhe cittassa akusalattaniyamena lokavajjattappasaṅgato paṇṇattivajjameva na siyā, idañca vacanaṃ niratthakaṃ siyā iminā vacanena nivattetabbassa sikkhāpadassa abhāvā. Na ca sekhiyesu vatthuvijānanacittena sacittakapakkhe cittaṃ pāṇātipātādīsu viya akusalamevāti niyamo atthi, yenettha lokavajjatā pasajjeyya, “anādariyaṃ paṭiccā”ti cetaṃ pāḷivacanaṃ vatthuṃ jānitvā tīhi cittehi vītikkamameva anādariyaṃ katvā vuttaṃ, na paṇṇattiṃ jānitvā akusalacitteneva vītikkamanti gahetabbaṃ. Aññathā khandhakapāḷiyā, aṭṭhakathāyañca pubbāparañca virujjhanatoti amhākaṃ khanti. Yathā vā na virujjhati, tathā ettha adhippāyo gavesitabbo. Anādariyaṃ, anāpattikāraṇābhāvo[M 2.0061], aparimaṇḍalanivāsananti [V 2.0059] imānettha tīṇi aṅgāni. Yathā cettha, evaṃ sabbattha. Kevalaṃ tattha tattha vuttapaṭipakkhakaraṇavasena tatiyaṅgayojanameva viseso.

Moreover, this is also established by this defining statement: 'That for which the mind is solely unwholesome on the side of having a mind, that is a worldly fault.' Here, 'on the side of having a mind' is said only by way of the mind that knows the object. Otherwise, if it were said by way of the mind that knows the rule, then for all training rules, due to the mind being invariably unwholesome on the side of having a mind, it would result in being a worldly fault, and thus a fault by regulation itself would not exist. And this statement would be meaningless, due to the absence of a training rule to be averted by this statement. And in the Sekhiya rules, there is no rule that the mind, in the case of having a mind that knows the object, is solely unwholesome, as in the case of killing living beings, etc., by which a worldly fault would arise here. And this Pāḷi phrase, 'on account of disrespect,' is said with reference to disrespecting the transgression itself, having known the object and transgressing with the three types of mind; it should not be understood as disrespecting the transgression with a solely unwholesome mind, having known the rule. Otherwise, it would contradict the Khandhaka Pāḷi and the Commentary, both preceding and following. This is our preference. Or, the meaning here should be sought in such a way that it does not contradict. Disrespect, the absence of a reason for no offense, and wearing the lower robe unevenly—these are the three factors here. As it is here, so it is in all cases. The only difference is the application of the third factor, by way of performing the opposite of what is stated in each respective case.

577. Dutiyādīsu gihipārutanti setapaṭapārutādi. Vihārepīti saṅghasannipātabuddhupaṭṭhānādikālaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

577. In the second and following cases, “clothed in a householder's garment” refers to being dressed in white robes and so on. “Even in the monastery” is said with reference to times such as gatherings of the Saṅgha or attending upon the Buddha.

578. Gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvātiādi paṭicchādanavidhidassanaṃ. Gīvaṃ paṭicchādetvātiādinā vuttattā sañcicca gīvaṃ, maṇibandhanañca appaṭicchādentassa āpatti. Etthāpi parimaṇḍalasikkhāpadassa sādhāraṇattā jāṇumaṇḍalato heṭṭhā caturaṅgulamattaṃ otāretvā anolambetvā parimaṇḍalameva pārupitabbaṃ.

578. “Having fastened the knot,” etc., is a demonstration of the method of covering. Because it is said, “having covered the neck,” etc., an offense is incurred by one who intentionally does not cover the neck and the wrist. Here too, because the training rule regarding the complete circle is applicable, it should be worn completely circularly, letting it hang down about four fingerbreadths below the knee-circle without letting it droop.

579. Vivaritvā nisīdatoti vihāre viya ekaṃsapārupanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Vāsatthāya upagatassā”ti vuttattā vāsādhippāyaṃ vinā dhammadesanaparittabhaṇanādiatthāya sucirampi nisīdantena sabbaṃ antaragharavattaṃ pūrenteneva nisīditabbaṃ. Nisīdanapaṭisaṃyuttesu eva ca sikkhāpadesu “vāsūpagatassā”ti anāpattiyā vuttattā vāsatthāya antaragharaṃ upagacchantenāpi suppaṭicchannatādisabbaṃ akopenteneva gantabbaṃ. “Vāsūpagatassā”ti hi vuttaṃ, na pana upagacchamānassāti. Keci pana “ekekasmiṃ paṭhamaṃ gantvā vāsapariggahe kate tato aññehi yathāsukhaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Apare pana “gehassāmikehi ‘yāva tumhe nivasissatha, tāva tumhākaṃ imaṃ gehaṃ demī’ti dinne aññehi avāsādhippāyehi antarārāme viya yathāsukhaṃ gantuṃ, nisīdituñca vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti, taṃ sabbaṃ na gahetabbaṃ tathāvacanābhāvā, dānalakkhaṇābhāvā, tāvattakena vihārasaṅkhyānupagamanato ca. “Yāva nisīdissatha, tāva tumhākaṃ imaṃ gehaṃ demī”ti dentopi hi tāvakālikameva deti vatthupariccāgalakkhaṇattā dānassa.

579. “Sitting down having opened up” is said with reference to draping the robe over one shoulder, as in a monastery. Since it is said, ‘for one who has come for the purpose of dwelling,’ one who is sitting even for a long time for the purpose of teaching the Dhamma, chanting protective texts, etc., without the intention of dwelling, must sit only after fulfilling all the duties for conduct within a village. And since it is only in the training rules connected with sitting that no-offense is stated ‘for one who has come for dwelling,’ even one who is approaching a house within a village for the purpose of dwelling must go without violating any of the rules such as being well-covered. For it is said, ‘for one who has come for dwelling,’ and not ‘for one who is approaching.’ Some, however, say: ‘When one monk has first gone and the taking of a residence has been done, it is then allowable for others to go as they please.’ Others, however, say: ‘When it is given by the householders, saying, “As long as you will reside, for so long I give this house to you,” it is allowable for other monks who also have the intention of dwelling to go and sit as they please, as if in a monastery compound.’ All of that should not be accepted, because there is no such statement, because there is no characteristic of a gift, and because by that much it does not come into the category of a monastery. For even one who gives saying, ‘As long as you will sit, for so long I give this house to you,’ gives only for that period of time, because a gift has the characteristic of relinquishing the object.

582. Catuhatthappamāṇanti vaḍḍhakīhatthaṃ sandhāya vuttanti vadanti.

582. “The measure of four cubits,” they say, is spoken with reference to a carpenter's cubit.

584. Ukkhittacīvaro [M 2.0062] hutvāti kaṭito uddhaṃ kāyabandhanādidassanavasenevukkhipanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ piṇḍāya carato pattaggahaṇādimattassa anuññātattā. Teneva “nisinnakāle pana dhamakaraṇa”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Nisinnakāle hi khandhe laggapattatthavikādito dhamakaraṇaṃ nīharantassa kaṭito uddhampi dissati, tathā adassetvā nīharitabbanti adhippāyo. Āsane nisīdantassāpi [V 2.0060] ca pārupitacīvaraṃ kiñci ukkhipitvā saṅghāṭiṃ jaṅghapiṇḍehi anukkhipitvāva nisīditabbaṃ. Imasmiññeva pana sikkhāpade “vāsūpagatassā”ti vuttattā nisīdanapaṭisaṃyuttesu chaṭṭhaaṭṭhamesu avuttattā vāsūpagatenāpi susaṃvutena okkhittacakkhunāva nisīditabbaṃ. Teneva mātikāṭṭhakathāyampi tesaṃ visesaṃ avatvā idheva “vāsūpagatassa pana anāpattī”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. ukkhittakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vuttā.

584. “Having a raised robe” is said with reference to lifting it above the waist only by way of showing the waistband, etc., because for one wandering for alms, only the mere holding of the bowl, etc., is permitted. For that very reason, it is said, “but when seated, the water-strainer,” etc. For when one is seated, while taking out the water-strainer from the bowl-bag slung on the shoulder, the part above the waist is also seen; the meaning is that it should be taken out without showing it like that. And even when sitting on a seat, one should sit only after lifting the upper robe a little, without lifting up the outer robe from the calves. However, since it is only in this very training rule that it is said, “for one who has come for dwelling,” and since it is not said in the sixth and eighth rules connected with sitting, even one who has come for dwelling must sit well-restrained and with downcast eyes. For that very reason, in the Mātikā Commentary as well, without stating a distinction for those rules, it is said only here, “but for one who has come for dwelling, there is no offense.”

Parimaṇḍalavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Parimaṇḍala Vagga is concluded.

2. Ujjagghikavaggavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Ujjagghika Vagga

586. Dutiyavaggādiujjagghikaappasaddesu nisīdanapaṭisaṃyuttesupi vāsūpagatassa anāpatti na vuttā, kāyappacālakādīsu eva pana vuttā. Pāḷipotthakesu panetaṃ kesuci peyyālena byāmohitattā na suṭṭhu viññāyati. Yattha ca antaraghare dhammaṃ vā desentassa, pātimokkhaṃ vā uddisantassa mahāsaddena yāvaparisasāvanepi anāpatti evāti daṭṭhabbaṃ tathā ānandattheramahindattherādīhi ācaritattā.

586. In the Ujjagghika and Appasadda training rules, which are at the beginning of the second vagga, even in those connected with sitting, no offense is stated for a monk who is dwelling. However, it is stated only in the cases of Kāyappacālaka and so on. But in some Pāḷi texts, this is not well understood because it is obscured by abbreviation. And it should be understood that it is indeed no offense when, inside a house, one is teaching the Dhamma or reciting the Pātimokkha, even causing it to be heard by the entire assembly with a loud voice, because it was practiced in that way by the Elder Ānanda, the Elder Mahinda, and others.

Ujjagghikavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Ujjagghika Vagga is concluded.

3. Khambhakatavaggavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Khambhakatavagga

603. Patte gahaṇasaññā assa atthīti pattasaññīti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “patte saññaṃ katvā”ti vuttaṃ.

603. To show this meaning: ‘He is one with perception of the bowl (pattasaññī) because for him there is the perception of holding the bowl,’ the phrase ‘having made a perception regarding the bowl’ is stated.

604. Oloṇīti ekā byañjanavikati. Kañjikatakkādirasoti keci. Maṃsarasādīnīti ādi-saddena avasesā sabbāpi byañjanavikati saṅgahitā.

604. ‘Oloṇī’ is a type of special dish. Some say it is the juice of rice-gruel, buttermilk, and so on. In the phrase ‘meat-broth and so on’ (maṃsarasādīni), by the word ‘and so on’ (ādi), all remaining types of special dishes are included.

605. Samabharitanti [M 2.0063] racitaṃ. Heṭṭhā orohatīti samantā okāsasambhavato hatthena samaṃ kariyamānaṃ heṭṭhā bhassati. Pattamatthake ṭhapitāni pūvāni eva vaṭaṃsakākārena ṭhapitattā “pūvavaṭaṃsaka”nti vuttāni. Keci pana “pattaṃ gahetvā thūpīkataṃ piṇḍapātaṃ racitvā diyyamānameva gaṇhato āpatti, hatthagate eva pana patte diyyamāne thūpīkatampi gahetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti [V 2.0061] vadanti, taṃ na gahetabbameva “samatittika”nti bhāvanapuṃsakavasena sāmaññato vuttattā.

605. ‘Samabharitaṃ’ means arranged. ‘It descends below’ means: while being made even by hand, it slips down because there is space all around. Only the cakes placed on top of the bowl are called ‘pūvavaṭaṃsaka’ (cake-garland) because they are placed in the shape of a head-garland. But some say: ‘There is an offense for one who receives almsfood that is being given arranged in a heap after taking the bowl; but when it is being given into the bowl that is already in hand, it is permissible to receive it even if heaped.’ That statement should not be accepted at all, because ‘samatittika’ is stated generally by way of the abstract neuter form.

Khambhakatavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Khambhakatavagga is concluded.

4. Sakkaccavaggavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Sakkaccavagga

608. Catutthavaggādīsu sapadānanti ettha dānaṃ vuccati avakhaṇḍanaṃ, apetaṃ dānato apadānaṃ, saha apadānena sapadānaṃ, avakhaṇḍanavirahitaṃ anupaṭipāṭiyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tenāha “tattha tattha odhiṃ akatvā”tiādi.

608. In the fourth vagga and so on, in the word ‘sapadānaṃ,’ ‘dānaṃ’ is called cutting; ‘apadānaṃ’ is that which is devoid of cutting; ‘sapadānaṃ’ is that which is together with being devoid of cutting. This means: devoid of cutting, in sequence. Therefore, he said, ‘without making a limit here and there,’ and so on.

611. Viññattiyanti sūpodanaviññattisikkhāpadaṃ sandhāya vadati. “Vattabbaṃ natthī”ti iminā pāḷiyāva sabbaṃ viññāyatīti dasseti. Tattha pāḷiyaṃ asañciccātiādīsu vatthumattaṃ ñatvā bhuñjanena āpattiṃ āpajjantasseva puna paṇṇattiṃ ñatvā mukhagataṃ chaḍḍetukāmassa yaṃ aruciyā paviṭṭhaṃ, taṃ asañcicca paviṭṭhaṃ nāma, tattha anāpatti. Tadeva puna aññavihitatāya vā aviññattamidantisaññāya vā bhuñjane “asatiyā”ti vuccati.

611. The word ‘viññattiyaṃ’ is said with reference to the training rule on soliciting curry and rice. By the phrase ‘there is nothing to be said,’ he shows that everything is understood from the Pāḷi itself. Therein, in the Pāḷi, in phrases such as ‘unintentionally,’ for a monk who incurs an offense by eating, knowing only the basis of the offense, and who then, having known the regulation, wishes to discard what has entered his mouth—whatever entered due to unwillingness is called ‘entered unintentionally.’ Therein, there is no offense. If that same food is eaten again, either through distraction or with the perception, ‘This was not solicited,’ it is called ‘due to unmindfulness.’

613. “Aññassatthāyā”ti idamassa sikkhāpadassa attano atthāya viññāpetvā sayaṃ bhuñjane eva paññattattā iminā sikkhāpadena anāpattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Pañcasahadhammikānaṃ pana atthāya aññātakaappavāritaṭṭhāne viññāpento viññattikkhaṇe aṭṭhakathāsu suttānulomato vuttaakataviññattidukkaṭato na muccati. Sañcicca bhuñjanakkhaṇe sayañca aññe ca micchājīvato na muccantīti gahetabbaṃ.

613. The phrase 'for the sake of another' is said with reference to there being no offense according to this training rule, because this training rule was laid down only for eating oneself after having solicited for one's own benefit. However, a monk who solicits for the benefit of five companions in the holy life in a place of non-relatives where one is not invited is not, at the moment of soliciting, freed from the dukkaṭa offense for an unfulfilled solicitation stated in the commentaries in accordance with the suttas. It should be understood that at the moment of eating intentionally, both he himself and the others are not freed from wrong livelihood.

615. “Kukkuṭaṇḍaṃ atikhuddaka”nti idaṃ asāruppavasena vuttaṃ, atimahante eva āpattīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Bhuñjantena pana corādibhayaṃ paṭicca mahantampi aparimaṇḍalampi [M 2.0064] katvā sīghaṃ bhuñjanavasenettha āpadā. Evamaññesupi yathānurūpaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

615. The phrase 'a chicken's egg is too small' is said by way of it being unsuitable; it should be understood that there is an offense only in the case of what is too large. But for one eating on account of fear of thieves and so on, making a large and also unrounded morsel and eating quickly constitutes a time of distress herein. Similarly, in other Sekhiya rules also, it should be understood as is appropriate.

Sakkaccavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Sakkacca Vagga is concluded.

5. Kabaḷavaggavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Kabaḷa Vagga

617. Anāhaṭe [V 2.0062] kabaḷe mukhadvāravivaraṇe pana payojanābhāvā “āpadāsū”ti na vuttaṃ. Evamaññesupi īdisesu.

617. When a morsel of food has not been brought, since there is no purpose in opening the mouth-door, 'in times of distress' was not said. It is the same in other such training rules.

618. Sabbaṃ hatthanti hatthekadesā aṅguliyo vuttā “hatthamuddā”tiādīsu viya, tasmā ekaṅgulimpi mukhe pakkhipituṃ na vaṭṭati.

618. By 'the whole hand,' the fingers, which are a part of the hand, are meant, just as in expressions such as 'hand-seal.' Therefore, it is not allowable to put even one finger into the mouth.

Kabaḷavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Kabaḷa Vagga is concluded.

6. Surusuruvaggavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Surusuru Vagga

627. Pāḷiyaṃ sītīkatoti sītapīḷito. Silakabuddhoti parihāsavacanametaṃ. Silakañhi kiñci disvā “buddho aya”nti voharanti.

627. In the Pāli, `sītīkato` means 'afflicted by cold.' The term `silakabuddho` is a word of mockery. For, having seen some stone, they call it, 'This is a Buddha.'

628. “Aṅguliyo mukhe pavesetvā bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti iminā sabbaṃ hatthaṃ antomukhe pakkhipanasikkhāpadassapi paviṭṭhaṅgulinillehanena imassapi sikkhāpadassa anāpattiṃ dasseti. Eseva nayoti ghanayāguādīsu pattaṃ hatthena, oṭṭhañca jivhāya nillehituṃ vaṭṭatīti atidisati. Tasmāti yasmā ghanayāguādivirahitaṃ nillehituṃ na vaṭṭati.

628. By the statement, 'It is allowable to eat by inserting the fingers into the mouth,' it shows a non-offense for both the training rule on inserting the whole hand into the mouth and for this training rule by means of licking fingers that have entered the mouth. By 'This is the method,' it extends the rule, thus: in the case of thick gruel and so forth, it is allowable to lick the bowl with the hand and the lips with the tongue. 'Therefore' means 'because': because it is not allowable to lick that which is without thick gruel and so forth.

634. Vilīvacchattanti veṇupesikāhi kataṃ. Maṇḍalabaddhānīti dīghasalākāsu tiriyaṃ valayākārena salākaṃ ṭhapetvā suttehi baddhāni dīghañca tiriyañca ujukameva salākāyo ṭhapetvā daḷhabaddhāni ceva tiriyaṃ ṭhapetvā dīghadaṇḍakeheva saṅkocārahaṃ katvā sutteheva tiriyaṃ baddhāni. Tatthajātakadaṇḍakena katanti saha daṇḍakena chinnatālapaṇṇādīhi kataṃ. Chattapādukāyāti yasmiṃ chattadaṇḍakoṭiṃ pavesetvā chattaṃ ujukaṃ ṭhapetvā heṭṭhā chāyāya nisīdanti, tiṭṭhanti vā, tādise chattādhāre.

634. `Vilīvacchatta` means an umbrella made of bamboo strips. `Maṇḍalabaddhāni` are those where a rod is placed crosswise in a circular shape on long splints and bound with threads. Another type are those firmly bound by placing rods straight both lengthwise and crosswise. Another type are those made collapsible by placing long sticks crosswise and binding them crosswise with only threads. `Tatthajātakadaṇḍakena kataṃ` means made with its own stalk, such as from cut palm leaves and so on, along with the stalk. `Chattapādukāya` refers to an umbrella stand, in which one may sit or stand in the shade beneath after inserting the tip of the umbrella staff to place the umbrella upright.

637. Cāpoti [M 2.0065] majjhe vaṅkakājadaṇḍasadisā dhanuvikati. Kodaṇḍoti viddhadaṇḍā dhanuvikati.

637. `Cāpa` is a type of bow, similar to a carrying-pole staff that is curved in the middle. `Kodaṇḍa` is a type of bow with a pierced shaft, that is, a crossbow.

Surusuruvaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Surusuru Vagga is concluded.

7. Pādukavaggavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Pāduka Vagga

647. Sattamavagge [V 2.0063] rukkhato patitoti ekaṃ olambanasākhaṃ gahetvā patito. Pāḷiyāti attano ācārappakāsakaganthassa. Dhīratthūti dhī atthu, nindā hotūti attho. Vinipātanahetunāti vinipātanassa hetubhāvena. Tvanti upayogatthe paccattavacanaṃ, taṃ icceva vā pāṭho. Asmāti pāsāṇo.

647. In the seventh chapter, 'he fell from the tree' means he fell after grasping a single hanging branch. `Pāḷiyā` refers to one's own text that explains conduct. `Dhīratthu` means 'Let there be disgust! Let there be blame!' This is the meaning. `Vinipātanahetunā` means by being the cause of the fall. The word `tvaṃ` is a nominative used in the sense of the accusative; or, the reading is simply `taṃ`. `Asmā` means stone.

649. Na kathetabbanti therena attano kaṅkhāṭṭhānassa pucchitattā vuttaṃ. Daharassa atthakosallaṃ ñātuṃ pucchitena uccāsane nisinnassa ācariyassa anuyogadānanayena vattuṃ vaṭṭati.

649. 'It should not be spoken' was said by the elder because he was asked about his own point of doubt. When asked in order for his skill in the meaning to be known, it is allowable for a junior monk to speak to a teacher sitting on a high seat in the manner of giving a clarification.

652. Kheḷena cettha siṅghāṇikāpi saṅgahitāti ettha udakagaṇḍusakaṃ katvā ucchukacavarādiñca mukheneva harituṃ udakesu chaḍḍetuṃ vaṭṭatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva.

652. Here, in the phrase 'By spittle, mucus is also included,' it should be understood thus: it is allowable to take a mouthful of water and discard it on green grass or in water, and also to discard sugarcane refuse and so forth from the mouth itself onto green grass or into water. The rest is clear everywhere.

Pādukavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Pāduka Vagga is concluded.

Sekhiyavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The method of the commentary on the Sekhiya is concluded.

655. Adhikaraṇasamathesu ca idha vattabbaṃ natthi.

655. And regarding the Adhikaraṇasamathas, there is nothing to be said here.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya vimativinodaniyaṃ

Thus in the Vimativinodanī, the sub-commentary to the Samantapāsādikā, the commentary on the Vinaya.

Bhikkhuvibhaṅgavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The method of the commentary on the Bhikkhuvibhaṅga is concluded.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Bhikkhunīvibhaṅgavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga

1. Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

The Pārājika Section

1. Ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning an Act Above the Kneecap

656. Bhikkhunīvibhaṅge [V 2.0064][M 2.0067] migāramātuyāti migāramātu, visākhāyāti attho.
