Pākaṭaṭṭhānepi pana nakhapiṭṭhippamāṇato ūnataraṃ avaḍḍhanakaṃ vaṭṭatīti ye gaṇheyyuṃ, tesaṃ taṃ gahaṇaṃ paṭisedhetuṃ “mukhe panā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

88-9. In the stories of the five diseases and so on, in the Pāli, 'somhi arogo, vibbhamissāmi' has the meaning: 'I am free from disease; I will disrobe.' In the phrase 'nakhapiṭṭhippamāṇaṃ' (the measure of the back of a nail), the back of the little fingernail is intended. Because it is said, 'In a covered place, a spot the measure of the back of a nail that is in a non-spreading state is allowable,' it is thereby established that in an uncovered place even such a spot is not allowable, and in a covered place, a spot that is in a spreading state is also not allowable. Furthermore, in order to refute the view of those who might hold that in a visible place a non-spreading spot smaller than the measure of the back of a nail is allowable, the passage beginning with 'mukhe pana' ('But on the face...') was spoken.

Kolaṭṭhimattakopīti badaraṭṭhippamāṇopi. Avaḍḍhanakapakkhe ṭhitopi na vaṭṭatīti ettha pi-saddena kolaṭṭhimattato khuddakataropi gaṇḍo na vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Tenāha “sacchaviṃ kāretvā”ti, vijjamānacchaviṃ katvāti attho. “Sañchavi”nti vā pāṭho, sañjātacchavinti attho. Gaṇḍādīsu vūpasantesupi gaṇḍānaṃ vivaṇṇampi hoti, taṃ vaṭṭati.

'Kolaṭṭhimattako pi' means 'even the size of a jujube stone' (badaraṭṭhi). Here, in the phrase 'even when it is in a non-spreading state, it is not allowable,' the word 'pi' ('even') shows that a boil even smaller than the size of a jujube stone is not allowable. Therefore, it was said, 'sacchaviṃ kāretvā', meaning 'having made the skin exist.' Or, the reading is 'sañchavi', meaning 'having made the skin well-formed.' Even when boils and so on have subsided, that place is also discolored; that is allowable.

Padumapuṇḍarīkapattavaṇṇanti rattapadumasetapadumapupphadalavaṇṇaṃ. Kuṭṭhe vuttanayenevāti paṭicchannaṭṭhāne avaḍḍhanakaṃ vaṭṭati, aññattha na kiñcipi vaṭṭatīti vuttanayaṃ dasseti. Sosabyādhīti khayarogo. Yakkhummāroti kadāci kadāci āgantvā bhūmiyaṃ pātetvā hatthamukhādikaṃ avayavaṃ bhūmiyaṃ ghaṃsanako yakkhova rogo.

'Padumapuṇḍarīkapattavaṇṇaṃ' means 'the color of the petals of a red lotus (rattapaduma) or a white lotus (setapaduma) flower.' The phrase 'kuṭṭhe vuttanayeneva' ('just as was stated in the case of leprosy') indicates the method that was stated: 'In a covered place, a non-spreading one is allowable; elsewhere, nothing at all is allowable.' 'Sosabyādhi' is consumption (khayaroga). 'Yakkhummāro' is a disease like a demon (yakkha) that, coming from time to time, fells one to the ground and causes one to rub a body part, such as a hand or face, on the ground.

Pañcābādhavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of the Five Diseases is finished.

Rājabhaṭavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of the Royal Servant

90. Na [V 2.0106] dānāhaṃ devassa bhaṭoti āpucchatīti raññā eva dinnaṭṭhānantaraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yo pana rājakammikehi amaccādīhi ṭhapito, amaccādīnaṃ eva vā bhaṭo hoti, tena taṃ taṃ amaccādimpi āpucchituṃ vaṭṭati.

90. The statement, 'I am not now a servant of the king, so I take leave,' was said with reference to a special position given by the king himself. However, as for one who is appointed by royal officials such as ministers, or is a servant of those ministers, it is allowable for him to take leave from those respective ministers.

Rājabhaṭavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of the Royal Servant is concluded.

Coravatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of the Thief

91. Tasmāti [M 2.0110] bhagavā sayaṃ yasmā dhammassāmī, tasmā aṅgulimālaṃ ehibhikkhubhāvena pabbājesi, bhikkhūnaṃ pana sikkhāpadaṃ paññapento evamāhāti adhippāyo. Evaṃ jānantīti sīlavā jātoti jānanti.

91. This is the meaning: because the Blessed One is himself the Lord of the Dhamma, therefore he ordained Aṅgulimāla with the 'Come, bhikkhu' status. But when wishing to lay down a training rule for the bhikkhus, he spoke thus. 'They know thus' means they know, 'He has become virtuous.'

92. Uparamanti viramanti. Bhinditvāti andubandhanaṃ bhinditvā. Chinditvāti saṅkhalikaṃ chinditvā. Muñcitvāti rajjubandhanaṃ muñcitvā. Vivaritvāti gāmabandhanādīsu gāmadvārādīnaṃ vivaritvā. Apassamānānanti purisaguttiyaṃ gopakānaṃ apassantānaṃ.

92. 'Uparamanti' means they refrain. 'Bhinditvā' means having broken into a prison. 'Chinditvā' means having cut an iron fetter. 'Muñcitvā' means having untied a rope bond. 'Vivaritvā' means having opened village gates and so on in village enclosures and so on. 'Apassamānānaṃ' means while the guards are not seeing during the watch.

95. Purimanayenevāti “kasāhato katadaṇḍakammo”ti ettha vuttanayeneva.

95. 'Purimanayeneva' means in the very manner stated in the passage, 'struck by a whip, one on whom punishment has been inflicted.'

Coravatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of the Thief is concluded.

Iṇāyikavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of the Debtor

96. Palātopīti iṇasāmikānaṃ āgamanaṃ ñatvā bhayena palāto. Gīvā hotīti iṇāyikabhāvaṃ ñatvā anādarena iṇamuttake bhikkhubhāve pavesitattā. Upaḍḍhupaḍḍhanti thokathokaṃ. Dātabbamevāti iṇāyikena dhanaṃ sampaṭicchatu vā mā vā, dāne saussāheneva bhavitabbaṃ. Aññehi ca bhikkhūhi “mā dhuraṃ nikkhipāhī”ti vatvā sahāyakehi bhavitabbanti dasseti. Dhuranikkhepena hissa bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbatā siyāti.

96. `Palāto` means: having known of the creditors' arrival, he has fled out of fear. `Gīvā hoti` means: because of having admitted him into the state of a bhikkhu, which is free from debt, without respect, knowing his status as a debtor, one becomes a substitute. `Upaḍḍhupaḍḍha` means little by little. By `dātabbameva`, it is shown that whether the debtor bhikkhu receives wealth or not, he should be diligent in giving. And other bhikkhus, having said, 'Do not lay down the burden,' should act as companions. Indeed, if the burden is laid down, he would have to be made to pay the value of the goods.

Iṇāyikavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of the Debtor is concluded.

Dāsavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of the Slave

97. “Dāsacārittaṃ [V 2.0107] āropetvā kīto”ti iminā dāsabhāvaparimocanatthāya kītakaṃ nivatteti. Tādiso hi dhanakkītopi adāso eva. Tattha tattha cārittavasenāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ janapade dāsapaṇṇajjhāpanādinā [M 2.0111] adāsakaraṇaniyāmena. Abhisekādīsu sabbabandhanāni mocāpenti, taṃ sandhāya “sabbasādhāraṇenā”ti vuttaṃ.

97. By this phrase, 'bought after imposing the conduct of a slave,' he annuls the state of being bought for the purpose of being freed from slavery. Indeed, such a one, even if bought with money, is not a slave at all. 'By the power of custom in various places' means: in this or that country, by the rule of making one not a slave, such as by the burning of the slave-register. At consecrations and so on, they cause all bonds to be released; with reference to that, it was said, 'by a general amnesty.'

Sayameva paṇṇaṃ āropenti, na vaṭṭatīti tā bhujissitthiyo “mayampi vaṇṇadāsiyo homā”ti attano rakkhaṇatthāya sayameva rājūnaṃ dāsipaṇṇe attano nāmaṃ likhāpenti, tāsaṃ puttāpi rājadāsāva honti, tasmā te pabbājetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Tehi adinnā na pabbājetabbāti yattakā tesaṃ sāmino, tesu ekena adinnepi na pabbājetabbā.

As for 'They themselves impose the registration; it is not allowable': those freedwomen, for their own protection, thinking, 'We too will be registered slave-women,' of their own accord have their names written in the kings' register of female slaves. Their sons also become royal slaves. Therefore, it is not allowable to ordain them. As for 'If not given by them, they should not be ordained': however many masters they have, even if not given permission by one of them, they should not be ordained.

Bhujisse pana katvā pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭatīti yassa vihārassa te ārāmikā dinnā, tasmiṃ vihāre saṅghaṃ ñāpetvā phātikammena dhanāni datvā bhujisse katvā pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Takkaṃ sīse āsittakasadisāva hontīti kesuci janapadesu adāse karontā takkaṃ sīse āsiñcanti, tena kira te adāsā honti, evamidampi ārāmikavacanena dānampīti adhippāyo. Tathā dinnepi saṅghassa ārāmikadāso evāti “neva pabbājetabbo”ti vuttaṃ. “Tāvakāliko nāmā”ti vuttattā kālaparicchedaṃ katvā vā pacchāpi gahetukāmatāya vā dinnaṃ sabbaṃ tāvakālikamevāti gahetabbaṃ. Nissāmikadāso nāma yassa sāmikulaṃ aññātikaṃ maraṇena parikkhīṇaṃ, na koci tassa dāyādo, so pana samānajātikehi vā nivāsagāmavāsīhi vā issarehi vā bhujisso katova pabbājetabbo. Devadāsāpi dāsā eva. Te hi katthaci dese rājadāsā honti, katthaci vihāradāsā, tasmā pabbājetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Dāsampi pabbājetvā sāmike disvā paṭicchādanatthaṃ apanento padavārena adinnādānāpattiyā kāretabbo, dāsassa pana palāyato anāpatti.

However, having made him a freeman, it is allowable to ordain him. This means: if those monastery attendants are given to a certain monastery, in that monastery, having informed the Sangha, having given wealth by way of a compensatory transaction, and having made them freemen, it is allowable to ordain them. 'They become just like one on whose head buttermilk has been poured' means: in some countries, when making non-slaves, they pour buttermilk on their heads, and by that, it is said, they become non-slaves. This is the intention of the Mahāpaccarī commentary: that this gift, signified by the term 'monastery attendant', is also like this. Even if given in that way, he is still a monastery slave of the Sangha; therefore, it is said in the Kurundī commentary, 'He should not be ordained at all.' Because it is said, 'It is temporary,' it should be understood that everything given either by setting a time limit or with the desire to take it back later is only temporary. An ownerless slave is one whose master's family, having no relatives, has been destroyed by death, and there is no heir of that family. Such a one, however, should be ordained only after being made a freeman by those of equal birth, or by the inhabitants of his village, or by the authorities. Temple slaves are also slaves. Indeed, in some places they are royal slaves; in other places, they are monastery slaves. Therefore, it is not allowable to ordain them. Having ordained a slave, if one, on seeing the masters, leads him away for the sake of concealment, he should be made to deal with an offense of theft according to the number of steps. For the fleeing slave-bhikkhu, however, there is no offense.

Dāsavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of the Slave is concluded.

Kammārabhaṇḍuvatthādikathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Stories Beginning with the Story of the Blacksmith Bhaṇḍu

98. Bhaṇḍukammāpucchānādikathāyaṃ kammārabhaṇḍūti daharatāya amoḷibandho muṇḍikasīso kammāradārako [V 2.0108] eva vutto. Tulādhāramuṇḍakoti ettha tulādhārāti tambasuvaṇṇādīnaṃ tulaṃ hatthena dhāretīti [M 2.0112] kammārā “tulādhārā”ti vuttā, tesu eko muṇḍikasīso daharoti attho. Tenāha “pañcasikho taruṇadārako”ti. Ekāva sikhā pañca veṇiyo katvā bandhanena pañcasikhāti vuccati, sā etassa atthīti pañcasikho, tassa sikhaṃ chindantā kañci bhikkhuṃ ajānāpetvāva pabbājesuṃ. Tena bhaṇḍukammāpalokanaṃ anuññātaṃ. Sīmāpariyāpanneti baddhasīmāya sati tadantogadhe, asati upacārasīmantogadheti attho. Ettha ca kiñcāpi “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghaṃ apaloketuṃ bhaṇḍukammāyā”ti ettakameva vuttaṃ, na pana anapalokentassa āpatti vuttā, tathāpi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “sabbe āpucchitā amhehītisaññino…pe… pabbājentassapi anāpattī”ti vuttattā sañcicca anāpucchā kese ohārentassa dukkaṭamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kesoropanampi samaṇapabbajanavohāraṃ labhatīti āha “imassa samaṇakaraṇa”ntiādi. Ekasikhāmattadharoti ettha ekena kesena sikhā ekasikhāti vadanti, appakesāva sikhā evaṃ vuttāti gahetabbā. Ekakesampi pana anāpucchā chindituṃ na vaṭṭatiyeva.

98. In the discussion on matters such as asking permission for the act concerning Bhaṇḍu, by 'kammārabhaṇḍu' is meant only the blacksmith's boy who, due to his youth, had no top-knot tied and had a shaven head. Here, in 'Tulādhāramuṇḍaka', blacksmiths are called 'tulādhārā' because they hold ('dhārenti') scales ('tulaṃ') in their hands for copper, gold, and so on; among them, one young boy with a shaven head is the meaning. Therefore, it is said, ‘a young boy with five top-knots.’ A single top-knot, when made into five braids and tied, is called 'pañcasikhā'; he who has this is called 'pañcasikho'. While cutting his top-knot, they ordained him without informing any bhikkhu. Therefore, announcing the act concerning Bhaṇḍu was permitted. By 'sīmāpariyāpanne' is meant, if there is a consecrated boundary, those within it; if not, those within the vicinity-boundary. And here, although only this much was said, ‘Bhikkhus, I permit the Saṅgha to be announced for the act concerning Bhaṇḍu,’ and no offense was stated for one who does not announce it, nevertheless, because it is said in the commentary, ‘For one who perceives, “All have been asked by us,”... and so on... there is no offense even for the one who ordains,’ it should be understood that for one who intentionally removes hair without asking, there is only a dukkaṭa offense. The removal of hair also receives the designation of ‘making an ascetic’ and ‘ordination’; therefore, it is said, ‘This is the making of an ascetic,’ and so on. Here, in 'ekasikhāmattadharo', some say that 'ekasikhā' is a top-knot made with a single hair; it should be taken that a top-knot with very little hair is so called. However, it is not at all proper to cut even a single hair without asking.

100. Vāmahatthenāti dakkhiṇahatthena bhuñjanato vuttaṃ.

100. ‘With the left hand’ is said because one eats with the right hand.

103-4. Nissayamuccanakassa vattesu pañcakachakkesu pana “ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni…pe… anubyañjanaso”ti ettha sabbopi cāyaṃ pabhedo mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ ñātāyaṃ ñāto hoti. “Āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānātī”ti idañca attanā ñātaṭṭhānesu āpattādiṃ sandhāya vuttanti na gahetabbaṃ.

However, in the fivefold and sixfold sections on the duties for one released from dependence, here in the phrase ‘both Pātimokkhas for him... and so on... down to the minor details,’ this entire distinction is known when the commentary on the Mātikā is known. And this statement, ‘He knows an offense, he knows a non-offense,’ should be taken as being said in reference to offenses and so on in instances that ought to be known by oneself.

Kammārabhaṇḍuvatthādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the stories beginning with the story of the blacksmith Bhaṇḍu is concluded.

Rāhulavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of Rāhula

105. Pokkharavassanti pokkhare padumagacche viya atemitukāmānaṃ sarīrato pavaṭṭanakavassaṃ. Tasmiṃ kira vassante temitukāmāva tementi, na itare. “Bhikkhaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vatvā gato nāma natthīti attano santake rajje sabbampi sāpateyyaṃ sayameva paribhuñjissatīti gāravena [M 2.0113] suddhodanamahārājāpi na nimantesi, gantvā pana gehe sakalarattiṃ mahādānañceva buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa āsanapaññattiṭṭhānālaṅkārañca saṃvidahantova vītināmesi.

105. Pokkharavassa (lotus-rain) means a rain that, like rain in a lotus grove, flows from the bodies of those who do not wish to be wet. When that rain falls, only those who wish to be wet become wet; the others do not. Thinking, 'It is not the case that he has gone away after saying, “Take alms,” and he himself will enjoy all the wealth in his own kingdom,' King Suddhodana, out of respect, did not invite him. Instead, having gone to the palace, he spent the entire night arranging a great offering, as well as the preparation of seats and the decoration of the place for the Sangha with the Buddha at its head.

Na [V 2.0109] koci…pe… pattaṃ vā aggahesīti bhagavā attano pitu nivesanameva gamissatītisaññāya naggahesi. Kulanagareti ñātikulantake nagare. Piṇḍacāriyavattanti attano ñātigāmesupi sapadānacārikavattaṃ. Bhikkhāya cāro caraṇaṃ etassāti bhikkhācāro, khattiyo.

‘No one…pe… took the bowl’ means: no one took it, with the thought that the Blessed One would go to his own father's residence. ‘In the clan city’ (kulanagare) means in the city belonging to the kinsmen-family. ‘The practice of the alms-round’ (piṇḍacāriyavattaṃ) means the practice of going from house to house in order even in the villages of one's own relatives. ‘His wandering is for alms, therefore he is an alms-farer’ (bhikkhācāro); this refers to the khattiya.

Uttiṭṭheti uttiṭṭhitvā paresaṃ gharadvāre uddissa ṭhatvā gahetabbapiṇḍe. Nappamajjeyyāti nimantanādivasena labbhamānapaṇītabhojanaṃ paṭikkhipitvā piṇḍāya caraṇavasena tattha nappamajjeyya. Dhammanti anesanaṃ pahāya sapadānaṃ caranto tameva bhikkhācariyadhammaṃ sucaritaṃ careyya. Sukhaṃ setīti catūhi iriyāpathehi sukhaṃ viharatīti attho.

‘Uttiṭṭhe’ (one should stand up): This refers to the alms-food to be received by standing at the doors of others' houses. ‘Nappamajjeyya’ (one should not be negligent) means: having rejected exquisite food obtained by way of invitations and so on, one should not be negligent in the alms-food obtained by wandering for alms. ‘Dhammaṃ’ means: having abandoned wrong livelihood, while wandering from house to house in order, one should practice well that very Dhamma of the alms-round. ‘Sukhaṃ seti’ (one dwells happily) means: one dwells happily in the four postures; this is the meaning.

Dutiyagāthāyaṃ na naṃ duccaritanti vesiyādibhede agocare caraṇavasena taṃ yathāvuttaṃ dhammaṃ duccaritaṃ na ca care. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Imaṃ pana gāthaṃ sutvāti nivesane nisinnena bhagavatā ñātisamāgame attano piṇḍāya caraṇaṃ nissāya pavattāya gāthāya vuttaṃ imaṃ dutiyagāthaṃ sutvā.

In the second verse, ‘na naṃ duccaritaṃ’ (one should not practice misconduct) means: one should not practice that misconduct as described, by way of wandering in unsuitable resorts of various kinds, such as a prostitute's house. The rest is as has been explained. ‘Imaṃ pana gāthaṃ sutvā’ (having heard this verse) means: having heard this second verse, which was spoken by the Blessed One, who was seated in the palace during an assembly of relatives, when a talk arose concerning his own wandering for alms-food.

Dhammapālajātakantiādīsu pana tato parakālesupi rañño pavatti parinibbānaṃ pāpetvā yathāpasaṅgavasena dassetuṃ vuttā. Tenāha “sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikatvā”tiādi. Sirigabbhaṃ gantvāti ettha yadi hi bhagavā tadaheva gantvā na passeyya, sā hadayena phalitena mareyyāti agamāsīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

In the Dhammapāla Jātaka and other texts, however, the king's story, leading up to his parinibbāna, is spoken of even in later times, in order to show it as the occasion arises. Therefore, it is said, 'having realized the fruit of stream-entry,' and so on. Regarding ‘sirigabbhaṃ gantvā’ (having gone to the glorious chamber): here, it should be understood that if the Blessed One had not gone on that very day and seen her, she would have died with a broken heart; therefore, he went.

Taṃ divasamevāti tasmiṃ rāhulamātudassanadivaseyeva. Dhammapadaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “satthā kapilapuraṃ gantvā tatiyadivase nandaṃ pabbājesī”ti (dha. pa. aṭṭha. 1.12 nandattheravatthu) vuttaṃ. Kesavissajjananti rājamoḷibandhanatthaṃ kumārakāle bandhitasikhāveṇimocanaṃ, taṃ kira karontā maṅgalaṃ karonti. Sāratthadīpaniyaṃ pana “kesavissajjananti kulamariyādavasena kesoropana”nti (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.105) vuttaṃ. Paṭṭabandhoti “asukarājā”ti naḷāṭe suvaṇṇapaṭṭabandhanaṃ. Abhinavapāsādappavesamaṅgalaṃ gharamaṅgalaṃ. Chattussāpane maṅgalaṃ chattamaṅgalaṃ. Janapadakalyāṇīti [M 2.0114] janapadamhi kalyāṇī parehi asādhāraṇehi pañcakalyāṇādīhi sahitattā sā evaṃ vuttā. Tuvaṭanti sīghaṃ. Anicchamānanti manasā arocentaṃ, vācāya pana bhagavatā “pabbajissasi nandā”ti vutte gāravena paṭikkhipituṃ avisahanto “āmā”ti avoca. Bhagavā ca etena lesena pabbājesi.

‘Taṃ divasameva’ (on that very day) means: on the very day of seeing Rāhula’s mother. In the Dhammapada commentary, however, it is said: 'The Teacher, having gone to Kapilapura, ordained Nanda on the third day.' ‘Kesavissajjanaṃ’ (releasing the hair) means the untying of the topknot-braid bound in his youth for the sake of tying the royal topknot; indeed, they perform a ceremony while doing this. In the Sāratthadīpanī, however, it is said: '‘Kesavissajjanaṃ’ means shaving the head in accordance with family custom.' ‘Paṭṭabandho’ (binding the fillet) means binding a golden plate on the forehead with the words 'such-and-such is king.' The ceremony for entering a new palace is the house-consecration ceremony. The ceremony for raising the parasol is the parasol-consecration ceremony. ‘Janapadakalyāṇī’ (the beauty of the country): she is the beauty in the country; she is called so because she is endowed with the five kinds of beauty and so on, which are uncommon and not shared with others. ‘Tuvaṭaṃ’ means: swiftly. ‘Anicchamānaṃ’ (unwilling) means: not delighting in it mentally; but with his speech, when the Blessed One said, 'Nanda, will you go forth?' he was unable to refuse out of respect and replied, 'Yes.' And the Blessed One ordained him with this pretext.

Brahmarūpavaṇṇanti [V 2.0110] brahmarūpasamānarūpaṃ. Tyassāti te assa. Nivattetuṃ na visahīti “mā naṃ nivattayitthā”ti bhagavatā vuttattā nāsakkhi. Sattavidhaṃ ariyadhananti –

‘Brahmarūpavaṇṇaṃ’ (having the appearance of a Brahmā) means: an appearance similar to the appearance of a Brahmā. ‘Tyassa’ is ‘te assa’. ‘Nivattetuṃ na vīsahi’ (he was not able to make him return) means: he was not able, because it had been said by the Blessed One, “Do not make him return.” ‘Sattavidhaṃ ariyadhanaṃ’ (the sevenfold noble wealth):

“Saddhādhanaṃ sīladhanaṃ, hiriottappiyaṃ dhanaṃ;

Sutadhanañca cāgo ca, paññā ve sattamaṃ dhana”nti. (a. ni. 7.5, 6) –

“The treasure of faith, the treasure of virtue, the treasure of conscience and prudence; the treasure of learning and generosity, and wisdom is indeed the seventh treasure.”

Evaṃ vuttaṃ sattavidhaṃ ariyadhanaṃ. Adhimattaṃ rāhuleti rāhule pabbajite nandapabbajjāya uppannadukkhatopi adhikataraṃ dukkhaṃ ahosīti attho. Ito pacchāti ito vuttasokuppattito aparadivasesu anāgāmīnaṃ ñātisinehapaṭighacittuppādābhāvā. Pāḷiyaṃ puttapemantiādi raññā puttasinehassa tibbabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Puttasineho hi attanā sahajātapītivegasamuṭṭhitānaṃ rūpadhammānaṃ sakalasarīraṃ khobhetvā pavattanavasena “chaviṃ…pe… aṭṭhimiñjaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhatī”ti vutto. Attano piyatarāti bhagavantaṃ sandhāya vadati. Putteti rāhulaṃ. Saddahantenāti tassa vacanena avematikenāti attho. Vimatiyā sati āpatti eva.

Thus is the sevenfold noble wealth spoken of. ‘Adhimattaṃ rāhule’ (exceedingly in the case of Rāhula) means: when Rāhula went forth, the suffering that arose was even greater than the suffering that arose from Nanda's going forth; this is the meaning. ‘Ito pacchā’ (after this) means: in the days after the arising of sorrow mentioned here, for non-returners there is no arising of a mind of affection and aversion for relatives. In the Pāḷi, ‘puttapemaṃ’ (love for a son), etc., was spoken by the king to show the intensity of his love for his son. For the love for a son is said to ‘pierce the skin…pe… and, having reached the bone marrow, it remains,’ by way of agitating the material phenomena of the entire body, which arise from the force of joy co-nascent with oneself. ‘Attano piyatarā’ (dearer than oneself) is said with reference to the Blessed One. ‘Putte’ (son) is said with reference to Rāhula. ‘Saddahantena’ (by one who has faith) means: by his word, without doubt; this is the meaning. If there is doubt, there is an offense.

Rāhulavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Story of Rāhula is concluded.

Sikkhāpadadaṇḍakammavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Discourse on the Grounds for Disciplinary Action Concerning the Training Rules

106. Sāmaṇerasikkhāpadādīsu pāḷiyaṃ sikkhāpadānīti sikkhākoṭṭhāsā. Adhisīlasikkhānaṃ vā adhigamūpāyā. Pāṇoti paramatthato jīvitindriyaṃ. Tassa atipātanaṃ pabandhavasena pavattituṃ adatvā satthādīhi atikkamma abhibhavitvā pātanaṃ pāṇātipāto. Pāṇavadhoti attho. So [M 2.0115] pana atthato pāṇe pāṇasaññino jīvitindriyupacchedakaupakkamasamuṭṭhāpikā vadhakacetanāva. Tasmā pāṇātipātā veramaṇi, verahetutāya verasaṅkhātaṃ pāṇātipātādipāpadhammaṃ maṇati nīharatīti virati “veramaṇī”ti vuccati, viramati etāyāti vā “viramaṇī”ti vattabbe niruttinayena “veramaṇī”ti samādānavirati vuttā. Esa nayo sesesupi.

106. In the Pāḷi concerning the training rules for novices and so on, `sikkhāpadāni` (training rules) are portions of training. Or, they are the means for attaining the training in higher virtue. `Pāṇa`, in the ultimate sense, is the life faculty. `Pāṇātipāta` is the felling of that [life faculty]; it is the felling by means of swords and so on, having transgressed and overpowered it, without allowing it to proceed by way of continuity. The meaning is the killing of a living being. But that `pāṇātipāta`, in essence, is just the killing volition that gives rise to the effort that cuts off the life faculty in a being, of one who has the perception of a living being. Therefore, `veramaṇi` (abstinence) from `pāṇātipāta`. Because it removes (`maṇati`, `nīharati`) the evil state of `pāṇātipāta`, etc., which is called `vera` (enmity) because it is a cause of enmity, `virati` (abstinence) is called `veramaṇī`. Alternatively, although it should be stated as `viramaṇī`—meaning 'one abstains by means of this'—by way of etymological method, `veramaṇī` is said of abstinence through undertaking. This is the method in the remaining cases as well.

Adinnassa ādānaṃ adinnādānaṃ, theyyacetanāva. Abrahmacariyanti aseṭṭhacariyaṃ, maggena maggapaṭipattisamuṭṭhāpikā methunacetanā. Musāti abhūtavatthu, tassa vādo abhūtataṃ ñatvāva bhūtato [V 2.0111] viññāpanacetanā musāvādo. Piṭṭhapūvādinibbattasurā ceva pupphāsavādibhedaṃ merayañca surāmerayaṃ. Tadeva madanīyaṭṭhena majjañceva pamādakāraṇaṭṭhena pamādaṭṭhānañca, taṃ yāya cetanāya pivati, tassa etaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

Taking what is not given is `adinnādāna`; it is just the volition to steal. `Abrahmacariya` (unchaste conduct) is ignoble conduct; it is the sexual volition that gives rise to the practice of the path by means of the [sexual] organ. `Musā` (falsehood) is an untrue matter; `musāvāda` is the volition to make known as true what is known to be untrue. Both liquor (`surā`) produced from flour, cakes, and the like, and spirits (`meraya`) of various kinds such as those from flowers and fruits, are `surāmeraya`. That very thing, because of its intoxicating nature, is `majja` (an intoxicant), and because it is a cause of heedlessness, it is `pamādaṭṭhāna` (a basis for heedlessness). This is the designation for the volition by which one drinks it.

Aruṇuggamanato paṭṭhāya yāva majjhanhikā ayaṃ ariyānaṃ bhojanassa kālo nāma, tadañño vikālo. Bhuñjitabbaṭṭhena bhojananti idha sabbaṃ yāvakālikaṃ vuccati, tassa ajjhoharaṇaṃ idha uttarapadalopena “bhojana”nti adhippetaṃ. Vikāle bhojanaṃ ajjhoharaṇaṃ vikālabhojanaṃ, vikāle vā yāvakālikassa bhojanaṃ ajjhoharaṇaṃ vikālabhojanantipi attho gahetabbo, atthato vikāle yāvakālikaajjhoharaṇacetanāva.

From the rising of the dawn up to midday is called the time for the meal of the noble ones; another time is the wrong time (`vikāla`). Here, because of the meaning 'to be eaten', all `yāvakālika` (allowable for a limited time) is called `bhojana` (food). Here, its swallowing is intended by the word `bhojana` through the elision of the latter word. Swallowing food at the wrong time is `vikālabhojana`. Alternatively, the meaning of `vikālabhojana` should also be taken as the swallowing of `yāvakālika` at the wrong time. In essence, it is just the volition to swallow `yāvakālika` at the wrong time.

Sāsanassa ananulomattā visūkaṃ paṭāṇībhūtaṃ dassanaṃ visūkadassanaṃ, naccagītādidassanasavanānañceva vaṭṭakayuddhajūtakīḷādisabbakīḷānañca nāmaṃ. Dassananti cettha pañcannampi viññāṇānaṃ yathāsakaṃ visayassa ālocanasabhāvatāya dassana-saddena saṅgahetabbattā savanampi saṅgahitaṃ. Naccagītavādita-saddehi cettha attano naccanagāyanādīnipi saṅgahitānīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

A show that is an obstacle (`visūkaṃ`) and a thorn (`paṭāṇībhūtaṃ`), being unsuitable for the Dispensation, is `visūkadassana`; it is the name for both seeing and hearing dancing, singing, and the like, and for all games such as quail fighting, dicing, and so on. And here, because the five consciousnesses are to be included by the word `dassana` (seeing) due to their nature of observing their respective objects, hearing is also included. And it should be understood that here, by the words 'dancing, singing, and instrumental music,' one's own dancing, singing, and so on are also included.

Mālāti baddhamabaddhaṃ vā antamaso suttādimayampi alaṅkāratthāya piḷandhiyamānaṃ “mālā”tveva vuccati. Gandhanti vāsacuṇṇādivilepanato aññaṃ yaṃ kiñci gandhajātaṃ. Vilepananti pisitvā gahitaṃ chavirāgakaraṇañceva gandhajātañca. Dhāraṇaṃ nāma piḷandhanaṃ. Maṇḍanaṃ nāma ūnaṭṭhānapūraṇaṃ. Gandhavasena, chavirāgavasena ca sādiyanaṃ vibhūsanaṃ nāma. Mālādīsu vā dhāraṇādīni yathākkamaṃ [M 2.0116] yojetabbāni. Tesaṃ dhāraṇādīnaṃ ṭhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ vītikkamacetanā.

`Mālā` (garland) is a flower, whether bound or unbound; even, at the lowest, that which is made of thread and so on, being worn for the sake of adornment, is called just `mālā`. `Gandha` (scent) is any kind of fragrant substance other than incense, powder, and other such unguents. `Vilepana` (unguent) is that which is taken by grinding, being both a cause of coloring on the skin and a collection of fragrant substances. `Dhāraṇa` (wearing) is called adorning. `Maṇḍana` (decorating) is called filling a deficient place. Enjoying by means of fragrance and by means of coloring the skin is called `vibhūsana` (embellishing). Alternatively, `dhāraṇa` and so on should be connected in sequence with `mālā` and so on. The cause of that wearing and so on is the volition to transgress.

Uccāti ucca-saddena samānattho nipāto, uccāsayanaṃ vuccati pamāṇātikkantaṃ āsandādi. Mahāsayanaṃ akappiyattharaṇehi atthataṃ, salohitavitānañca. Etesu hi āsanaṃ, sayanañca uccāsayanamahāsayana-saddehi gahitāni uttarapadalopena. Jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇāti ettha rajata-saddena dārumāsakādi sabbaṃ rūpiyaṃ saṅgahitaṃ, muttāmaṇiādayopettha dhaññakhettavatthādayo ca saṅgahitāti daṭṭhabbā. Paṭiggahaṇa-saddena paṭiggāhāpanasādiyanāni saṅgahitāni. Nāsanavatthūti pārājikaṭṭhānatāya liṅganāsanāya kāraṇaṃ.

`Uccā` is a particle with the same meaning as the word `ucca` (high). A seat, etc., that exceeds the standard measure is called `uccāsayana`. A seat spread with unallowable coverings, and a seat together with a canopy, is called `mahāsayana`. Indeed, in these, both sitting and lying down are taken by the words `uccāsayana` and `mahāsayana` through the elision of the latter word. In the term `jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇa`, by the word `rajata`, all `rūpiya` (currency) such as wooden `māsaka` coins, etc., is included. It should be understood that here, pearls, gems, and so on, and also paddy, fields, and so on, are included. By the word `paṭiggahaṇa`, causing to accept, consenting, and so on are included. `Nāsanavatthu` is a cause for the destruction of the characteristic [of a monk] because it is a ground for a `pārājika` (defeat) offense.

107. Pāḷiyaṃ sabbaṃ saṅghārāmaṃ āvaraṇaṃ karontīti sabbasaṅghārāme pavesanivāraṇaṃ karonti. Saṅghārāmo āvaraṇaṃ kātabboti saṅghārāmo āvaraṇo kātabbo, saṅghārāme vā āvaraṇaṃ [V 2.0112] kātabbanti attho. Teneva “tattha āvaraṇaṃ kātu”nti bhummavasena vuttaṃ. Āhāraṃ āvaraṇantiādīsupi eseva nayo. “Yattha vā vasatī”ti iminā sāmaṇerassa vassaggena laddhaṃ vā sakasantakameva vā nibaddhavasanakasenāsanaṃ vuttaṃ. Yattha vā paṭikkamatīti ācariyupajjhāyānaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ vuttaṃ. Tenāha “attano”tiādi. Attanoti hi sayaṃ, ācariyassa, upajjhāyassa vāti attho. Daṇḍenti vinenti etenāti daṇḍo, so eva kattabbattā kammanti daṇḍakammaṃ, āvaraṇādi. Udakaṃ vā pavesetunti pokkharaṇīādiudake pavesetuṃ.

107. In the Pāḷi, `sabbaṃ saṅghārāmaṃ āvaraṇaṃ karonti` means they make a prevention of entry in the entire monastic compound. `Saṅghārāmo āvaraṇaṃ kātabbo` means the monastic compound should be made an enclosure, or alternatively, an enclosure should be made in the monastic compound; this is the meaning. For that very reason, `tattha āvaraṇaṃ kātuṃ` (to make an enclosure there) is stated by way of the locative. This is the same method in cases such as `āhāraṃ āvaraṇaṃ` (food as an obstruction). By `yattha vā vasati` (or wherever one dwells), a novice’s lodging—whether obtained by seniority in the rains-residence, or being their own property, or a permanently assigned lodging—is stated. By `yattha vā paṭikkamati` (or wherever one departs), the dwelling place of the teacher and preceptor is stated. Therefore, it says `attano` (one's own), etc. Indeed, the meaning of `attano` is 'one's own', or 'of the teacher', or 'of the preceptor'. That by which they discipline or train is `daṇḍa`; that very thing, because it is to be done, is `kamma`; hence `daṇḍakamma` (disciplinary action), such as obstruction, etc. As for `udakaṃ vā pavesetuṃ` (or to make enter the water), it means to submerge [someone] in water such as a lotus pond.

Sikkhāpadadaṇḍakammavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Discourse on the Grounds for Disciplinary Action Concerning the Training Rules is concluded.

Anāpucchāvaraṇavatthuādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse Beginning with the Case of Barring Without Asking Permission

108. Saddhivihārikaantevāsikānampīti upasampanne sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tesupi hi ācariyupajjhāyesu yathā oramanti, tathā tesaṃ niggahaṃ akarontesu aññehi āvaraṇādiniggahakammaṃ kātabbameva. Saṅgaṇhantīti “paraparisato bhinditvā gaṇhissāmī”ti dānādicatūhi saṅgahavatthūhi (dī. ni. 3.210; a. ni. 4.32, 256) upalāḷanavasena [M 2.0117] saṅgaṇhanti. So bhijjatu vā mā vā, saṅgaṇhantassa payoge āpatti eva. Bhinditvā gaṇhituṃ na vaṭṭatīti bhinditumpi na vaṭṭati, gaṇhitumpi na vaṭṭatīti attho. Ādīnavaṃ pana vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti sāsanagāravena vā parānuddayatāya vā vattuṃ vaṭṭati, na parisalolatāya.

108. The words 'Even for co-residents and pupils' are said with reference to the ordained. For indeed, in their case, if teachers and preceptors do not restrain them as is proper, others must perform disciplinary actions such as barring, etc. 'They win over' means they win them over by means of coaxing with the four bases of sympathy, such as giving, with the thought, 'I will take them, having split them from another's assembly.' Whether that assembly is split or not, for the one who wins them over, there is an offense in every single attempt. 'It is not allowable to split and take' means it is not allowable to split, and it is not allowable to take; this is the meaning. 'However, it is allowable to speak of the disadvantage' means it is allowable to speak out of respect for the Teaching or out of compassion for others, not out of fickleness for a following.

“Senāsanaggāho ca paṭippassambhatī”ti iminā vassacchedaṃ dasseti. Upasampannānampi pārājikasamāpattiyā saraṇagamanādisāmaṇerabhāvassāpi vinassanato senāsanaggāho ca paṭippassambhati, saṅghalābhampi te na labhantīti veditabbaṃ. Purimikāya puna saraṇāni gahitānīti saraṇaggahaṇena saha tadahevassa vassūpagamanampi dasseti. Pacchimikāya vassāvāsikanti vassāvāsikalābhaggahaṇadassanamattamevetaṃ, tato purepi, pacchāpi vā vassāvāsikañca cīvaramāsesu saṅghe uppannaṃ kālacīvarañca purimikāya upagantvā avipannasīlo sāmaṇero labhati eva. Sace pacchimikāya gahitānīti pacchimikāya vassūpagamanañca chinnavassatañca dasseti. Tassa hi kālacīvare bhāgo na pāpuṇāti. Tasmā “apaloketvā lābho dātabbo”ti vuttaṃ.

By the words, “The taking of a dwelling also ceases,” it shows the breaking of the rains-residence. Even for the ordained, due to falling into a pārājika offense, because of the destruction of even the state of a novice, which begins with going for refuge, the taking of a dwelling also ceases. It should be understood that they also do not receive the Saṅgha's gains. By the words, “In the earlier period, the refuges are taken again,” it shows his undertaking of the rains-residence on that very day, together with the taking of the refuges. The words, “a rains-resident in the later period,” are merely a showing of the taking of the gain of the rains-residence robe. Before or after that, a novice of unbroken virtue, having entered the rains in the earlier period, certainly receives both the rains-residence robe and the timely robe that arose for the Saṅgha during the robe-months. By the words, “If taken in the later period,” it shows both the undertaking of the rains-residence in the later period and the state of having a broken rains-residence. Indeed, for him, a share in the timely robe is not obtained. Therefore, it is said, “The gain should be given after having informed.”

Vassāvāsikalābho [V 2.0113] pana yadi senāsanasāmikā dāyakā senāsanaguttatthāya pacchimikāya upagantvā vattaṃ katvā attano senāsane vasantassapi vassāvāsikaṃ dātabbanti vadanti, anapaloketvāpi dātabbova. Yaṃ pana sāratthadīpaniyaṃ “pacchimikāya vassāvāsikaṃ lacchatīti pacchimikāya puna vassaṃ upagatattā lacchatī”ti (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.108) vuttaṃ, tampi vassāvāsike dāyakānaṃ imaṃ adhippāyaṃ nissāya vuttañce, sundaraṃ. Saṅghikaṃ, kālacīvarampi sandhāya vuttañce, na yujjatīti veditabbaṃ.

However, regarding the gain of the rains-residence robe, if the donors who own the dwelling say, “The rains-residence robe should be given even to one who, for the sake of guarding the dwelling, entered the later rains-residence, performed his duties, and is living in his own dwelling,” it should indeed be given even without informing the Saṅgha. As for the statement made in the Sāratthadīpanī, “‘He receives the rains-residence robe in the later period’ means ‘he receives it because he has again undertaken the rains in the later period’” — if that statement was also made relying on this intention of the donors regarding the rains-residence robe, it is good. If it was made with reference to what belongs to the Saṅgha, that is, the timely robe, it should be understood that it is not proper.

Na ajānitvāti “surā”ti ajānitvā pivato pāṇātipātaveramaṇiādisabbasīlabhedaṃ, saraṇabhedañca na āpajjati, akusalaṃ pana surāpānaveramaṇisīlabhedo ca hoti mālādidhāraṇādīsu viyāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Itarānīti vikālabhojanaveramaṇiādīni. Tānipi hi sañcicca vītikkamantassa taṃ taṃ bhijjati eva, itarītaresaṃ pana abhijjamānena nāsanaṅgāni na honti. Teneva “tesu bhinnesū”ti bhedavacanaṃ vuttaṃ.

Regarding “Not knowing”: for one who drinks without knowing it is “liquor,” he does not fall into the breach of all precepts, such as abstaining from taking life, nor the breach of the refuges. However, there is an unwholesome act and a breach of the precept of abstaining from drinking liquor; this should be seen as being like in the cases of wearing garlands, etc. “The others” means abstaining from eating at the wrong time, etc. Indeed, for one who intentionally transgresses those, that particular precept is certainly broken. But because the other precepts remain unbroken, the factors for expulsion do not arise. For that very reason, the word for “breach” was spoken in the phrase “when those are broken.”

Accayaṃ [M 2.0118] desāpetabboti “accayo maṃ, bhante, accagamā”tiādinā saṅghamajjhe desāpetvā saraṇasīlaṃ dātabbanti adhippāyo pārājikattā tesaṃ. Tenāha “liṅganāsanāya nāsetabbo”ti. Ayameva hi nāsanā idha adhippetāti liṅganāsanākāraṇehi pāṇātipātādīhi avaṇṇabhāsanādīnaṃ saha patitattā vuttaṃ.

Regarding “The offense should be confessed”: the intention is that after having him confess in the midst of the Saṅgha with the words, “Venerable sir, an offense has overcome me,” etc., the refuges and precepts should be given, because for them it is a pārājika. Therefore, he said, “He should be expelled by the destruction of the insignia.” The words “This very expulsion is intended here” are said because of offenses like speaking dispraise, etc., falling together with the causes for the destruction of the insignia, such as taking life, etc.

Nanu ca kaṇṭakasāmaṇeropi micchādiṭṭhiko eva, tassa ca heṭṭhā daṇḍakammanāsanāva vuttā. Idha pana micchādiṭṭhikassa liṅganāsanā vuccati, ko imesaṃ bhedoti codanaṃ manasi nidhāyāha “sassatucchedānañhi aññataradiṭṭhiko”ti. Ettha cāyamadhippāyo – yo hi “attā issaro vā nicco dhuvo”tiādinā vā “attā ucchijjissati vinassissatī”tiādinā vā titthiyaparikappitaṃ yaṃ kiñci sassatucchedadiṭṭhiṃ daḷhaṃ gahetvā voharati, tassa sā pārājikaṭṭhānaṃ hoti. So ca liṅganāsanāya nāsetabbo. Yo pana īdisaṃ diṭṭhiṃ aggahetvā sāsanikova hutvā kevalaṃ buddhavacanādhippāyaṃ viparītato gahetvā bhikkhūhi ovadiyamānopi appaṭinissajjitvā voharati, tassa sā diṭṭhi pārājikaṃ na hoti, so pana kaṇṭakanāsanāya eva nāsetabboti.

But surely, the novice Kaṇṭaka was also one of wrong view, and for him, below, only expulsion by disciplinary action was stated. Here, however, for one of wrong view, the destruction of the insignia is stated. What is the difference between these two? Having kept this objection in mind, he said: “For he is one with a view that is one of either eternalism or annihilationism.” And here this is the intended meaning: Whatever novice, having firmly grasped and spoken some eternalist or annihilationist view devised by sectarians—such as “The self is a lord, or is eternal and permanent,” etc., or “The self will be annihilated, will be destroyed,” etc.—for him that view is a basis for pārājika. And he should be expelled by means of the destruction of the insignia. But whatever novice, not having grasped such a view, being one within the Teaching, merely grasps the meaning of the Buddha's word perversely and, though being admonished by the monks, speaks without renouncing it—for him that view is not a pārājika. But that novice should be expelled only by the Kaṇṭaka-expulsion.

Anāpucchāvaraṇavatthuādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Story Beginning with the Case of Barring Without Asking Permission is concluded.

Paṇḍakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse of the Paṇḍaka

109. Paṇḍakavatthusmiṃ [V 2.0114] āsittausūyapakkhapaṇḍakā tayopi purisabhāvaliṅgādiyuttā ahetukapaṭisandhikā, te ca kilesapariyuṭṭhānassa balavatāya napuṃsakapaṇḍakasadisattā “paṇḍakā”ti vuttā. Tesu āsittausūyapaṇḍakānaṃ dvinnaṃ kilesapariyuṭṭhānaṃ yonisomanasikārādīhi vītikkamato nivāretumpi sakkā, tena te pabbājetabbā vuttā. Pakkhapaṇḍakassa pana kāḷapakkhesu ummādo viya kilesapariḷāho avattharanto āgacchati, vītikkamaṃ patvā eva ca nivattati. Tasmā so tasmiṃ pakkhe na pabbājetabboti vutto. Tadetaṃ vibhāgaṃ dassetuṃ “yassa paresa”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha āsittassāti mukhe āsittassa attanopi asucimuccanena [M 2.0119] pariḷāho vūpasammati. Usūyāya uppannāyāti usūyāya vasena attano sevetukāmatārāge uppanne asucimuttiyā pariḷāho vūpasammati.

109. In the matter of the paṇḍaka, the three—the āsitta-paṇḍaka, usūya-paṇḍaka, and pakkha-paṇḍaka—are endowed with male nature, male characteristics, and so on, and have a rootless rebirth-linking. And due to the strength of the obsession of defilements, because of their similarity to a neuter paṇḍaka, they are called “paṇḍakas.” Among them, for the two, the āsitta-paṇḍaka and usūya-paṇḍaka, the obsession of defilements can be prevented from transgression by means of wise attention and so on; therefore, it is said they should be given the going forth. But for the pakkha-paṇḍaka, during the dark fortnights, the burning of defilements comes, overwhelming like madness, and it subsides only after having reached transgression. Therefore, it is said that he should not be given the going forth during that fortnight. To show this distinction, the passage beginning with “yassa paresaṃ” was spoken. Therein, “āsittassa” means: for one into whose mouth something is poured, the burning subsides by the discharge of impurity even of oneself. “Usūyāya uppannāya” means: when, through the power of envy, the lust which is the desire to engage in sexual activity oneself arises, the burning subsides by the discharge of impurity.

“Bījāni apanītānī”ti vuttattā bījesu ṭhitesu nimittamatte apanīte paṇḍako na hoti. Bhikkhunopi anābādhapaccayā tadapanayane thullaccayameva, na pana paṇḍakattaṃ, bījesu pana apanītesu aṅgajātampi rāgena kammaniyaṃ na hoti, pumabhāvo vigacchati, massuādipurisaliṅgampi upasampadāpi vigacchati, kilesapariḷāhopi dunnivāravītikkamo hoti napuṃsakapaṇḍakassa viya. Tasmā īdiso upasampannopi nāsetabboti vadanti. Yadi evaṃ kasmā bījuddharaṇe pārājikaṃ na paññattanti? Ettha tāva keci vadanti “paññattamevetaṃ bhagavatā ‘paṇḍako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabbo’ti vuttattā”ti. Keci pana “yasmā bījuddharaṇakkhaṇe paṇḍako na hoti, tasmā tasmiṃ khaṇe pārājikaṃ na paññattaṃ. Yasmā pana so uddhaṭabījo bhikkhu aparena samayena vuttanayena paṇḍakattaṃ āpajjati, abhāvako hoti, upasampadāya avatthu, tato eva cassa upasampadā vigacchati, tasmā esa paṇḍakattupagamanakālato paṭṭhāya jātiyā napuṃsakapaṇḍakena saddhiṃ yojetvā ‘upasampanno nāsetabbo’ti abhabboti vutto, na tato pubbe. Ayañca kiñcāpi sahetuko, bhāvakkhayena panassa ahetukasadisatāya maggopi na uppajjatī”ti vadanti. Apare pana “pabbajjato pubbe upakkamena paṇḍakabhāvamāpannaṃ sandhāya ‘upasampanno nāsetabbo’ti vuttaṃ, upasampannassa pana pacchā upakkamena upasampadāpi na vigacchatī”ti, taṃ na yuttaṃ. Yadaggena hi pabbajjato pubbe upakkamena abhabbo hoti, tadaggena pacchāpi hotīti vīmaṃsitvā gahetabbaṃ.

Because it is said, 'The seeds have been removed,' when the seeds remain and only the sign is removed, one does not become a paṇḍaka. Even for a bhikkhu, for that removal without a reason of illness, it is only a thullaccaya offense, not the state of being a paṇḍaka. But when the seeds are removed, the sexual organ is not serviceable for intercourse through lust, masculinity is lost, male characteristics such as a beard and also the higher ordination are lost, and the burning of defilements also has a transgression that is difficult to prevent, like that of a neuter paṇḍaka. Therefore, they say, such an ordained one should also be expelled. If so, why was a pārājika offense not laid down for removing the seeds? Herein, some say, 'It was indeed laid down by the Blessed One, because it was said: "A paṇḍaka, bhikkhus, who is not ordained should not be ordained; if ordained, he should be expelled."' But some say, 'Because at the moment of removing the seeds one does not become a paṇḍaka, therefore at that moment a pārājika was not laid down. But because that bhikkhu with seeds removed, at a later time, in the aforesaid manner, attains the state of a paṇḍaka, becomes one without male nature, and is not a basis for higher ordination, for that very reason his higher ordination is lost. Therefore, from the time he reaches the state of a paṇḍaka, being grouped with a neuter paṇḍaka by birth, he is said to be unfit, as in 'an ordained one should be expelled'; not before that. And this person, although he has roots, due to the destruction of his male nature, because of being similar to one without roots, the path also does not arise for him.' Others, however, say, 'Referring to one who reached the state of a paṇḍaka through effort before the going forth, it was said, "an ordained one should be expelled"; but for one who has been ordained, the higher ordination is not lost afterwards through effort.' That is not correct. For to the extent that one is unfit through effort before the going forth, to that extent one is also unfit afterwards. This should be understood after investigation.

Itthattādi [V 2.0115] bhāvo natthi etassāti abhāvako. Pabbajjā na vāritāti ettha pabbajjāgahaṇeneva upasampadāpi gahitā. Tenāha “yassa cettha pabbajjā vāritā”tiādi. Tasmiṃyevassa pakkhe pabbajjā vāritāti ettha pana apaṇḍakapakkhepi pabbajjāmattameva labhati, upasampadā pana tadāpi na vaṭṭati, paṇḍakapakkhe pana āgate liṅganāsanāya nāsetabboti veditabbaṃ.

For this person, there is no nature such as femaleness, etc.; therefore, he is called 'abhāvaka' (one without nature). In the phrase 'the going forth is not forbidden,' by the taking of the word 'going forth' itself, higher ordination is also included. Therefore, it is said, 'For whom the going forth here is forbidden...' and so on. But in this phrase, 'for him, in that very case, the going forth is forbidden,' even in the case where he is not a paṇḍaka, he obtains only the going forth. But higher ordination, even then, is not allowable. It should be known that when the case of being a paṇḍaka arrives, he should be expelled by the destruction of the sign.

Paṇḍakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the story of the paṇḍaka is concluded.

Theyyasaṃvāsakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of One Who Lives in Communion by Theft

110. Theyyasaṃvāsakavatthumhi [M 2.0120] kolaññāti kule jātā, tattha vā viditā ñātā pasiddhā, taṃ vā jānanti kolaññāti ñātakānaṃ nāmaṃ. Theyyāya liṅgaggahaṇamattampi idha saṃvāso evāti āha “tayo theyyasaṃvāsakā”ti. Na yathāvuḍḍhaṃ vandananti bhikkhūnaṃ, sāmaṇerānaṃ vā vandanaṃ na sādiyati.

110. In the story of one who lives in communion by theft: 'Kolaññā' means born into a family, or known, recognized, and famous there, or they know that family; thus, 'kolaññā' is a name for known persons or relatives. Even the mere taking of the sign by way of theft is, in this context, communion itself. Therefore, it is said, 'There are three types of those who live in communion by theft.' As for 'not homage according to seniority,' it means he does not consent to the homage of monks or novices.

Yathāvuḍḍhaṃ vandananti attanā musāvādena dassitavassakkamena bhikkhūnaṃ vandanaṃ sādiyati, daharasāmaṇero pana vuḍḍhasāmaṇerānaṃ, daharabhikkhu ca vuḍḍhānaṃ vandanaṃ sādiyantopi theyyasaṃvāsako na hoti. Imasmiṃ attheti saṃvāsatthenakatthe.

As for 'homage according to seniority,' it means he consents to the homage of monks according to the order of seniority he has shown by a false statement. However, a junior novice, even when consenting to the homage of senior novices, or a junior monk to that of senior monks, does not become one who lives in communion by theft. As for 'in this meaning,' it is in the meaning of a thief by way of communion.

“Bhikkhuvassānī”ti idaṃ saṃvāsatthenake vuttapāṭhavasena vuttaṃ, sayameva pana pabbajitvā sāmaṇeravassāni gaṇentopi ubhayatthenako eva. Na kevalañca purisova, itthīpi bhikkhunīsu evaṃ paṭipajjati, theyyasaṃvāsikāva. Ādikammikāpi cettha na muccanti, upasampannesu eva paññattāpattiṃ paṭicca ādikammikā vuttā, tenevettha ādikammikopi na mutto.

This phrase, 'a monk's years,' is stated by the power of the spoken text in the section on the thief by way of communion. However, one who has gone forth by himself and counts the novice's years is also indeed a thief in both ways. And not only a man; a woman, too, who practices thus among bhikkhunīs is indeed one who lives in communion by theft. Even first offenders are not exempt here. First offenders are spoken of in connection with an offense prescribed only for the fully ordained; for that very reason, even a first offender is not exempt here.

Rāja…pe… bhayenāti ettha bhaya-saddo paccekaṃ yojetabbo. Yāva so suddhamānasoti “iminā liṅgena bhikkhū vañcetvā tehi saṃvasissāmī”ti asuddhacittābhāvena suddhacitto. Tena hi asuddhacittena liṅge gahitamatte pacchā bhikkhūhi saha saṃvasatu vā mā vā, liṅgatthenako hoti. Pacchā saṃvasantopi abhabbo hutvā saṃvasati. Tasmā ubhayatthenakopi liṅgatthenake eva pavisatīti veditabbaṃ. Yo pana rājādibhayena suddhacittova liṅgaṃ gahetvā vicaranto pacchā “bhikkhuvassāni gaṇetvā jīvissāmī”ti asuddhacittaṃ uppādeti, so cittuppādamattena theyyasaṃvāsakopi na hoti suddhacittena gahitaliṅgattā. Sace pana so bhikkhūnaṃ santikaṃ [V 2.0116] gantvā sāmaṇeravassagaṇanādiṃ karoti, tadā saṃvāsatthenako, ubhayatthenako vā hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana parato saha dhuranikkhepena “ayampi theyyasaṃvāsako, vā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ bhikkhūhi saṅgamma saṃvāsādhivāsanavasena dhuranikkhepaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “saṃvāsaṃ nādhivāseti yāvā”ti. Tassa tāva theyyasaṃvāsako nāma na vuccatīti sambandho daṭṭhabbo. Ettha ca corādibhayaṃ [M 2.0121] vināpi kīḷādhippāyena liṅgaṃ gahetvā bhikkhūnaṃ santike pabbajitālayaṃ dassetvā vandanādiṃ asādiyantopi “sobhati nu kho me pabbajitaliṅga”ntiādinā suddhacittena gaṇhantopi theyyasaṃvāsako na hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

In the phrase 'Out of fear of the king... etc.,' the word 'fear' should be applied to each case individually. As for 'as long as his mind is pure,' it means his mind is pure because of the absence of an impure thought such as, 'With this sign, having deceived the monks, I will live in communion with them.' Indeed, for one with an impure mind, upon the mere taking of the sign, whether he later lives in communion with monks or not, he becomes a thief by way of the sign. Even if he lives in communion later, he does so having become unworthy. Therefore, it should be known that the thief in both ways is also included in the category of the thief by way of the sign. But as for one who, out of fear of the king and so on, takes the sign with a pure mind and wanders about, and later gives rise to an impure thought, thinking, 'I will make a living by counting the monks' years,' he does not become one who lives in communion by theft merely by the arising of that thought, because the sign was taken with a pure mind. If, however, that person goes to the presence of monks and does things such as counting the novice's years, then it should be understood that he becomes a thief by way of communion or a thief in both ways. But as for what was said later regarding the laying down of the yoke together, 'This one, too, is one who lives in communion by theft,' that was said with reference to the laying down of the yoke by way of consenting to communion, having associated with monks. Therefore it was said, 'As long as he does not consent to communion...' The connection should be understood thus: for that long, he is not called one who lives in communion by theft. And here it should be understood that even without fear of thieves and so on, one who takes the sign with playful intent, and having shown the appearance of one gone forth in the presence of monks, does not consent to homage and so on; or one who takes it with a pure mind, thinking, 'Does the sign of one gone forth suit me?' and so on, does not become one who lives in communion by theft.

Sabbapāsaṇḍiyabhattānīti sabbasāmayikānaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ katvā paññattabhattāni, idañca bhikkhūnaññeva niyamitabhattagahaṇe saṃvāsopi sambhaveyyāti sabbasādhāraṇabhattaṃ vuttaṃ. Saṃvāsaṃ pana asādiyitvā abhikkhukavihārādīsu vihārabhattādīni bhuñjantopi theyyasaṃvāsako na hoti eva. Kammantānuṭṭhānenāti kasiādikammakaraṇena. Pattacīvaraṃ ādāyāti bhikkhuliṅgavesena sarīrena dhāretvā.

As for 'meals for all sectarians,' these are meals established as common to all sectarians. And this common meal is mentioned because, in the partaking of a meal specified for bhikkhus only, communion might also occur. However, without consenting to communion, even one who eats monastery meals and so on in places like monasteries where there are no bhikkhus does not become one who lives in communion by theft at all. As for 'by undertaking work,' it means by doing work such as ploughing. As for 'taking the bowl and robes,' it means bearing them on the body by means of the outward sign of a bhikkhu.

“Yo evaṃ pabbajati, so theyyasaṃvāsako nāma hotī”ti idaṃ nidassanamattaṃ, “theyyasaṃvāsako”ti pana nāmaṃ ajānantopi “evaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vā “evaṃ karonto samaṇo nāma na hotī”ti vā “yadi ārocessāmi, chaḍḍessanti ma”nti vā “yena kenaci pabbajjā me na ruhatī”ti jānāti, theyyasaṃvāsako hoti. Yo pana paṭhamaṃ “pabbajjā evaṃ me gahitā”tisaññī kevalaṃ antarā attano setavatthanivāsanādivippakāraṃ pakāsetuṃ lajjanto na katheti, so theyyasaṃvāsako na hoti. Anupasampannakāleyevāti ettha avadhāraṇena upasampannakāle theyyasaṃvāsakalakkhaṇaṃ ñatvā vañcanāyapi nāroceti, theyyasaṃvāsako na hotīti dīpeti. So parisuddhacittena gahitaliṅgattā liṅgatthenako na hoti, laddhūpasampadattā tadanuguṇasseva saṃvāsassa sāditattā saṃvāsatthenakopi na hoti. Anupasampanno pana liṅgatthenako hoti, saṃvāsārahassa liṅgassa gahitattā saṃvāsasādiyanamattena saṃvāsatthenako hoti.

The statement, 'Whoever goes forth in this way, he is called one who lives in communion by theft,' is merely an example. But even without knowing the name 'one who lives in communion by theft,' if one knows, 'It is not proper to do this,' or 'Doing this, one is not a recluse,' or 'If I inform them, they will expel me,' or 'For some reason or other, my going forth is not valid,' he becomes one who lives in communion by theft. But one who at first has the perception, 'My going forth was undertaken thus,' and, merely being ashamed to reveal his own irregularity, such as wearing white clothes, does not speak, he does not become one who lives in communion by theft. Here, by the emphasis in 'only at the time of being unordained,' it shows that if, at the time of being fully ordained, having known the characteristic of one who lives in communion by theft, he does not inform them even out of deceit, he does not become one who lives in communion by theft. Indeed, because the outward sign was taken with a pure mind, he is not a thief by way of the outward sign; because higher ordination has been obtained, and because he consents to a communion that is in accordance with it, he is also not a thief by way of communion. An unordained person, however, is not a thief by way of the outward sign. Why? Because he has taken the outward sign that is worthy of communion. By merely consenting to communion, he becomes a thief by way of communion.

Saliṅge ṭhitoti saliṅgabhāve ṭhito. Theyyasaṃvāsako na hotīti bhikkhūhi dinnaliṅgassa apariccattattā liṅgatthenako na hoti, bhikkhupaṭiññāya apariccattattā saṃvāsatthenako na hotīti. Yaṃ pana mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ “liṅgānurūpassa saṃvāsassa sāditattā na saṃvāsatthenako”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanā) kāraṇaṃ vuttaṃ, tampi idameva kāraṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Itarathā [M 2.0122][V 2.0117] sāmaṇerassapi bhikkhuvassagaṇanādīsu liṅgānurūpasaṃvāso eva sāditoti saṃvāsatthenakatā na siyā bhikkhūhi dinnaliṅgassa ubhinnampi sādhāraṇattā. Yathā cettha bhikkhu, evaṃ sāmaṇeropi pārājikaṃ samāpanno sāmaṇerapaṭiññāya apariccattattā saṃvāsatthenako na hotīti veditabbo. Sobhatīti sampaṭicchitvāti kāsāvadhāraṇe dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā gihibhāvaṃ sampaṭicchitvā.

Standing in one's own mark means being established in the state of having one's own mark. He is not one who lives in communion by theft: because the mark given by the bhikkhus has not been relinquished, he is not a thief of the mark; and because the acknowledgment of being a bhikkhu has not been relinquished, he is not a thief of communion. However, the reason stated in the Mātikā Commentary—"Because he enjoys communion that conforms to the mark, he is not a thief of communion"—this too is said with reference to this very reason. Otherwise, even for a novice, who enjoys communion appropriate to the mark in matters such as counting the years as a bhikkhu, there would be no state of being a thief of communion, since the mark given by the bhikkhus is common to both. Just as a bhikkhu here is not a thief of communion, so too a novice who has committed a pārājika offense is not a thief of communion because his acknowledgment of being a novice has not been relinquished—this should be understood. "It is fitting" means "having accepted": having laid down the burden of wearing the saffron robe, he has accepted the state of a householder.

Yo koci vuḍḍhapabbajitoti sāmaṇeraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Mahāpeḷādīsūti vilīvādimayesu gharadvāresu ṭhapitabhattabhājanavisesesu, etena vihāre bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ vassagaṇanādīnaṃ akaraṇaṃ dasseti.

The phrase 'Whoever is an elder who has gone forth' is said with reference to a novice. 'In large baskets and so forth' refers to special food containers made of woven bamboo strips and so forth, placed at the doors of houses. By this, it shows the non-performance of counting the rains-residence and so forth together with the bhikkhus in the monastery.

Theyyasaṃvāsakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the account of one who lives in communion by theft is concluded.

Titthiyapakkantakakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of One Who Has Gone Over to the Sectarians

Titthiyapakkantakādikathāsu tesaṃ liṅge ādinnamatteti vīmaṃsādiadhippāyaṃ vinā “titthiyo bhavissāmī”ti sanniṭṭhānavasena liṅge kāyena dhāritamatte. Sayamevāti titthiyānaṃ santikaṃ agantvā sayameva saṅghārāmepi kusacīrādīni nivāseti. Ājīvako bhavissāmi…pe… gacchatīti ājīvakānaṃ santike tesaṃ pabbajanavidhinā “ājīvako bhavissāmī”ti gacchati. Tassa hi titthiyabhāvūpagamanaṃ pati sanniṭṭhāne vijjamānepi “gantvā bhavissāmī”ti parikappitattā padavāre dukkaṭameva vuttaṃ. Dukkaṭanti pāḷiyā avuttepi methunādīsu vuttapubbapayogadukkaṭānulomato vuttaṃ. Etena ca sanniṭṭhānavasena liṅge sampaṭicchite pārājikaṃ, tato purimapayoge thullaccayañca vattabbameva, thullaccayakkhaṇe nivattantopi āpattiṃ desāpetvā muccati evāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yathā cettha, evaṃ saṅghabhedepi lohituppādepi bhikkhūnaṃ pubbapayogādīsu dukkaṭathullaccayapārājikāhi muccanasīmā ca veditabbā. Sāsanaviruddhatāyettha ādikammikānampi anāpatti na vuttā. Pabbajjāyapi abhabbatādassanatthaṃ panete, aññe ca pārājikakaṇḍe visuṃ sikkhāpadena pārājikādiṃ adassetvā idha abhabbesu eva vuttāti veditabbaṃ.

In the accounts of one who has gone over to the sectarians and so forth, 'merely by taking up their mark' means merely wearing the sect's mark on the body with a firm decision, 'I will become a sectarian,' without any intention of investigation and so forth. 'By himself' means that without going to the sectarians, he of his own accord dons grass garments and so forth, even within the monastery compound. 'I will become an Ājīvaka... he goes' means he goes to the Ājīvakas with the thought, 'I will become an Ājīvaka,' according to their ordination procedure. For him, although a firm decision to go over to the state of a sectarian is present, because it was conceived as 'Having gone, I will become one,' only a dukkaṭa offense is stated for each step. 'Dukkaṭa' is stated, although not stated in the Pāḷi, by analogy with the dukkaṭa for a preliminary act stated in cases such as sexual intercourse. And by this it should be understood that when the mark is accepted with a firm decision, it is a pārājika offense, and in the preceding preliminary act, a thullaccaya offense is also to be stated. Even one who turns back at the moment of the thullaccaya is freed only by confessing the offense. Just as here, so too in cases of causing a schism and of shedding a Buddha's blood, the boundary for being freed from dukkaṭa, thullaccaya, and pārājika offenses in the preliminary acts and so forth of bhikkhus should be known. Because of its opposition to the Dispensation, here no-offense is not stated even for the first offenders. However, to show their ineligibility for ordination, it should be understood that these offenses and others are stated here only among the cases of ineligibility, without being shown as pārājika offenses by a separate training rule in the Pārājika section.

Taṃ [M 2.0123] laddhinti titthiyavese seṭṭhabhāvaggahaṇameva sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tesañhi titthiyānaṃ sassatādiggāhaṃ gaṇhantopi liṅge asampaṭicchite titthiyapakkantako na hoti, taṃ laddhiṃ aggahetvāpi “etesaṃ vatacariyā sundarā”ti liṅgaṃ sampaṭicchanto titthiyapakkantako hoti eva[V 2.0118]. Laddhiyā abhāvenāti bhikkhubhāve sālayatāya titthiyabhāvūpagamanaladdhiyā abhāvena, etena ca āpadāsu kusacīrādiṃ pārupantassāpi naggassa viya anāpattiṃ dasseti.

'That doctrine' is said with reference only to the grasping of the state of excellence in the guise of a sectarian. Indeed, even if one holds the eternalist and other views of those sectarians, as long as their mark is not accepted, one does not become one who has gone over to the sectarians. But one who, without holding that doctrine, accepts the mark, thinking, "Their practices and conduct are excellent," certainly becomes one who has gone over to the sectarians. 'Due to the absence of the doctrine' means due to the absence of a doctrine inclined towards going over to the state of a sectarian, because of having an attachment to the state of a bhikkhu. And by this, it shows that for one who wears a grass garment or the like in times of calamity, there is no offense, just as for one who is naked.

Upasampannabhikkhunā kathitoti ettha saṅghabhedakopi upasampannabhikkhunāva kathito, mātughātakādayo pana anupasampannenāpīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Here, in the phrase 'spoken of by a fully ordained bhikkhu,' a schismatic is also spoken of as being only a fully ordained bhikkhu. But it should be understood that matricides and so forth can be even those who are not fully ordained.

Titthiyapakkantakakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the account of one who has gone over to the sectarians is concluded.

Tiracchānavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of the Animal Story

111. Udakasañcārikaṃ maṇḍūkabhakkhaṃ nāgasarīranti sambandhitabbaṃ. Vissarabhayenāti nāgassa sarīraṃ disvā bhikkhuno viravanabhayena. Kapimiddhādīsu nāgasarīraṃ nuppajjatīti taduppattisīmaṃ dassento āha “vissaṭṭho”tiādi.

111. The water-roaming, frog-eating nāga's body should be thus connected. 'Through fear of an outcry' means through fear of the bhikkhu crying out upon seeing the nāga's body. In cases of monkey-sleep and so forth, a nāga's body does not arise. Thus, wishing to show the limit of its arising, he said the words beginning with 'vissaṭṭho'.

Tiracchānavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story Concerning Animals is concluded.

Mātughātakādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse Concerning Matricide and So Forth

112. Apavāhananti sodhanaṃ. Tiracchānādiamanussajātito manussajātikānaññeva puttesu mettādayopi tikkhavisadā honti lokuttaraguṇā viyāti āha “manussitthibhūtā janikā mātā”ti. Yathā manussānaññeva kusalappavatti tikkhavisadā, evaṃ akusalappavattipīti āha “sayampi manussajātikenevā”tiādi. Ānantariyenāti ettha cutianantaraṃ niraye paṭisandhiphalaṃ anantaraṃ nāma, tasmiṃ anantare janakattena niyuttaṃ ānantariyaṃ, tena. Vesiyā puttoti upalakkhaṇamattaṃ, kulitthiyā aticāriniyā puttopi attano pitaraṃ ajānitvā ghātento pitughātakova hoti.

112. `Apavāhanaṃ` means purification. Compared to those of animal or other non-human birth, only in the children of those of human birth are loving-kindness and so forth sharp and clear, like supramundane qualities. Therefore, he said, 'a mother who is a human female, a genetrix.' Just as for humans alone the arising of the wholesome is sharp and clear, so too is the arising of the unwholesome sharp and clear. Therefore, he said the words beginning with 'even by one of human birth himself.' Here, in the phrase `ānantariyena`, the fruit of rebirth-linking in hell immediately after death is called 'immediate' (`anantaraṃ`). The kamma that is appointed by its nature as a generator of that immediate result is an `ānantariya` kamma. `Tena` means by that kamma. The phrase 'son of a prostitute' is merely an illustration; even the son of a transgressing woman of good family, not knowing his own father and killing him, becomes a patricide indeed.

114. Avasesanti [M 2.0124] anāgāmiādikaṃ. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ manussaviggahapārājike vuttameva.

114. `Avasesaṃ` refers to the non-returner and so forth. Whatever should be said here has already been said in the section on the Pārājika concerning a human body.

115. Ayaṃ saṅghabhedakoti pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Pubbe eva pārājikaṃ samāpanno [V 2.0119] vā vatthādidosena vipannopasampado vā saṅghaṃ bhindantopi anantariyaṃ na phusati, saṅgho pana bhinnova hoti, pabbajjā cassa na vāritāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

115. The phrase 'This is a schismatic' is said in reference to a bhikkhu of normal virtue. One who has previously committed a Pārājika offense, or one whose higher ordination is invalid due to a defect in the object and so forth, even while splitting the Saṅgha, does not incur an `ānantariya` kamma. The Saṅgha, however, is indeed split, and for such a person, the going forth is not forbidden. Thus it should be understood.

“Duṭṭhacittenā”ti vuttamevatthaṃ vibhāveti “vadhakacittenā”ti. Lohitaṃ uppādetīti tathāgatassa verīhi abhejjakāyatāya kenaci balakkārena cammādichedaṃ katvā bahi lohitaṃ paggharāpetuṃ na sakkā, āvudhādipahārena pana lohitaṃ ṭhānato calitvā kuppamānaṃ ekattha sañcitaṃ hoti, ettakena pana pahāradāyako lohituppādako nāma hoti devadatto viya. Cetiyaṃ pana bodhiṃ vā paṭimādiṃ vā bhindato ānantariyaṃ na hoti, ānantariyasadisaṃ mahāsāvajjaṃ hoti. Bodhirukkhassa pana ojoharaṇasākhā ceva sadhātukaṃ cetiyaṃ bādhayamānā ca chinditabbā, puññamevettha hoti.

He clarifies the meaning already stated by 'with a corrupt mind' with the phrase 'with a murderous mind.' As for 'producing blood': because the Tathāgata has an indestructible body, it is not possible for anyone, by using force, to make a cut in the skin, etc., and cause blood to flow outside. However, due to a blow from a weapon, etc., the blood, moving from its place and becoming agitated, gathers in one spot. By just this much, the one who delivers the blow is called a 'producer of blood,' like Devadatta. For one who destroys a cetiya, a Bodhi tree, or an image, etc., an `ānantariya` kamma does not occur; it is a great fault similar to an `ānantariya` kamma. However, of a Bodhi tree, a dry branch that has lost its sap, and a branch that is damaging a cetiya containing relics, should be cut. In this, there is only merit.

Mātughātakādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse Concerning Matricide and So Forth is concluded.

Ubhatobyañjanakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse Concerning the Case of the Ubhatobyañjanaka (One with Dual Sexual Characteristics)

116. Itthiubhatobyañjanakoti itthindriyayutto, itaro pana purisindriyayutto. Ekassa hi bhāvadvayaṃ saha nuppajjati yamake (yama. 3.indriyayamaka.188) paṭikkhittattā. Dutiyabyañjanaṃ pana kammasahāyena akusalacitteneva bhāvavirahitaṃ uppajjati. Pakatitthipurisānampi kammameva byañjanaliṅgānaṃ kāraṇaṃ, na bhāvo tassa kenaci paccayena paccayattassa paṭṭhāne avuttattā. Kevalaṃ bhāvasahitānaṃyeva byañjanaliṅgānaṃ pavattidassanatthaṃ aṭṭhakathāsu “itthindriyaṃ paṭicca itthiliṅgādīnī”tiādinā (dha. sa. aṭṭha. 632) indriyaṃ byañjanakaāraṇattena vuttaṃ, idha pana akusalabalena indriyaṃ vināpi byañjanaṃ uppajjatīti vuttaṃ. Ubhinnampi cesaṃ ubhatobyañjanakānaṃ yadā itthiyā rāgo uppajjati, tadā purisabyañjanaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti, itaraṃ paṭicchannaṃ. Yadā purise rāgo uppajjati, tadā itthibyañjanaṃ [M 2.0125] pākaṭaṃ hoti, itaraṃ paṭicchannaṃ. Tattha vicāraṇakkamoti paṭisandhikkhaṇe eva itthipurisaliṅgānampi pātubhāvappakāsake kurundivacane ayuttatāpakāsanatthaṃ atthavicāraṇakkamo. Aṭṭhasāliniyañhi “itthiliṅgādīni pana itthindriyaṃ paṭicca pavatte samuṭṭhitānī”tiādi (dha. sa. aṭṭha. 632) vuttaṃ. Nevassa pabbajjā atthīti yojanā. Yo ca paṭikkhitte abhabbe, bhabbe ca puggale ñatvā pabbājeti, upasampādeti vā, dukkaṭaṃ. Ajānantassa sabbattha anāpattīti veditabbaṃ.

116. As for the female ubhatobyañjanaka, it is one endowed with the female faculty; the other, however, the male ubhatobyañjanaka, is endowed with the male faculty. Indeed, for one person, the pair of faculties does not arise together, because it is rejected in the Yamaka. The second characteristic, however, having kamma as its companion, arises devoid of the faculty, solely through an unwholesome mind. For ordinary women and men as well, kamma alone is the cause of their characteristics and signs, not the faculty, because its being a condition through any factor is not stated in the Paṭṭhāna. Merely in order to show the occurrence of characteristics and signs only for those who possess the faculty, it is stated in the commentaries, by way of 'Dependent on the female faculty, the female characteristics, etc.,' that the faculty is the cause of the characteristics. Here, however, it is said that due to the power of the unwholesome, a characteristic arises even without the faculty. For both of these ubhatobyañjanakas, when lust for a woman arises, the male characteristic becomes manifest, while the other is concealed. When lust for a man arises, the female characteristic becomes manifest, while the other is concealed. As for the 'method of investigation therein,' it is the sequence of investigating the meaning in order to show the unsuitability in the statement of the Kurundī which declares the manifestation of the female and male characteristics at the very moment of rebirth-linking. Indeed, in the Aṭṭhasālinī it is stated: 'The female characteristics, etc., however, have arisen in the course of existence dependent on the female faculty,' and so on. The connection is: 'For this person, there is no going forth.' And whoever, knowing the rejected, unfit persons and the fit persons, gives the going forth or the higher ordination, commits a dukkaṭa offense. It should be known that for one who does not know, there is no offense in any case.

Ubhatobyañjanakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse Concerning the Case of the Ubhatobyañjanaka is concluded.

Anupajjhāyakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse Concerning the Cases of Those Without a Preceptor, and so forth

117. Anupajjhāyādivatthūsu [V 2.0120] sikkhāpadaṃ apaññattanti “na, bhikkhave, anupajjhāyako upasampādetabbo”ti idheva paññāpiyamānasikkhāpadaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Kammaṃ pana na kuppatī”ti idaṃ upajjhāyābhāvepi “itthannāmassa upasampadāpekkho, itthannāmena upajjhāyenā”ti matassa vā vibbhamantassa vā purāṇaupajjhāyassa, aññassa vā yassa kassaci avijjamānassāpi nāmena sabbattha upajjhāyakittanassa katattā vuttaṃ. Yadi hi upajjhāyakittanaṃ na kareyya, “puggalaṃ na parāmasatī”ti vuttakammavipatti eva siyā. Teneva pāḷiyaṃ “anupajjhāyaka”nti vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyampissa “upajjhāyaṃ akittetvā”ti avatvā “upajjhāyaṃ agāhāpetvā sabbena sabbaṃ upajjhāyavirahitaṃ”icceva atthoti vutto. Pāḷiyaṃ saṅghena upajjhāyenāti “ayaṃ itthannāmo saṅghassa upasampadāpekkho, itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati saṅghena upajjhāyenā”ti evaṃ kammavācāya saṅghameva upajjhāyaṃ kittetvāti attho. Evaṃ gaṇena upajjhāyenāti etthāpi “ayaṃ itthannāmo gaṇassa upasampadāpekkho”tiādinā yojanā veditabbā, evaṃ vuttepi kammaṃ na kuppati eva dukkaṭasseva vuttattā. Aññathā “so ca puggalo anupasampanno”ti vadeyya. Tenāha “saṅghenā”tiādi. Tattha paṇḍakādīhi upajjhāyehi kariyamānesu kammesu paṇḍakādike vināva yadi pañcavaggādigaṇo pūrati, kammaṃ na kuppati, itarathā kuppatīti veditabbaṃ.

117. In the cases of those without a preceptor, and so forth, the statement 'the training rule was not laid down' was said in reference to the training rule that was being laid down right here, namely: 'Monks, one without a preceptor is not to be given the higher ordination.' The statement, 'The formal act, however, is not invalid,' was said because, even in the absence of a preceptor, the declaration of a preceptor has been made in all instances by the name of some non-existent person—be it a deceased preceptor, one who has disrobed, a former preceptor, or some other unspecified person—with the words: 'So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination with So-and-so as preceptor.' For if one were not to make the declaration of a preceptor, there would be precisely that failure of the formal act which is stated as: 'It does not refer to the person.' For that very reason, in the Pāḷi it is said 'without a preceptor.' And in its commentary, without saying 'without declaring a preceptor,' the meaning is stated only as 'without having a preceptor accepted, being completely and utterly without a preceptor.' In the Pāḷi, 'with the Saṅgha as preceptor' means that the Saṅgha itself is declared as the preceptor with the formal motion thus: 'This So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination from the Saṅgha; So-and-so requests the higher ordination from the Saṅgha, with the Saṅgha as preceptor.' This is the meaning. Similarly, here too in the phrase 'with the chapter as preceptor,' the connection should be understood by way of 'This So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination from the chapter,' and so on. Even when it is stated thus, the formal act is still not invalid, because only a dukkaṭa offense was stated. Otherwise, He would have said: 'And that person is not one who has received the higher ordination.' Therefore, He said 'by the Saṅgha,' and so on. Therein, regarding formal acts being performed with preceptors who are paṇḍakas, etc., if the chapter of five or more is complete even without the paṇḍaka, etc., the formal act is not invalid; otherwise, it is invalid. Thus it should be known.

Anupajjhāyakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Cases of Those Without a Preceptor, and so forth, is concluded.

Apattakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Cases of the One Without a Bowl, and so forth.

118. Apattacīvaravatthūsupi [M 2.0126] pattacīvarānaṃ abhāvepi “paripuṇṇassa pattacīvara”nti kammavācāya sāvitattā kammakopaṃ avatvā dukkaṭameva vuttaṃ. Itarathā sāvanāya hāpanato kammakopo eva siyā. Keci pana “paṭhamaṃ anuññātakammavācāya upasampannā viya idānipi ‘paripuṇṇassa pattacīvara’nti avatvā kammavācāya upasampannāpi sūpasampannāevā”ti vadanti, taṃ na yuttaṃ. Anuññātakālato paṭṭhāya hi aparāmasanaṃ sāvanāya hāpanavipatti eva hoti “itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācatī”ti padassa hāpane viya. Tampi hi pacchā anuññātaṃ, “saṅghaṃ, bhante, upasampadaṃ yācāmī”tiādivākyena ayācetvā tampi upasampādento “ayaṃ itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācatī”ti vatvāva yadi kammavācaṃ karoti, kammaṃ sukatameva hoti[V 2.0121], no ce vipannaṃ. Sabbapacchā hi anuññātakammavācato kiñcipi parihāpetuṃ na vaṭṭati, sāvanāya hāpanameva hoti. Aññe vā bhikkhū dātukāmā hontīti sambandho.

118. Also in the cases of one without a bowl and robes, even in the absence of a bowl and robes, because it is proclaimed in the formal act, 'The bowl and robes are complete,' without stating the invalidation of the act, only a dukkaṭa offense is stated. Otherwise, due to the omission in the proclamation, the act would indeed be invalidated. Some, however, say: 'Just as those ordained at first by the authorized formal act were well-ordained, so too now, those ordained by a formal act without saying, "The bowl and robes are complete," are also well-ordained.' That is not proper. Indeed, starting from the time it was permitted, not reciting it is a failure due to omission from the proclamation, just as in the case of omitting the phrase, 'So-and-so requests ordination from the Saṅgha.' Indeed, that too was permitted later. Even if one has not requested with a statement such as, 'Venerable Sir, I request ordination from the Saṅgha,' if the one ordaining that person performs the formal act only after saying, 'This so-and-so requests ordination from the Saṅgha,' the act is indeed well-done. If not, it is invalid. Indeed, from the formal act that was permitted last of all, it is not proper to omit anything; it is simply an omission from the proclamation. Or, other monks may wish to give; this is the connection.

Anāmaṭṭhapiṇḍapātanti bhikkhūhi laddhabhikkhato aggahitaggaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ. Sāmaṇerabhāgasamakoti ettha kiñcāpi sāmaṇerānampi āmisabhāgassa samakameva diyyamānattā visuṃ sāmaṇerabhāgo nāma natthi, pattacīvaraparikammamattapaṭibaddhapabbajjatāya pana sāmaṇerasadisā ete paṇḍupalāsāti dassanatthaṃ evaṃ vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Niyatāsannapabbajjasseva cāyaṃ bhāgo dīyati. Teneva “yāva patto paccatī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Āmisabhāgoti vihāre dinnaṃ saṅghabhattaṃ, tatruppādañca sandhāya vuttaṃ, na dāyakānaṃ gehesu tehi diyyamānaṃ. Teneva salākabhattādi paṭikkhittaṃ, dāyakā vippaṭisārino hontīti. Bhesajjantiādinā pana gihīnaṃ bhesajjakaraṇādidoso ettha na hotīti dasseti.
