`Anāmaṭṭhapiṇḍapāta` means almsfood, from the alms obtained by the monks, from which the first portion has not been taken. Regarding `sāmaṇerabhāgasamako` (equal to a novice’s share): here, although a share of material requisites is given equally also to novices, and thus there is no separate thing called a 'novice's share,' it should be understood that it is said thus in order to show that these `paṇḍupalāsas` (candidates, lit. 'withered leaves') are like novices, because their going forth is connected only with the preparation of the bowl and robes. And this share is given only to one whose going forth is certain and imminent. For that very reason, it is said, 'until the bowl is fired,' and so on. `Āmisabhāga` (a share of material requisites) is said in reference to a communal meal given in the monastery and material requisites arising there, not to what is given by donors in their homes. For that very reason, ticket-food and so on were rejected by the commentator, with the thought that donors might become regretful. By the text beginning with `bhesajja` (medicine), it shows that in this case, the fault of laypersons preparing medicine, and so on, does not occur.

Apattakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Cases of the One Without a Bowl, and so forth, is concluded.

Hatthacchinnādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Cases of One Whose Hand is Cut Off, and so forth.

119. Hatthacchinnādivatthūsu [M 2.0127] kaṇṇamūleti sakalassa kaṇṇassa chedaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Kaṇṇasakkhalikāyāti kaṇṇacūḷikāya. Yassa pana kaṇṇāviddheti heṭṭhā kuṇḍalādiṭhapanacchiddaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tañhi saṅghaṭanakkhamaṃ. Ajapadaketi ajapadanāsikaṭṭhikoṭiyaṃ. Tato hi uddhaṃ na vicchindati. Sakkā hoti sandhetunti avirūpasaṇṭhānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, virūpaṃ pana parisadūsakataṃ āpādeti.

119. In the cases beginning with 'one whose hand is cut off,' the phrase 'at the root of the ear' is said in reference to the cutting of the entire ear. The phrase 'at the cartilage of the ear' means at the earlobe. The phrase 'one whose ear is pierced' is said in reference to the hole made below for placing earrings and so on, for that is suitable for joining. The phrase 'like a goat's foot' means at the tip of the nose-bone which has the shape of a goat's foot, for it is not cut off above that point. The phrase 'it is possible to join' is said in reference to a joining that is not deformed; a deformed one, however, leads to being a defiler of the assembly.

Khujjasarīroti vaṅkasarīro. Brahmuno viya ujukaṃ gattaṃ sarīraṃ yassa, so brahmujjugatto, bhagavā.

'One with a hunchbacked body' means one with a crooked body. He whose body is straight like that of Brahma is `brahmujjugatto`; this refers to the Blessed One.

Parivaṭumoti samantato vaṭṭakāyo, etena evarūpā eva vāmanakā na vaṭṭantīti dasseti.

'One with a globular body' means a body that is round all around. By this, it is shown that dwarfs of such a nature are not suitable.

Kūṭakūṭasīsoti anekesu ṭhānesu piṇḍikamaṃsataṃ dassetuṃ āmeḍitaṃ kataṃ. Tenāha “tālaphalapiṇḍisadisenā”ti, tālaphalānaṃ mañjarī piṇḍi nāma. Anupubbatanukena sīsenāti cetiyathūpikā [V 2.0122] viya kamena kisena sīsena, thūlaveḷupabbaṃ viya ādito paṭṭhāya yāvapariyosānaṃ samathūlena uccena sīsena samannāgato nāḷisīso nāma. Kappasīsoti gajamatthakaṃ viya dvidhā bhinnasīso. “Kaṇṇikakeso vā”ti imassa vivaraṇaṃ “pāṇakehī”tiādi. Makkaṭasseva naḷāṭepi kesānaṃ uṭṭhitabhāvaṃ sandhāyāha “sīsalomehī”tiādi.

Regarding 'one with a lumpy, lumpy head,' the repetition is made to show the state of having lumps of flesh in many places. Therefore, it is said, 'like a cluster of palm fruits.' The fruit-stalk of palm fruits is called `piṇḍi`. 'With a head that gradually tapers' means with a head that is sequentially slender like the spire of a cetiya. One endowed with a head that is uniformly thick and high from beginning to end, like a thick bamboo joint, is called `nāḷisīso`. 'One with a monkey's head' means one with a head split in two, like an elephant's head. The explanation of 'or with hair like corn-silk' is the phrase beginning with 'by insects.' Referring to the state of hair growing even on the forehead, as on a monkey, the phrase beginning with 'by the hairs of the head' is stated.

Makkaṭabhamukoti naḷāṭalomehi avibhattalomabhamuko. Akkhicakkalehīti kaṇhamaṇḍalehi. Kekaroti tiriyaṃ passanako. Udakatārakāti olokentānaṃ udake paṭibimbikacchāyā, udakapubbuḷanti keci. Akkhitārakāti abhimukhe ṭhitānaṃ chāyā, akkhigaṇḍakātipi vadanti. Atipiṅgalakkhīti majjārakkhi. Madhupiṅgalanti madhuvaṇṇapiṅgalaṃ. Nippakhumakkhīti ettha pakhuma-saddo akkhidalalomesu nirūḷho, tadabhāvā nippakhumakkhi. Akkhipākenāti akkhidala pariyantesu pūtibhāvāpajjanarogena.

'One with a monkey's brow' means one whose eyebrow-hairs are not distinguished from the hairs on the forehead. 'With eye-circles' means with the black circles of the eyes. 'One who squints' means one who looks sideways. 'Water-star' means the reflected image in the water of those looking; some say it means a water bubble. 'Eye-star' means the reflection of those standing in front; they also say it means a sty in the eye. 'One with very tawny eyes' means one with cat-like eyes. 'Honey-tawny' means tawny with the color of honey. Regarding 'one with no eyelashes,' here the word `pakhuma` is established for the hairs on the eyelids; due to their absence, one is called `nippakhumakkhi`. 'By eye-inflammation' means by the disease that causes a state of putrefaction at the edges of the eyelids.

Cipiṭanāsikoti [M 2.0128] anunnatanāsiko. Paṭaṅgamaṇḍūko nāma mahāmukhamaṇḍūko. Bhinnamukhoti upakkamukhapariyosāno, sabbadā vivaṭamukho vā. Vaṅkamukhoti ekapasse apakkamma ṭhitaheṭṭhimahanukaṭṭhiko. Oṭṭhacchinnakoti ubhosu oṭṭhesu yattha katthaci jātiyā vā pacchā vā satthādinā apanītamaṃsena oṭṭhena samannāgato. Eḷamukhoti niccapaggharitalālāmukho.

'One with a flat nose' means one with a nose that is not raised. A `paṭaṅgamaṇḍūka` is a frog with a wide mouth. 'One with a split mouth' means one whose mouth-ends are split, or one whose mouth is always open. 'One with a crooked mouth' means one whose lower jaw-bone is displaced to one side. 'One with a cut lip' means one endowed with a lip, on either of the two lips, from which flesh has been removed by a knife or the like, either from birth or later. 'One with a drooling mouth' means one whose mouth constantly drips with saliva.

Bhinnagaloti avanatagato. Bhinnauroti atininnauramajjho. Evaṃ bhinnapiṭṭhipi. Sabbañcetanti “kacchugatto”tiādiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ettha ca vinicchayo kuṭṭhādīsu vutto evāti āha “vinicchayo”tiādi.

'One with a broken neck' means one with a bent-down neck. 'One with a broken chest' means one whose mid-chest is very sunken. 'One with a broken back' is also similar. The phrase `sabbañcetaṃ` is said with reference to the phrase beginning with 'one with a scabby body.' And here, the decision is just as was stated in the section on leprosy and so on; therefore, the phrase beginning with 'the decision' is stated.

Vātaṇḍikoti aṇḍavātarogena uddhutabījaṇḍakosena samannāgato, yassa nivāsanena paṭicchannampi unnataṃ pakāsati, sova na pabbājetabbo. Vikaṭoti tiriyaṃgamanapādo, yassa caṅkamato jāṇukā bahi nigacchanti. Paṇhoti pacchato parivattanakapādo, yassa caṅkamato jāṇukā anto pavisanti. Mahājaṅghoti thūlajaṅgho. Mahāpādoti mahantena pādatalena yutto. Pādavemajjheti piṭṭhipādavemajjhe, etena aggapādo ca paṇhi ca sadisoti dasseti.

'One with a hydrocele' means one endowed with a scrotum swollen due to the disease of 'wind in the testicles'; for whom, even when covered by a lower garment, it appears raised. That person also should not be ordained. 'One who is deformed' means one whose feet move sideways, whose knees go outwards when walking. 'One whose knees knock' means one whose feet turn backwards, whose knees go inwards when walking. 'One with large shanks' means one with thick shanks. 'One with a large foot' means one endowed with a large sole. 'In the middle of the foot' means in the middle of the instep; by this, it is shown that the forefoot and the heel are similar.

Majjhe saṅkuṭitapādattāti kuṇḍapādatāya kāraṇavibhāvanaṃ. Agge saṅkuṭitapādattāti kuṇḍapādatāya sakuṇapādasseva gamanavibhāvanaṃ. Piṭṭhipādaggena caṅkamantoti “pādassa bāhirantenāti [V 2.0123] ca abbhantarantenā”ti ca idaṃ pādatalassa ubhohi pariyantehi caṅkamanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

The phrase 'because the feet are contracted in the middle' is a statement of the cause for the state of having feet like a bow. The phrase 'because the feet are contracted at the tip' is an explanation of the gait, like that of a bird's feet, due to the state of having feet like a bow. Regarding 'walking on the top of the foot,' this statement, 'on the outer edge of the foot' and 'on the inner edge,' was said in reference to walking on both edges of the sole of the foot.

Mammananti ṭhānakaraṇavisuddhiyā abhāvena ayuttakkharavacanaṃ. Vacanānukaraṇena hi so mammano vutto. Yo ca karaṇasampannopi ekamevakkharaṃ hikkārabahuso vadati, sopi idheva saṅgayhati. Yo vā pana hikkaṃ niggahetvāpi anāmeḍitakkharameva siliṭṭhavacanaṃ vattuṃ samattho, so pabbājetabbo.

'Stammering' means speech with improper syllables due to the lack of purity in the place and instrument of articulation. For, due to imitating speech, that person is called a stammerer. And whoever, though endowed with the instruments of articulation, utters a single syllable many times with a stutter, he too is included right here. But whoever, having suppressed the stutter, is able to speak smooth speech with unrepeated syllables, he should be ordained.

Āpattito na muccatīti ñatvā karontova na muccati. Jīvitantarāyādiāpadāsu aruciyā kāyasāmaggiṃ dentassa anāpatti. Appatto osāraṇanti osāraṇāya anarahoti attho.

'Is not freed from the offense' means that only one who performs the ordination while knowing is not freed. There is no offense for one who gives communal consent out of dislike due to dangers such as loss of life. 'Not having reached admission' means 'unworthy of admission'; this is the meaning.

Hatthacchinnādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Cases Beginning with 'One Whose Hand is Cut Off' is finished.

Alajjinissayavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Story concerning Dependence on the Shameless

120. Nissayapaṭisaṃyuttavatthūsu [M 2.0129] bhikkhūhi samāno bhāgo diṭṭhisīlādiguṇakoṭṭhāso assāti bhikkhusabhāgo, tassa bhāvo bhikkhusabhāgatā.

120. In the stories connected with dependence: because a person has a share—a portion of qualities such as view and virtue—that is common with the monks, he is a `bhikkhusabhāga`. The state of being that person is `bhikkhusabhāgatā`.

Alajjinissayavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Story concerning Dependence on the Shameless is finished.

Gamikādinissayavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Story concerning Dependence on Travelers and Others

121. Nissayakaraṇīyoti ettha nissayaggahaṇaṃ nissayo, so karaṇīyo yassāti visesanassa paranipāto daṭṭhabbo. Vissamento vā…pe… anāpattīti gamanasaussāhatāya tathā vasantopi addhiko eva, tattha nissayadāyake asati anāpattīti adhippāyo. Etena ca parissamādiabhāve senāsanādisampadaṃ paṭicca vasato āpattīti dasseti. Tañca agamanapaccayā divase divase āpajjatīti vadanti. Cīvararajanādikiccatthāya garūhi pesitassāpi kiccapariyosānameva vasitabbaṃ, na tato paraṃ. Garūhipi tāvakālikakiccatthameva pesaladaharā pesitabbā, na niccakālakiccatthanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Nāvāya gacchantassa…pe… anāpattī”ti [V 2.0124] vuttattā evarūpaṃ avidheyyataṃ vinā nissayadāyakarahitaṭṭhāne vassaṃ upagantuṃ na vaṭṭatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

121. Regarding `Nissayakaraṇīyo`: here, `nissaya` means the taking of dependence. It should be understood that this is a case of the post-position of the adjective, as in: `so karaṇīyo yassa` (for whom it is to be done). Regarding `Vissamento vā…pe… anāpatti`: due to exertion in travel, one dwelling thus is still a traveler; the intention is that there is no offense if a dependence-giver is absent there. And by this, it is shown that in the absence of fatigue and so forth, an offense is incurred for one who dwells depending on the abundance of lodgings and so forth. And they say that this offense is incurred day by day due to the factor of not traveling. Even for one sent by teachers for the purpose of tasks such as dyeing robes, one should dwell only until the completion of the task, not beyond that. Teachers, too, should send amiable young monks only for the sake of temporary tasks, not for the sake of permanent tasks; this should be understood. Because it is said, 'For one going by boat…pe… no offense,' it should be understood that without such an unavoidable situation, it is not proper to enter the rains-residence in a place devoid of a dependence-giver.

Tassa nissāyāti taṃ nissāya. Āsāḷhīmāse…pe… tattha gantabbanti ettha pana sacepi “asuko thero ettha āgamissati āgamissatī”ti āgamentasseva vassūpanāyikadivaso hoti. Hotu, vasitaṭṭhāne vassaṃ anupagamma yattha nissayo labbhati, dūrepi tattha gantvā pacchimikāya upagantabbaṃ.

`Tassa nissāya` means `taṃ nissāya` (depending on him). Now, regarding the passage `Āsāḷhīmāse…pe… tattha gantabbaṃ`: even if the day for entering the rains-residence arrives while one is still expecting, “Such-and-such an elder will come, will come here,” so be it. Without entering the first rains-residence in the place one has dwelt, one should go to wherever dependence is obtainable, even if it is far, and enter upon the later rains-residence.

122. Gottenapīti “āyasmato pippalissa upasampadāpekkho”ti evaṃ nāmaṃ avatvā gottanāmenapīti attho, tena “konāmo te upajjhāyo”ti puṭṭhena gottanāmena “āyasmā kassapo”ti vattabbanti siddhaṃ hoti. Tasmā aññampi kiñci tassa nāmaṃ pasiddhaṃ, tasmiṃ vā khaṇe sukhaggahaṇatthaṃ nāmaṃ paññāpitaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ gahetvāpi anussāvanā kātabbā. Yathā [M 2.0130] upajjhāyassa, evaṃ upasampadāpekkhassapi gottādināmena, taṅkhaṇikanāmena ca anussāvanaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Tasmimpi khaṇe “ayaṃ tisso”ti vā “nāgo”ti vā nāmaṃ karontehi anusāsakasammutito paṭhamameva kātabbaṃ, evaṃ katvāpi antarāyikadhammānusāsanapucchanakālesu “kinnāmosi, ahaṃ bhante nāgo nāma, konāmo te upajjhāyo, upajjhāyo me bhante tisso nāmā”tiādinā viññāpentena ubhinnampi citte “mamedaṃ nāma”nti yathā saññā uppajjati, evaṃ viññāpetabbaṃ. Sace pana tasmiṃ khaṇe pakatināmena vatvā pacchā tissa-nāmādiapubbanāmena anussāveti, na vaṭṭati.

122. `Gottenapi` means: even by the clan name, without stating the name as in, 'the ordination-candidate of the Venerable Pippali'; this is the meaning. By this, it is established that when the ordination-candidate is asked, 'What is your preceptor's name?', it should be stated with the clan name, 'The Venerable Kassapa.' Therefore, any other well-known name of his, or a name designated at that moment for ease of grasping—taking all of that, the formal announcement should be performed. Just as for the preceptor, so too for the ordination-candidate, it is proper to perform the formal announcement by the clan name and so forth, and by a name given at that moment. At that moment, those giving a name such as, 'This is Tissa,' or 'This is Nāga,' should do so right from the beginning, from the appointment of the instructor. Even without having done so, at the times of instruction and questioning about the obstructing conditions, by making it known with, 'What is your name? Bhante, my name is Nāga. What is your preceptor's name? Bhante, my preceptor's name is Tissa,' and so forth, it should be made known in such a way that the perception, 'This is my name,' arises in the minds of both. But if at that moment one states the ordinary name and later announces with a new name such as Tissa, it is not proper.

Tattha ca kiñcāpi upajjhāyasseva nāmaṃ aggahetvā yena kenaci nāmena “tissassa upasampadāpekkho”tiādināpi puggale parāmaṭṭhe kammaṃ sukatameva hoti anupajjhāyakādīnaṃ upasampadākammaṃ viya upajjhāyassa abhāvepi abhabbattepi kammavācāya puggale parāmaṭṭhe kammassa sijjhanato. Upasampadāpekkhassa pana yathāsakaṃ nāmaṃ vinā aññena nāmena anussāvite kammaṃ kuppati, so anupasampannova hoti. Tattha ṭhito añño anupasampanno viya gahitanāmassa vatthupuggalassa tattha abhāvā, etassa ca nāmassa anussāvanāya avuttattā. Tasmā upasampadāpekkhassa pakatināmaṃ parivattetvā anupubbena nāgādināmena anussāvetukāmena paṭikacceva “tvaṃ nāgo”tiādinā viññāpetvā anusāsanaantarāyikadhammapucchanakkhaṇesupi tassa ca saṅghassa ca yathā pākaṭaṃ hoti, tathā pakāsetvāva nāgādināmena anussāvetabbaṃ. Ekassa bahūni nāmāni honti, tesu ekaṃ gahetuṃ vaṭṭati.

And here, although if the preceptor's name is not taken and the person is referred to by some other name, such as 'the ordination-candidate of Tissa,' the act is indeed well-performed—like the ordination act of those without a preceptor, because the act succeeds when the person is referred to in the Kammavācā even in the absence of a preceptor or his unsuitability—nevertheless, for the ordination-candidate, if the announcement is made with another name without his own respective name, the act is spoiled; he is indeed unordained. Like whom? Like another unordained person standing there. Why? Because of the absence there of the subject person whose name was taken, and because this candidate's name was not stated in the announcement. Therefore, one who wishes to announce with a new name, such as Nāga, having changed the candidate's ordinary name, should first make it known by saying, 'You are Nāga,' and so forth. And also at the moments of instruction and questioning about the obstructing conditions, having declared it in such a way that it is manifest to the candidate and to the Saṅgha, only then should one announce with the name Nāga, and so forth. A single person may have many names; it is proper to take one of them.

Yaṃ [V 2.0125] pana upasampadāpekkhaupajjhāyānaṃ ekattha gahitaṃ nāmaṃ, tadeva ñattiyā, sabbattha anussāvanāsu ca gahetabbaṃ. Gahitato hi aññasmiṃ gahite byañjanaṃ bhinnaṃ nāma hoti, kammaṃ vipajjati. Atthato, hi byañjanato ca abhinnā eva ñatti, anussāvanā ca vaṭṭanti, upajjhāyanāmassa pana purato “āyasmato tissassā”tiādinā āyasmanta-padaṃ sabbattha yojetvāpi anussāveti, tathā ayojitepi doso natthi.

Whatever name of the ordination-candidate and preceptor is taken in one place, that very name should be taken in the motion and in all the announcements. For if a different name from the one taken is used, it is called 'different in wording,' and the act fails. For the motion and announcements are valid only when they are not different in meaning and in wording. However, regarding the preceptor's name, whether one announces by joining the word `āyasmanta` before it everywhere—as in 'of the Venerable Tissa'—or does not join it, there is no fault.

Pāḷiyaṃ pana kiñcāpi “itthannāmassa āyasmato”ti pacchato “āyasmato”ti padaṃ vuttaṃ, tathāpi “āyasmā sāriputto atthakusalo”tiādinā [M 2.0131] nāmassa purato āyasmanta-padayogassa dassanato puratova payogo yuttataro. Tañca ekattha yojetvā aññattha ayojitepi ekattha purato yojetvā aññattha pacchato yojanepi sāvanāya hāpanaṃ nāma na hoti nāmassa ahāpitattā. Teneva pāḷiyampi “itthannāmassa āyasmato”ti ekattha yojetvā “itthannāmena upajjhāyenā”tiādīsu “āyasmato”ti na yojitanti vadanti. Tañca kiñcāpi evaṃ, tathāpi sabbaṭṭhānepi ekeneva pakārena yojetvā eva vā ayojetvā vā anussāvanaṃ pasatthataranti gahetabbaṃ.

However, in the Pāli, although the word `āyasmato` is stated after the name in the phrase `itthannāmassa āyasmato`, nevertheless, because the usage of the word `āyasmanta` before the name is seen in examples like `āyasmā sāriputto atthakusalo`, its usage before the name is more suitable. And even if it is joined in one place and not joined in another, or joined before in one place and after in another, it is not called a diminishing of the announcement, because the name itself has not been diminished. For that very reason, they say that in the Pāli too, it is joined in one place as `itthannāmassa āyasmato`, but `āyasmato` is not joined in other places like `itthannāmena upajjhāyena`. And although they say thus, nevertheless, it should be understood that the announcement is more praiseworthy when it is done in one uniform manner in all instances, either by always joining it or by always not joining it.

Gamikādinissayavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Story concerning Dependence on Travelers and Others is concluded.

Dveupasampadāpekkhādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discussion of Matters Concerning Two Candidates for Higher Ordination, etc.

123. Ekato saheva ekasmiṃ khaṇe anussāvanaṃ etesanti ekānussāvanā, upasampadāpekkhā, ete ekānussāvane kātuṃ. Tenāha “ekānussāvane kātu”nti, idañca ekaṃ padaṃ vibhattialopena daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ekena vāti dvinnampi ekasmiṃ khaṇe ekāya eva kammavācāya anussāvane ekenācariyenāti attho. “Ayaṃ buddharakkhito ca ayaṃ dhammarakkhito ca āyasmato saṅgharakkhitassa upasampadāpekkho”tiādinā nayena ekena ācariyena dvinnaṃ ekasmiṃ khaṇe anussāvananayo daṭṭhabbo. Imināva nayena tiṇṇampi ekena ācariyena ekakkhaṇe anussāvanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

123. Because for them there is an announcement together at the same time in a single moment, they are called `ekānussāvanā` (those of a single announcement); this refers to candidates for higher ordination. `ete ekānussāvane kātuṃ` means to perform the ordination for these with a single announcement. Therefore, he said, 'to perform with a single announcement.' And this should be understood as a single phrase due to the elision of the inflectional ending. As for 'or by one': the meaning is that even for two candidates, the announcement is made by one teacher with just one recitation of the Kammavācā in a single moment. The method of announcement for two candidates by one teacher in a single moment should be understood according to the formula beginning, 'This Buddharakkhita and this Dhammarakkhita are candidates for higher ordination of the venerable Saṅgharakkhita.' By this very method, the announcement for three candidates by one teacher in a single moment should also be understood.

Purimanayeneva ekato anussāvane kātunti “ekena ekassa, aññena itarassā”tiādinā pubbe vuttanayena dvinnaṃ dvīhi vā, tiṇṇaṃ tīhi vā ācariyehi, ekakena vā ācariyena tayopi ekato anussāvane kātunti attho, tañca kho ekena upajjhāyena. “Na tveva nānupajjhāyenā”ti idaṃ ekena ācariyena dvīhi vā tīhi vā upajjhāyehi [V 2.0126] dve vā tayo vā upasampadāpekkhe ekakkhaṇe ekāya anussāvanāya ekānussāvane kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti paṭikkhepapadaṃ. Na pana nānācariyehi nānupajjhāyehi tayo ekānussāvane kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti āha “sace pana nānācariyā nānupajjhāyā…pe… vaṭṭatī”ti. Yañcettha [M 2.0132] “tissatthero sumanattherassa saddhivihārikaṃ, sumanatthero tissattherassa saddhivihārika”nti evaṃ upajjhāyehi aññamaññaṃ saddhivihārikānaṃ anussāvanakaraṇaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ upalakkhaṇamattaṃ. Tasmā sace tissatthero sumanattherassa saddhivihārikaṃ, sumanatthero nandattherassa saddhivihārikaṃ anussāveti, aññamaññañca gaṇapūrakā honti, vaṭṭati eva. Sace pana upajjhāyo sayameva attano saddhivihārikaṃ anussāvetīti ettha vattabbameva natthi, kammaṃ sukatameva hoti. Anupajjhāyakassapi yena kenaci anussāvite upasampadā hoti, kimaṅgaṃ pana saupajjhāyakassa upajjhāyeneva anussāvaneti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Teneva navaṭṭanapakkhaṃ dassetuṃ “sace panā”tiādimāha.

As for 'to perform a single announcement by the previous method': the meaning is that, by the method previously stated beginning 'one for one, another for the other,' for two candidates by two teachers, or for three candidates by three teachers, or even by one teacher for all three, the single announcement is to be performed; and that, with one preceptor. The phrase 'But not with different preceptors' is a term of rejection, stating that it is not allowable for one teacher with two or three preceptors to perform a single announcement for two or three candidates in a single moment with a single recitation. It is not, however, a term of rejection stating that it is not allowable for different teachers with different preceptors to perform a single announcement for three candidates; therefore, he said, 'But if there are different teachers and different preceptors... it is allowable.' And what is stated here, 'The elder Tissa for the co-resident of the elder Sumana, and the elder Sumana for the co-resident of the elder Tissa,' is merely an illustration. Therefore, if the elder Tissa announces for the co-resident of the elder Sumana, and the elder Sumana for the co-resident of the elder Nanda, and they complete the quorum for each other, it is indeed allowable. But if the preceptor himself announces for his own co-resident, there is nothing more to be said; the act is perfectly well done. Even for one without a preceptor, higher ordination occurs when announced by anyone whatsoever; how much more so, it should be understood, for one with a preceptor when the announcement is by the preceptor himself. Therefore, to show the allowable side, he stated the passage beginning, 'But if...'

Dveupasampadāpekkhādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discussion of Matters Concerning Two Candidates for Higher Ordination, etc., is concluded.

Upasampadāvidhikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Procedure for Higher Ordination

126. Upajjhāti upajjhāya-saddasamānattho ākāranto upajjhāsaddoti dasseti. Upajjhāya-saddo eva vā upajjhā upayogapaccattavacanesu ya-kāralopaṃ katvā evaṃ vutto karaṇavacanādīsu upajjhā-saddassa payogābhāvāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ attanāva attānaṃ sammannitabbanti attanāva kattubhūtena karaṇabhūtena attānameva kammabhūtaṃ pati sammananakiccaṃ kātabbaṃ. Attānanti vā paccatte upayogavacanaṃ, attanāva attā sammannitabboti attho. Na kevalañca ettheva, aññatrāpi terasasammutiādīsu imināva lakkhaṇena attanāva attā sammannitabbova. Apica sayaṃ kammārahattā attānaṃ muñcitvā catuvaggādiko gaṇo sabbattha icchitabbo.

126. The term 'upajjhā' shows that there exists the word 'upajjhā' which ends in 'ā' and has the same meaning as the word 'upajjhāya'. Alternatively, it should be understood that the word 'upajjhāya' itself, having elided the letter 'ya' in the accusative and nominative cases, is thus spoken as 'upajjhā', because there is no usage of the word 'upajjhā' in the instrumental case and so on. In the Pāḷi, 'attanāva attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ' means: the act of appointment should be performed by oneself, being the agent and the instrument, upon oneself, being the object. Alternatively, 'attānaṃ' is an accusative word in the sense of the nominative; the meaning is: oneself is to be appointed by oneself. And not only here, but also elsewhere in the thirteen appointments and so on, oneself is indeed to be appointed by oneself by this very characteristic. Moreover, because one is fit for the act, having excluded oneself, a group beginning with four should be desired everywhere.

Saccakāloti “nigūhissāmī”ti vañcanaṃ pahāya saccasseva te icchitabbakālo. Bhūtakāloti vañcanāya abhāvepi manussattādivatthuno bhūtatāya avassaṃ icchitabbakālo, itarathā kammakopādiantarāyo hotīti adhippāyo. Maṅkūti adhomukho. Uddharatūti anupasampannabhāvato upasampattiyaṃ patiṭṭhapetūti attho.

The 'time of truth' is the time when you should desire only truth, having abandoned the deception of thinking, 'I will conceal.' The 'time of reality' is the time when, even in the absence of deception, the fact of being a human, etc., must certainly be desired; otherwise, an obstacle such as the invalidation of the act occurs. This is the intention. 'Maṅkū' means with face cast down. 'Uddharatu' means: may he establish him in higher ordination from the state of not being ordained; this is the meaning.

Sabbakammavācāsu [V 2.0127] atthakosallatthaṃ panettha upasampadākammavācāya evamattho daṭṭhabbo – suṇātūti savanāṇattiyaṃ paṭhamapurisekavacanaṃ. Tañca [M 2.0133] kiñcāpi yo saṅgho savanakiriyāya niyojīyati, tassa sammukhattā “suṇāhī”ti majjhimapurisekavacanena vattabbaṃ, tathāpi yasmā saṅgha-saddasannidhāne paṭhamapurisapayogova saddavidhūhi samāciṇṇo bhagavantaāyasmantādisaddasannidhānesu viya “adhivāsetu me bhavaṃ gotamo (pārā. 22). Etassa sugata kālo, yaṃ bhagavā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapeyya (pārā. 21). Pakkamatāyasmā (pārā. 436). Suṇantu me āyasmanto”tiādīsu viya. Tasmā idha paṭhamapurisapayogo kato. Atha vā gāravavasenevetaṃ vuttaṃ. Garuṭṭhānīyesu hi gāravavasena majjhimapurisapayoguppattiyampi paṭhamapurisapayogaṃ payujjanti “desetu sugato dhamma”ntiādīsu (dī. ni. 2.66; ma. ni. 2.338; saṃ. ni. 1.172; mahāva. 8) viyāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Keci pana “bhante, āvusoti sadde apekkhitvā idha paṭhamapurisapayogo”ti vadanti, taṃ na yuttaṃ “ācariyo me bhante hohi, (mahāva. 77) iṅghāvuso upāli, imaṃ pabbajitaṃ anuyuñjāhī”tiādīsu (pārā. 517) tappayogepi majjhimapurisapayogasseva dassanato.

For skill in the meaning of all formal acts, the meaning of the formal act of higher ordination should be understood here thus: 'suṇātu' is a third-person singular word in the sense of a command to hear. And although it should be said with the second-person singular word 'suṇāhi', since the Saṅgha which is enjoined with the act of hearing is present, nevertheless, because the use of the third person in the context of the word 'saṅgha' is well-practiced by grammarians—as in the context of words like 'bhagavanta', 'āyasmanta', etc., in phrases such as 'May the venerable Gotama consent to me,' 'This is the time, Sugata, for the Bhagavā to lay down a training rule for the disciples,' 'May the venerable one depart,' and 'May the venerable ones hear me'—therefore the third person is used here. Alternatively, this is said out of respect. For in situations deserving respect, they use the third person even when the use of the second person has arisen, as in 'May the Sugata teach the Dhamma,' etc.; it should be understood thus. Some, however, say, 'The third person is used here in connection with the words 'bhante' and 'āvuso',' but that is not correct. Why? Because even when those are used, the use of the second person is seen, as in 'Venerable sir, be my teacher,' and 'Come, friend Upāli, question this one who has gone forth,' etc.

Meti yo sāveti, tassa attaniddese sāmivacanaṃ. Bhanteti ālapanatthe vuḍḍhesu sagāravavacanaṃ. “Āvuso”ti padaṃ pana navakesu. Tadubhayampi nipāto “tumhe bhante, tumhe āvuso”ti bahūsupi samānarūpattā. Saṅghoti avisesato catuvaggādike pakatattapuggalasamūhe vattati. Idha pana paccantimesu janapadesu pañcavaggato paṭṭhāya, majjhimesu janapadesu dasavaggato paṭṭhāya saṅghoti gahetabbo. Tatrāyaṃ piṇḍattho – bhante, saṅgho mama vacanaṃ suṇātūti. Idañca navakatarena vattabbavacanaṃ. Sace pana anussāvako sabbehi bhikkhūhi vuḍḍhataro hoti, “suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho”ti vattabbaṃ. Sopi ce “bhante”ti vadeyya, navakataro vā “āvuso”ti, kammakopo natthi. Keci pana “ekattha ‘āvuso’ti vatvā aññattha ‘bhante’ti vuttepi natthi doso ubhayenāpi ālapanassa sijjhanato”ti vadanti.

‘Me’ is the genitive case in the self-reference of the one who makes the announcement. ‘Bhante’ is a respectful word for elders in the sense of addressing. The word ‘āvuso’, however, is for juniors. Both of these are particles because they have the same form even in the plural, as in ‘tumhe bhante, tumhe āvuso’. ‘Saṅgho’ generally applies to a group of individuals of normal virtue, beginning with a group of four. Here, however, in the border regions, it should be taken as ‘Saṅgha’ starting from a group of five, and in the middle regions, starting from a group of ten. Therein, this is the summary meaning: ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my word.’ And this is a statement to be said by a more junior monk. However, if the announcer is more senior than all the monks, it should be said, ‘Āvuso, may the Saṅgha hear me.’ If he were to say ‘bhante’, or a more junior monk were to say ‘āvuso’, there is no invalidation of the act. Some, however, say: ‘There is no fault even if ‘āvuso’ is said in one place and ‘bhante’ in another, because the addressing is accomplished by both.’

Idāni yamatthaṃ ñāpetukāmo “suṇātū”ti saṅghaṃ savane niyojeti, taṃ ñāpento “ayaṃ itthannāmo”tiādimāha. Tattha ayanti [M 2.0134] upasampadāpekkhassa hatthapāse sannihitabhāvadassanaṃ. Tena ca hatthapāse ṭhitasseva upasampadā ruhatīti sijjhati hatthapāsato bahi ṭhitassa “aya”nti na vattabbato. Teneva anusāsakasammutiyaṃ so hatthapāsato bahi ṭhitattā “aya”nti na vutto. Tasmā upasampadāpekkho anupasampanno hatthapāse ṭhapetabbo. Ayaṃ itthannāmoti ayaṃ-saddo ca avassaṃ payujjitabbo. So ca imasmiṃ paṭhamanāmapayoge evāti gahetabbaṃ[V 2.0128]. “Itthannāmo”ti idaṃ aniyamato tassa nāmadassanaṃ. Ubhayenapi ayaṃ buddharakkhitotiādināmaṃ dasseti. “Upasampadāpekkho”ti bhinnādhikaraṇavisaye bahubbīhisamaāso, upasampadaṃ me saṅgho apekkhamānoti attho. Tassa ca upajjhāyataṃ samaṅgibhāvena dassetuṃ “itthannamassa āyasmato”ti vuttaṃ. Etena “ayaṃ buddharakkhito āyasmato dhammarakkhitassa saddhivihārikabhūto upasampadāpekkho”ti evamādinā nayena nāmayojanāya saha attho dassitoti. Ettha ca “āyasmato”ti padaṃ avatvāpi “ayaṃ buddharakkhito dhammarakkhitassa upasampadāpekkho”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Teneva pāḷiyaṃ “itthannāmena upajjhāyenā”ti ettha “āyasmato”ti padaṃ na vuttaṃ. Yañcettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva.

Now, wishing to make known the purpose, he directs the Saṅgha to listen by saying, “May it hear.” Making that purpose known, he says, “This so-and-so,” and so on. Herein, ‘this’ indicates that the candidate for higher ordination is present within arm’s reach. And by this, it is established that ordination is successful only for one standing within arm’s reach, because ‘this’ is not to be said of one standing outside of arm’s reach. For that very reason, in the appointment of an instructor, he is not called ‘this’ because he stands outside of arm’s reach. Therefore, the unordained candidate for higher ordination must be placed within arm’s reach. And the word ‘this’ must certainly be used in the phrase “This so-and-so.” And it should be understood that it is to be used only in this first usage of the name. ‘So-and-so’ is an unrestricted indication of his name. By both together, it indicates a name such as, “This Buddharakkhita.” The term ‘candidate for higher ordination’ is a bahubbīhi compound in the sense of a different case relation, with the meaning, “one whose ordination the Saṅgha is considering.” And to show that he is endowed with a preceptor, it is said, “of the venerable so-and-so.” By this, the meaning is shown, together with the application of the name, according to the method, “This Buddharakkhita, being the co-resident of the venerable Dhammarakkhita, is a candidate for ordination,” and so on. And here, even without saying the word ‘venerable,’ it is permissible to say, “This Buddharakkhita is the candidate for ordination of Dhammarakkhita.” For that very reason, in the Pāḷi, in the phrase “by the preceptor so-and-so,” the word ‘venerable’ is not stated. And whatever should be said here has already been stated below.

Nanu cettha upajjhāyopi upasampadāpekkho viya hatthapāse ṭhito eva icchitabbo, atha kasmā “ayaṃ itthannāmo imassa itthannāmassa upasampadāpekkho”ti evaṃ upajjhāyaparāmasanepi ima-saddassa payogo na katoti? Nāyaṃ virodho upajjhāyassa abhāvepi kammakopābhāvato. Kevalañhi kammanipphattiyā santapadavasena avijjamānassapi upajjhāyassa nāmakittanaṃ anupajjhāyassa upasampadādīsupi karīyati. Tasmā upajjhāyassa asannihitatāyapi tapparāmasanamatteneva kammasiddhito “imassā”ti niddisituṃ na vaṭṭati.

Is it not desirable that here the preceptor, like the candidate for ordination, should also be standing within arm’s reach? If so, why then, even when referring to the preceptor, is the word ‘this’ (ima) not used, as in, “This so-and-so is the candidate for ordination of this so-and-so”? This is not a contradiction, because the formal act is not vitiated even in the absence of the preceptor. Indeed, merely for the accomplishment of the formal act, by means of an existing term, the name of even an absent preceptor is mentioned, even in the ordination and so on of one who is without a preceptor. Therefore, even when the preceptor is not present, since the formal act is accomplished merely by referring to him, it is not proper to specify ‘of this one’.

Parisuddho antarāyikehi dhammehīti abhabbatādikehi upasampadāya avatthukarehi ceva pañcābādhahatthacchinnādīhi ca āpattimattakarehi antarāyikehi sabhāvehi parimutto. Evaṃ vutto eva ca āpattimattakarehi pañcābādhādīhi aparimuttassapi upasampadā ruhati, nāññathā. Paripuṇṇassa pattacīvaranti paripuṇṇamassa upasampadāpekkhassa pattacīvaraṃ. Evaṃ vutte eva apattacīvarassāpi upasampadā ruhati, nāññathā. Upasampadaṃ yācatīti [M 2.0135] “saṅghaṃ, bhante, upasampadaṃ yācāmī”tiādinā (mahāva. 71, 126) yācitabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Evaṃ tena saṅghe ayācitepi “itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācatī”ti vutte eva kammaṃ avipannaṃ hoti, nāññathā. Upajjhāyenāti upajjhāyena karaṇabhūtena itthannāmaṃ upajjhāyaṃ katvā kammabhūtaṃ upasampadaṃ dātuṃ nipphādetuṃ kattubhūtaṃ saṅghaṃ yācatīti attho. Yācadhātuno pana dvikammakattā “saṅghaṃ, upasampada”nti dve kammapadāni vuttāni.

‘Purified from obstructive factors’ means he is free from obstructive conditions that render the ordination baseless, such as unsuitability and so on, and also from obstructive conditions that merely constitute an offense, such as the five diseases, having a severed hand, and so forth. And only when it is stated thus is the higher ordination successful even for one not free from the five diseases and other factors that merely constitute an offense; not otherwise. ‘His bowl and robes are complete’ means this candidate for higher ordination’s bowl and robes are complete. Only when it is stated thus is the higher ordination successful even for one without a bowl and robes; not otherwise. ‘He requests higher ordination’ is said with reference to the fact of his having requested, as in the phrase, “Venerable sirs, I request the Saṅgha for higher ordination,” and so on. Thus, even if he has not requested the Saṅgha, only when it is said, “So-and-so requests the Saṅgha for higher ordination,” is the formal act not vitiated; not otherwise. ‘By a preceptor’ means: he requests the Saṅgha (the agent) to grant and accomplish the ordination (the object) by means of the preceptor (the instrument), having made so-and-so his preceptor. And because the root yāc (to request) takes two objects, the two object-words ‘the Saṅgha’ and ‘ordination’ are stated.

Yadi saṅghassa pattakallanti ettha patto kālo imassāti pattakālaṃ, apalokanādicatubbidhasaṅghakammaṃ, tadeva sakatthe ya-paccayena “pattakalla”nti vuccati. Idha pana ñatticatutthaupasampadākammaṃ adhippetaṃ, taṃ kātuṃ saṅghassa pattakallaṃ jātaṃ. Yadīti anumatigahaṇavasena kammassa [V 2.0129] pattakallataṃ ñāpeti. Yo hi koci tattha apattakallataṃ maññissati, so vakkhati. Imameva hi atthaṃ sandhāya anussāvanāsu “yassāyasmato khamati…pe… so bhāseyyā”ti (mahāva. 127) vuttaṃ. Taṃ panetaṃ pattakallaṃ vatthusampadā, antarāyikehi dhammehi cassa parisuddhatā, sīmāsampadā, parisasampadā, pubbakiccaniṭṭhāpananti imehi pañcahi aṅgehi saṅgahitaṃ.

Regarding ‘If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha’: here, pattakāla means ‘the time has arrived for this,’ referring to the four kinds of formal acts of the Saṅgha beginning with proclamation. That very term, by means of the suffix ‘-ya’ in its own sense, is called pattakalla. Here, however, the ordination act that is fourth with the motion is intended; it has become the proper time for the Saṅgha to perform it. The word ‘if’ indicates the suitability of the formal act by way of obtaining consent. For should anyone there consider it unsuitable, he will speak. Indeed, with this very meaning in mind, it is said in the announcements: “To whichever venerable one it is agreeable, he should remain silent; to whomever it is not, he should speak.” This suitability, moreover, is comprised of these five factors: perfection of the subject, his purity from obstructive factors, perfection of the boundary, perfection of the assembly, and completion of the preliminary duties.

Tattha vatthusampadā nāma yathāvuttehi ekādasahi abhabbapuggalehi ceva antimavatthuajjhāpannehi ca añño paripuṇṇavīsativasso anupasampannabhūto manussapuriso, etasmiṃ puggale sati eva idaṃ saṅghassa upasampadākammaṃ pattakallaṃ nāma hoti, nāsati. Katañca kuppameva hoti.

Herein, perfection of the subject means a human male, fully twenty years old and not yet ordained, who is other than the eleven types of unsuitable individuals already mentioned and those who have incurred a terminal offense. Only when such a person is present is this act of the Saṅgha's higher ordination called 'pattakalla'; if such a person is not present, it is not. And if it is performed, it is indeed invalid.

Antarāyikehi dhammehi cassa parisuddhatā nāma yathāvuttasseva upasampadāvatthubhūtassa puggalassa ye ime bhagavatā paṭikkhittā pañcābādhaphuṭṭhatādayo mātāpitūhi ananuññātatāpariyosānā ceva hatthacchinnatādayo ca dosadhammā kārakasaṅghassa āpattādiantarāyahetutāya “antarāyikā”ti vuccanti tehi antarāyikehi dosadhammehi parimuttattā, imissā ca sati eva idaṃ kammaṃ pattakallaṃ nāma hoti, nāsati. Kataṃ pana kammaṃ sukatameva hoti ṭhapetvā ūnavīsativassapuggalaṃ.

His purity from obstructive factors means freedom for the person who is the subject of the higher ordination as described. This is freedom from those faulty qualities rejected by the Blessed One—such as being afflicted with the five diseases and so on, ending with not having parental consent, and having a severed hand and so on—which are called ‘obstructive’ because they are a cause of offenses and other obstructions for the Saṅgha performing the formal act. And only when this freedom from such obstructive, faulty qualities is present is this formal act called 'pattakalla'; if it is not present, it is not. The formal act, however, if performed, is indeed valid, with the exception of the case of a person under twenty years of age.

Sīmāsampadā [M 2.0136] pana uposathakkhandhake (mahāva. 147-148) vakkhamānanayena sabbadosavirahitāya baddhābaddhavasena duvidhāya sīmāya vaseneva veditabbā. Tādisāya hi sīmāya sati eva idaṃ kammaṃ pattakallaṃ nāma hoti, nāsati. Katañca kammaṃ vipajjati.

The perfection of the boundary, however, should be understood, according to the method to be explained in the Uposathakkhandhaka, only by way of a boundary of two kinds—a bound and an unbound boundary—that is free from all faults. For indeed, only when such a boundary exists is this act called 'pattakalla'; if it does not exist, it is not. And an act that has been performed is invalid.

Parisasampadā pana ye ime upasampadākammassa sabbantimena paricchedena kammappattā dasahi vā pañcahi vā anūnā pārājikaṃ anāpannā, anukkhittā ca samānasaṃvāsakā bhikkhū, tesaṃ ekasīmāyaṃ hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā ṭhānaṃ, chandārahānañca chandassa ānayanaṃ, sammukhībhūtānañca appaṭikkosanaṃ, upasampadāpekkharahitānaṃ uposathakkhandhake paṭikkhittānaṃ gahaṭṭhādianaupasampannānañceva pārājikukkhittakanānāsaṃvāsakabhikkhunīnañca vajjanīyapuggalānaṃ saṅghassa hatthapāse abhāvo cāti imehi catūhi aṅgehi saṅgahitā. Evarūpāya ca parisasampadāya sati eva idaṃ pattakallaṃ nāma hoti, nāsati. Tattha purimānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ aṅgānaṃ aññatarassapi abhāve kataṃ kammaṃ vipajjati, na pacchimassa.

The perfection of the assembly, however, is comprised of these four factors: (1) the standing, within a single boundary and without abandoning the hand-reach, of those bhikkhus who are suitable for the formal act by the lowest limit of not being fewer than ten or five, who have not fallen into a pārājika offense, who are not suspended, and who are of the same communion; (2) the bringing of the consent of those worthy of giving consent; (3) the non-protest of those who are present; and (4) the absence within the Saṅgha's hand-reach of persons to be avoided—who are apart from the candidate for higher ordination, who are rejected in the Uposathakkhandhaka, such as householders and other unordained persons, and bhikkhunīs who have committed a pārājika, are suspended, or are of a different communion. And only when such a perfection of the assembly exists is this act called 'pattakalla'; if it does not exist, it is not. Among these, if any of the first three factors is absent, the act performed is invalid, but not if the last is.

Pubbakiccaniṭṭhāpanaṃ [V 2.0130] nāma yānimāni “paṭhamaṃ upajjhaṃ gāhāpetabbo”tiādinā pāḷiyaṃ vuttāni “upajjhaṃ gāhāpanaṃ, pattacīvarācikkhanaṃ, tato taṃ hatthapāsato bahi ṭhapetvā anusāsakasammutikammakaraṇaṃ, sammatena ca gantvā anusāsanaṃ, tena ca paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā saṅghassa ñāpetvā upasampadāpekkhaṃ ‘āgacchāhī’ti hatthapāse eva abbhānaṃ, tena ca bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vandāpetvā upasampadāyācāpanaṃ, tato antarāyikadhammapucchakasammutikaraṇaṃ, sammatena ca pucchana”nti imāni aṭṭha pubbakiccāni, tesaṃ sabbesaṃ yāthāvato karaṇena niṭṭhāpanaṃ. Etasmiñca pubbakammaniṭṭhāpane sati eva idaṃ saṅghassa upasampadākammaṃ pattakallaṃ nāma hoti, nāsati. Etesu pana pubbakammesu akatesupi kataṃ kammaṃ yathāvuttavatthusampattiādīsu vijjamānesu akuppameva hoti. Tadevamettha pattakallaṃ imehi pañcahi aṅgehi saṅgahitanti veditabbaṃ. Imināva nayena heṭṭhā vuttesu, vakkhamānesu ca sabbesu kammesu pattakallatā yathārahaṃ yojetvā ñātabbā.

The completion of preliminary duties means the completion of all these eight preliminary duties mentioned in the Pāli—beginning with 'First, a preceptor should be caused to be taken'—by performing them properly. These are: (1) causing a preceptor to be taken; (2) announcing the bowl and robes; (3) then, having placed the candidate outside the hand-reach, performing the formal act to appoint an instructor; (4) the appointed one going and giving the instruction; (5) that appointed one, having returned first and informed the Saṅgha, summoning the candidate for higher ordination into the very hand-reach, saying, 'Come!'; (6) causing that candidate to venerate the feet of the bhikkhus and to request the higher ordination; (7) then, performing the formal act to appoint one to ask about the obstructing conditions; and (8) the appointed one asking. And only when this completion of the preliminary duties exists is this act of higher ordination of the Saṅgha called 'pattakalla'; if it does not exist, it is not. However, even if these preliminary duties are not performed, the act that is performed is indeed inviolable, provided the aforesaid perfection of the subject and other factors are present. Thus, it should be understood that 'pattakalla' here is comprised of these five factors. By this very method, the state of being 'pattakalla' should be known in all formal acts, those previously mentioned and those yet to be mentioned, by applying it as is appropriate.

Itthannāmaṃ [M 2.0137] upasampādeyyāti upasampadānipphādanena taṃsamaṅgiṃ kareyya karotūti patthanāyaṃ, vidhimhi vā idaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yathā hi “devadattaṃ sukhāpeyyā”ti vutte sukhamassa nipphādetvā taṃ sukhasamaṅginaṃ kareyyāti attho hoti, evamidhāpi upasampadamassa nipphādetvā taṃ upasampadāsamaṅginaṃ kareyyāti attho. Payojakabyāpāre cetaṃ yathā sukhayantaṃ kañci suddhakattāraṃ koci hetukattā sukhahetunipphādanena sukhāpeyyāti vuccati, evamidhāpi upasampajjantaṃ suddhakattāraṃ puggalaṃ hetukattubhūto saṅgho upasampadāhetunipphādanena upasampādeyyāti vutto. Etena ca sukhaṃ viya sukhadāyakena saṅghena puggalassa diyyamānā tathāpavattaparamatthadhamme upādāya ariyajanapaññattā upasampadā nāma sammutisaccatā atthīti samatthitaṃ hoti. Ettha ca “itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācatī”ti vuttattā parivāsādīsu viya yācanānuguṇaṃ “itthannāmassa upasampadaṃ dadeyyā”ti avatvā “itthannāmaṃ upasampādeyyā”ti vuttattā idaṃ upasampadākammaṃ dāne asaṅgahetvā kammalakkhaṇe eva saṅgahitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Iminā nayena “itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti, upasampanno saṅghenā”ti etthāpi attho veditabbo. Kevalañhi tattha vattamānakālaatītakālavasena, idha pana anāmaṭṭhakālavasenāti ettakameva viseso.

'May one ordain so-and-so' (`Itthannāmaṃ upasampādeyyā`ti) means: by accomplishing the higher ordination, one should make him endowed with it. This should be understood either as a wish ('may he do so') or as an injunction. For just as when it is said, 'May one make Devadatta happy,' the meaning is that by bringing about his happiness, one should make him endowed with happiness, so too here the meaning is that by bringing about his higher ordination, one should make him endowed with higher ordination. And this refers to the action of a causative agent. Just as a causative agent is said to 'make happy' some direct agent who is becoming happy by bringing about the cause of happiness, so too here the Saṅgha, being the causative agent, is said to 'ordain' a person, the direct agent who is undergoing ordination, by bringing about the cause of higher ordination. And by this it is established that, just as there is happiness that is given by a giver of happiness, so too there exists as a conventional truth, designated by the noble ones by depending on ultimate realities that have so occurred, something called 'higher ordination' that is given by the Saṅgha to a person. And here, because it is said, 'So-and-so requests the Saṅgha for higher ordination,' and yet, unlike in the cases of probation and so forth, it is not said in accordance with the request, 'May one give the higher ordination to so-and-so,' but rather 'May one ordain so-and-so,' this act of higher ordination should be understood as being included not under 'giving' but only under the characteristic of a formal act. By this method, the meaning should also be understood in the phrases, 'One ordains so-and-so' and 'He has been ordained by the Saṅgha.' The only difference is that there, it is by way of the present and past tenses, whereas here, it is by way of an unspecified tense.

Esā ñattīti “saṅgho ñāpetabbo”ti vuttañāpanā esā. Idañca anussāvanānampi sabbhāvasūcanatthaṃ vuccati. Avassañcetaṃ vattabbameva, ñattikamme eva taṃ na vattabbaṃ. Tattha pana yya-kāre vuttamatte eva ñattikammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Khamatīti ruccati. Upasampadāti saṅghena diyyamānā nipphādiyamānā upasampadā yassa khamati. So tuṇhassāti yojanā. Tuṇhīti [V 2.0131] ca akathanatthe nipāto, akathanako assa bhaveyyāti attho. Khamati saṅghassa itthannāmassa upasampadāti pakatena sambandho. Tattha kāraṇamāha “tasmā tuṇhī”ti. Tattha “āsī”ti seso. Yasmā “yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyyā”ti tikkhattuṃ vuccamānopi saṅgho tuṇhī niravo ahosi, tasmā khamati saṅghassāti attho. Evanti iminā pakārena. Tuṇhībhāvenevetaṃ saṅghassa ruccanabhāvaṃ dhārayāmi bujjhāmi pajānāmīti attho. Iti-saddo parisamāpanatthe kato, so ca kammavācāya anaṅgaṃ. Tasmā anussāvakena “dhārayāmī”ti ettha mi-kārapariyosānameva [M 2.0138] vatvā niṭṭhāpetabbaṃ, iti-saddo na payujjitabboti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Iminā nayena sabbattha kammavācānamattho veditabbo.

Regarding `Esā ñatti`: this is the stated information, ‘The Saṅgha should be informed.’ And this is stated to indicate the true nature of the announcements (kammavācā). And this must certainly be stated; it should not, however, be stated in an act consisting only of a motion (ñattikamma). In that case, it should be understood that the act consisting only of a motion is completed merely by the utterance of the syllable ‘yya’. `Khamati` means it is agreeable. `Upasampadā` means the higher ordination, being given and accomplished by the Saṅgha. ‘To whom it is agreeable, he should be silent’—this is the syntactical connection. And `tuṇhī` is a particle in the sense of not speaking; the meaning is ‘he should be one who does not speak.’ ‘The higher ordination of one with such-and-such a name is agreeable to the Saṅgha’—this is the connection with the preceding text. Therein, he states the reason: ‘Therefore, he was silent.’ Here, `āsī` (was) is the remainder. Because, although it was said three times, ‘To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak,’ the Saṅgha was silent and without a sound, therefore it is agreeable to the Saṅgha—this is the meaning. `Evam` means in this manner. By the very state of being silent, I hold, understand, and know this state of the Saṅgha's agreement—this is the meaning. The word `iti` is used in the sense of conclusion, and it is not a component of the formal act (kammavācā). Therefore, the announcer, at the word `dhārayāmi`, should conclude by reciting only up to the end with the syllable `mi`; the word `iti` should not be used—this should be understood. In this way, the meaning of the formal acts should be understood everywhere.

Upasampadāvidhikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourse on the procedure for higher ordination is completed.

Cattāronissayādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Four Supports and Related Topics

128. Ekaporisā vātiādi sattānaṃ sarīracchāyaṃ pādehi minitvā jānanappakāradassanaṃ. Chasattapadaparamatā hi chāyā “porisā”ti vuccati. Idañca utuppamāṇācikkhanādi ca āgantukehi saddhiṃ vīmaṃsitvā vuḍḍhanavabhāvaṃ ñatvā vandanavandāpanādikaraṇatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Eti āgacchati, gacchati cāti utu, sova pamiyate anena saṃvaccharanti pamāṇanti āha “utuyeva utuppamāṇa”nti. Aparipuṇṇāti upasampadādivasena aparipuṇṇā. Yadi utuvemajjhe upasampādito, tadā tasmiṃ utumhi avasiṭṭhadivasācikkhanaṃ “divasabhāgācikkhana”nti dasseti. Tenāha “yattakehi divasehi yassa yo utu aparipuṇṇo, te divase”ti. Tattha yassa taṃ khaṇaṃ laddhūpasampadassa puggalassa sambandhī yo utu yattakehi divasehi aparipuṇṇo, te divaseti yojanā.

128. The phrase beginning with `Ekaporisā vā` shows the method of knowing by measuring the body-shadow of beings with the feet. Indeed, a shadow with a maximum length of six or seven foot-lengths is called a `porisā`. And this, as well as the announcing of the measure of the season and so on, is stated for the purpose of performing salutation, causing to be saluted, etc., after having investigated with the newcomers and known their state of being senior or junior. It comes (eti) and it goes (gacchati), thus it is a season (utu); by this the year is measured (pamiyate), thus it is a measure (pamāṇa); therefore, he said, ‘the season itself is the measure of the season.’ `Aparipuṇṇā` means incomplete by way of the day of higher ordination. If one was ordained in the middle of a season, then the announcing of the remaining days in that season is shown as ‘the announcing of the portion of the days.’ Therefore, he said, ‘by however many days a certain season of someone is incomplete, those days.’ Therein, the syntactical connection is: those days by which a certain season related to the person who received higher ordination at that moment is incomplete.

Chāyādikameva sabbaṃ saṅgahetvā gāyitabbato kathetabbato saṅgītīti āha “idamevā”tiādi. Tattha ekato katvā ācikkhitabbaṃ. Tvaṃ kiṃ labhasīti tvaṃ upasampādanakāle kataravassaṃ, katarautuñca labhasi, katarasmiṃ te upasampadā laddhāti attho. Vassanti vassānautu. Idañca saṃvaccharācikkhanaṃ vinā vuttampi na ñāyatīti iminā utuācikkhaneneva sāsanavassesu vā kaliyugavassādīsu vā sahassime vā satime vā asukaṃ utuṃ labhāmīti dassitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Chāyā”ti idaṃ pāḷiyaṃ āgatapaṭipāṭiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vattabbakamato pana kaliyugavassādīsu sabbadesapasiddhesu asukavasse asukautumhi asukamāse [V 2.0132] asuke kaṇhe vā sukke vā pakkhe asukatithivāravisesayutte nakkhatte pubbaṇhādidivasabhāge ettake chāyāpamāṇe, nāḍikāpamāṇe vā mayā upasampadā laddhāti vadeyyāsīti evaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. “Idaṃ suṭṭhu uggahetvā āgantukehi [M 2.0139] vuḍḍhapaṭipāṭiṃ ñatvā paṭipajjāhī”ti vattabbaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ kissa tvanti kiṃ tvaṃ ettakaṃ kālaṃ akāsīti attho.

Because everything, such as the shadow, is to be recited and spoken after collecting it together, it is called a `saṅgīti` (recital); therefore, he said the phrase beginning with `idamevā`. Therein, it should be announced together. `Tvaṃ kiṃ labhasi` means: At the time of your higher ordination, what year and what season do you obtain? In which was the higher ordination obtained by you? This is the meaning. `Vassaṃ` means the rainy season. And this, even if stated, is not understood without the announcing of the year. Therefore, it should be understood that by this very announcing of the season, it is shown thus: ‘In the years of the Dispensation, or in the years of the Kaliyuga era and so on, in the thousandth or in the hundredth, I obtain such-and-such a season.’ The word `chāyā` is stated with reference to the sequence that has come down in the Pāḷi. But from the point of view of what should be said, it should be announced thus: You should say, ‘In the years of the Kaliyuga era and so on, which are well-known in all regions, in such-and-such a year, in such-and-such a season, in such-and-such a month, in such-and-such a fortnight, whether dark or bright, on a day endowed with the distinction of such-and-such a lunar date and day of the week, under such-and-such a constellation, in a part of the day such as the forenoon, at such-and-such a measure of the shadow or measure of the water-clock, the higher ordination was obtained by me.’ It should be said: ‘Having learned this well, and having known the order of seniority with the newcomers, you should practice accordingly.’ In the Pāḷi, `kissa tvaṃ` means ‘What were you doing for so long?’—this is the meaning.

130. Upasampadaṃ yācīti pabbajjañca upasampadañca yācīti attho. Passissāmīti ettha vadatīti seso, evaṃ uparipi. “Osāretabbo”ti iminā purimo ukkhittabhāvo vibbhamitvā puna laddhūpasampadampi na muñcati. Tena ca sambhuñjanādīsupi bhikkhūnaṃ pācittiyamevāti dasseti. Anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāseti ettha sahaseyyāpi saṅgahitāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ettha cāyamadhippāyo – yasmā ayaṃ osāritattā pakatatto, tasmā ukkhittasambhogādipaccayena pācittiyenettha anāpattīti. Yo pana āpattiṭṭhāne anāpattidiṭṭhitāya āpattiṃ na passati, teneva paṭikammampi na karoti, so yasmā ettāvatā alajjī nāma na hoti. Paṇṇattiṃ ñatvā vītikkamaṃ karonto eva hi alajjī nāma hoti. “Sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjatī”tiādi (pari. 359) hi vuttaṃ. Tasmā ettha alajjisambhogādipaccayā dukkaṭāpattiniyamo natthi. Tena sāpettha āpatti na vuttāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo panettha imaṃ adhippāyaṃ asallakkhentena kenaci “anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāse”ti iminā pācittiyena anāpatti vuttā, alajjisambhogapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ pana āpajjati evāti āpattiniyamo vutto, so alajjitte sati eva vutto, nāsatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

130. ‘He requested higher ordination’ means: he requested both the going forth (pabbajjā) and the higher ordination (upasampadā). This is the meaning. At the word `passissāmi` (I will see), ‘he says’ is the remainder; likewise above. By this word `osāretabbo` (he should be reinstated), the former state of being suspended, even if he disrobes and again receives higher ordination, does not leave him. And by that, it shows that for the bhikkhus, even in communal eating and so on, there is only a pācittiya offense. At the phrase `anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāse` (no offense in communion and co-residence), it should be understood that co-sleeping is also included. And herein, this is the intention: because this one, having been reinstated, is of normal status, therefore, there is no offense here of pācittiya on account of communion, etc., with one who is suspended. But a bhikkhu who, in a matter of an offense, does not see an offense due to holding the view that there is no offense, and for that very reason does not make amends, is not, on that account alone, called ‘shameless’ (alajjī). Indeed, only one who commits a transgression knowing the regulation is called ‘shameless.’ Indeed, it is said: ‘He intentionally commits an offense,’ and so on. Therefore, here there is no fixed rule of a dukkaṭa offense on account of communion, etc., with a shameless one. For that reason, that offense is not mentioned here, it should be understood. As for the fixed rule of an offense stated by someone here who did not discern this intention—that by `anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāse` no-offense is stated for the pācittiya, but one does indeed incur a dukkaṭa on account of communion with a shameless one—that rule was stated only when shamelessness is present, not when it is absent. This should be understood.

131. Vinayamhītiādigāthāsu niggahānanti niggahakaraṇesu. Pāpiccheti pāpapuggalānaṃ niggahakaraṇesu, lajjīnaṃ paggahesu ca pesalānaṃ sukhāvahe mahante vinayamhi yathā atthakārī atthānuguṇaṃ karontova yasmā yoniso paṭipajjati nāma hoti, tasmā uddānaṃ pavakkhāmīti sambandhayojanā daṭṭhabbā. Sesaṃ sabbattha suviññeyyameva.

131. In the verses beginning with 'Vinayamhi,' `niggahānaṃ` means in acts of restraint. `Pāpicche` means in acts of restraining wicked individuals, and in acts of supporting the modest, and in the great Vinaya which brings happiness to the virtuous. Because a monk who acts in accordance with the meaning is indeed said to practice properly, therefore, 'I will declare the summary'—thus the connection and construction should be understood. The remainder is everywhere easy to understand.

Cattāronissayādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourse on the four requisites and so forth is concluded.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya vimativinodaniyaṃ

In the Vimativinodanī, the sub-commentary to the Samantapāsādikā, the commentary on the Vinaya.

Mahākhandhakavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The method of exposition of the Mahākhandhaka is concluded.

2. Uposathakkhandhako

2. The Chapter on the Uposatha

Sannipātānujānanādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Permission for Assemblies and So Forth

132. Uposathakkhandhake [M 2.0140][V 2.0133] taranti otaranti etthāti titthaṃ, laddhi. Itoti sāsanaladdhito.

132. In the Uposathakkhandhaka: Because they cross over (taranti) or descend (otaranti) here (ettha), it is thus (iti) a `tittha` (a ford, a sectarian view); a doctrine (laddhi). `Ito` means: from the doctrine of the Dispensation.

135. Āpajjitvā vā vuṭṭhitoti ettha desanārocanānampi saṅgaho. Teneva mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ “vuṭṭhitā vā desitā vā ārocitā vā āpatti…pe… asantī nāma hotī”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) vuttaṃ.

135. Here, in 'having committed an offense or having recovered from it,' the confession and announcement are also included. For that very reason, in the Mātikā-aṭṭhakathā, it is said: 'An offense that one has recovered from, or has confessed, or has announced... is said to be non-existent.'

Manujenāti āsannena saha. Pareti dūraṭṭhepi parapuggale sandhāya giraṃ no ca bhaṇeyyāti yojanā.

`Manujena` means: together with a person who is near. `Pare` means: referring to other persons, even those at a distance, one should not speak a word. This is the construction.

“Āvikatā hissa phāsu hotī”ti (mahāva. 134) vuttattā garukāpattipi āvikaraṇamattena vuṭṭhātīti keci vadanti, taṃ tesaṃ matimattaṃ parivāsādividhānasuttehi virujjhanato. Ayaṃ panettha adhippāyo – yathābhūtañhi attānamāvikarontaṃ pesalā bhikkhū “akāmā parivatthabba”ntiādivacanaṃ nissāya anicchamānampi naṃ upāyena parivāsādīni datvā avassaṃ suddhante patiṭṭhāpessanti, tato tassa avippaṭisārādīnaṃ vasena phāsu hoti. Paṭhamaṃ pātimokkhuddesanti nidānuddesaṃ dasseti. Pubbe avijjamānaṃ paññāpesīti. Na kevalañca etaṃ, pubbe paññattampi pana pārājikādisikkhāpadaṃ sabbaṃ bhagavā “tatrime cattāro pārājikā dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchantī”tiādinā pārājikuddesādivasena vinayamātikaṃ katvā nidānuddesena saha sayameva saṅgahetvā “pātimokkha”nti paññāpesīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tadetaṃ sabbampi sandhāya “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pātimokkhaṃ uddisitu”nti (mahāva. 133) vuttaṃ.

Because it was said, 'For him, openness is ease,' some say that even a grave offense is absolved by the mere act of making it known. That is merely their own opinion, because it contradicts the suttas that lay down probation and so on. This, herein, is the intended meaning: virtuous monks, relying on the statement 'he should be put on probation against his will,' and so on, will, by some means, have a monk who reveals himself as he truly is—even if he is unwilling—undertake probation and so on, and will certainly establish him in a state of purity. Then, for him, through the absence of remorse and so on, there is ease. 'The first recitation of the Pātimokkha' indicates the recitation of the introduction. He promulgated what did not exist before. And not only this, but it should be understood that the Blessed One himself, having formulated the Vinaya matrix by way of the recitation of the Pārājikas and so on, beginning with 'These four Pārājika rules come up for recitation,' summarized all the previously laid down training rules beginning with the Pārājikas, together with the recitation of the introduction, and promulgated it as the 'Pātimokkha'. Referring to all of this, it was said: 'I allow, O monks, the recitation of the Pātimokkha.'

136. Etaṃ 34 veditabbanti yasmiṃ tasmiṃ cātuddase vā pannarase vāti evaṃ atthajātaṃ.

136. `Etaṃ veditabbaṃ` (this should be known) refers to this collection of meanings: 'on whatever fourteenth or fifteenth day.'

Sannipātānujānanādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourse on the permission for assembly is concluded.

Sīmānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Permission for Boundaries

138. “Puratthimāya [M 2.0141] disāyā”ti idaṃ nidassanamattaṃ. Tassaṃ pana disāyaṃ nimitte asati yattha atthi, tato paṭṭhāya paṭhamaṃ “puratthimāya anudisāya, dakkhiṇāya disāyā”tiādinā samantā vijjamānaṭṭhānesu nimittāni kittetvā puna “puratthimāya anudisāyā”ti paṭhamakittitaṃ kittetuṃ vaṭṭati, tīhi nimittehi siṅghāṭakasaṇṭhānāyapi sīmāya sammannitabbato. Tikkhattuṃ sīmāmaṇḍalaṃ sambandhantenāti vinayadharena sayaṃ ekasmiṃyeva ṭhāne ṭhatvā kevalaṃ nimittakittanavacaneneva sīmāmaṇḍalaṃ samantā nimittena nimittaṃ bandhantenāti attho. Taṃ taṃ nimittaṭṭhānaṃ agantvāpi hi kittetuṃ vaṭṭati. Tiyojanaparamāya sīmāya samantato tikkhattuṃ anuparigamanassa ekadivasena dukkarattā vinayadharena sayaṃ adiṭṭhampi pubbe bhikkhūhi yathāvavatthitaṃ nimittaṃ “pāsāṇo bhante”tiādinā kenaci vuttānusārena sallakkhetvā “eso pāsāṇo nimitta”ntiādinā kittetumpi vaṭṭati eva.

138. The phrase “in the eastern direction” is merely an example. However, if there is no landmark in that direction, then starting from wherever one does exist, one should first announce the landmarks in the available surrounding places with phrases such as “in the intermediate eastern direction, in the southern direction,” and so on. Then, it is proper to announce again the first-announced landmark, “in the intermediate eastern direction,” because even a boundary shaped like a crossroads is to be established with three landmarks. As for the phrase “by one connecting the boundary-circle three times,” the meaning is: by a Vinaya expert who, standing in one single place, binds landmark to landmark all around the boundary-circle merely by the words announcing the landmarks. Indeed, it is proper to announce them even without going to each and every landmark-place. Because, for a boundary with a maximum extent of three yojanas, it is difficult to circumambulate it all around three times in a single day, it is indeed proper for a Vinaya expert, even if he has not seen it himself, to note a landmark as it was previously determined by monks, in accordance with what was said by someone, such as, “Venerable sir, a stone,” and to announce it with the words, “This stone is the landmark,” and so on.

Suddhapaṃsupabbatoti na kenaci kato sayaṃjātova vutto. Tathā sesāpi. Itaropīti suddhapaṃsupabbatādikopi pabbato. Hatthippamāṇatoti ettha bhūmito uggatappadesena hatthippamāṇaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Catūhi vā tīhi vāti sīmābhūmiyaṃ catūsu, tīsu vā disāsu ṭhitehi. Ekissā eva pana disāya ṭhitehi tato bahūhipi sammannituṃ na vaṭṭati. Dvīhi pana dvīsu disāsu ṭhitehipi na vaṭṭati. Tasmāti yasmā ekena na vaṭṭati, tasmā. Taṃ bahiddhā katvāti kittitanimittassa asīmattā antosīmāya karaṇaṃ ayuttanti vuttaṃ. Tenāha “sace”tiādi.

A “mountain of pure soil” is said to be one not made by anyone, but one that has arisen by itself. Likewise for the remaining ones. “The other one also” means a mountain such as one of pure soil. Here, in the phrase “of the size of an elephant,” the measure of an elephant should be taken by the part that has risen up from the ground. “By four or by three” refers to landmarks standing in four or three directions on the boundary-ground. However, it is not proper to establish a boundary even with many more landmarks than that if they stand in only one direction. And it is not proper with two, even if they are standing in two directions. “Therefore” means: because it is not proper with one, therefore... Regarding the phrase “having placed that outside,” it was said that because the announced landmark is not the boundary itself, it is unsuitable to make it part of the inner boundary. For that reason, he said, “if,” and so on.

Dvattiṃsapalaguḷapiṇḍappamāṇatā saṇṭhānato gahetabbā, na tulagaṇanāvasena, bhārato palaparimāṇañca magadhatulāya gahetabbaṃ. Sā ca lokiyatulāya dviguṇāti vadanti. Atimahantopīti bhūmito hatthippamāṇaṃ anuggantvā heṭṭhābhūmiyaṃ otiṇṇaghanato anekayojanappamāṇopi. Sace hi tato hatthippamāṇaṃ kūṭaṃ uggacchati, pabbatasaṅkhyameva gacchati.

The state of having the size of a lump of jaggery of thirty-two palas should be taken by its form, not by way of weighing or counting. And the measure of a pala by weight should be taken by the Magadhan weight. And they say that this is double the worldly weight. As for “even extremely large”: even if it has a measure of many yojanas by its solid mass that has descended into the ground below, without having risen up the measure of an elephant from the ground, it is proper. For if a peak the size of an elephant rises up from that, it goes into the category of a mountain.

Antosārānanti [V 2.0135] tasmiṃ khaṇe taruṇatāya sāre avijjamānepi pariṇāmena bhavissamānasārepi sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tādisānañhi sūcidaṇḍakappamāṇapariṇāhānaṃ catupañcamattampi vanaṃ vaṭṭati. Antosāramissakānanti antosārehi [M 2.0142] rukkhehi sammissānaṃ. Etena ca sārarukkhamissampi vanaṃ vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Catupañcarukkhamattampīti sārarukkhe sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vanamajjhe vihāraṃ karontīti rukkhaghaṭāya antare rukkhe acchinditvā vatiādīhi vihāraparicchedaṃ katvāva antorukkhantaresu eva pariveṇapaṇṇasālādīnaṃ karaṇavasena yathā antovihārampi vanameva hoti, evaṃ vihāraṃ karontīti attho. Yadi hi sabbaṃ rukkhaṃ chinditvā vihāraṃ kareyyuṃ, vihārassa avanattā taṃ parikkhipitvā ṭhitaṃ vanaṃ ekattha kittetabbaṃ siyā. Idha pana antopi vanattā “vanaṃ na kittetabba”nti vuttaṃ. Sace hi taṃ kittenti, “nimittassa upari vihāro hotī”tiādinā anantare vuttadosaṃ āpajjati. Ekadesanti vanekadesaṃ, rukkhavirahitaṭṭhāne katavihārassa ekapasse ṭhitavanassa ekadesanti attho.

Regarding “of those with inner heartwood,” this is said with reference also to trees that will have heartwood through maturation, even though at that moment, due to their youthfulness, heartwood does not exist. Indeed, for such trees having a circumference the size of a needle-handle, even a forest of just four or five is proper. “Of those mixed with inner heartwood” means of those mixed with trees having inner heartwood. By this, it is shown that even a forest mixed with heartwood trees is proper. “Just four or five trees” is said with reference to heartwood trees. As for “they make a monastery in the middle of a forest,” the meaning is: they make the monastery in such a way that the inside of the monastery is also just a forest, by making the monastery's enclosure with fences and so on without cutting the trees within a cluster of trees, and by making the cells, leaf-huts, and so on only in the spaces between the trees. For if they were to make the monastery by cutting down all the trees, since the monastery would not be a forest, the forest standing surrounding it would have to be announced at some point. But here, since the inside is also a forest, it was said, “the forest is not to be announced.” For if they do announce it, they fall into the fault mentioned immediately after, beginning with “the monastery is on top of the landmark.” “A certain part” means a part of the forest; the meaning is a part of the forest standing on one side of a monastery that was made in a place devoid of trees.

Sūcidaṇḍakappamāṇoti vaṃsadaṇḍappamāṇo. Lekhanidaṇḍappamāṇoti keci. Mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana avebhaṅgiyavinicchaye “yo koci aṭṭhaṅgulasūcidaṇḍakamattopi veḷu…pe… garubhaṇḍa”nti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. dubbattasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vuttattā tanutaro veḷudaṇḍoti ca sūcidaṇḍoti ca gahetabbaṃ. Vaṃsanaḷakasarāvādīsūti veḷupabbe vā naḷapabbe vā kapallakādimattikabhājanesu vāti attho. Taṅkhaṇampīti taruṇapotake amilāyitvā viruhanajātike sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ye pana pariṇatā samūlaṃ uddharitvā ropitāpi chinnasākhā viya milāyitvā cirena navamūlaṅkuruppattiyā jīvanti, mīyantiyeva vā, tādise kittetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Etanti navamūlasākhāniggamanaṃ.

As for 'of the size of a needle-handle,' it is the size of a bamboo staff. Some say it is the size of a writing-stylus. However, in the Mātikā-Aṭṭhakathā, in the decision on the Avebhaṅgiya, because it is said, “any bamboo, even as small as an eight-aṅgula needle-handle… is a heavy article,” it should be taken that a sūcidaṇḍa is a very slender bamboo staff. As for “in bamboo, reeds, potsherds, etc.,” the meaning is: in a bamboo joint, or in a reed joint, or in earthenware vessels such as potsherds. Regarding the phrase “at that moment,” it is said with reference to young saplings of a nature to sprout without withering. But it is not proper to announce those mature trees which, even when uprooted with their roots and replanted, wither like a cut-off branch and live only after a long time through the arising of new roots and shoots, or which just die. “This” is the emerging of new roots and branches.

Majjheti sīmāya mahādisānaṃ anto. Koṇanti sīmāya catūsu koṇesu dvinnaṃ dvinnaṃ maggānaṃ sambandhaṭṭhānaṃ. Parabhāge kittetuṃ vaṭṭatīti tesaṃ catunnaṃ koṇānaṃ bahi nikkhamitvā ṭhitesu maggesu ekissā disāya ekaṃ, aññissā disāya cāparanti evaṃ cattāropi maggā catūsu disāsu kittetuṃ vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. Evaṃ pana kittitamattena kathaṃ ekābaddhatā vigacchatīti viññāyatīti. Parato gataṭṭhānepi ete eva te cattāro maggā. “Catūsu disāsu gacchantī”ti hi vuttaṃ. Tasmā ettha kāraṇaṃ vicinitabbaṃ.

As for “in the middle,” it is the interior of the great directions of the boundary. As for “a corner,” it is the place of connection of two paths each at the four corners of the boundary. As for “it is proper to announce in the further part,” the intention is this: on the paths that, having gone out, stand outside those four corners, it is proper to announce one path in one direction, and another in another direction, and thus to announce all four paths in the four directions. But how is it to be understood that by merely announcing thus, their state of being interconnected is removed? Even in the place they have gone to further on, are they not these very same four paths? For was it not said, “They go in the four directions”? Therefore, the reason here should be investigated.

“Uttarantiyā bhikkhuniyā”ti idañca pāḷiyaṃ (pāci. 692) bhikkhunīnaṃ nadīpāragamane nadilakkhaṇassa āgatattā vuttaṃ. Bhikkhūnaṃ antaravāsakatemanamattampi vaṭṭati eva[M 2.0143]. “Nadicatukkepi eseva nayo”ti iminā ekattha kittetvā aññattha parato gataṭṭhānepi kittetuṃ [V 2.0136] na vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Teneva ca “assammissanadiyo catassopi kittetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti asammissa-ggahaṇaṃ kataṃ. Mūleti ādikāle. Nadiṃ bhinditvāti yathā udakaṃ anicchantehi kassakehi mahoghe nivattetuṃ na sakkā, evaṃ nadikūlaṃ bhinditvā.

“By a bhikkhunī crossing over”: this is stated because in the Pāḷi, in the training rule concerning bhikkhunīs crossing a river, the characteristic of a river has been mentioned. For bhikkhus, even a river with only enough water to wet an under-robe is indeed allowable. By the text, “The same method applies also in the fourfold river,” it is shown that having announced it in one place, it is not allowable to announce it in another place one has gone to further on. For that very reason, in the text, “It is allowable to announce even the four unmixed rivers,” the inclusion of the word 'unmixed' is made. “At the root” means in the beginning time. “Having broken the river”: just as it is not possible for farmers who do not want the water to turn back a great flood, so it is with having broken the riverbank.

Ukkhepimanti dīgharajjunā kuṭena ussiñcanīyaṃ.

“Ukkhepimaṃ” means that which is to be drawn up and poured with a pot attached to a long rope.

Asammissehīti sabbadisāsu ṭhitapabbatehi eva, pāsāṇādīsu aññatarehi vā nimittantarābyavahitehi. Sammissehīti ekattha pabbato, aññattha pāsāṇoti evaṃ ṭhitehi aṭṭhahipi. “Nimittānaṃ satenāpī”ti iminā ekissāya eva disāya bahunimittāni “puratthimāya disāya kiṃ nimittaṃ? Pabbato bhante. Puna puratthimāya disāya kiṃ nimittaṃ? Pāsāṇo bhante”tiādinā kittetuṃ vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Siṅghāṭakasaṇṭhānāti tikoṇā. Caturassāti samacaturassā, mudiṅgasaṇṭhānā pana āyatacaturassā. Ekakoṭiyaṃ saṅkocitā, tadaññāya vitthiṇṇā vā hotīti. Sīmāya upacāraṃ ṭhapetvāti āyatiṃ bandhitabbāya sīmāya nesaṃ vihārānaṃ paricchedato bahi sīmantarikappahonakaṃ upacāraṃ ṭhapetvā. Baddhā sīmā yesu vihāresu, te baddhasīmā. Pāṭekkanti paccekaṃ. Baddhasīmāsadisānīti yathā baddhasīmāsu ṭhitā aññamaññaṃ chandādiṃ anapekkhitvā paccekaṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ labhanti, evaṃ gāmasīmāsu ṭhitāpīti dasseti. Āgantabbanti sāmīcimattavasena vuttaṃ. Tenāha “āgamanampī”tiādi.

“Asammissehi” means only by mountains standing in all directions, or by one or another of rocks and so forth, that are not separated by another boundary marker. “Sammissehi” means with a mountain standing in one place and a rock in another, and so on, using any of the eight types of landmarks. By “even with a hundred boundary markers,” it is shown that it is allowable to announce many boundary markers even in a single direction, such as: “What is the boundary marker in the eastern direction, venerable sir?” “A mountain, venerable sir.” “Again, what is the boundary marker in the eastern direction?” “A rock, venerable sir,” and so on. “Siṅghāṭaka-shaped” means three-cornered. “Caturassā” means a perfect square, but a “mudiṅga-shaped” sīmā is an oblong rectangle, or it is contracted at one end and wide at the other. By “having set aside the approach-ground of the sīmā” is meant: regarding the sīmā to be established in the future, having set aside an approach-ground sufficient for a sīmantarika outside the boundary of those monasteries. Those monasteries in which a sīmā has been established are baddhasīmā. “Pāṭekkaṃ” means individually. By “similar to consecrated sīmās,” it is shown that just as monks abiding in consecrated sīmās can perform formal acts individually without regard for one another's consent and so forth, so too can those abiding in village-sīmās. “Āgantabbaṃ” (should be come to) is said by way of mere respect. Therefore, he said “āgamanampi” and so on.

Pabbajjūpasampadādīnanti ettha bhaṇḍukammāpucchanaṃ sandhāya pabbajjāgahaṇaṃ. Ekavīsati bhikkhūti nisinne sandhāya vuttaṃ. Idañca kammārahena saha abbhānakārakānampi pahonakatthaṃ vuttaṃ. “Nimittupagā pāsāṇā ṭhapetabbā”ti idaṃ yathārucitaṭṭhāne rukkhanimittādīnaṃ dullabhatāya vaḍḍhitvā ubhinnaṃ baddhasīmānaṃ saṅkarakaraṇato ca pāsāṇanimittassa ca tadabhāvato yattha katthaci ānetvā ṭhapetuṃ sukaratāya ca vuttaṃ. Tathā sīmantarikapāsāṇā ṭhapetabbāti etthāpi. Caturaṅgulappamāṇāpīti yathā khandhasīmāparicchedato bahi nimittapāsāṇānaṃ caturaṅgulamattaṭṭhānaṃ samantā nigacchati, avasesaṃ ṭhānaṃ antokhandhasīmāya hotiyeva, evaṃ tesupi ṭhapitesu caturaṅgulamattā sīmantarikā hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

In the phrase 'Pabbajjūpasampadādīnaṃ,' the word 'pabbajjā' is included with reference to asking about the act of shaving. The phrase 'Twenty-one bhikkhus' is said with reference to those who are seated. And this is said for the purpose of being sufficient for those performing the rehabilitation, together with the one worthy of the formal act.
