The explanation of the discourse on the authorization of a storeroom and so on is concluded.

Cīvararajanakathādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Dyeing Robes and so on

344. Evañhi kateti vaṭṭādhārassa anto rajanodakaṃ, bahi challikañca katvā viyojane kate. Na uttaratīti kevalaṃ udakato pheṇuṭṭhānābhāvā na uttarati. Rajanakuṇḍanti pakkarajanaṭṭhapanakaṃ mahāghaṭaṃ.

344. “Evañhi kate” means: when a separation is made after having placed the dye-water inside the cotton and the scum outside. “Na uttarati” means: it does not rise or overflow because of the absence of foam rising from the water alone. “Rajanakuṇḍa” means a large pot for placing cooked dye.

345. Anuvātādīnaṃ dīghapattānanti āyāmato, vitthārato ca anuvātaṃ. Ādi-saddena dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ antarā mātikākārena ṭhapitapattañca “dīghapatta”nti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Āgantukapattanti diguṇacīvarassa upari aññaṃ paṭṭaṃ appenti, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Taṃ kira idāni na karonti.

345. “Anuvātādīnaṃ dīghapattānaṃ” means the border by length and by width. By the word “and so on,” the strip placed in the form of a channel between the two sections should also be understood as a “long strip.” “Āgantukapatta” means they apply another strip on top of a double-layered robe; this is said with reference to that. It is said that this is not done now.

346. Pāḷiyaṃ [V 2.0188] nandimukhiyāti tuṭṭhimukhiyā, pasannadisāmukhāyāti attho.

346. In the Pāli, ‘nandimukhiyā’ means ‘with a joyful face’; the meaning is ‘with a pleased countenance’.

348. Acchupeyyanti patiṭṭhapeyyaṃ. Hatavatthakānanti purāṇavatthānaṃ. Anuddharitvāvāti aggaḷe viya dubbalaṭṭhānaṃ anapanetvāva.

346. “Accupeyyaṃ” means “I would place.” “Hatavatthakānaṃ” means of old cloths. “Anuddharitvāva” means only without removing the weak spot, like on a plank.

349-351. Visākhavatthumhi [M 2.0199] kallakāyāti akilantakāyā. Gatīti ñāṇagati adhigamo. Abhisamparāyoti “sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karotī”tiādinā (saṃ. ni. 5.1048) vutto ñāṇābhisamparāyo, maggañāṇayuttehi gantabbagativisesoti attho. Taṃ bhagavā byākarissati. “Dadāti dāna”nti idaṃ annapānavirahitānaṃ sesapaccayānaṃ dānavasena vuttaṃ. Sovaggikanti saggasaṃvattanikaṃ.

348. In the story of Visākhā, “kallakāyā” means with an unwearied body. “Gati” means attainment, the course of knowledge. “Abhisamparāyo” is the future life attained through knowledge, spoken of by way of the phrase, “having come to this world but once, he makes an end of suffering,” and so on; the meaning is it is the special destiny to be reached by those endowed with path-knowledge. The Blessed One will declare that. “Dadāti dānaṃ” is said by way of giving the remaining requisites, apart from food and drink. “Sovaggikaṃ” means conducive to heaven.

359. Aṭṭhapadakacchannenāti aṭṭhapadakasaṅkhātajūtaphalakalekhāsaṇṭhānena.

“Aṭṭhapadakacchannena” means with the pattern of a gaming board's lines, known as an aṭṭhapadaka.

362. Pāḷiyaṃ nadīpāraṃ gantunti bhikkhuno nadīpāragamanaṃ hotīti attho. Aggaḷaguttiyeva pamāṇanti imehi catūhi nikkhepakāraṇehi ṭhapentenapi aggaḷaguttivihāre eva ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. Nissīmāgatanti vassānasaṅkhātaṃ kālasīmaṃ atikkantaṃ, taṃ vassikasāṭikacīvaraṃ na hotīti attho.

359. In the Pāḷi, “gone to the far shore of the river” means it is the monk's going to the far shore of the river; this is the meaning. “Only a place secured by a bolt is the standard” means that the intention is that even for a monk who deposits something for these four reasons, it is only allowable to deposit it in a monastery secured with a bolt. “Gone beyond the boundary” means having passed beyond the time-boundary known as the rains-period; the meaning is that it is not a rains-season cloth.

Cīvararajanakathādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

362. The explanation of the discourse on dyeing robes and so on is concluded.

Saṅghikacīvaruppādakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of the Arising of Robes Belonging to the Sangha

363. Pañca māseti accantasaṃyoge upayogavacanaṃ. Vaḍḍhiṃ payojetvā ṭhapitaupanikkhepatoti vassāvāsikassatthāya dāyakehi vaḍḍhiṃ payojetvā ṭhapitaupanikkhepato. “Idha vassaṃvutthasaṅghassā”ti idaṃ abhilāpamattaṃ. Idha-saddaṃ pana vinā “vassaṃvutthasaṅghassa demā”ti vuttepi so eva nayo. Anatthatakathinassāpi pañca māse pāpuṇātīti vassāvāsikalābhavasena uppannattā anatthatakathinassāpi vutthavassassa pañca māse pāpuṇāti. Vakkhati hi “cīvaramāsato paṭṭhāya yāva hemantassa pacchimo divaso, tāva vassāvāsikaṃ demāti vutte kathinaṃ atthataṃ vā hotu anatthataṃ vā, atītavassaṃvutthānameva pāpuṇātī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379). Tato paranti pañcamāsato paraṃ, gimhānassa paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāyāti [V 2.0189] attho. “Kasmā? Piṭṭhisamaye uppannattā”ti idaṃ “udāhu anāgatavasse”ti [M 2.0200] imassānantaraṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Potthakesu pana “anatthatakathinassāpi pañca māse pāpuṇātī”ti imassānantaraṃ “kasmā piṭṭhisamaye uppannattā”ti idaṃ likhanti, taṃ pamādalikhitaṃ piṭṭhisamaye uppannaṃ sandhāya “anatthatakathinassāpī”ti vattabbato. Vutthavasse hi sandhāya “anatthatakathinassāpī”ti vuttaṃ, na ca piṭṭhisamaye uppannaṃ vutthavassasseva pāpuṇātīti sammukhībhūtānaṃ sabbesampi pāpuṇanato. Teneva vakkhati “sace pana gimhānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya evaṃ vadati, tatra sammukhībhūtānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Kasmā? Piṭṭhisamaye uppannattā”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 179).

363. In 'pañca māse' (five months), it is the accusative case in the sense of continuous connection. The phrase 'from a deposit placed after applying interest' means from a deposit placed by donors after applying interest for the purpose of the rains-residence robe. The phrase 'here, for the Sangha who has completed the rains-residence' is merely a manner of speaking. But even without the word 'here,' if one says, 'We give to the Sangha who has completed the rains-residence,' the meaning is the same. As for 'it reaches even one for whom the kathina has not been spread for five months': because it arose by way of the rains-residence gain, it is received for five months even by one who has completed the rains-residence for whom the kathina has not been spread. For it will be said: 'If one says, "From the robe-month onward until the last day of winter, we give the rains-residence gain," whether the kathina has been spread or not, it applies only to those who have completed the past rains-residence.' 'Beyond that' means beyond the five months, that is, starting from the first day of summer. The phrase 'Why? Because it arises in the piṭṭhisamaya' should be understood immediately after 'or for the future rains-residence.' In the manuscripts, however, they write 'Why? Because it arises in the piṭṭhisamaya' immediately after 'it reaches even one for whom the kathina has not been spread for five months.' That is a careless writing. For 'even for one for whom the kathina has not been spread' is said with reference to one who has completed the rains-residence, and what arises in the piṭṭhisamaya does not apply only to one who has completed the rains-residence, since it applies to all who are present. Therefore, it will be said: 'But if one speaks thus starting from the first day of summer, then it applies to all who are present. Why? Because it arises in the piṭṭhisamaya.'

Duggahitānīti aggahitāni. Saṅghikānevāti attho. Itovāti therānaṃ dātabbatova, idānevāti vā attho.

'Wrongly taken' means 'not taken.' The meaning is 'only what belongs to the Sangha.' 'From here' means from the fact that it is to be given to the elders, or it means 'just now'.

Saṅghikacīvaruppādakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Account of the Arising of Robes Belonging to the Sangha is concluded.

Upanandasakyaputtavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Story of Upananda the Sakyan Son

364. “Sattāhavārena aruṇameva uṭṭhāpetī”ti idaṃ nānāsīmāvihāresu kattabbanayena ekasmimpi vihāre dvīsu senāsanesu nivutthabhāvadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, aruṇuṭṭhāpaneneva tattha vuttho hoti, na pana vassacchedaparihārāya. Antoupacārasīmāyapi yattha katthaci aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpento attanā gahitasenāsanaṃ appaviṭṭhopi vutthavasso eva hoti, gahitasenāsane pana nivuttho nāma na hoti, tattha ca aruṇuṭṭhāpane pana sati hoti. Tenāha “purimasmiṃ bahutaraṃ nivasati nāmā”ti, etena ca itarasmiṃ sattāhavārenāpi aruṇuṭṭhāpane sati eva appakataraṃ nivasati nāma hoti, nāsatīti dīpitaṃ hoti. Nānālābhehīti visuṃ visuṃ nibaddhavassāvāsikalābhehi. Nānūpacārehīti nānāparikkhepanānādvārehi. Ekasīmāvihārehīti dvinnaṃ vihārānaṃ ekena pākārena parikkhittattā ekāya upacārasīmāya antogatehi dvīhi vihārehi. Senāsanaggāho paṭippassambhatīti paṭhamaṃ gahito paṭippassambhati. Tatthāti yattha senāsanaggāho paṭippassaddho, tattha.

364. “By a seven-day turn, one causes the dawn to rise.” This is said in order to show the state of having resided in two lodgings even in a single monastery, according to the method to be followed in monasteries with different boundaries. By causing the dawn to rise there, one is considered to have resided, but not for the purpose of guarding against the breaking of the rains-residence. Even within the precinct boundary, wherever one causes the dawn to rise, even without entering the lodging taken by oneself, one is indeed considered to have completed the rains-residence. However, one is not considered to have resided in the taken lodging. But when there is the causing of the dawn to rise there, one is considered to have resided. Therefore, he said, “In the former, one is said to reside more.” And by this it is shown that in the other case, only when there is the causing of the dawn to rise even by a seven-day turn is one said to reside less; if not, it is not so. “By various gains” means by separate, fixed gains for the rains-residence. “By various precincts” means by various enclosures and various gates. “In monasteries with a single boundary” means by two monasteries which, because of being surrounded by a single wall, are included within a single precinct boundary. “The taking of a lodging is annulled” means the one first taken is annulled. “There” means where the taking of a lodging has been annulled, there.

Upanandasakyaputtavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Story of Upananda the Sakyan Son is concluded.

Gilānavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of the Sick Person

365-6. Bhūmiyaṃ [M 2.0201][V 2.0190] paribhaṇḍaṃ akāsīti gilānena nipannabhūmiyaṃ kiliṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ dhovitvā haritūpalittaṃ kāresīti attho. Bhesajjaṃ yojetuṃ asamatthoti parehi vuttavidhimpi kātuṃ asamattho. Pāḷiyaṃ gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ cīvaradāne sāmaṇerānaṃ ticīvarādhiṭṭhānābhāvā “cīvarañca pattañcā”tiādi sabbattha vuttaṃ. Sacepi sahassaṃ agghati, gilānupaṭṭhākānaññeva dātabbanti sambandho.

365-6. “He made a mess on the ground” means: the sick person had the soiled place on the ground where he lay washed and had it smeared with fresh cow-dung—this is the meaning. “Unable to prepare medicine” means: unable to carry out even the procedure spoken of by others. In the Pāḷi, regarding the giving of robes to the attendants of the sick, because novices do not have the determination of the three robes, it is said everywhere, “and a robe and a bowl,” etc. Even if it is worth a thousand, it should be given only to the attendants of the sick—this is the connection.

Gilānavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Account of the Sick Person is concluded.

Matasantakakathādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation Beginning with the Account of Goods Belonging to a Deceased Person

369. Aññanti cīvarapattato aññaṃ. Appagghanti atijiṇṇādibhāvena nihīnaṃ. Tatoti avasesaparikkhārato. Sabbanti pattaṃ, ticīvarañca.

369. “Other” means other than the robe and bowl. “Of little value” means inferior due to being extremely worn out, etc. “From that” means from the remaining requisites. “All” means the bowl and the three robes.

Tattha tattha saṅghassevāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ vihāre saṅghasseva. Pāḷiyaṃ avissajjikaṃ avebhaṅgikanti āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghasseva santakaṃ hutvā kassaci avissajjikaṃ avebhaṅgikaṃ bhavituṃ anujānāmīti attho.

“Of the Sangha alone, in each case” means: in each and every monastery, it is the property of the Sangha alone. In the Pāḷi, “not to be given away, not to be divided” means: “Having become the property of the Sangha of the four directions, of those who have arrived and are yet to arrive, I permit it to be something that is not to be given away to anyone and not to be divided”—this is the meaning.

371-2. Akkanāḷamayanti akkadaṇḍamayaṃ. Akkadussānīti akkavākena katadussāni, potthakagatikāni dukkaṭavatthukānīti attho. Dupaṭṭacīvarassa vā majjheti yaṃ niṭṭhite tipaṭṭacīvaraṃ hoti, tassa majjhe paṭalaṃ katvā dātabbānīti attho.

371-2. “Made of akka reed” means made from akka stalks. “Akka cloths” means cloths made from akka bark. “Potthakagatikāni” means they are objects of a dukkaṭa offense—this is the meaning. “Or in the middle of a double-layered robe” means: for that which becomes a three-layered robe when finished, a layer is to be made in the middle and they are to be given—this is the meaning.

374. “Sante patirūpe gāhake”ti vuttattā gāhake asati adatvā bhājitepi subhājitamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

374. Because it is said, “When there are suitable recipients,” it should be understood that even if it is divided without being given when there is no recipient, it is still well-divided.

376. Dakkhiṇodakaṃ pamāṇanti “ettakāni cīvarāni dassāmī”ti paṭhamaṃ udakaṃ pātetvā pacchā denti. Taṃ yehi gahitaṃ, te bhāginova hontīti [M 2.0202] adhippāyo. Parasamuddeti jambudīpe. Tambapaṇṇidīpañhi upādāyesa evaṃ vutto.

376. “The water of dedication is the measure” means: first they pour the water, saying, “We will give this many robes,” and afterward they give. The intention is that those by whom it has been received are indeed the recipients. “Beyond the ocean” means in Jambudīpa. Indeed, this is said with reference to the island of Tambapaṇṇi.

Matasantakakathādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation Beginning with the Account of Goods Belonging to a Deceased Person is concluded.

Aṭṭhacīvaramātikākathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Chapter on the Eight Robes

379. Puggalādhiṭṭhānanayena [V 2.0191] vuttanti “sīmāya dāna”ntiādinā vattabbe “sīmāya detī”tiādi puggalādhiṭṭhānena vuttaṃ. “Apicā”tiādinā paṭhamaleḍḍupātabhūtaparikkhepārahaṭṭhānato bahi dutiyaleḍḍupātopi upacārasīmā evāti dasseti. Dhuvasannipātaṭṭhānādikampi pariyante ṭhitameva gahetabbaṃ. Loke gāmasīmādayo viya lābhasīmā nāma visuṃ pasiddhā nāma natthi, kenāyaṃ anuññātāti āha “neva sammāsambuddhenā”tiādi. Etena nāyaṃ sāsanavohārasiddhā, lokavohārasiddhā evāti dasseti. “Janapadaparicchedo”ti idaṃ lokapasiddhasīmāsaddatthavasena vuttaṃ. Paricchedabbhantaraṃ pana sabbaṃ janapadasīmāti gahetabbaṃ, janapado eva janapadasīmā. Evaṃ raṭṭhasīmādīsupi. Tenāha “āṇāpavattiṭṭhāna”ntiādi.

379. It is said by way of the individual-determination method that what should be stated as 'a gift within the boundary' (sīmāya dānaṃ) is instead stated as 'he gives within the boundary' (sīmāya deti), which is spoken with individual determination. Moreover, by 'apicā' and so on, it is shown that even the second clod's throw outside the place suitable for the perimeter marked by the first clod's throw is indeed a vicinity boundary (upacārasīmā). Places of permanent assembly (dhuvasannipātaṭṭhāna) and similar locations should also be taken as being situated at the extremity. In the world, there is no separately established boundary for gains (lābhasīmā) like village boundaries (gāmasīmā) and so on. Due to the objection, 'By whom was this permitted?', it is said, 'not by the Perfectly Enlightened One' (neva sammāsambuddhena) and so on. By this, it is shown that this is not established by the convention of the Dispensation (sāsanavohāra), but only by worldly convention (lokavohāra). The phrase 'demarcation of a country' (janapadaparicchedo) is spoken in the sense of the worldly meaning of the term 'boundary' (sīmā). But the entire interior of the demarcation should be taken as the country's boundary (janapadasīmā); the country itself is the country's boundary. The same applies to kingdom boundaries (raṭṭhasīmā) and others. Therefore, it is said, 'the place where authority prevails' (āṇāpavattiṭṭhānaṃ) and so on.

Pathavīvemajjhe gatassāti yāva udakapariyantā khaṇḍasīmattā vuttaṃ, upacārasīmādīsu pana abaddhasīmāsu heṭṭhāpathaviyaṃ sabbattha ṭhitānaṃ na pāpuṇāti, kūpādipavesārahaṭṭhāne ṭhitānaññeva pāpuṇātīti heṭṭhā sīmākathāyaṃ vuttanayena taṃtaṃsīmaṭṭhabhāvo veditabbo. Cakkavāḷasīmāya pana dinnaṃ pathavīsandhārakaudakaṭṭhānepi ṭhitānaṃ pāpuṇāti sabbattha cakkavāḷavohārattā.

The phrase 'gone to the middle of the earth' (pathavīvemajjhe gatassa) is said because it is a fragmented boundary extending as far as the water's limit. However, in the case of vicinity boundaries (upacārasīmā) and the like, which are unbound boundaries, it does not extend to those standing everywhere below the earth. It extends only to those standing in places suitable for entering, such as wells. Thus, the state of being within each respective boundary should be understood according to the method explained in the discourse on the lower boundary. As for what is given within the world-sphere boundary (cakkavāḷasīmā), it extends even to those standing in the place of the earth-supporting water, because of the designation 'world-sphere' being used everywhere.

Buddhādhivutthoti buddhena bhagavatā nivuttho. Pākavaṭṭanti nibaddhadānaṃ. Vattatīti pavattati. Tehīti yesaṃ sammukhe esa deti, tehi bhikkhūhi. Dutiyabhāge pana therāsanaṃ āruḷheti yāva saṅghanavakā ekavāraṃ sabbesaṃ bhāgaṃ datvā cīvare aparikkhīṇe puna sabbesaṃ dātuṃ dutiyabhāge therassa dinneti attho. Paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭatīti ettha “tuyhaṃ demā”ti avuttattāti kāraṇaṃ vadanti. Yadi evaṃ “saṅghassa demā”ti vuttepi [M 2.0203] vaṭṭeyya, “bhikkhūnaṃ dema, therānaṃ dema, saṅghassa demā”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) vacanato bhedo na dissati. Vīmaṃsitabbamettha kāraṇaṃ.

'Buddhādhivuttho' means inhabited by the Buddha, the Blessed One. 'Pākavaṭṭa' refers to a regular donation. 'Vattati' means it occurs. 'Tehi' refers to those monks in whose presence this donor gives. Regarding 'in the second portion, the elder has ascended the seat', the meaning is that after giving a share to all, down to the most junior monk of the Sangha, once, and the robe-cloth is not exhausted, in order to give to all again, the second share is given to the elder. Regarding 'It is allowable for wearers of rag-robes too' (paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭati), they state the reason that it is not said, 'We give to you' (tuyhaṃ demā). If this is so, it would be allowable even if it were said, 'We give to the Sangha' (saṅghassa demā), for no difference is seen between the phrases 'We give to the monks, we give to the elders, we give to the Sangha'. The reason here should be investigated.

Pārupituṃ vaṭṭatīti paṃsukūlikānaṃ vaṭṭati. Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunīnañca dammīti vutte pana na majjhe bhinditvā dātabbanti ettha yasmā bhikkhunipakkhe saṅghassa paccekaṃ aparāmaṭṭhattā bhikkhunīnaṃ gaṇanāya bhāgo dātabboti dāyakassa adhippāyoti sijjhati, tathā dānañca bhikkhūpi gaṇetvā dinne eva yujjati. Itarathā hi kittakaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dātabbaṃ, kittakaṃ bhikkhunīnanti na viññāyati, tasmā “bhikkhusaṅghassā”ti vuttavacanampi “bhikkhūna”nti vuttavacanasadisamevāti āha “bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca gaṇetvā dātabba”nti. Tenāha “puggalo [V 2.0192] …pe… bhikkhusaṅghaggahaṇena aggahitattā”ti. Bhikkhusaṅgha-saddena bhikkhūnaññeva gahitattā, puggalassa pana “tuyhañcā”ti visuṃ gahitattā ca tatthassa aggahitatā daṭṭhabbā, “bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañcā”ti vuttaṭṭhānasadisattāti adhippāyo. Puggalappadhāno hettha saṅgha-saddo daṭṭhabbo. Keci pana “bhikkhusaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā”ti (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.379) pāṭhaṃ likhanti, taṃ na sundaraṃ tassa visuṃ lābhaggahaṇe kāraṇavacanattā. Tathā hi visuṃ saṅghaggahaṇena gahitattāti visuṃ puggalassapi bhāgaggahaṇe kāraṇaṃ vuttaṃ. Yathā cettha puggalassa aggahaṇaṃ, evaṃ upari “bhikkhusaṅghassa ca tuyhañcā”tiādīsupi saṅghādi-saddehi puggalassa aggahaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yadi hi gahaṇaṃ siyā, saṅghatopi, visumpīti bhāgadvayaṃ labheyya ubhayattha gahitattā.

Regarding 'It is allowable to wear', this is not allowable for wearers of rag-robes. When it is said, 'I give to the community of monks and to the nuns', it should not be given by dividing it in the middle. Here, because on the nuns' side the Sangha is not individually considered, it is established that the donor's intention is for a share to be given according to the number of nuns. And such a gift is proper only when given after having counted the monks also. Otherwise, it would not be known how much should be given to the monks and how much to the nuns. Therefore, the statement 'to the community of monks' is just like the statement 'to the monks'. Thus, he said, 'it should be given after counting the monks and the nuns'. Because by the term 'community of monks' only the monks are included, and because the individual is included separately with 'and to you', it should be understood that he is not included therein; this is the intention, because of its similarity to the case where it is said, 'to the monks, and to the nuns, and to you'. Here, the word 'saṅgha' should be seen as having individuals as its primary meaning. Some, however, write the reading as 'because of being included by the taking of the community of monks', but that is not good, because that is stated as the reason for the separate receiving of a gain. Indeed, just as the individual is not included here, so too in the cases above, such as 'to the community of monks and to you', the non-inclusion of the individual by terms like 'Sangha' should be understood. For if there were inclusion, one would receive a double share—from the Sangha and separately—because of being included in both places.

Pūjetabbantiādi gihikammaṃ na hotīti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa harā”ti idaṃ piṇḍapātaharaṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tenāha “bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti. “Antohemante”ti iminā anatthate kathine vassānaṃ pacchime māse dinnaṃ purimavassaṃvutthānaññeva pāpuṇāti, tato paraṃ hemante dinnaṃ pacchimavassaṃvutthānampi vutthavassattā pāpuṇāti. Hemantato pana paraṃ piṭṭhisamaye “vassaṃvutthasaṅghassā”ti evaṃ vatvā dinnaṃ anantare vasse vā tato paresu vā yattha katthaci tasmiṃ vutthavassānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Ye pana sabbathā avutthavassā, tesaṃ na pāpuṇātīti dasseti. Sabbesampīti hi tasmiṃ bhikkhubhāve vutthavassānaṃ sabbesampīti attho [M 2.0204] daṭṭhabbo. “Vassaṃvutthasaṅghassā”ti vuttattā sammukhībhūtānaṃ sabbesanti etthāpi eseva nayo. Atītavassanti anantarātītavassaṃ.

'To be honored' (pūjetabbaṃ) and so on are said in order to show that it is not a householder's task. 'Take it for the community of monks' (bhikkhusaṅghassa harā) is said referring to the carrying of alms-food. Therefore, it is said, 'It is allowable to eat' (bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati). By 'within the winter' (antohemante), it is shown that when the kathina is not spread, a robe given in the last month of the rains-residence reaches only those who have completed the earlier rains-residence. After that, a robe given in the winter reaches also those who have completed the later rains-residence, because they have completed the rains-residence. But after the winter, in the hot season, a robe given after saying thus, 'For the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence' (vassaṃvutthasaṅghassā), reaches all who have completed the rains-residence in any rains-residence whatsoever, whether in the immediately preceding rains-residence or in subsequent ones. But it is shown that it does not reach those who have not completed the rains-residence at all. 'For all' (sabbesampi) should be understood to mean 'for all who have completed the rains-residence in that state of being a monk'. Because it is said 'for the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence', this same method applies also in the case of 'for all who are present'. 'The past rains-residence' (atītavassaṃ) means the immediately past rains-residence.

Uddesaṃ gahetuṃ āgatoti uddese aggahitepi antevāsikovāti vuttaṃ. Gahetvā gacchantoti pariniṭṭhitauddeso hutvā gacchanto. “Vattaṃ katvā uddesaparipucchādīni gahetvā vicarantāna”nti idaṃ “uddesantevāsikāna”nti imasseva visesanaṃ, tena uddesakāle āgantvā uddesaṃ gahetvā gantvā aññattha nivasante anibaddhacārike nivatteti.

Regarding the phrase 'has come to take the recitation' (`Uddesaṃ gahetuṃ āgato`): it is said that he is a resident pupil (`antevāsika`) even before the recitation is taken. As for 'having taken, he goes' (`Gahetvā gacchanto`): it means one who, having completed the recitation, goes. This phrase, 'of those who, having performed their duties, wander about having taken up recitation, questioning, and so on' (`Vattaṃ katvā uddesaparipucchādīni gahetvā vicarantānaṃ`), is a qualifier for this very phrase, 'of the pupils for recitation' (`uddesantevāsikānaṃ`). By that qualifier, it excludes the unattached wanderers (`anibaddhacārike`) who, at the time of recitation, come, take the recitation, go, and reside in another place.

Aṭṭhacīvaramātikākathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourse on the matrix of eight robes is finished.

Cīvarakkhandhakavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The method for explaining the Chapter on Robes is finished.

9. Campeyyakkhandhako

9. The Campeyyaka Chapter

Kassapagottabhikkhuvatthukathādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourses Beginning with the Story of the Monk Kassapagotta

380. Campeyyakkhandhake [M 2.0205][V 2.0193] tantibaddhoti tanti vuccati byāpāro, tattha baddho, ussukkaṃ āpannoti attho. Tenāha “tasmiṃ āvāse”tiādi.

380. In the Campeyyaka Chapter, regarding `tantibaddho`: `tanti` is called exertion (`byāpāro`); `baddho` therein means engaged, has undertaken diligence (`ussukkaṃ āpanno`). This is the meaning. Therefore, he said the phrase beginning with 'in that residence...'

387-8. Hāpanaṃ vā aññathā karaṇaṃ vā natthīti ñattikammassa ñattiyā ekattā hāpanaṃ na sambhavati, tassā ekattā eva pacchā ñattiṭhapanavasena, dvikkhattuṃ ṭhapanavasena ca aññathā karaṇaṃ natthi. Paratoti parivāre. Tanti pabbājanīyakammaṃ, tassāti attho.

As for 'There is no reduction or alteration': because an act consisting of a motion has a single motion, reduction is not possible. Precisely because of its being single, there is no alteration by way of placing the motion afterwards or by way of placing it twice. As for `parato`: it means in the Parivāra. `Tanti` is the act of banishment; 'for that' (`tassa`) is the meaning.

Kassapagottabhikkhuvatthukathādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourses beginning with the story of the monk Kassapagotta is finished.

Dvenissaraṇādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourses Beginning with the Two Expulsions

395. Esāti “bālo”tiādinā niddiṭṭhapuggalo, appattoti sambandho. Tattha kāraṇamāha “yasmā”tiādi. Tattha āveṇikena lakkhaṇenāti pabbājanīyakammassa nimittabhāvena pāḷiyaṃ vuttattā asādhāraṇabhūtena kuladūsakabhāvena. Yadi hesa taṃ kammaṃ appatto, kathaṃ pana sunissāritoti āha “yasmā panassa ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyyāti vuttaṃ, tasmā sunissārito”ti. Tattha vuttanti kammakkhandhake (cūḷava. 27) vuttaṃ.

395. `Esa` (`he`) is the person indicated by 'a fool,' and so on; the connection is with `appatto` (`has not attained`). To show the reason for that, he said the phrase beginning with 'Because...' (`yasmā`). Therein, 'by a unique characteristic' (`āveṇikena lakkhaṇena`) means: by the state of being a corrupter of families, which is an uncommon trait, because it is stated in the Pāḷi Canon as being the cause for the act of banishment. Due to the objection, “If this person has not attained that act, how then is he well expelled?”, he said: 'Because it is stated, “Moreover, the Sangha, if it wishes, may carry out the act of banishment on him,” therefore he is well expelled.' 'Stated therein' means stated in the Kammakkhandhaka.

Ettha pana kuladūsakakammaṃ katvā pabbājanīyakammakatassa terasakakaṇḍakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “yasmiṃ vihāre vasantena yasmiṃ gāme kuladūsakakammaṃ kataṃ hoti, tasmiṃ vihāre vā tasmiṃ gāme vā na vasitabba”ntiādinā (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.433) yā sammāvattanā vuttā, sā itarenāpi [V 2.0194] pūretabbā. Yaṃ pana paṭippassaddhakammassa kuladūsakassa tattheva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “yesu kulesu kuladūsakakammaṃ kataṃ, tato paccayā na gahetabbā”tiādi vuttaṃ, taṃ na pūretabbaṃ kulasaṅgahassa akatattā. Evaṃ sesakammesupi. Yadi evaṃ “tajjanīyakammārahassa [M 2.0206] niyasakammaṃ karoti…pe… evaṃ kho, upāli, adhammakammaṃ hotī”tiādivacanaṃ (mahāva. 402) virujjhatīti? Na virujjhati saṅghasanniṭṭhānavasena tajjanīyādikammārahattassa sijjhanato. Yassa hi saṅgho “tajjanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvā kammavācaṃ sāvento pabbājanīyakammavācaṃ sāveti, tassa kammaṃ adhammakammaṃ hoti. Sace pana “tasseva pabbājanīyakammameva karomā”ti sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvā tadeva karoti, tassa taṃ kammaṃ dhammakammanti veditabbaṃ.

Here, for one who has committed the act of corrupting families and upon whom the act of banishment has been carried out, the proper conduct stated in the commentary on the thirteen sections—beginning with, 'One should not dwell in the monastery or the village where the act of corrupting families was committed'—should also be fulfilled by another upon whom an act was carried out for a different offense. However, for a corrupter of families whose act has been revoked, the duty stated in that same commentary—beginning with, 'Requisites should not be accepted from those families where the act of corrupting families was committed'—should not be fulfilled, because the supporting of families has not been done. It is the same for the remaining acts. If this is so, does the statement beginning with, 'For one deserving the act of censure, he carries out the act of subordination... thus, Upāli, it is an unlawful act,' contradict this? It does not contradict, because the state of being deserving of the act of censure and so on is established by the power of the Sangha's resolution. Indeed, if the Sangha, having made the resolution, 'We will carry out the act of censure,' while announcing the formal procedure, announces the formal procedure for the act of banishment, that act for him is an unlawful act. But if, having made the resolution, 'We will carry out only the act of banishment for this very one,' he then carries out just that, that act for him should be known as a lawful act.

Evamidha “nissāraṇa”nti adhippetassa pabbājanīyakammassa vasena atthaṃ dassetvā idāni tadaññesaṃ tajjanīyādīnaṃ vasena nissāraṇe adhippete “appatto nissāraṇa”nti imassa paṭipakkhavasena sampatto nissāraṇaṃ, “tañce saṅgho nissāreti. Sunissārito”ti atthasambhavaṃ dassetuṃ puna “tañce saṅgho nissāretīti sace saṅgho”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tajjanīyādikammavisaye, ekenāpi aṅgena nissāraṇā anuññātāti yojanā. Pāḷiyaṃ appatto nissāraṇanti ettha āpanno āveṇikavasena tajjanīyādisaṅkhātaṃ nissāraṇaṃ pattoti attho gahetabbo.

Thus, having here shown the meaning by way of the act of banishment, which is intended by 'expulsion' (`nissāraṇa`), now, when expulsion is intended by way of other acts such as the act of censure, to show the possible meaning—'He has attained expulsion; and if the Sangha expels him, he is well expelled'—by way of the opposite of 'has not attained expulsion', it is again stated, 'And if the Sangha expels him, meaning if the Sangha...' and so on. Therein, `tattha` means: in the matter of the acts of censure and so on, expulsion is permitted even by one factor; this is the construction. In the Pāḷi, regarding 'has not attained expulsion,' the meaning to be taken is: one who has incurred it has, by way of a unique characteristic, attained the expulsion reckoned as the act of censure and so on.

Dvenissaraṇādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourses beginning with the two expulsions is finished.

Campeyyakkhandhakavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The method for explaining the Campeyyaka Chapter is finished.

10. Kosambakakkhandhako

10. The Kosambaka Chapter

Kosambakavivādakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Kosambi Dispute

451. Kosambakakkhandhake [M 2.0207][V 2.0195] sace hoti, desessāmīti vinayadharassa vacanena āpattidiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhitvā evamāha. Teneva pāḷiyaṃ “so tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Natthi āpattīti udakassa ṭhapanabhāvaṃ ajānitvā vā ṭhapitaṃ chaḍḍetvā vissaritvā vā gamane asañcicca asatiyā anāpattipakkhopi sambhavatīti vinayadharo tattha anāpattidiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhitvā evamāha. Teneva pāḷiyaṃ “aññe bhikkhū tassa āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhino hontī”ti vuttaṃ. Parisāyapissa anāpattidiṭṭhiyā uppannattā “aññe”ti bahuvacanaṃ kataṃ. Anāpattidiṭṭhi ahosīti suttantikattherassa vinaye apakataññutāya vinayadharassa vacanamattena so evamahosi, sā panassa āpatti eva udakāvasesassa ṭhapanabhāvaṃ ñatvā ṭhapitattā. Vatthumattajānane eva hi sekhiyā sacittakā, na paṇṇattivijānane. Teneva pāḷiyaṃ “tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi hotī”ti sabbattha āpatti icceva vuttaṃ. “Āpattiṃ āpajjamāno”ti idaṃ vinayadharatthero “tayā idaṃ udakaṃ ṭhapita”nti attanā puṭṭhena suttantikattherena “āmāvuso”ti vuttavacanaṃ saritvā paṇṇattiakovidatāya sañcicceva akāsīti āpattidiṭṭhi hutvāva avoca. Teneva pāḷiyaṃ “aññe bhikkhū tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhino hontī”ti vuttaṃ.

451. In the Kosambakakkhandhaka: Regarding the words, “If it is so, I will declare it,” he spoke thus after having obtained the view that it is an offense through the word of the Vinaya-expert. For that very reason, it is said in the Pāḷi: “He has the view of no-offense regarding that offense.” The words, “There is no offense,” are explained thus: the side of no-offense can also occur through not knowing the fact of having placed the water, or having discarded what was placed and forgotten, or in going, being unintentional through a lapse of mindfulness. Therefore, the Vinaya-expert, having obtained the view of no-offense in that matter, spoke thus. For that very reason, it is said in the Pāḷi: “Other monks have the view of no-offense regarding his offense.” Because for his assembly also the view of no-offense had arisen, the plural “others” is used. The Suttantika elder had the view of no-offense; due to his lack of expertise in the Vinaya, he became so merely by the word of the Vinaya-expert. But for him, it was indeed an offense, because of having placed it knowing the fact of leaving leftover water. Indeed, the Sekhiya rules are intentional only in the knowing of the object-matter, not in the knowing of the rule. For that very reason, it is said everywhere in the Pāḷi, “He has the view of no-offense regarding that offense,” yet it is still stated to be an offense. The Vinaya-expert elder spoke the words, “committing an offense,” having the view that it was an offense, remembering the words “Yes, friend” spoken by the Suttantika elder when he was asked by him, “Was this water placed by you?” and thinking, “Due to his lack of skill in the rule, he did it intentionally.” For that very reason, it is said in the Pāḷi: “Other monks have the view of an offense regarding his offense.”

453. “Na tāva bhinno”ti idaṃ ukkhipanatadanuvattanamattena saṅgho bhinno nāma na hoti, taṃ nissāya pana ubhayapakkhikānaṃ pakkhaṃ pariyesitvā aññamaññaṃ kodhavasena kāyavacīkalahavaḍḍhaneneva hotīti imamatthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tenāha “so ca kho kalahavasenā”ti. Sambhamaatthavasenāti turitatthavasena.

453. Regarding the words, “Not yet split”: the Saṅgha is not called ‘split’ merely by the act of suspension and by following the suspended one. But, it is said with reference to this meaning: relying on that, after the monks of both factions have sought out their own party, it happens by the power of increasing bodily and verbal conflict with one another through the power of anger. Therefore, He said, “And that is by means of conflict.” As for `sambhamaatthavasena`, it is by the power of the meaning ‘hastily’.

454. Akāraṇetiādi [V 2.0196] anukkhipitvāva upāyena saññāpetvā hitesitāya āpattito mocetuṃ yuttaṭṭhāne kodhacittavasena viheṭhanatthāya katabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na pana kammaṅgassa abhāvaṃ sandhāya. Teneva [M 2.0208] pāḷiyaṃ “āpatti esā, bhikkhave, nesā anāpatti…pe… ukkhitto eso bhikkhū”tiādi vuttaṃ.

454. Regarding the words, “Without reason,” etc.: this is said with reference to the fact that, in a situation where it was suitable to release him from the offense by making him understand through a stratagem with a desire for his welfare, without suspending him, it was instead done for the purpose of harassment by the power of an angry mind. But it is not said with reference to the absence of a factor of the formal act. For that very reason, it is said in the Pāḷi: “This is an offense, monks, this is not a no-offense… and so on… this monk is suspended,” etc.

455. “Adhammavādīnaṃ pakkhe nisinno”ti idaṃ upalakkhaṇamattaṃ, dhammavādīnaṃ pakkhe nisīditvā adhammavādīnaṃ laddhiṃ gaṇhantopi dhammavādīnaṃ nānāsaṃvāsako hoti eva. Kammaṃ kopetīti taṃ vinā gaṇassa apūraṇapakkhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yattha vā tattha vāti dhammavādīnaṃ pakkhe vā adhammavādīnaṃ pakkhe vāti attho. Ime dhammavādinoti gaṇhātīti taṃtaṃpakkhagate bhikkhū yāthāvato vā ayāthāvato vā “ime dhammavādino”ti gaṇhāti, ayaṃ taṃtaṃpakkhagatānaṃ attānaṃ samānasaṃvāsakaṃ karoti.

455. The phrase “sitting in the faction of the non-Dhamma-speakers” is merely an indication. A monk who, while sitting in the faction of the Dhamma-speakers, takes up the view of the non-Dhamma-speakers, is indeed of non-communion with the Dhamma-speakers. “It invalidates the formal act” is said with reference to the group being incomplete without him. “Wherever” means in the faction of the Dhamma-speakers or in the faction of the non-Dhamma-speakers. “He holds, ‘These are Dhamma-speakers’” means: he holds, “These are Dhamma-speakers” regarding the monks belonging to this or that faction, whether correctly or incorrectly. This monk makes himself to be of common communion with those belonging to this or that faction.

456. Upadaṃsentīti pavattenti. Pāḷiyaṃ ettāvatāti “ettakapadesaṃ muñcitvā nisinnā mayaṃ kodhacitte uppannepi aññamaññaṃ ananulomikaṃ kāyakammādiṃ pavattetuṃ na sakkhissāmā”ti sallekkhetvā dūre nisīditabbanti adhippāyo. Tenāha “upacāraṃ muñcitvā”ti.

456. “They incite” means they cause to occur. In the Pāḷi, `ettāvatā` has this intention: one should sit at a distance, having considered, “We, sitting having left this much space, will not be able to cause unsuitable bodily actions, etc., towards one another, even if an angry mind arises.” Therefore, He said, “having left the vicinity.”

457. Pāḷiyaṃ bhaṇḍanajātātiādīsu kalahassa pubbabhāgo bhaṇḍanaṃ nāma. Hatthaparāmāsādi kalaho nāma. Viruddhavādo vivādo nāma.

457. In the Pāḷi, in such phrases as `bhaṇḍanajātā`, etc., the preliminary stage of a conflict (`kalaha`) is called a quarrel (`bhaṇḍana`). Touching with the hand, etc., is called a conflict (`kalaha`). Contradictory speech is called a dispute (`vivāda`).

458. Paripuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāroti ettha koso nāma suvaṇṇamaṇiādibhaṇḍāgārasāragabbho. Koṭṭhaṃ vuccati dhaññassa āvasanaṭṭhānaṃ, koṭṭhabhūtaṃ agāraṃ koṭṭhāgāraṃ, dhaññasaṅgahaṭṭhānaṃ. Abbhuyyāsīti yuddhāya abhimukho nikkhamīti attho. Ekasaṅghātampīti ekayuddhampi. Dhovananti dhovanudakaṃ.

458. In the term `paripuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāro`: `kosa` is the treasure-core-chamber which is the storehouse for goods such as gold, gems, etc. The place for keeping grain is called `koṭṭha`; a house that is a granary is a `koṭṭhāgāra`, a place for collecting grain. `Abbhuyyāsi` means: he went forth facing for battle. `Ekasaṅghātampi` means even one battle. `Dhovanaṃ` is water for washing.

463. Pariyādinnarūpāti kodhacittena pariggahitasabhāvā.

463. `Pariyādinnarūpā` means having a nature that is seized by an angry mind.

464. Taṃ na jānantīti taṃ kalahaṃ na jānanti. Ye upanayhantīti yathāvuttaṃ kodhākāraṃ citte bandhanti. Pākaṭaparissayeti sīhādike. Paṭicchannaparissayeti rāgādike. Pāḷiyaṃ natthi bāle 97 sahāyatāti bālaṃ nissāya sīlādiguṇasaṅkhātā sahāyatā natthi, na sakkā laddhunti attho.

464. “They do not know it” means they do not know that conflict. “Those who are resentful” means they bind in the mind the mass of anger as was stated. “Manifest dangers” means dangers such as lions. “Concealed dangers” means dangers such as lust. In the Pāḷi, “There is no companionship with a fool” means: relying on a fool, there is no companionship designated as the qualities of virtue, etc.; it cannot be obtained.

466. Attakāmarūpāti [M 2.0209] attano hitakāmayamānasabhāvā. Anuruddhāti ekasesanayena tiṇṇampi kulaputtānaṃ ālapanaṃ, teneva bahuvacananiddeso kato. Khamanīyaṃ sarīraṃ yāpanīyaṃ jīvitaṃ “kacci vo sarīrañca dhāretuṃ, jīvitañca yāpetuṃ sakkā”ti pucchati. Tagghāti ekaṃsatthe nipāto, ekaṃsena mayaṃ bhanteti attho. Yathā kathanti ettha yathāti nipātamattaṃ, yathākathanti vā eko nipāto kāraṇapucchanattho, kena pakārenāti attho. Ekañca pana maññe cittanti ekassa cittavasena itaresampi pavattanato sabbesaṃ no ekaṃ viya cittanti attho. Kacci pana vo anuruddhāti ettha voti nipātamattaṃ, paccattavacanaṃ vā, kacci tumheti attho. Amhākanti niddhāraṇe sāmivacanaṃ, amhesu tīsu yo paṭhamaṃ paṭikkamatīti attho.

466. `Attakāmarūpā` means having a nature that desires one's own welfare. The word `Anuruddhā` is a form of address for all three clansmen by way of `ekasesa` (ellipsis); for that very reason, the plural designation is made. “Is the body tolerable? Is life sustainable?” means he asks thus: “Well, are you able to maintain the body and to sustain life?” `Taggha` is a particle in the sense of certainty; the meaning is, “Certainly, we are.” In the term `yathā kathaṃ`, `yathā` is merely a particle; or, `yathākathaṃ` is a single particle for asking the reason; the meaning is “by what means?” `Ekañca pana maññe cittaṃ` means: because the others also act according to the mind of one, the mind of all of us is like one. In the phrase `kacci pana vo Anuruddhā`, the word `vo` is merely a particle; or, it is a nominative plural; the meaning is “Well, are you...?” The word `amhākaṃ` is a genitive of specification; the meaning is: “among us three, whoever returns first...”

Kosambakavivādakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Kosambi Dispute is concluded.

Pālileyyakagamanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Account of the Journey to Pālileyyaka

467. Yena pālileyyakanti paccatte upayogavacanaṃ, yattha pālileyyako gāmo, tattha avasarīti attho. Daharapotakehīti bhiṅkacchāpehi. “Ogāhi”ntipi pāṭho, nahānapokkharaṇinti attho.

467. In the phrase 'yena pālileyyakaṃ', the accusative case is used in the sense of the nominative. The meaning is: 'Where the village of Pālileyyaka is, there he went.' 'Daharapotakehi' means 'by young elephants.' 'Ogāhi' is also a reading; the meaning is 'they entered the bathing pond.'

Udānagāthāyaṃ pana – rathaīsasadisadantassa nāgassa hatthino etaṃ vivekaninnaṃ cittaṃ nāgena buddhanāgassa vivekaninnacittena sameti. Kasmā? Yaṃ yasmā ekova ramati vane, tasmā evaṃ yojanā daṭṭhabbā.

In the Udāna verse, however, the mind of the elephant, whose tusks are like chariot poles, inclining to seclusion, agrees with the mind, inclining to seclusion, of the Buddha-elephant. Why? Because he alone delights in the forest; thus, the connection should be understood.

Pālileyyakagamanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Account of the Journey to Pālileyyaka is concluded.

Aṭṭhārasavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Eighteen Grounds

468. Yathā dhammo tathā tiṭṭhāhīti yathā dhammo ca vinayo ca ṭhito, tathā tiṭṭha, dhammavādīpakkhe tiṭṭhāti attho.

468. 'Yathā dhammo tathā tiṭṭhāhi' means 'stand as the Dhamma and Vinaya stand'; that is, 'stand on the side of those who speak according to the Dhamma.'

473. “Yo [V 2.0198] paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti idaṃ sāmaggībhedassa akārake sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ye pana bhedakārakā viruddhā alajjino[M 2.0210], tesaṃ paṭibāhituṃ vaṭṭati tesaṃ santakassapi senāsanassa vināsanavacanato. “Vivittaṃ katvāpi dātabba”nti vuttattā pana yathāvuḍḍhaṃ varasenāsanaṃ adatvā vuḍḍhānampi asaññatānaṃ saññatehi vivittaṃ katvā dātabbanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

473. This statement, 'Whoever should obstruct, it is an offense of wrong conduct,' was said in reference to those who do not cause a break in harmony. But as for those who are schismatics, contentious, and shameless, it is proper to obstruct them, because of the statement about destroying even the lodging belonging to them. And because it was said, 'It should be given after having been made secluded,' it should be understood that without giving a superior lodging according to seniority, it should be given by the restrained ones to even the unrestrained elders after having made it secluded.

475. Kammavācāya osāretvāti ettha ukkhittassa bhikkhuno āpattiyāpannabhāvaṃ paṭijānitvā sammāvattanena ukkhepakānaṃ samuppannaosāraṇacchandassa pageva ñātattā paṭippassambhanakammavācāya ukkhittānuvattakā sayameva naṃ osāresunti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

475. Here, in 'having reinstated by a formal act,' it should be understood that because the desire to reinstate had already arisen in the suspending monks—this being known beforehand through the suspended monk's acknowledgment of his offense and his proper conduct—the followers of the suspended monk reinstate him themselves with the formal act of revocation.

476. Atthato apagatāti sāmaggīatthavirahitā, tucchabyañjanāti attho.

476. ‘Atthato apagatā’ means ‘devoid of the purpose of harmony’; the meaning is ‘empty expression’.

477. Appaṭicchannācāroti appaṭicchādetabbasundarācāro. Anapagatanti kāraṇato anapetaṃ. Ādātabbato gahetabbato ādāyanti ācariyavādo vuttoti āha “ādāyaṃ attano ācariyavāda”nti.

476. 'Appaṭicchannācāro' means one who has beautiful conduct that should not be concealed. 'Anapagataṃ' means not devoid of a reason. Because it is to be taken up and to be grasped, the teacher's doctrine is called 'ādāyaṃ'; therefore, he said, 'ādāyaṃ attano ācariyavādaṃ' (taking up one's own teacher's doctrine).

Aṭṭhahi dūtaṅgehīti “sotā ca hoti sāvetā ca uggahetā ca dhāretā ca viññātā ca viññāpetā ca kusalo ca sahitāsahitassa no ca kalahakārako”ti (a. ni. 8.16) evaṃ vuttehi aṭṭhahi dūtaṅgehi. Sesamettha, heṭṭhā ca sabbattha suviññeyyamevāti.

477. 'Aṭṭhahi dūtaṅgehi' means with the eight qualities of a messenger spoken of thus: 'He is a listener and one who makes others listen, one who learns and one who remembers, one who understands and one who makes others understand, he is skilled in what is beneficial and what is not, and he is not a creator of quarrels.' The rest here, and below, and everywhere, is indeed easy to understand.

Aṭṭhārasavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Eighteen Grounds is concluded.

Kosambakakkhandhakavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The Method of the Commentary on the Kosambaka Chapter is concluded.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya vimativinodaniyaṃ

Thus in the Vimatavinodanī, a sub-commentary on the Samantapāsādikā, which is the Vinaya Commentary.

Mahāvaggavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The Method of the Commentary on the Mahāvagga is concluded.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Cūḷavaggavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Cūḷavagga

1. Kammakkhandhako

The Chapter on Formal Acts

Tajjanīyakammakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Act of Rebuke

1. Cūḷavaggassa [M 2.0211][V 2.0199] paṭhame kammakkhandhake tāva “balavābalava”nti idaṃ ekapadaṃ. “Balavabalava”nti vattabbe ākāraṃ katvā “balavābalava”nti vuttaṃ. Tañca “dukkhadukkha”ntiādīsu viya atisayatthe vattatīti āha “suṭṭhu balavaṃ paṭivadathā”ti, ati viya balavaṃ katvā paṭivacanaṃ dethāti attho.

1. In the first chapter on formal acts of the Cūḷavagga, firstly, this 'balavābalava' is a single word. Although it should be stated as 'balavabalava,' it is stated as 'balavābalava' by making the 'ā' long. And since that occurs in the sense of excessiveness, just as in 'dukkhadukkha' and so on, the commentary says, 'suṭṭhu balavaṃ paṭivadathā' (retort very strongly), which means, 'Give a reply, having made it extremely strong.'

2. Pāḷiyaṃ āpatti āropetabbāti ettha kiñcāpi “mā kho tumhe āyasmanto eso ajesī”tiādike bhaṇḍanādijanake vacane paññattā kāci āpatti nāma natthi musāpesuññādīsu etassa appaviṭṭhattā, tathāpi bhikkhūhi visuṃ, saṅghamajjhe ca “mā, āvuso, bhikkhū [V 2.0200] aññamaññaṃ payojetvā bhaṇḍanādiṃ akāsi, nedaṃ appicchatādīnaṃ atthāya vattatī”ti evaṃ apaññattena vuccamānassa bhikkhuno anādariyena anoramanapaccayā vā aññavādavihesādikaraṇapaccayā vā yā āpatti hoti, sā āpatti āropetabbā diṭṭhivipannassa viyāti evamattho daṭṭhabbo.

Regarding the Pāḷi text, 'an offense is to be charged': Here, although in dispute-generating speech such as, 'Venerable sirs, do not let him win,' there is no specific offense laid down by name, because this is not included in false speech, slander, and so on; nevertheless, for a monk who is addressed by monks, either individually or in the midst of the Saṅgha, with an unprescribed statement such as, 'Friend, do not, having instigated monks against one another, create quarrels and so on; this does not conduce to the benefit of having few wishes, etc.,' whatever offense occurs due to disrespect, or due to the cause of not desisting, or due to a cause such as speaking of other things or causing vexation—that offense is to be charged, just as for one with wrong views. Thus, the meaning should be understood.

Yassa pana idaṃ vacanaṃ vināva kāyavācāhi āpannā lahukāpatti atthi, tassapi āropetabbāva. Yaṃ pana kammavācāya “attanā bhaṇḍanakārakā”ti attanā-saddaggahaṇaṃ, “yepi caññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā…pe… te upasaṅkamitvā”tiādivacanañca, taṃ vatthuvasena gahitaṃ. Yo pana sayameva bhaṇḍanakārako hoti, aññe pana bhaṇḍanakārake upasaṅkamitvā “mā kho tumhe”tiādivacanaṃ na vadati, tassāpetaṃ kammaṃ kātabbameva. Karontehi ca “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo [M 2.0212] bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Yadi saṅghassa pattakalla”ntiādināva kammavācā kātabbā. Yo ca aññepi bhikkhū kalahāya samādapeti, tassāpi evameva kammavācaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati aññesaṃ samādāpanassapi bhaṇḍanakārakatte eva pavisanato. Aññesaṃ samādāpanākārampi vatvāva, kammavācaṃ kātukāmenapi ca tehi vuttavacanatthameva gahetvā tadanuguṇaṃ yojetvāva kātabbaṃ, na idhāgatavaseneva sabbesampi idhāgatavaseneva vacanāsambhavā. Bhūtena vatthunā katameva hi avipannaṃ hoti, nāññanti gahetabbaṃ. Esa nayo niyassakammādīsupi.

1. For any monk who, even without this specific statement, has committed a light offense by body or speech, it must also be charged. In the formal act, the inclusion of the word 'oneself' in 'oneself a maker of quarrels,' and the statement 'and whatever other monks are makers of quarrels... having approached them...,' are included based on the actual circumstances. If a monk is himself a maker of quarrels but does not approach other quarrel-makers to say, 'Do not...,' and so on, this formal act must still be carried out against him. When performing it, the formal act should be stated as follows: 'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This monk of such-and-such a name is a maker of quarrels... a creator of legal questions in the Saṅgha. If the Saṅgha is ready...,' and so on. And if a monk also instigates other monks to quarrel, it is proper to perform the formal act for him in the same way, because instigating others is also included in being a maker of quarrels. And one who wishes to perform the formal act, even when stating the manner of instigation, should do so by taking the meaning of the words that were spoken and framing it accordingly, not simply by following the wording given here, because it is not possible for the wording for all cases to be based on what is given here. Indeed, only an act done based on a true matter is valid; another is not. This should be understood. This is the same method for the Act of Dependence and so on.

Tajjanīyakammakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

2. The Commentary on the Discourse on the Act of Rebuke is concluded.

Adhammakammadvādasakakathādivaṇṇanā

The Commentary Beginning with the Discourse on the Twelve Unrighteous Acts

4. Appaṭiññāya katanti vatthuṃ vā āpattiṃ vā asampaṭicchāpetvā kataṃ. Yo pana sabbesaṃ passantānaṃ eva vatthuvītikkamaṃ katvā pacchā kammakaraṇabhayena “na karomī”ti musā vadati, tassa bhikkhūnaṃ sammukhe vītikkamakaraṇameva paṭiññā. Tathato jānanatthameva paṭiññāya karaṇaṃ anuññātaṃ. Yattha pana sandeho hoti, tattha sampaṭicchāpetvāva kattabbanti gahetabbaṃ.

4. ‘Done without acknowledgment’ means done without having the matter or the offense acknowledged. As for a monk who, having committed a transgression in the very sight of all, afterwards speaks falsely out of fear that a formal act will be carried out, saying, ‘I did not do it,’ for him, the very act of transgressing in the presence of the monks is the acknowledgment. The act of acknowledgment is permitted solely for the purpose of knowing truthfully. But where there is doubt, it should be understood that it must be done only after having it acknowledged.

“Pārājikāpattiyā vā”ti idaṃ liṅganāsananimittatāya pārājikassa kammena atikicchanīyato vuttaṃ. “Saṅghādisesāpattiyā vā”ti idaṃ pana parivāsādinissāraṇakammassa āveṇikassa [V 2.0201] vijjamānattā vuttaṃ. Yaṃ pana parato “adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti…pe… tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyyā”ti (cūḷava. 6) vuttaṃ, taṃ “āyatiṃ saṃvare ṭhatvā vuṭṭhānaṃ karohī”ti ovadiyamānassa anādariyādipaccayalahukāpattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sīlavipattimūlakañhi lahukāpattiṃ āpanno idha abhedūpacārena “adhisīle sīlavipanno”ti vutto “atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno”ti ettha viya.

The phrase ‘or by a Pārājika offense’ is said because it is a cause for the destruction of the monastic sign and because a Pārājika is irremediable by a formal act. But the phrase ‘or by a Saṅghādisesa offense’ is said because of the existence of a specific formal act of rehabilitation, such as probation. As for what is stated later, ‘he is corrupt in higher virtue… he should perform an act of rebuke,’ that is said in reference to a light offense caused by disrespect and so forth on the part of one being advised, ‘Having established yourself in future restraint, you should effect your rehabilitation.’ For a monk who has committed a light offense rooted in corruption of virtue is here called ‘corrupt in higher virtue’ by means of a metaphor of non-distinction, just as in the case of ‘corrupt in view due to an extreme view.’

Yathā ca diṭṭhiṃ gahetvā voharantassa “ito diṭṭhito oramāhī”ti avatvā katakammaṃ kevalāya diṭṭhivipattiyā katattā anāpattiyā kataṃ nāma adhammakammaṃ hoti, evaṃ sīlavipattiṃ āpajjitvā lajjidhamme [M 2.0213] okkante yathādhammaṃ vuṭṭhāya saṃvare ṭhātukāmassa kataṃ tajjanīyādikammaṃ kevalāya sīlavipattiyā katattā adesanāgāminiyā kataṃ nāma adhammakammaṃ hoti. Teneva niyassakammepi “apissu bhikkhū pakatā parivāsaṃ dentā”tiādinā saṃvare aṭṭhānameva kammanimittabhāvena vuttaṃ. Adantaṃ damanatthameva hi tajjanīyādikammāni anuññātānīti. Keci pana “adesanāgāminiyāti idaṃ pārājikāpattiṃyeva sandhāya vuttaṃ, na saṅghādisesa”nti (sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.4) vadanti, taṃ sukkapakkhe “desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā kataṃ hotī”ti iminā vacanena virujjhati. Saṅghādisesassāpi ca pariyāyato desanāgāminivohāre gayhamāne “āpattiyā kataṃ hotī”ti vuttavārato imassa vārassa viseso na siyā, aṭṭhakathāyampettha visesabhāvo na dassito. Tasmā vuttanayenevettha adhippāyo gahetabbo.

And just as a formal act performed for one who makes declarations after adopting a wrong view, without having said, ‘Desist from this view!’, is an unrighteous act called ‘done in the absence of an offense’ because it was done solely on account of a corruption of view; so too, for a monk who, having fallen into a corruption of virtue, has entered into the state of a conscientious person, has rehabilitated himself according to the Dhamma, and desires to stand in restraint, a formal act of rebuke and so forth, if performed, is an unrighteous act called ‘done for a non-confessable offense’ because it was done solely on account of the corruption of virtue. For that very reason, even in the case of the act of dependence, it is said with the words ‘Would the monks, being of normal status, impose probation…’ and so on, that not standing in restraint is itself the reason for the formal act. For the formal acts of rebuke and so forth are permitted solely for the purpose of taming the untamed. However, some say, ‘This phrase “for a non-confessable offense” is said in reference to a Pārājika offense only, not a Saṅghādisesa.’ That statement contradicts this statement in the positive section: ‘it is done for a confessable offense.’ And if the term ‘confessable’ were to be taken as applying to a Saṅghādisesa offense by extension, there would be no distinction between this case and the case stated as ‘it is done for an offense’; and in the commentary, no distinction is shown here. Therefore, the meaning here should be understood in the way that has been explained.

6. Sabbānipīti tajjanīyaniyassapabbājanīyakammāni tīṇipi. Aññakammassa vatthunāti tajjanīyato aññassa kammassa vatthunā aññakammakaraṇaṃ nāma koci dosopi na hotīti adhippāyo. Kāraṇamāha “kasmā”tiādinā.

6. ‘All’ refers to the three acts: rebuke, dependence, and banishment. ‘With the grounds for another act’ means that there is no fault whatsoever in performing another act with the grounds for an act other than the act of rebuke; this is the meaning. He states the reason with ‘Why?’ and so on.

8. Pannalomāti patitamānalomā.

8. ‘With fallen hair’ means with the hair of conceit having fallen.

Adhammakammadvādasakakathādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the section beginning with the account of the twelve unrighteous acts is concluded.

Niyassakammakathādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Section Beginning with the Account of the Act of Dependence

11. Niyassakamme pāḷiyaṃ apissūti apicāti imasmiṃ atthe nipātasamudāyo. Nissāya [V 2.0202] te vatthabbanti ettha keci kalyāṇamittāyattavuttitaṃ sandhāya vuttanti vadanti, aññe pana nissayaggahaṇamevāti, ubhayenapissa serivihāro na vaṭṭatīti dīpitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

11. In the Pāḷi text on the act of dependence, the word ‘apissū’ is a collection of particles in the sense of ‘apica’ (and also). Regarding ‘You should dwell in dependence,’ some say this is said with reference to a livelihood dependent on a good friend, while others say it is said with reference only to the taking of dependence. It should be understood that it is shown thus: in either case, for that monk, dwelling at will is not allowable.

21. Pabbājanīyakamme “pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhetū”ti idaṃ pakkamanādiṃ akatvā sammāvattantānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ.

21. Regarding the act of banishment, this statement, ‘Let the act of banishment be revoked,’ is said with respect to those who are conducting themselves well without having departed and so forth.

33. Paṭisāraṇīyakamme [M 2.0214] neva bhikkhuvacanaṃ, na gihivacananti ettha pariyāyatopi bhikkhū parakhuṃsanaṃ na vadanti, gahaṭṭhā pana sarūpeneva akkosituṃ samatthāpi upakārīsu akāraṇaṃ evarūpaṃ na vadanti, tvaṃ gihiguṇatopi parihīnoti adhippāyo.

33. In the act of reconciliation, regarding ‘neither the word of a monk nor the word of a householder,’ the meaning is this: even indirectly, monks do not revile another. But householders, though able to revile directly, do not speak such a thing without reason towards their benefactors. You are inferior even to the virtue of householders.

39. “Aṅgasamannāgamo purimehi asadiso”ti iminā tajjanīyādīnaṃ vuttakāraṇamattena idaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti dīpeti. Idha vuttena pana gihīnaṃ alābhāya parisakkanādinā aṅgena tānipi kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti gahetabbaṃ. Ettha ca “saddhaṃ pasannaṃ dāyakaṃ kārakaṃ saṅghupaṭṭhākaṃ hīnena khuṃsetī”ti vuttattā tādisesu gihīsu khuṃsanādīhi gihipaṭisaṃyuttehi eva aṅgehi kammārahatā, na ārāmikaceṭakādīsu khuṃsanādīhi. Tatthāpi dāyakādīsu khamāpitesu kammārahatā natthi, āpatti ca yattha katthaci desetuṃ vaṭṭati. Yo ce tikkhattuṃ khamāpiyamānopi na khamati, akatakammenapi dassanūpacāre āpatti desetabbā. So ce kālakato hoti, desantaraṃ vā gato, gatadisā na ñāyati, antarāmagge vā jīvitantarāyo hoti, katakammenapi akatakammenapi saṅghamajjhe yathābhūtaṃ viññāpetvā khamāpetvā āpatti desetabbāti vadanti. Dhammikapaṭissavassa asaccāpane pana tesaṃ santikaṃ gantvā “mayā asamavekkhitvā paṭissavaṃ katvā so na saccāpito, taṃ me khamathā”tiādinā khamāpane vacanakkamo ñāpetabbo.

39. By this, ‘The endowment with factors is dissimilar to the former ones,’ it is shown that it is not allowable to perform this act merely for the reasons stated for the acts of rebuke and so forth. Here, however, it should be understood that it is allowable to perform even those acts by means of the factor stated here, such as striving for the non-gain of householders. And here, since it is said, ‘One reviles a faithful, devoted donor, a benefactor, or a supporter of the Saṅgha with something base,’ worthiness for the formal act comes about only through factors connected with householders, such as reviling, in regard to such householders, not through reviling monastery attendants, servants, and so forth. Even in that case, if the donors and so forth have been asked for forgiveness, there is no worthiness for the formal act; and it is allowable to confess the offense anywhere. If someone, though being asked for forgiveness three times, does not forgive, the offense should be confessed within the range of sight even by a monk on whom the formal act has not been performed. If that person has died, or has gone to another country and the direction of their departure is not known, or there is a danger to life on the way, then by a monk on whom the formal act has been performed as well as by one on whom it has not been performed, the offense should be confessed in the midst of the Saṅgha after making it known truthfully and asking for forgiveness, so they say. But in the case of not making true a righteous promise, one should go to them, and the sequence of words for asking forgiveness should be known, beginning with: ‘I, having made a promise without due consideration, did not make it true. Forgive me for that fault.’

41. Pāḷiyaṃ maṅkubhūto nāsakkhi cittaṃ gahapatiṃ khamāpetunti tiṃsayojanamaggaṃ puna gantvāpi mānathaddhatāya yathābhūtaṃ dosaṃ āvikatvā akhamāpanena “nāhaṃ khamāmī”ti tena paṭikkhitto maṅkubhūto khamāpetuṃ na sakkhi, so punadeva sāvatthiṃ paccāgantvāpi mānaniggahatthāyeva punapi satthārā pesito purimanayeneva khamāpetuṃ asakkonto punāgacchi. Athassa bhagavā “asantaṃ bhāvanamiccheyyā”tiādināva (dha. pa. 73) dhammaṃ desetvā mānanimmathanaṃ katvā anudūtadānaṃ anuññāsīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

41. In the Pāḷi text, regarding “Being dispirited, he was not able to persuade the householder Citta to forgive,” it should be understood thus: even after going again on the thirty-yojana road, due to his stiff pride, by not revealing the fault as it truly was and by not asking for forgiveness, he was rejected by that householder with the words, “I do not forgive.” Being dispirited, he was not able to persuade him to forgive. Even after returning again to Sāvatthī, he was sent again by the Teacher for the very purpose of crushing his pride. Being unable to persuade him to forgive in the same way as before, he came again. Then the Blessed One, having taught the Dhamma with the verse beginning, “One might wish for esteem from the unworthy,” crushed his pride and permitted the sending of a suitable messenger.

42. “No [V 2.0203] ce khamati…pe… āpattiṃ desāpetabbo”ti vuttattā pageva gahaṭṭho khamati ce, dassanūpacāre āpattidesanākiccaṃ natthīti gahetabbaṃ.

42. Since it is said, “If he does not forgive… he should be made to confess the offense,” it should be understood that if the householder forgives at the very outset, there is no duty of confessing the offense within the range of sight.

46. Ukkhepanīyakammesu [M 2.0215] tīsu ariṭṭhavatthusmiṃ āpattiṃ āropetvāti visuṃ saṅghamajjheva pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissajjanapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ, samanubhāsanapariyosāne pācittiyaṃ vā āpattiṃ āropetvā. Etthāpi kammavācāya “tathāhaṃ bhagavatā”tiādi vatthuvasena vuttaṃ. Yena yena pakārena diṭṭhigatikā vohariṃsu, tena tena pakārena yojetvā kammavācā kātabbā. Gahaṇākāraṃ pana vināpi “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, itthannāmassa bhikkhuno pāpikaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ, so taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjati, yadi saṅghassa pattakalla”nti evaṃ sāmaññatopi kammavācaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati.

46. In the three acts of suspension, regarding the case of Ariṭṭha, “having imposed an offense on him” means having imposed an offense—either a dukkaṭa, because of not abandoning a bad view, separately or in the midst of the Saṅgha; or a pācittiya at the end of the admonition. Here too, in the formal act text, the passage beginning “Thus I, by the Blessed One…” is said only by way of the case. In whatever manner those holding wrong views spoke, the formal act text should be performed by connecting it with that very manner. However, even without the specific manner of holding the view, it is allowable to perform the formal act text even generally, thus: “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. For the bhikkhu of such a name, a bad view has arisen. He does not abandon that view…”

65. “Yaṃ diṭṭhiṃ nissāya bhaṇḍanādīni karotī”ti iminā diṭṭhiṃ nissāya uppannāni eva bhaṇḍanādīni idha adhippetāni, na kevalānīti dasseti. Yo pana “bhaṇḍanādīnaṃ karaṇe doso natthī”ti diṭṭhiko hutvā bhaṇḍanādiṃ karoti, sāpissa diṭṭhi eva hoti, tassapi appaṭinissagge kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati.

65. By this, “Based on which view one engages in quarrels, etc.,” it is shown that here, only quarrels and so forth that have arisen depending on a view are intended, not mere quarrels. But as for one who engages in quarrels and so forth, having the view, “There is no fault in engaging in quarrels, etc.,” that view of his is also a view indeed. For him too, in the case of not abandoning it, it is allowable to perform the formal act.

Niyassakammakathādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourse on the Act of Dependence and so forth is concluded.

Kammakkhandhakavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The Method of Explaining the Chapter on Acts is concluded.

2. Pārivāsikakkhandhako

2. The Chapter on Probation

Pārivāsikavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Pārivāsika Duties

75. Pārivāsikakkhandhake [M 2.0216][V 2.0204] antamaso mūlāyapaṭikassanārahādīnampīti ādi-saddena mānattārahamānattacārikaabbhānārahe saṅgaṇhāti. Te hi pārivāsikānaṃ, pārivāsikā ca tesaṃ pakatattaṭṭhāne eva tiṭṭhanti. Adhotapādaṭṭhapanakanti yattha ṭhatvā pāde dhovanti, tādisaṃ dāruphalakakhaṇḍādiṃ. Pādaghaṃsananti sakkharakathalādiṃ. “Vattaṃ karontī”ti ettakamattasseva vuttattā saddhivihārikādīhipi abhivādanādiṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati.

In the Chapter on Probation, regarding the phrase ‘even those deserving reinstatement to the root, etc.’: by the word ‘etc.’ (ādi), it includes those deserving mānatta, those undergoing mānatta, and those deserving restoration. For they stand in the position of an ordinary monk to the probationers, and the probationers stand in the position of an ordinary monk to them. ‘A stand for unwashed feet’ means a piece of wooden board or the like, where, having stood, they wash their feet. ‘A foot-scraper’ means a piece of stone, a potsherd, or the like. Because only this much is stated, ‘they perform the duties,’ it is not proper for even co-residents and others to perform acts like salutation.

“Pārisuddhiuposathe kariyamāne”ti idaṃ pavāraṇādivasesu saṅghe pavārente anupagatachinnavassādīhi kariyamānapārisuddhiuposathampi sandhāya vuttaṃ. Attano pāḷiyāti navakānaṃ purato.

75. The phrase ‘When the Pārisuddhi Uposatha is being performed’ is said with reference also to the Pārisuddhi Uposatha being performed by those who have not undertaken the rains-residence, those whose rains-residence has been broken, and so on, when the Saṅgha is performing the Pavāraṇā on the Pavāraṇā days. ‘By one's own Pāḷi text’ means in front of the junior monks.

“Pārivāsikassevā”ti idaṃ abbhānārahapariyosāne sabbe garukaṭṭhe sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tesampi paccekaṃ oṇojanassa anuññātattā tadavasesā pakatattā eva taṃ na labhanti.

The phrase ‘only for the one on probation’ is said with reference to all those subject to a grave offense, ending with those deserving restoration. Why? Because for them too, food set aside from the previous day (oṇojana) is individually permitted; therefore, the remaining ones, who are ordinary monks, do not receive it.

Catussālabhattanti bhojanasālāya paṭipāṭiyā diyyamānabhattaṃ. Hatthapāse ṭhitenāti dāyakassa hatthapāse paṭiggahaṇaruhanaṭṭhāneti adhippāyo. Mahāpeḷabhattepīti mahantesu bhattapacchiādibhājanesu ṭhapetvā diyyamānabhattesupi.

‘A meal from the four halls’ (catussālabhattaṃ) means a meal given in order in the dining hall. ‘By one standing within hand-reach’ (hatthapāse ṭhitena): the intention is, in a place where receiving is valid, within the hand-reach of the donor. ‘Even in the case of a meal from a large basket’ (mahāpeḷabhattepi): also in the case of meals given after being placed in large containers such as large food baskets and so on.

76. Pāpiṭṭhatarāti pārājikāpattīti ukkaṃsavasena vuttaṃ. Sañcarittādipaṇṇattivajjato pana sukkavissaṭṭhādikā lokavajjāva, tatthāpi saṅghabhedādikā pāpiṭṭhatarā eva.

The statement, ‘The more wicked (pāpiṭṭhatarā) is a pārājika offense,’ is said by way of maximization. However, worldly offenses (lokavajja) such as the emission of semen are more wicked than offenses by designation (paṇṇattivajja) such as acting as a go-between (sañcaritta); and even among those, causing a schism in the Saṅgha and so on are indeed even more wicked.

“Kammanti [V 2.0205] pārivāsikakammavācā”ti etena kammabhūtā vācāti kammavācā-saddassa atthopi siddhoti veditabbo. Savacanīyanti ettha “sadosa”nti (sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga. 3.76) atthaṃ vadati. Attano vacane pavattanakammanti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo, “mā pakkamāhī”ti vā “ehi vinayadharānaṃ sammukhībhāva”nti vā [M 2.0217] evaṃ attano āṇāya pavattanakakammaṃ na kātabbanti adhippāyo. Evañhi kenaci savacanīye kate anādarena atikkamituṃ na vaṭṭati, buddhassa saṅghassa āṇā atikkantā nāma hoti.

76. By the text ‘Kamma means the formal act of probation (pārivāsikakammavācā)’, it should be known that the meaning of the word kammavācā as ‘speech that has become an act’ is also established. In the word savacanīyaṃ, the particle ‘sa’ conveys the meaning of ‘one's own’. The meaning here should be understood as ‘an act that occurs because of one's own word’. The intention is that an act that occurs by one's own authority, such as saying, ‘Do not depart,’ or ‘Come into the presence of the experts in the Vinaya,’ should not be done. For if such an act enforceable by one's own word has been done by someone, it is not proper to transgress it disrespectfully; it would be called a transgression of the command of the Buddha and the Saṅgha.

Rajohatabhūmīti paṇṇasālāvisesanaṃ. Paccayanti vassāvāsikacīvaraṃ. Senāsanaṃ na labhatīti vassaggena na labhati.

‘A place where the dust has been removed’ (rajohata-bhūmi) means a dwelling such as a leaf-hut. ‘Requisite’ (paccayaṃ) means the rains-residence robe. ‘He does not receive a dwelling’ (senāsanaṃ na labhati) means he does not receive it according to his seniority in the rains-residence.

Apaṇṇakapaṭipadāti aviraddhapaṭipadā. Sace vāyamantopīti ettha avisayabhāvaṃ ñatvā avāyamantopi saṅgayhati.

‘The certain practice’ (apaṇṇakapaṭipadā) means the unerring practice. In the phrase ‘even if one strives,’ one who does not strive, having known it to be beyond his capacity, is also included.

81. Avisesenāti pārivāsikukkhittakānaṃ sāmaññena. Pañcavaṇṇacchadanabaddhaṭṭhānesūti pañcappakāracchadanehi channaṭṭhānesu.

‘Without distinction’ (avisesena) means in common with those on probation (pārivāsika) and those suspended (ukkhittaka). ‘In places bound with five-colored coverings’ (pañcavaṇṇacchadanabaddhaṭṭhānesu) means in places roofed with five kinds of coverings.

Obaddhanti uṭṭhānādibyāpārapaṭibaddhaṃ. Pīḷitanti attho. Mañce vā pīṭhe vāti ettha vā-saddo samuccayattho, tena taṭṭikācammakhaṇḍādīsu dīghāsanesupi nisīdituṃ na vaṭṭatīti dīpitaṃ hoti.

81. ‘Bound’ (obaddhaṃ) means afflicted by being tied to the business of attending upon others and so on; this is the meaning. In the phrase ‘on a bed or a chair,’ the word ‘or’ (vā) has a conjunctive sense. By this, it is shown that it is not proper to sit even on long seats such as rush-mats, pieces of hide, and so on.

Na vattabhedadukkaṭanti vuḍḍhatarassa jānantassāpi vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ natthīti dasseti. “Vattaṃ nikkhipāpetvā”ti idaṃ pārivāsādimeva sandhāya vuttaṃ.

‘No dukkaṭa offense for breaking the duty’ shows that for a more senior monk, even though he knows, there is no dukkaṭa offense for breaking the duty. The phrase ‘having had the duty laid down’ is said with reference only to probation (pārivāsa) and so on.

Pārivāsikavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourse on the duties of one on probation is concluded.

Pārivāsikakkhandhakavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The method for the explanation of the Chapter on Probation is concluded.

3. Samuccayakkhandhako

The Chapter on Collection

Sukkavissaṭṭhikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account on Emission of Semen

97. Samuccayakkhandhake [M 2.0218][V 2.0206] vedayāmahanti jānāpemi ahaṃ, ārocemītiattho. Anubhavāmītipissa atthaṃ vadanti. Purimaṃ pana pasaṃsanti āropanavacanattā. Ārocetvā nikkhipitabbanti dukkaṭaparimocanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Keci pana “tadaheva puna vattaṃ samādiyitvā aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpetukāmassa ratticchedaparihāratthampī”ti vadanti.

97. In the Samuccaya Chapter, as for vedayāmahanti (I declare), the meaning is: 'I make known, I announce.' Some also say its meaning is 'I experience.' However, they praise the former meaning, because it is a word of announcing. 'Having announced, it should be set aside' is said for the purpose of release from the dukkaṭa offense. Some, however, say: 'It is also said for the purpose of preventing the breach of night for one who, on that very day, having undertaken the observance again, wishes to cause the dawn to arise.'

“Sabhāgā bhikkhū vasantī”ti vuttattā visabhāgānaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne vattaṃ asamādiyitvā bahi eva kātumpi vaṭṭatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā”ti idaṃ vihāre bhikkhūnaṃ sajjhāyādisaddasavanūpacāravijahanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. “Mahāmaggato okkammā”ti idaṃ maggapaṭipannānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ upacārātikkamanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Gumbena vātiādi dassanūpacāravijahanatthaṃ.

Because it is said, 'Monks of the same communion dwell,' it should be understood that it is not proper for monks not of the same communion to perform the observance outside without having undertaken it in their dwelling place. 'Having gone beyond two clod-throws' is said for the purpose of abandoning the range of hearing the sound of chanting and so forth of the monks in the monastery. 'Having stepped aside from the main road' is said for the purpose of going beyond the proximity of monks traveling on the road. 'By a thicket,' and so forth, is said for the purpose of abandoning the range of sight.

“Sopi kenaci kammena pure aruṇe eva gacchatī”ti iminā ārocanāya katāya sabbesupi bhikkhūsu vihāragatesu ūne gaṇe caraṇadoso vā vippavāsadoso vā na hoti ārocitattā sahavāsassāti dasseti. Tenāha “ayañcā” tiādi. Abbhānaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti katampi akatameva hotīti attho.

By this text, 'He too goes at dawn itself on some business,' it is shown that when the announcement has been made, even if all the monks have gone outside the monastery, there is neither the fault of conduct in a deficient group nor the fault of living separately, because the purpose of co-residence is the announcement. Therefore, he said, 'And this,' and so forth. As for 'It is not proper to perform rehabilitation,' the meaning is that even if it is performed, it is as if not performed.

Sukkavissaṭṭhikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Account on Emission of Semen is concluded.

Paṭicchannaparivāsakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account on Concealed Probation

102. Suddhassāti sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ anāpannassa, tato vuṭṭhitassa vā. Aññasminti suddhantaparivāsavasena [V 2.0207] āpattivuṭṭhānato aññasmiṃ āpattivuṭṭhāne. Pāḷiyaṃ “paṭikassito saṅghena udāyi bhikkhu antarā ekissā āpattiyā…pe… mūlāyapaṭikassanā”ti idaṃ karaṇavasena vipariṇāmetvā mūlāyapaṭikassanāya paṭikassitoti yojetabbaṃ. Atha vā “mūlāya paṭikassanā khamati saṅghassā”ti uttarapadena saha paccattavaseneva yojetumpi vaṭṭati.

102. As for suddhassa (of a pure one): of one who has not incurred a similar saṅghādisesa offense, or who has emerged from it. As for aññasmiṃ (in another): in another emergence from an offense, other than the emergence from an offense by way of suddhanta probation. In the Pāḷi, this text, 'The monk Udāyi was recalled by the Saṅgha in the interval of one offense... up to... reinstatement to the root,' should be construed by changing it into the instrumental case, thus: 'recalled by means of reinstatement to the root.' Or else, it is also proper to connect it with the following word in the nominative case, thus: 'Reinstatement to the root is approved by the Saṅgha.'

“Udāyiṃ [M 2.0219] bhikkhuṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā…pe… mūlāya paṭikassitvā”ti ettha antarā ekissā āpattiyā hetubhūtāya udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ mūlāya paṭikassitvā mūladivase ākaḍḍhitvā tassā antarāpattiyā samodhānaparivāsaṃ detūti yojanā. Āvikārāpetvā vissajjetabboti tassa atekicchabhāvaṃ teneva saṅghassa pākaṭaṃ kāretvā lajjigaṇato viyojanavasena vissajjetabbo.

Here in the text, 'Having reinstated the monk Udāyi to the root... in the interval of one offense...': because of one intervening offense which was the cause, having reinstated the monk Udāyi to the root, having drawn back the root days, the construction is: 'Let them give combined probation for that intervening offense.' As for 'Having caused him to make it manifest, he should be dismissed': having caused the incurable nature of that monk to be made manifest to the Saṅgha by that very monk, he should be dismissed by way of separation from the group of scrupulous monks.

Sataṃ āpattiyoti kāyasaṃsaggādivasena ekadivase āpannā sataṃ āpattiyo. Dasasatanti sahassā āpattiyo. Rattisataṃ chādayitvānāti yojetabbo. Sabbaparivāsakammavācāvasāneti heṭṭhā dassitānaṃ dvinnaṃ suddhantaparivāsānaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ samodhānaparivāsānañcāti imesaṃ sabbesaṃ parivāsānaṃ kammavācāpariyosāne. Purimanayenevāti paṭicchannaparivāse vuttanayena.

As for sataṃ āpattiyo (a hundred offenses): a hundred offenses incurred in a single day by way of bodily contact and so forth. As for dasasataṃ (ten hundred): a thousand offenses. It should be construed thus: 'having concealed for a hundred nights.' As for sabbaparivāsakammavācāvasāne (at the conclusion of the formal act of all probations): at the conclusion of the formal act of all these probations, namely, of the two suddhanta probations and the three samodhāna probations shown below. As for purimanayeneva (by the very same previous method): by the method stated in the section on concealed probation.

Vihārūpacāratopīti bahigāme bhikkhūnaṃ vihārūpacāratopi. “Dve leḍḍupātā atikkamitabbā”ti idaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ savanūpacārātikkamanaṃ vuttaṃ. Gāmassāti na vuttanti gāmassa upacāraṃ muñcituṃ vaṭṭatīti na vuttaṃ. Tena gāmūpacāre ṭhitāpi tattha dassanasavanūpacāre atikkamitvā ṭhitā bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca tassā ratticchedaṃ na karontīti dīpeti.

As for vihārūpacāratopi (even from the monastery's vicinity): even from the monastery's vicinity for monks in an outlying village. This text, 'Two clod-throws should be passed beyond,' refers to the monks' passing beyond the range of hearing. As for 'gāmassa' (of the village) is not said: it is not said that it is proper to leave the village's vicinity. Thereby it shows that even monks and nuns standing within the village's vicinity do not cause a breach of night for her, provided they have passed beyond the range of sight and hearing there.
