300. 'There is no access' means there is not enough space for walking all around outside the inner chamber. 'Having pierced the tree' means having pierced the trimmed heartwood near the top. 'Katvā' means having inserted it into the hole. Only a support-post made by driving in heartwood pegs, as if it were made allowable, is called a 'movable wall-base'. 'To establish it on the ground for support' means to make it stand on the ground by its base, having raised it with the head of a peg to bear an equal load outside, alongside the old wall-base. 'For protection' means for protecting the place of a hut plastered inside and out from being soaked by rain. 'Kiṭika' is a screen made of palm leaves and so on. 'Pounded clay' is said for the purpose of closing a hole where rain leaks.

Ubhatokuṭṭaṃ nīharitvā katapadesassāti yathā bahi ṭhitā ujukaṃ anto nisinne na passanti, evaṃ dvārābhimukhaṃ pidahanavasena bhittiñca aññato dvārañca yojetvā kataṭṭhānaṃ vadati. Samantā pariyāgāroti samantato āviddhapamukhaṃ. Vaṃsaṃ datvāti purisappamāṇe pāde nikhaṇitvā tesaṃ upari piṭṭhivaṃsasadisaṃ passavaṃsaṃ ṭhapetvā osāretvā. Ekaṃ daṇḍakoṭiṃ atiuccāya vihārabhittikoṭiyā ekaṃ koṭiṃ nīce vaṃsapiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhapanavasena daṇḍake pasāretvā. Cakkalayutto kiṭikoti kavāṭaṃ viya vivaraṇathakanasukhatthaṃ cakkalabandhakiṭikaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ ugghāṭanakiṭikanti āpaṇādīsu anatthikakāle ukkhipitvā, upari ca bandhitvā pacchā otaraṇakiṭikaṃ, kappasīsehi vā upatthambhanīhi ukkhipitvā pacchā otaraṇakiṭikampi.

'Of a place made by removing the wall on both sides' refers to a place made by joining a wall and a door from another side in such a way as to block the doorway, so that those standing outside cannot see those sitting straight inside. 'Samantā pariyāgāro' is a porch that is open all around. 'Having given a rafter' means having planted posts of a man's height, and on top of them, having placed and lowered a side-rafter similar to a ridge-pole; and having spread out the poles by way of placing one end at the very high edge of the monastery wall and one end on the low rafter-back. 'Cakkalayuttokiṭika' is a screen fitted with a wheel mechanism for the ease of opening and closing, like a door-leaf. In the Pāḷi, 'ugghāṭanakiṭika' is a screen in shops and so on that is lowered later, after being lifted up and fastened above when not needed. Alternatively, it is also a screen that is lowered later, after being propped up with forked supports.

301. Pānīyaṃ otappatīti pānīyabhājanesu ṭhapitapānīyaṃ ātapena santappati.

301. 'The drinking water is heated' means the water placed in drinking water vessels is heated by the sun's heat.

303. Tayo vāṭeti tayo parikkhepe. Veḷuvāṭanti sabbaṃ dāruparikkhepaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Kaṇṭakavāṭanti sabbasākhāparikkhepaṃ.

303. 'Three fences' means three enclosures. By 'bamboo fence' is included every wooden enclosure. By 'thorn fence' is included every branch enclosure.

305. Āloko antaradhāyīti yo buddhārammaṇāya pītiyā ānubhāvena mahanto obhāso ahosi, yena cassa padīpasahassena viya vigatandhakāro maggo ahosi, so bahinagare chavasarīrasamākulaṃ duggandhaṃ bībhacchaṃ āmakasusānaṃ pattassa bhayena pītivege mandībhūte antaradhāyi.

305. 'The light disappeared' means: that great radiance which had arisen through the power of joy that has the Buddha as its object, and by which his path had become free of darkness as if by a thousand lamps, disappeared when the force of his joy weakened due to fear upon his reaching the raw charnel ground outside the city, which was crowded with corpses, foul-smelling, and repulsive.

Sataṃ [M 2.0240] hatthīti gāthāya hatthino satasahassānīti evaṃ paccekaṃ sahassa-saddena yojetvā attho ñātabbo. Padavītihārassāti “buddhaṃ vandissāmī”ti ratanattayaṃ uddissa gacchato ekapadavītihārassa[V 2.0228], tappaccayakusalaphalassāti attho. Tassa soḷasamo bhāgo kalaṃ nāma, taṃ soḷasiṃ kalaṃ yathāvuttā hatthiādayo sabbe nāgghanti nārahanti, nidassanamattañcetaṃ. Anekasatasahassabhāgampi nāgghanti.

In the verse beginning, 'A hundred elephants,' the meaning should be understood by connecting each item with the word 'thousand,' thus: 'a hundred thousand elephants.' 'Of a single footstep' means: of the fruit of the wholesome kamma conditioned by a single footstep of one going having directed his mind to the Triple Gem with the thought, 'I will pay homage to the Buddha.' The sixteenth part of that is called a 'kala.' All the aforementioned elephants and so on are not worth, are not equal to, that sixteenth part. And this is merely an illustration. They are not worth even a part beyond a hundred thousand.

Andhakāro antaradhāyīti puna balavapītiyā āloke samuppanne antaradhāyi. Āsattiyoti taṇhāyo. Vayakaraṇanti deyyadhammamūlaṃ navakammaṃ.

'The darkness disappeared' means it disappeared when the light arose again due to strong joy. 'Āsattiyo' means cravings. 'Vayakaraṇaṃ' means the value of things to be given, new work.

309. Dadeyyāti navakammaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ vihāre issariyaṃ dadeyyāti attho. Dinnoti navakammaṃ kātuṃ vihāro dinno, vihāre navakammaṃ dinnanti vā attho.

309. 'One should give new work' means: one should give authority in the monastery to supervise the new work. 'Given' means: the monastery is given in order to do the new work; or alternatively, the meaning is: the new work in the monastery is given.

313-4. Santhāgāreti sannipātamaṇḍape. Okāseti nivāsokāse. Uddissa katanti saṅghaṃ uddissa kataṃ. Gihivikaṭanti gihīhi kataṃ paññattaṃ, gihisantakanti attho.

'In a council hall' means in assembly halls. 'Places' means dwelling places. 'Made with a designation' means made having designated it for the Saṅgha. 'Prepared by householders' means made and spread by householders; the meaning is that it belongs to householders.

Vihārānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the discourse concerning the allowance of monasteries is concluded.

Senāsanaggāhakathāvaṇṇanā

Elucidation of the Discourse on the Assigner of Lodgings.

318. “Chamāsaccayena chamāsaccayenā”ti idaṃ dvikkhattuṃ paccayadānakālaparicchedadassanaṃ, evaṃ uparipi. “Taṃ na gāhetabba”nti vacanassa kāraṇamāha “paccayeneva hi ta”ntiādinā, paccayaññeva nissāya tattha vasitvā paṭijagganā bhavissantīti adhippāyo.

318. This twice-stated phrase, 'At the passing of six months, at the passing of six months,' is for showing the demarcation of the time for offering requisites; the same is also true for the text above. To show the reason for the statement, 'That should not be accepted,' he stated the words beginning with, 'For by the requisite itself...' The meaning is: relying only on the requisite, one will dwell there and the act of maintaining it will occur.

Ubbhaṇḍikāti ukkhittabhaṇḍā bhavissanti. Dīghasālāti caṅkamanasālā. Maṇḍalamāḷoti upaṭṭhānasālā. Anudahatīti pīḷeti. “Adātuṃ na labbhatī”ti iminā sañcicca adadantassa paṭibāhane pavisanato dukkaṭanti dīpeti.

`Ubbhaṇḍikā` means: they will have their goods packed up. `Dīghasālā` means: a walking hall. `Maṇḍalamāḷo` means: an assembly hall. `Anudahati` means: it oppresses. By this phrase, 'It is not allowable not to give,' he shows that for one who intentionally does not give, there is a dukkaṭa offense for engaging in refusal.

“Na [M 2.0241] gocaragāmo ghaṭṭetabbo”ti vuttamevatthaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “na tattha manussā vattabbā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Vitakkaṃ chinditvāti “iminā nīhārena gacchantaṃ disvā nivāretvā paccaye dassantī”ti evarūpaṃ vitakkaṃ anuppādetvā. Bhaṇḍappaṭicchādananti paṭicchādanabhaṇḍaṃ. Sarīrappaṭicchādanacīvaranti attho. “Suddhacittattāva anavajja”nti idaṃ pucchitakkhaṇe kāraṇācikkhanaṃ [V 2.0229] sandhāya vuttaṃ na hoti asuddhacittassapi pucchitapañhavisajjane dosābhāvā. Evaṃ pana gate maṃ pucchissantītisaññāya agamanaṃ sandhāya vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

`Na gocaragāmo ghaṭṭetabbo` (The alms-round village should not be disturbed)—to clarify this very meaning that was stated, the words beginning with `na tattha manussā vattabbā` (the people there should not be spoken to) were said. `Vitakkaṃ chinditvā` (having cut off the thought) means: without giving rise to a thought of this kind, 'Seeing him going in this manner, they will stop him and give requisites.' `Bhaṇḍappaṭicchādanaṃ` means an item for covering; the meaning is a robe that covers the body. This statement, `Suddhacittattāca anavajjaṃ` (And because of purity of mind, it is blameless), is not said with reference to explaining the reason at the moment of being asked, because even for one with an impure mind, there is no fault in answering a question that is asked. However, it should be understood that it was said with reference to his coming with the perception, 'If I go in this way, they will question me.'

Paṭijaggitabbānīti khaṇḍaphullapaṭisaṅkharaṇasammajjanādīhi paṭijaggitabbāni. Muddavedikāyāti cetiyassa hammiyavedikāya ghaṭākārassa upari caturassavedikāya. Kasmā pucchitabbantiādi yato pakatiyā labhati. Tatthāpi pucchanassa kāraṇasandassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ.

`Paṭijaggitabbāni` (They should be maintained) means: they should be maintained by means of repairing what is broken and split, sweeping, and so on. `Muddavedikāya` (On the crowning railing) means: on the square railing above the pot-shaped element on the terrace-railing of the cetiya. The words beginning with `Kasmā pucchitabbaṃ` (Why should one ask?) are stated because one obtains it naturally. Even in that case, it was said in order to show the reason for asking.

Paṭikkammāti vihārato apasakkitvā. Tamatthaṃ dassento “yojanadviyojanantare hotī”ti āha. Upanikkhepaṃ ṭhapetvāti vaḍḍhiyā kahāpaṇādiṃ ṭhapetvā, khettādīni vā niyametvā. Iti saddhādeyyeti evaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayena saddhāya dātabbe vassāvāsikalābhavisayeti attho.

`Paṭikkamma` means: having withdrawn from the monastery. Showing that meaning, he said, 'It is within one or two yojanas.' `Upanikkhepaṃ ṭhapetvā` (having placed a deposit) means: having placed kahāpaṇas and so forth for interest, or having designated fields and so forth. `Iti saddhādeyye` (Thus, in a faith-offering) means: the meaning is, in the matter of the rains-residence gain that should be given with faith, in the manner stated below.

Vatthu panāti tatruppāde uppannarūpiyaṃ, tañca “tato catupaccayaṃ paribhuñjathā”ti dinnakhettādito uppannattā kappiyakārakānaṃ hatthe “kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ paribhuñjathā”ti dāyakehi dinnavatthusadisaṃ hotīti āha “kappiyakārakānaṃ hī”tiādi.

`Vatthu pana` (As for the property, however) means: the gold and silver that has arisen from the produce of that place. And since that arises from a field, etc., that was given with the words, 'From that, you may use the four requisites,' it is similar to an item given by donors into the hands of the stewards with the words, 'You may use the allowable goods.' Therefore, he stated the words beginning with, `kappiyakārakānaṃ hi` (For to the stewards...).

Saṅghasuṭṭhutāyāti saṅghassa hitāya. Puggalavasenāti “bhikkhū cīvarena kilamantī”ti evaṃ puggalaparāmāsavasena, na “saṅgho kilamatī”ti evaṃ saṅghaparāmāsavasena.

`Saṅghasuṭṭhutāya` means: for the welfare of the Sangha. `Puggalavasena` (by way of individuals) means: by way of considering individuals, as in 'The monks are troubled by [lack of] robes,' and not by way of considering the Sangha, as in 'The Sangha is troubled.'

“Kappiyabhaṇḍavasenā”ti sāmaññato vuttamevatthaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “cīvarataṇḍulādivaseneva cā”ti vuttaṃ. Ca-kāro cettha pana-saddatthe vattati, na samuccayattheti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Puggalavaseneva, kappiyabhaṇḍavasena ca apalokanappakāraṃ dassetuṃ “taṃ pana evaṃ kattabba”ntiādi vuttaṃ.

`Kappiyabhaṇḍavasenā` (By way of allowable goods)—to clarify this very meaning that was stated generally, it was stated, `cīvarataṇḍulādivaseneva cā` (and only by way of robes, rice, etc.). Here, the particle `ca` functions in the meaning of the particle `pana` (however); it should be understood that it does not function in the conjunctive sense. In order to show the manner of announcement by way of individuals and by way of allowable goods, the words beginning with `taṃ pana evaṃ kattabbaṃ` (But that should be done thus) were stated.

Cīvarapaccayaṃ sallakkhetvāti saddhādeyyatatruppādādivasena tasmiṃ vassāvāse labbhamānaṃ cīvarasaṅkhātaṃ paccayaṃ “ettaka”nti paricchinditvā. Senāsanassāti senāsanaggāhāpanassa. “Navako vuḍḍhatarassa, vuḍḍho ca [M 2.0242] navakassā”ti idaṃ senāsanaggāhassa attanāva attano gahaṇaṃ asāruppanti vuttaṃ, dve aññamaññaṃ gāhessantīti adhippāyo. Aṭṭhapi soḷasapi jane sammannituṃ vaṭṭatīti ekakammavācāya sabbepi ekato sammannituṃ vaṭṭati. Niggahakammameva hi saṅgho saṅghassa na karoti. Teneva sattasatikakkhandhake “ubbāhikakammasammutiyaṃ aṭṭhapi janā ekatova sammatāti.

`Cīvarapaccayaṃ sallakkhetvā` (having considered the robe-requisite) means: having demarcated as 'this much' the requisite known as robes, which is obtainable during that rains-residence by way of faith-offerings, produce of that place, and so on. `Senāsanassa` (of the lodging) means: of the assigning of lodgings. This statement, `Navako vuḍḍhatarassa, vuḍḍho ca navakassā` (The junior for the senior, and the senior for the junior), was said because it is unsuitable for the assigner of lodgings to take one for himself by himself; the meaning is that two will cause each other to take one. `Aṭṭhapi soḷasapi jane sammannituṃ vaṭṭati` (It is allowable to appoint eight or sixteen people) means: it is allowable to appoint all of them together with a single kammavācā. Indeed, it is only an act of censure that the Sangha does not perform for the Sangha. Therefore, in the Sattasatikakkhandhaka, it is stated, 'In the formal appointment for the act of suspension, even eight people were appointed all at once.'

Āsanagharanti [V 2.0230] paṭimāgharaṃ. Maggoti upacārasīmabbhantaragate gāmābhimukhamagge katasālā vuccati. Evaṃ pokkharaṇīrukkhamūlādīsupi.

`Āsanagharaṃ` means: an image house. `Maggo` refers to a hall built on the road facing the village, situated within the precincts of the boundary. The same is also true in the case of ponds, the foot of trees, and so on.

Labhantīti tatravāsino bhikkhū labhanti. Vijaṭetvāti “ekekassa pahonakappamāṇena viyojetvā. Āvāsesu pakkhipitvāti “ito uppannaṃ asukasmiṃ asukasmiñca āvāse vasantā pāpetvā gaṇhantū”ti vācāya upasaṃharitvā. Pavisitabbanti mahālābhe pariveṇe vasitvāva lābho gahetabboti adhippāyo.

`Labhanti` means: the monks residing there receive. `Vijaṭetvā` (having disentangled) means: having separated it in a sufficient amount for each one. `Āvāsesu pakkhipitvā` (having placed it in the dwellings) means: having presented it verbally, saying, 'Let the monks dwelling in such-and-such a monastery receive and take the gain that has arisen from here.' `Pavisitabbaṃ` (One should enter) means: the meaning is that the gain should be taken only after having resided in the monastic compound where there is great gain.

Ayampīti ettha yo paṃsukūliko paccayaṃ vissajjeti. Teneva vissaṭṭho ayaṃ cīvarapaccayopīti yojanā. Pādamūle ṭhapetvā sāṭakaṃ dentīti paccayadāyakā denti. Etena gahaṭṭhehi pādamūle ṭhapetvā dinnampi paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Atha vassāvāsikaṃ demāti vadantīti ettha paṃsukūlikānaṃ na vaṭṭatīti ajjhāharitvā yojetabbaṃ. Vassaṃvutthabhikkhūnanti paṃsukūlikato aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ.

Here, in `ayampi`, the construction is: the rag-robe-wearing monk who relinquishes a requisite—by that very one, this robe-requisite is also relinquished. `Pādamūle ṭhapetvā sāṭakaṃ denti` means the donors of the requisites give. By this, it is shown that what is given by householders, having placed it at the feet, is also allowable for rag-robe-wearing monks. Here, in the phrase `Atha vassāvāsikaṃ demāti vadantī`, it should be connected by supplying the words 'it is not allowable for rag-robe-wearing monks.' `Vassaṃvutthabhikkhūnaṃ` means for monks other than the rag-robe-wearing ones.

Upanibandhitvā gāhāpetabbanti idha rukkhādīsu vasitvā cīvaraṃ gaṇhathāti paṭibandhaṃ katvā gāhetabbaṃ.

`Upanibandhitvā gāhāpetabbaṃ` means it should be caused to be taken after making the stipulation, 'Having dwelt here among the trees and so forth, take the robe.'

Pāṭipadaaruṇatotiādi vassūpanāyikadivasaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Antarāmuttakaṃ pana pāṭipadaṃ atikkamitvāpi gāhetuṃ vaṭṭati. Nibaddhavattaṃ ṭhapetvāti sajjhāyamanasikārādīsu nirantarakaraṇīyesu kattabbaṃ katikavattaṃ katvā. Kasāvaparibhaṇḍanti kasāvarasehi bhūmiparikammaṃ.

The words beginning with `Pāṭipadaaruṇato` were said with reference to the day of entering the rains-residence. The `antarāmuttaka`, however, is allowable to be accepted even after the first day has passed. `Nibaddhavattaṃ ṭhapetvā` means having made an agreement regarding the duties to be done in continuously practicable matters such as recitation, attention, and so on. `Kasāvaparibhaṇḍaṃ` means the preparation of the ground with astringent liquids.

Tividhampīti pariyattipaṭipattipaṭivedhavasena tividhampi. Sodhetvāti ācārādīsu upaparikkhitvā. Ekacārikavattanti bhāvanākammaṃ. Tañhi gaṇasaṅgaṇikaṃ pahāya ekacārikeneva vattitabbattā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Dasavatthukakathā [M 2.0243] nāma appicchakathā, santuṭṭhi, paviveka, asaṃsagga, vīriyārambha, sīla, samādhi, paññā, vimutti, vimuttiñāṇadassanakathāti imā dasa.

`Tividhampi` means threefold by way of learning, practice, and penetration. `Sodhetvā` means having well examined conduct and so forth. `Ekacārikavattaṃ` is the work of meditation. For, having abandoned association with groups, it should be practiced only by one who wanders alone; hence, it is said thus. The tenfold discourse is: the discourse on having few desires, on contentment, on seclusion, on non-association, on the arousal of energy, on virtue, on concentration, on wisdom, on liberation, and the discourse on the knowledge and vision of liberation—these ten.

Dantakaṭṭhakhādanavattanti dantakaṭṭhamāḷake nikkhittesu dantakaṭṭhesu “divase divase ekameva dantakaṭṭhaṃ gahetabba”ntiādinā (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.109) adinnādāne dantaponakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ vattaṃ. Pattaṃ vā…pe… na kathetabbanti pattaguttatthāya vuttaṃ. Visabhāgakathāti tiracchānakathā. Khandhakavattanti [V 2.0231] vattakkhandhake (cūḷava. 365) āgataṃ piṇḍacārikavattato avasiṭṭhavattaṃ tassa “bhikkhācāravatta”nti visuṃ gahitattā.

`Dantakaṭṭhakhādanavattaṃ` is the duty stated in the discourse on the tooth-cleaner in the training rule on taking what is not given, regarding the tooth-sticks placed in the tooth-stick stand, beginning with 'Each day, only one tooth-stick should be taken.' `Pattaṃ vā…pe… na kathetabbaṃ` is said for the sake of protecting the bowl. `Visabhāgakathā` means talk that is contrary to the path and fruition. `Khandhakavattaṃ` is the remaining duty from the duty of going for alms that comes in the Vattakkhandhaka, because that 'duty of the alms-round' is taken separately.

Idāni yaṃ dāyakā pacchimavassaṃvutthānaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ denti, tattha paṭipajjanavidhiṃ dassetuṃ “pacchimavassūpanāyikadivase panā”ti āraddhaṃ. Āgantuko sace bhikkhūti cīvare gāhite pacchā āgato āgantuko bhikkhu. Pattaṭṭhāneti vassaggena pattaṭṭhāne. Paṭhamavassūpagatāti āgantukassa āgamanato puretarameva pacchimikāya vassūpanāyikāya vassūpagatā. Laddhaṃ laddhanti punappunaṃ dāyakānaṃ santikā āgatāgatasāṭakaṃ.

Now, in order to show the procedure to be practiced regarding the rains-residence robe that donors give to those who have observed the later rains-residence, it is begun with, `pacchimavassūpanāyikadivase pana`. `Āgantuko sace bhikkhu` means a visiting monk who arrived after the robe had been caused to be taken. `Pattaṭṭhāne` means at the place reached according to seniority in the rains. `Paṭhamavassūpagatā` means the monks who entered the rains-residence on the later rains-entry day, even before the arrival of the visiting monk. `Laddhaṃ laddhaṃ` means the cloth that comes again and again from the donors.

Neva vassāvāsikassa sāminoti chinnavassattā vuttaṃ. Paṭhamameva katikāya katattā “neva adātuṃ labhantī”ti vuttaṃ, dātabbaṃ vārentānaṃ gīvā hotīti adhippāyo. Tesameva dātabbanti vassūpagatesu aladdhavassāvāsikānaṃ ekaccānameva dātabbaṃ.

`Neva vassāvāsikassa sāmino` is said because their rains-residence is broken. Because an agreement was made from the very beginning, it is said, `neva adātuṃ labhanti`; the meaning is that for those who prevent it, it becomes a forfeiture. `Tesameva dātabbaṃ` means that among those who have entered the rains, it should be given only to some who did not get the rains-residence robe.

Bhatiniviṭṭhanti pānīyupaṭṭhānādibhatiṃ katvā laddhaṃ. Saṅghikaṃ panātiādi kesañci vādadassanaṃ. Tattha apalokanakammaṃ katvā gāhitanti “chinnavassānaṃ vassāvāsikañca idāni uppajjanakavassāvāsikañca imesaṃ dātuṃ ruccatī”ti anantare vuttanayena apalokanaṃ katvā gāhitaṃ saṅghena dinnattā vibbhantopi labhati. Pageva chinnavasso. Paccayavasena gāhitaṃ pana temāsaṃ vasitvā gahetuṃ attanā, dāyakehi ca anumatattā bhatiniviṭṭhampi chinnavassopi vibbhantopi na labhatīti keci ācariyā vadanti. Idañca pacchā vuttattā pamāṇaṃ. Teneva vassūpanāyikadivase eva dāyakehi dinnavassāvāsikaṃ gahitabhikkhuno vassacchedaṃ akatvā vāsova heṭṭhā vihito, na pānīyupaṭṭhānādibhatikaraṇavattaṃ. Yadi hi taṃ [M 2.0244] niviṭṭhameva siyā, bhatikaraṇameva vidhātabbaṃ. Tasmā vassaggena gāhitaṃ chinnavassādayo na labhantīti veditabbaṃ.

`Bhatiniviṭṭhaṃ` means that which is obtained by performing a service such as providing water. The phrase `Saṅghikaṃ pana` and so forth is to show the view of some teachers. Therein, `apalokanakammaṃ katvā gāhitaṃ` means the robe is caused to be taken after making an announcement in the manner stated immediately before, 'It is approved to give the rains-residence robe of the monks whose rains are broken and the rains-residence robe that is now to arise to these monks.' Because it is given by the Sangha, even one who has disrobed receives it; how much more so a monk whose rains are broken. But as for that which is caused to be taken by way of requisites, some teachers say that because it is consented to by oneself and by the donors to be taken after residing for three months, one who has entered service, one whose rains are broken, and one who has disrobed do not receive it. And this, because it is stated later, is the authority. For that very reason, for a monk who has taken the rains-residence robe given by donors on the very day of entering the rains, only residence without breaking the rains is prescribed below, not the duty of performing service such as providing water. For if that robe were indeed obtained by entering into service, the performance of service itself should be prescribed. Therefore, it should be understood that monks whose rains are broken and others do not receive what is caused to be taken according to seniority in the rains.

“Saṅghikaṃ hotī”ti etena vutthavassānampi vassāvāsikabhāgo saṅghikato amocito tesaṃ vibbhamena saṅghiko hotīti dasseti. Labhatīti “mama pattabhāgaṃ etassa dethā”ti dāyake sampaṭicchāpenteneva saṅghikato viyojitaṃ hotīti vuttaṃ.

By `Saṅghikaṃ hoti`, it is shown that even for those who have completed the rains-residence, if their share of the rains-residence robe is not released from being the Sangha's property, it becomes the Sangha's property upon their disrobing. The word `labhati` ('he receives') is stated because the share becomes separated from being the Sangha's property only by causing the donors to consent thus: 'Give the share that has come to me to this monk.'

Varabhāgaṃ sāmaṇerassāti tassa paṭhamagāhattā, therena pubbe paṭhamabhāgassa gahitattā, idāni gayhamānassa dutiyabhāgattā ca vuttaṃ.

`Varabhāgaṃ sāmaṇerassa` is said because he is the first to take it, because the elder had previously taken the first portion, and because the portion now being taken is the second portion.

Senāsanaggāhakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the discourse concerning the allocator of lodgings is concluded.

Upanandavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of Upananda

319. Pāḷiyaṃ [V 2.0232] ubhayattha paribāhiroti kamena ubhayassapi muttattā vuttaṃ, na sabbathā ubhayato paribāhirattā. Tenāha “pacchime…pe… tiṭṭhatī”ti.

319. In the Pāḷi, `ubhayattha paribāhiro` is said because one is sequentially freed from both, not because one is outside of both in every way. Therefore, it is said: `pacchime…pe… tiṭṭhati`.

320. Yaṃ tiṇṇaṃ pahotīti mañcapīṭhavinimuttaṃ yaṃ āsanaṃ tiṇṇaṃ sukhaṃ nisīdituṃ pahoti, idaṃ pacchimadīghāsanaṃ. Ettha mañcapīṭharahitesu asamānāsanikāpi tayo nisīdituṃ labhanti. Mañcapīṭhesu pana dve. Adīghāsanesu mañcapīṭhesu samānāsanikā eva dve nisīdituṃ labhanti duvaggasseva anuññātattā.

320. As for `yaṃ tiṇṇaṃ pahoti`: whatever seat, free from a couch or chair, is sufficient for three to sit comfortably, this is the smallest long seat. Here, on these seats devoid of couches and chairs, even three monks who do not have the same seating are able to sit. But on couches and chairs, only two. On couches and chairs that are not long seats, only two who have the same seating are able to sit, because only a group of two is permitted.

Hatthinakho heṭṭhābhāge etassa atthīti hatthinakho, pāsādo. Pāsādassa nakho nāma heṭṭhimabhāgo pādanakhasadisattā, so sabbadisāsu anekehi hatthirūpehi samalaṅkato ṭhito. Tassūpari kato pāsādo hatthikumbhe patiṭṭhito viya hotīti āha “hatthikumbhe patiṭṭhita”nti. Suvaṇṇarajatādivicitrānīti saṅghikasenāsanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Puggalikaṃ pana suvaṇṇādivicitraṃ bhikkhussa sampaṭicchitumeva na vaṭṭati “na kenaci pariyāyena jātarūparajataṃ sāditabba”nti (mahāva. 299) vuttattā. Tenevettha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “saṅghikavihāre vā puggalikavihāre vā”ti na [M 2.0245] vuttaṃ, gonakādiakappiyabhaṇḍavisaye eva vuttaṃ ekabhikkhussāpi tesaṃ gahaṇe dosābhāvā. Gihivikaṭanīhārenāti gihīhi katanīhārena, gihīhi attano santakaṃ attharitvā dinnaniyāmenāti attho. Labbhantīti nisīdituṃ labbhanti.

Because in its lower part there is an elephant figure, it is called Hatthinakha, a palace. The lower part of the palace is called 'nakha' because of its resemblance to a foot-nail; it stands adorned on all sides with many elephant figures. The palace built on top of it is as if established on an elephant's frontal globe, thus it is said, 'established on an elephant's frontal globe.' 'Adorned with gold, silver, etc.' is said with reference to a lodging belonging to the Saṅgha. But a personal lodging adorned with gold, etc., is not allowable for a bhikkhu even to accept, because it is said, 'Gold and silver are not to be accepted in any way.' For that very reason, it is not said in the commentary here, 'in a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha or in a personal monastery'; it is said only in the context of unallowable items such as goat's-hair blankets, because there is no fault even for a single bhikkhu in accepting them. 'By the method of what is prepared by householders' means by the method prepared by householders; the meaning is, by the rule of what is given after householders have spread out their own property. 'Are obtained' means they are obtained for sitting.

Upanandavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the story of Upananda is concluded.

Avissajjiyavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The commentary on the story of items not to be relinquished.

321. Arañjaroti bahuudakagaṇhanikā mahācāṭi, jalaṃ gaṇhitumalanti arañjaro.

321. As for `arañjaro`: it is a large pot that holds much water. Because it is able to take water (`jalaṃ gaṇhituṃ alaṃ`), it is called `arañjaro`.

Thāvarena ca thāvarantiādīsu pañcasu koṭṭhāsesu purimadvayaṃ thāvaraṃ, pacchimattayaṃ garubhaṇḍanti veditabbaṃ. Samakameva detīti ettha ūnakaṃ dentampi vihāravatthusāmantaṃ gahetvā dūrataraṃ dukkhagopaṃ vissajjetuṃ vaṭṭatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vakkhati hi “bhikkhūnaṃ ce mahagghataraṃ…pe… sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 321). Jānāpetvāti bhikkhusaṅghassa [V 2.0233] jānāpetvā, apaloketvāti attho. “Nanu tumhākaṃ bahutarā rukkhāti vattabba”nti idaṃ sāmikesu attano bhaṇḍassa mahagghataṃ ajānitvā dentesu taṃ ñatvā theyyacittena gaṇhato avahāro hotīti vuttaṃ.

In the five portions beginning with 'immovable with immovable,' the first two are to be known as immovable property, and the last three as heavy goods. Here, regarding 'gives equally,' it should be understood that even when giving less, it is allowable to take the vicinity of the monastery grounds and relinquish a more distant and difficult-to-guard property. For it will be said: 'If a more valuable thing... for the bhikkhus... it is allowable to accept.' 'Having informed' means having informed the community of bhikkhus; the meaning is 'having asked permission.' The statement, 'Should you not say, "You have more trees"?' is said because if the owners, not knowing the great value of their property, are giving it, for one who, knowing this, accepts it with a thieving mind, it becomes a theft.

Vihārena vihāro parivattetabboti savatthukena aññesaṃ bhūmiyaṃ katapāsādādinā, avatthukena vā savatthukaṃ parivattetabbaṃ. Avatthukaṃ pana avatthukeneva parivattetabbaṃ. Kevalaṃ pāsādassa bhūmito athāvarattā. Evaṃ thāvaresupi thāvaravibhāgaṃ ñatvāva parivattetabbaṃ.

As for 'A monastery should be exchanged for a monastery': a monastery with its site may be exchanged either for one with a site, or for one without a site, such as a palace, etc., built on another's land. But a monastery without a site should be exchanged only for one without a site. This is because a mere palace is not immovable with respect to the land. Likewise, even with immovable properties, they should be exchanged only after knowing the division of immovable properties.

“Kappiyamañcā sampaṭicchitabbā”ti iminā suvaṇṇādivicittaṃ akappiyamañcaṃ “saṅghassā”ti vuttepi sampaṭicchituṃ na vaṭṭatīti dasseti. “Vihārassa demā”ti vutte saṅghassa vaṭṭati, na puggalassa khettādi viyāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Etesūti mañcādīsu. Kappiyākappiyaṃ vuttanayamevāti āsandītūlikādivinicchayesu vuttanayameva. Akappiyaṃ vāti āsandīādi, pamāṇātikkantaṃ [M 2.0246] bimbohanādi ca. Mahagghaṃ kappiyaṃ vāti suvaṇṇādivicittaṃ kappiyavohārena dinnaṃ.

By this text, 'Allowable couches are to be accepted,' it is shown that it is not allowable to accept an unallowable couch adorned with gold, etc., even when it is said, 'It is for the Saṅgha.' When it is said, 'We give to the monastery,' it is allowable for the Saṅgha, but not for an individual, like a field, etc.—this should be understood. `Etesu` means among couches, etc. 'Allowable and unallowable is just the method stated' means it is just the method stated in the decisions concerning high-backed chairs, mattresses, etc. 'Or unallowable' means a high-backed chair, etc., and a pillow, etc., that exceeds the proper size. 'Or valuable and allowable' means something adorned with gold, etc., given with the designation of 'allowable'.

“Kāḷaloha…pe… bhājetabbo”ti vuttattā vaṭṭakaṃsalohamayampi bhājanaṃ puggalikampi sampaṭicchitumpi pariharitumpi vaṭṭati puggalapariharitabbasseva bhājetabbattāti vadanti. Taṃ upari “kaṃsalohavaṭṭalohabhājanavikati saṅghikaparibhogena vā gihivikaṭā vā vaṭṭatī”tiādikena mahāpaccarivacanena virujjhati. Imassa hi “vaṭṭalohakaṃsalohānaṃ yena kenaci kato sīhaḷadīpe pādaggaṇhanako bhājetabbo”ti vuttassa mahāaṭṭhakathāvacanassa paṭikkhepāya taṃ mahāpaccarivacanaṃ pacchā dassitaṃ. Tasmā vaṭṭalohakaṃsalohamayaṃ yaṃ kiñci pādaggaṇhanakavārakampi upādāya abhājanīyameva. Gihīhi diyyamānampi puggalassa sampaṭicchitumpi na vaṭṭati. Pārihāriyaṃ na vaṭṭatīti pattādiparikkhāraṃ viya sayameva paṭisāmetvā paribhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭati. Gihisantakaṃ viya ārāmikādayo ce sayameva gopetvā viniyogakāle ānetvā paṭinenti, paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. “Paṭisāmetvā bhikkhūnaṃ dethā”ti vattumpi vaṭṭati.

Because it is said, 'Black metal... is to be divided,' some say that a vessel made of bronze or white copper is allowable for an individual to accept and to carry about, because only what is to be carried about by an individual is to be divided. That statement contradicts the Mahāpaccari statement above, which begins, 'A modified vessel of bronze or white copper is allowable for the Saṅgha's use or as prepared by householders.' For that Mahāpaccari statement was later shown in order to reject this Mahā-aṭṭhakathā statement which says, 'A foot-washer made by anyone in the island of Sīhaḷa from bronze or white copper is to be divided.' Therefore, anything made of bronze or white copper, up to and including a foot-washer, is not to be divided at all. Even if given by householders, it is not allowable for an individual to accept. 'It is not for carrying about' means it is not allowable to store it oneself and use it, like a bowl and other requisites. If monastery attendants and others guard it themselves, as if it were the property of householders, and bring it at the time of use and then take it back, it is allowable to use it. It is also allowable to say, 'Store it and give it to the bhikkhus.'

Paṇṇasūci nāma lekhanīti vadanti. “Attanā laddhānipī”tiādinā paṭiggahaṇe doso natthi, pariharitvā paribhogova āpattikaroti dasseti. Yathā cettha, evaṃ upari abhājanīyavāsiādīsu attano santakesupi.

They say that `paṇṇasūci` is a stylus. By the text beginning with 'Even those obtained by oneself,' it is shown that there is no fault in accepting; only using it after carrying it about incurs an offense. Just as here, so too it should be understood above in the case of one's own property such as an adze, etc., that is not to be divided.

Anāmāsampīti [V 2.0234] suvaṇṇādimayampi sabbaṃ taṃ āmasitvāpi paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Upakkhareti upakaraṇe. Aḍḍhabāhuppamāṇā nāma aḍḍhabāhumattā. Aḍḍhabyāmamattātipi vadanti. Yottānīti cammarajjukā.

As for 'even what is not to be touched': even if it is made of gold, etc., it is allowable to use all of it even after touching it. `Upakkhare` means in the equipment. `Aḍḍhabāhuppamāṇā` means the measure of half a forearm. Some also say it is the measure of half a fathom. `Yottāni` means leather ropes.

Aṭṭhaṅgulasūcidaṇḍamattopīti tasaradaṇḍādisūciākāratanudaṇḍakamattopi. Rittapotthakopīti alikhitapotthako. Idañca paṇṇappasaṅgena vuttaṃ.

'Even a stick the size of an eight-finger needle' means even a thin stick having the shape of a needle, such as an arrow shaft and so forth. 'Even an empty palm-leaf manuscript' means an unwritten palm-leaf manuscript. And this was said in connection with leaves.

“Ghaṭṭanaphalakaṃ ghaṭṭanamuggaro”ti idaṃ rajitacīvaraṃ ekasmiṃ maṭṭhe daṇḍamuggare veṭhetvā ekassa maṭṭhaphalakassa upari ṭhapetvā upari aparena maṭṭhaphalakena nikujjitvā eko upari akkamitvā tiṭṭhati. Dve janā upari phalakaṃ dvīsu koṭīsu gahetvā aparāparaṃ ākaḍḍhanavikaḍḍhanaṃ karonti, etaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Hatthe ṭhapāpetvā hatthena paharaṇaṃ pana [M 2.0247] niṭṭhitarajanassa cīvarassa allakāle kātabbaṃ. Idaṃ pana phalakamuggarehi ghaṭṭanaṃ sukkhakāle thaddhabhāvavimocanatthanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ambaṇanti ekadoṇikanāvāphalakehi pokkharaṇīsadisaṃ kataṃ. Pānīyabhājanantipi vadanti. Rajanadoṇīti ekadārunāva kataṃ rajanabhājanaṃ. Udakadoṇīpi ekadārunāva kataṃ udakabhājanaṃ.

“A rubbing board, a rubbing mallet”: this is said with reference to a dyed robe. Having wrapped it around one smooth, handled mallet, and having placed it on top of one smooth board, another smooth board is placed face down on top, and one person, stepping on top, stands there. Two people, holding the upper board at the two ends, pull and push it back and forth; this is said in reference to this. However, striking with the hand after placing it in the hand should be done when the completely dyed robe is wet. But this rubbing with boards and mallets should be understood as something to be done when it is dry, for the purpose of releasing it from a state of stiffness. “Ambaṇa” means a water container made like a pond from boat-planks of one-trough capacity. They also call it a water vessel. A “dyeing trough” means a dyeing vessel made from a single piece of wood. A “water trough” also means a water vessel made from a single piece of wood.

Bhūmattharaṇaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti akappiyacammaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tattha bhūmattharaṇasaṅkhepena sayitumpi vaṭṭatiyeva. “Paccattharaṇagatika”nti iminā mañcādīsu attharitabbaṃ mahācammaṃ eḷakacammaṃ nāmāti dasseti.

“It is permissible to make a ground covering”: this was said with reference to an unallowable hide. In that case, it is indeed permissible also to lie down on it under the designation of a ground covering. By “belonging to the category of coverings,” it is shown that a large hide, namely a goat hide, is what should be spread on beds and the like.

Chattamuṭṭhipaṇṇanti tālapaṇṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Pattakaṭāhanti pattapacanakaṭāhaṃ.

“A parasol-handle leaf” is said with reference to a palm leaf. “A bowl-pan” means a pan for baking a bowl.

Avissajjiyavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on Things Not to Be Relinquished is concluded.

Navakammadānakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Granting of New Work

323. Pāḷiyaṃ piṇḍanikkhepanamattenātiādīsu khaṇḍaphullaṭṭhāne mattikāpiṇḍaṭṭhapanaṃ piṇḍanikkhepanaṃ nāma. Navakammanti navakammasammuti. Aggaḷavaṭṭi nāma kavāṭabandho. Chādanaṃ nāma tiṇādīhi gehacchādanaṃ. Bandhanaṃ nāma daṇḍavalliādīhi chadanabandhanameva. Catuhatthavihāreti vitthārappamāṇato vuttaṃ. Ubbedhato pana anekabhūmakattā vaḍḍhakīhatthena vīsatihatthopi [V 2.0235] nānāsaṇṭhānavicittopi hoti. Tenassa catuvassikaṃ navakammaṃ vuttaṃ. Evaṃ sesesupi.

323. In the Pāḷi, in phrases such as “merely by placing a lump”: the placing of a lump of clay in a broken or cracked spot is called “placing a lump” (piṇḍanikkhepana). “New work” (navakamma) means the designation for new work. “Door-bar” (aggaḷavaṭṭi) is a fastening for the door-leaf. “Roofing” (chādana) is the roofing of a monastery with grass and so on. “Binding” (bandhana) is just the binding of the roof with poles, vines, and so on. “A four-cubit monastery” is stated in terms of the measurement of its breadth. But as for its height, because of being multi-storied, it can be twenty cubits by a carpenter's cubit and can be variegated with various shapes. Therefore, for it, new work to be completed in four years is stated. It is the same also for the remaining monasteries.

Pāḷiyaṃ sabbe vihāreti bhummatthe upayogabahuvacanaṃ. Ekassa sabbesu vihāresu navakammaṃ detīti attho. Sabbakālaṃ paṭibāhantīti navakammikā attano gāhitaṃ varaseyyaṃ sampattānaṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ akatvā utukālepi paṭibāhanti.

In the Pāḷi, the phrase “all monasteries” (sabbe vihāre) is an accusative plural in the locative sense. The meaning is: “He gives new work in all monasteries.” “They obstruct at all times” means: the monks undertaking the new work, having taken an excellent lodging for themselves, do not act according to seniority towards the monks who have arrived, and they obstruct them even during the season.

“Sace so āvāso jīratī”tiādi pāḷimuttakavinicchayo. Mañcaṭṭhānaṃ datvāti mañcaṭṭhānaṃ puggalikaṃ datvā. Tibhāganti tatiyabhāgaṃ. Evaṃ vissajjanampi thāvarena thāvaraparivattanaṭṭhāne eva pavisati, na itarathā sabbasenāsanānaṃ [M 2.0248] vinassanato. Sace saddhivihārikānaṃ dātukāmo hotīti sace so saṅghassa bhaṇḍakaṭṭhapanaṭṭhānaṃ vā aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ vā dātuṃ na icchati, attano saddhivihārikānaññeva dātukāmo hoti, tādisassa tuyhaṃ puggalikameva katvā jaggāti na sabbaṃ tassa dātabbanti adhippāyo. Tattha pana kattabbavidhiṃ dassento āha “kamma”ntiādi. Evañhītiādimhi vayānurūpaṃ tatiyabhāge vā upaḍḍhabhāge vā gahite taṃ bhāgaṃ dātuṃ labhatīti attho.

“If that residence deteriorates,” and so on, is a decision independent of the Pāḷi. “Having given a bed-space” means having given a bed-space as personal property. “A third part” means the third part. Even such a relinquishment enters only into the category of exchanging permanent property for permanent property; not otherwise, because of the destruction of all lodgings. “If he wishes to give to his co-residents” means: if that monk does not wish to give a place for storing goods to the Sangha or a dwelling place to other monks, but wishes to give only to his own co-residents, for such a one the intention is this: “For your own sake, only after making it personal property should you maintain it.” Thus, not all of it should be given to him. Here, explaining the procedure to be followed, he said, “an act,” and so on. In the text beginning with “Thus indeed,” the meaning is that when a third part or a half part is taken corresponding to the years, he is able to give that portion.

Yenāti tesu dvīsu bhikkhūsu yena. So sāmīti tassā bhūmiyā vihārakaraṇe sova sāmī, taṃ paṭibāhitvā itarena na kātabbanti adhippāyo. So hi paṭhamaṃ gahito. Akataṭṭhāneti cayādīnaṃ akatapubbaṭṭhāne. Cayaṃ vā pamukhaṃ vāti saṅghikasenāsanaṃ nissāya tato bahi cayaṃ bandhitvā, ekaṃ senāsanaṃ vā. Bahikuṭṭeti kuṭṭato bahi, attano kataṭṭhāneti attho.

“By whichever” means by whichever of those two monks. “He is the owner” means that in building a monastery on that Sangha land, he alone is the owner. The intention is that, having obstructed him, it should not be done by the other monk. For he was the one who took it first. “At a place not made before” means at a place where a platform and so on has not been made before. “A platform or a porch” means: relying on the Sangha's lodging, and then outside of it, having constructed a platform or a single lodging. “Outside the wall” means outside the wall; the meaning is, in a place made by oneself.

Navakammadānakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Granting of New Work is concluded.

Aññatraparibhogapaṭikkhepādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Rejection of Use by Others and so on

324. Vaḍḍhikammatthāyāti yathā tammūlagghato na parihāyati, evaṃ kattabbassa evaṃ nipphādetabbassa mañcapīṭhādino atthāya.

324. “For the purpose of value-increasing work” means: for the sake of beds, chairs, and so on, that are to be made and accomplished in such a way that their value does not diminish from their original cost.

Cakkalikanti pādapuñchanatthaṃ cakkākārena kataṃ. Paribhaṇḍakatabhūmi vāti kāḷavaṇṇādikatasaṇhabhūmi vā. Senāsanaṃ vāti mañcapīṭhādi vā.

“Cakkalikaṃ” means: something made in the shape of a wheel for the purpose of wiping the feet. “Or a prepared surface” means: or a smooth surface made of black color and so on. “Or a lodging” means: or a bed, chair, and so on.

“Tatheva [V 2.0236] vaḷañjetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti iminā nevāsikehi dhotapādādīhi vaḷañjanaṭṭhāne sañcicca adhotapādādīhi vaḷañjantasseva āpatti paññattāti dasseti.

By this statement, “Similarly, it is fitting to use,” it is shown that an offense is laid down only for one who, in a place used by resident monks with washed feet and so on, intentionally uses it with unwashed feet and so on.

“Dvārampī”tiādinā sāmaññato vuttattā dvāravātapānādayo aparikammakatāpi na apassayitabbā. Ajānitvā apassayantassapi idha lomagaṇanāya āpatti.

By the phrase beginning with “even a door,” because it is stated in general terms, doors, windows, and the like, even if unprepared, should not be leaned against. For one who leans against them unknowingly, there is an offense here countable by the number of hairs.

Aññatraparibhogapaṭikkhepādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Rejection of Use by Others and so on is concluded.

Saṅghabhattādianujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Allowance of Saṅgha Meals and so on

325. Uddesabhattaṃ [M 2.0249] nimantananti imaṃ vohāraṃ pattānīti ettha iti-saddo ādiattho, uddesabhattaṃ nimantanantiādivohāraṃ pattānīti attho. Tampīti saṅghabhattampi.

325. Herein, in the phrase “uddesabhattaṃ nimantananti imaṃ vohāraṃ pattāni,” the word “iti” has the meaning of “ādi” (and so on). The meaning is: they have attained the usage beginning with “a designated meal is an invitation.” “Tampi” means: the Saṅgha meal also.

Saṅghabhattādianujānanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Allowance of Saṅgha Meals and so on is concluded.

Uddesabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Designated Meal

Bhojanasālāyāti bhattuddesaṭṭhānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ekavaḷañjanti ekadvārena vaḷañjitabbaṃ. Nānānivesanesūti nānākulassa nānūpacāresu nivesanesu.

“In the dining hall” was said referring to the place for designating the meal. “A single compound” means: to be used via a single door. “In various dwellings” means: in the dwellings of various families, which have various precincts.

Nisinnassapi niddāyantassapīti anādare sāmivacanaṃ, vuḍḍhatare niddāyante navakassa gāhitaṃ suggahitanti attho.

“Even of one seated, even of one sleeping”—this is the genitive case in the sense of disregard. The meaning is that when a more senior monk is sleeping, what is taken by a junior monk is well-taken.

Vissaṭṭhadūtoti yathāruci vattuṃ labhanato nirāsaṅkadūto. Pucchāsabhāgenāti pucchāvacanapaṭibhāgena. “Ekā kūṭaṭṭhitikā nāmā”ti vuttamevatthaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “rañño vā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ.

A `vissaṭṭhadūta` is a messenger without hesitation because he is able to speak as he wishes. `By way of a similar question` means: by way of a counterpart to the words of the question. To make clear the very meaning that was stated as, “There is one called ‘a peak situation’,” the phrase beginning with “of the king or…” was stated.

Sabbaṃ pattassāmikassa hotīti cīvarādikampi sabbaṃ pattassāmikasseva hoti, mayā bhattameva sandhāya vuttaṃ, na cīvarādinti vatvā gahetuṃ na vaṭṭatīti attho.

The statement `Everything belongs to the owner of the bowl` means that everything, including robes and so on, belongs only to the owner of the bowl. The meaning is that it is not proper to take other items, saying, “I spoke referring only to the food, not to the robes and so on.”

Akatabhāgonāmāti [V 2.0237] āgantukabhāgo nāma, adinnapubbabhāgoti attho.

The so-called `akatabhāgo` (unmade portion) is the so-called `āgantukabhāgo` (newcomer’s portion); the meaning is a portion not previously given.

Kiṃ āharīyatīti avatvāti “katarabhattaṃ vā tayā āharīyatī”ti dāyakaṃ apucchitvā. Pakatiṭṭhitikāyāti uddesabhattaṭṭhitikāya.

`Without saying, 'What is being brought?'` means: without asking the donor, 'Which meal is being brought by you?' `By the normal procedure` means: by the procedure for the designated meal.

Uddesabhattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Designated Meal is concluded.

Nimantanabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on Invitation Meals

Vicchinditvāti [M 2.0250] “bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti padaṃ avatvā. Tenevāha “bhattanti avadantenā”ti.

‘Having cut off’ means not having said the phrase, “Take the meal.” For that very reason, he said, “by one not saying ‘meal.’”

Ālopasaṅkhepenāti ekekapiṇḍavasena, evañca bhājanaṃ uddesabhatte na vaṭṭati. Tattha hi ekassa pahonakappamāṇeneva bhājetabbaṃ.

‘By way of a summary of morsels’ means by way of each single morsel. And such a division is not allowable for a designated meal. For in that case, it should be divided only by an amount sufficient for one person.

Āruḷhāyeva mātikaṃ, saṅghato aṭṭha bhikkhūti ettha ye mātikaṃ āruḷhā, te aṭṭha bhikkhūti yojetabbaṃ. Uddesabhattanimantanabhattādisaṅghikabhattamātikāsu nimantanabhattamātikāya ṭhitivasena āruḷhe bhattuddesakena vā sayaṃ vā saṅghato uddisāpetvā gahetvā gantabbaṃ, na attano rucite gahetvāti adhippāyo. Mātikaṃ āropetvāti “saṅghato gaṇhāmī”tiādinā vuttamātikābhedaṃ dāyakassa viññāpetvāti attho.

In the phrase, ‘The register has been ascended, eight monks from the Saṅgha,’ it should be connected thus: those who have ascended the register are those eight monks. Among the registers for communal meals such as designated meals, invitation meals, and so on, regarding those who have ascended by being established in the register for invitation meals, one should go after having taken them, having had them appointed from the Saṅgha either by the meal-appointer or by oneself. The intention is that one should not go after taking those of one's own preference. ‘Having placed on the register’ means having informed the donor of the type of register mentioned, with such phrases as, ‘I take from the Saṅgha.’

Paṭibaddhakālato pana paṭṭhāyāti tattheva vāsassa nibaddhakālato paṭṭhāya.

‘But beginning from the appointed time’ means beginning from the fixed time of residence right there.

Nimantanabhattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on Invitation Meals is concluded.

Salākabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on Ticket-Meals

Upanibandhitvāti likhitvā. Gāmavasenapīti yebhuyyena samalābhagāmavasenapi. Bahūni salākabhattānīti tiṃsaṃ vā cattārīsaṃ vā bhattāni. “Sace hontī”ti ajjhāharitvā yojetabbaṃ.

‘Having bound to’ means having written. ‘Even by way of a village’ means for the most part, even by way of a village with equal gain. ‘Many ticket-meals’ means thirty or forty meals. ‘If there are’ should be supplied and connected.

Sallakkhetvāti [V 2.0238] tāni bhattāni pamāṇavasena sallakkhetvā. Niggahena datvāti dūraṃ gantuṃ anicchantassa niggahena sampaṭicchāpetvā datvā. Puna vihāraṃ āgantvāti ettha vihāraṃ anāgantvā bhattaṃ gahetvā pacchā vihāre attano pāpetvā bhuñjitumpi vaṭṭati.

‘Having marked’ means having marked those meals by way of being equal. ‘Having given with insistence’ means having given after causing one who is unwilling to go far to accept it with insistence. As for ‘having come again to the monastery,’ it is also allowable not to come to the monastery, but to take the meal and later, having had it brought to oneself in the monastery, to eat it.

Ekagehavasenāti vīthiyampi ekapasse gharapāḷiyā vasena. Uddisitvāpīti asukakule salākabhattāni tuyhaṃ pāpuṇantīti vatvā.

‘By way of a single house’ means by way of a row of houses on one side, even on a street. ‘Even having specified’ means having said, “The ticket-meals from such-and-such family will come to you.”

Vāragāmeti [M 2.0251] atidūrattā vārena gantabbagāme. Saṭṭhito vā paṇṇāsato vāti daṇḍakammatthāya udakaghaṭaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vihāravāroti sabbabhikkhūsu bhikkhatthāya gatesu vihārarakkhaṇavāro.

‘In a village-by-turns’ means in a village that should be gone to by turns due to its being very far. ‘From sixty or from fifty’ is said with reference to a water pot for the purpose of a penalty. ‘Monastery-turn’ means the turn for guarding the monastery when all the monks have gone for alms.

Tesanti vihāravārikānaṃ. Phātikammamevāti vihārarakkhaṇakiccassa pahonakapaṭipādanameva. Ekasseva pāpuṇantīti divase divase ekekasseva pāpitānīti attho.

‘For them’ means for those on monastery duty. ‘Just compensation’ means just the provision of what is sufficient for the duty of guarding the monastery. ‘They reach only one’ means the meaning is that they are caused to reach only one each day.

Rasasalākanti ucchurasasalākaṃ. “Salākavasena gāhitattā pana na sāditabbā”ti idaṃ asāruppavasena vuttaṃ, na dhutaṅgabhedavasena. “Saṅghato nirāmisasalākā…pe… vaṭṭatiyevā”ti (visuddhi. 1.26) hi visuddhimagge vuttaṃ. Aggabhikkhāmattanti ekakaṭacchubhikkhāmattaṃ. Laddhā vā aladdhā vā svepi gaṇheyyāsīti laddhepi appamattatāya vuttaṃ. Tenāha “yāvadatthaṃ labhati…pe… alabhitvā ‘sve gaṇheyyāsī’ti vattabbo”ti.

‘A ticket for juice’ means a ticket for sugarcane juice. The statement, ‘However, because it is taken by way of a ticket, it should not be enjoyed,’ is said by way of unsuitability, not by way of the breaking of an ascetic practice. For it is said in the Visuddhimagga: ‘A non-flesh ticket from the Saṅgha… is indeed allowable.’ ‘The amount of the top alms’ means the amount of alms of a single ladle. The statement, ‘Whether it is received or not, you may take it tomorrow,’ is said because of the small amount, even when it is received. Therefore, he said, ‘As much as one gets… having not received it, one should be told, “You may take it tomorrow.”’

Tatthāti tasmiṃ disābhāge. Taṃ gahetvāti taṃ vāragāme salākaṃ attano gahetvā. Tenāti disaṃgamikato aññena tasmiṃ disaṃgamike. Devasikaṃ pāpetabbāti upacārasīmāya ṭhitassa yassa kassaci vassaggena pāpetabbā. Evaṃ etesu agatesu āsannavihāre bhikkhūnaṃ bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati itarathā saṅghikato.

‘There’ means in that region. ‘Having taken it’ means having taken for oneself that ticket in the village-by-turns. ‘By him’ means by another monk, other than the one going to another region. ‘It should be delivered daily’ means it should be delivered according to seniority to whichever monk is staying within the vicinity-boundary. Thus, when these monks have not gone, it is allowable for the monks in a nearby monastery to eat it; otherwise, it is not allowable, because it belongs to the Saṅgha.

Amhākaṃ gocaragāmevāti salākabhattadāyakānaṃ gāmaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vihāre therassa pattasalākabhattanti vihāre ekekasseva ohīnattherassa sabbasalākānaṃ attano pāpanavasena pattasalākabhattaṃ.

‘In our alms-resort village’ is said in reference to the village of the donors of the ticket-meals. ‘The ticket-meal received by the elder in the monastery’ means the ticket-meal received by the single elder who was left behind in the monastery, by way of causing all the tickets to reach himself.

Salākabhattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on Ticket-Meals is concluded.

Pakkhikabhattādikathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on the Fortnightly Meal and So On

“Sve [V 2.0239] pakkho”ti ajja pakkhikaṃ na gāhetabbanti aṭṭhamiyā bhuñjitabbaṃ sattamiyā bhuñjanatthāya na gāhetabbaṃ, dāyakehi niyamitadivaseneva gāhetabbanti attho. Tenāha “sace panā”tiādi. Sve lūkhanti ajja āvāhamaṅgalādikaraṇato atipaṇītabhojanaṃ karīyati, sve tathā na bhavissati, ajjeva bhikkhū bhojessāmīti adhippāyo.

“Tomorrow is the fortnight”: this means that today the fortnightly meal should not be accepted; that which is to be eaten on the eighth day should not be accepted on the seventh day for the purpose of eating it. The meaning is that it should be caused to be accepted by the donors only on the fixed day. Therefore, he said, “But if,” and so on. “Tomorrow will be coarse”: this means that today, due to wedding ceremonies and so on, a very excellent meal is prepared, but tomorrow it will not be so. The intention is, “I will feed the monks today.”

Pakkhikabhattato [M 2.0252] uposathikassa bhedaṃ dassento āha “uposathaṅgāni samādiyitvā”tiādi. Nibandhāpitanti “asukavihāre āgantukā bhuñjantū”ti niyamitaṃ.

Wishing to show the difference of the Uposatha meal from the fortnightly meal, he says, “Having undertaken the Uposatha factors,” and so on. “Set aside” means it is designated thus: “Let visiting monks eat in such-and-such a monastery.”

Gamiko āgantukabhattampīti gāmantarato āgantvā avūpasantena gamikacittena vasitvā puna aññattha gacchantaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Āvāsikassa pana gantukāmassa gamikabhattameva labbhati. “Lesaṃ oḍḍetvā”ti vuttattā lesābhāve yāva gamanaparibandho vigacchati, tāva bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatīti ñāpitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

“A traveler is also entitled to the incoming guest meal”: this is said with reference to a monk who, having come from another village and having stayed with the unsettled mind of a traveler, goes to another place again. However, a resident monk who wishes to travel is eligible only for the traveler’s meal. Because it is said, “Having set up a pretext,” it should be understood that it is made known that in the absence of a pretext, it is allowable to eat for as long as the impediment to travel is gone.

Taṇḍulādīni pesenti…pe… vaṭṭatīti abhihaṭabhikkhattā vaṭṭati. Tathā paṭiggahitattāti bhikkhānāmena paṭiggahitattā.

“They send rice, etc.… it is permissible”: this means it is permissible because it is alms-food brought forward. “Because it was received thus” means because it was accepted under the name of alms-food.

Avibhattaṃ saṅghikaṃ bhaṇḍanti kukkuccuppattiākāradassanaṃ. Evaṃ kukkuccaṃ katvā pucchitabbakiccaṃ natthi, apucchitvā dātabbanti adhippāyo.

“Undivided property belonging to the Sangha”: this is a showing of the manner in which scruples arise. Thus, having had scruples, there is no need to ask; the intention is that it should be given without asking.

Pakkhikabhattādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Talk on the Fortnightly Meal and So On is concluded.

Senāsanakkhandhakavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The Method of the Exposition of the Senāsana Khandhaka is concluded.

7. Saṅghabhedakakkhandhako

7. The Chapter on Schism in the Sangha

Chasakyapabbajjākathādivaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Story of the Going Forth of the Six Sakyans and so on

330. Saṅghabhedakakkhandhake [M 2.0253][V 2.0240] pāḷiyaṃ anupiyaṃ nāmāti anupiyā nāma. Heṭṭhā pāsādāti pāsādato heṭṭhā heṭṭhimatalaṃ, “heṭṭhāpāsāda”ntipi pāṭho. Abhinetabbanti vapitakhettesu pavesetabbaṃ. Ninnetabbanti tato nīharitabbaṃ. Niddhāpetabbanti sassadūsakatiṇādīni uddharitabbaṃ. Ujuṃ kārāpetabbanti puñjaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ, ayameva vā pāṭho.

330. In the Saṅghabhedaka Khandhaka, in the Pāli, ‘Anupiyaṃ by name’ means the city named Anupiyā. ‘Below the palace’ means below the palace, on the lower level; ‘heṭṭhāpāsāda’ is also a reading. ‘To be led in’ means to be brought into the sown fields. ‘To be led out’ means to be removed from there. ‘To be cleared’ means weeds, etc., that destroy the crop should be removed. ‘To be made straight’ means to be made into a pile; alternatively, this itself is the reading.

332. Paradattoti parehi dinnapaccayehi pavattamāno. Migabhūtena cetasāti katthaci alaggatāya migassa viya jātena cittena.

332. ‘Sustained by others’ means subsisting on requisites given by others. ‘With a mind become like a deer’ means with a mind that has arisen like that of a deer due to non-attachment to any particular place.

333. Manomayaṃ kāyanti jhānamanena nibbattaṃ brahmakāyaṃ, “kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ pasādeyyaṃ, yasmiṃ me pasanne bahulābhasakkāro uppajjeyyā”ti paṭhamaṃ uppannaparivitakkassa mandapariyuṭṭhānatāya devadattassa tasmiṃ khaṇe jhānaparihāni nāhosi, pacchā eva ahosīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tenāha “saha cittuppādā”tiādi. Dve vā tīṇi vā māgadhakāni gāmakhettānīti ettha magadharaṭṭhe khuddakaṃ gāmakhettaṃ gāvutamattaṃ, majjhimaṃ pana diyaḍḍhagāvutamattaṃ, mahantaṃ anekayojanampi hoti. Tesu majjhimena gāmakhettena dve vā khuddakena tīṇi vā gāmakhettāni, tassa sarīraṃ tigāvutappamāṇo attabhāvoti vuttaṃ hoti.

333. ‘A mind-made body’ means the Brahma-body produced by the jhāna-mind. It should be understood that because of the weak obsession of the initial thought that arose in Devadatta—“Whom, I wonder, should I cause to have confidence, in whom, if they had confidence in me, much gain and honour would arise?”—at that moment there was no loss of jhāna for him; it occurred only later. Therefore, he said, “simultaneously with the arising of the thought,” and so on. Regarding “two or three Magadhan village-fields”: here, in the country of Magadha, a small village-field is about a gāvuta in size, a medium one is one and a half gāvutas, and a large one can be many yojanas. Among these, it means two village-fields by the measure of a medium one, or three by the measure of a small one. It is said that the individual existence of that being is three gāvutas in size.

334. Satthāroti gaṇasatthāro. Nāssassāti na etassa bhaveyya. Tanti satthāraṃ. Tenāti amanāpena. Sammannatīti cīvarādinā amhākaṃ sammānaṃ karoti, parehi vā ayaṃ satthā sammānīyatīti attho.

334. ‘Teachers’ means leaders of groups. ‘He should not have’ means ‘it should not be for him.’ `Taṃ` means the teacher. ‘By that’ means by the disagreeable. ‘Honors’ means he honors us with robes, etc., or this teacher is honored by others; this is the meaning.

335. Nāsāya [V 2.0241] pittaṃ bhindeyyunti acchapittaṃ vā macchapittaṃ vā nāsāpuṭe pakkhipeyyuṃ. Assatarīti vaḷavāya kucchismiṃ gadrabhassa jātā. Tassā hi gahitagabbhāya vijāyitumasakkontiyā udaraṃ phāletvā potakaṃ nīharanti. Tenāha “attavadhāya gabbhaṃ gaṇhātī”ti.

335. ‘They would break bile through the nose’ means they would put bear's bile or fish's bile into the nostrils. ‘A mule’ is one born from a male donkey in the womb of a mare. Indeed, when that pregnant mare is unable to give birth, they cut open her belly and take out the young one. Therefore, it is said, “She conceives a pregnancy for her own destruction.”

339. Potthanikanti churikaṃ, “khara”ntipi vuccati.

339. ‘A small knife’ means a dagger; it is also called ‘khara’.

342. Mā [M 2.0254] kuñjara nāgamāsadoti he kuñjara buddhanāgaṃ vadhakacittena mā upagaccha. Dukkhanti dukkhakāraṇattā dukkhaṃ. Itoti ito jātito. Yatoti yasmā, yantassa vā, gacchantassāti attho. Mā ca madoti mado tayā na kātabboti attho.

342. ‘O elephant, do not approach the Nāga’ means ‘O elephant, do not approach the Buddha-Nāga with a murderous mind.’ ‘Suffering’ means it is suffering because it is a cause of suffering. ‘From this’ means from this birth. ‘From which’ means ‘because,’ or it means ‘of one who is going’; this is the meaning. ‘And no intoxication’ means ‘intoxication should not be done by you’; this is the meaning.

343. Tikabhojananti tīhi bhuñjitabbaṃ bhojanaṃ, tato adhikehi ekato paṭiggahetvā bhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭanakaṃ gaṇabhojanapaṭipakkhaṃ bhojananti attho. Kokālikotiādīni devadattaparisāya gaṇapāmokkhānaṃ nāmāni. Kappanti mahāniraye āyukappaṃ, taṃ antarakappanti keci. Keci pana “asaṅkhyeyyakappa”nti.

343. ‘A meal for three’ means a meal to be eaten by three people; the meaning is that it is a meal that is the opposite of a group meal, which is not allowable for more than that number to accept and eat together. ‘Kokālika’, etc., are the names of the group leaders in Devadatta's assembly. ‘An eon’ means a life-eon in the great hell; some say it is an intermediate eon. But others say it is an ‘incalculable eon’.

Chasakyapabbajjākathādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Story of the Going Forth of the Six Sakyans and so on is concluded.

Saṅghabhedakakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Talk on Schism in the Sangha

345. Parassa cittaṃ ñatvā kathanaṃ ādesanāpāṭihāriyaṃ. Kevalaṃ dhammadesanā anusāsanīpāṭihāriyaṃ. Tadubhayampi dhammī kathā nāma. Tāya thero ovadi. Iddhividhaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ nāma. Tena sahitā anusāsanī eva dhammī kathā. Tāya thero ovadi.

345. Speaking after having known another's mind is the miracle of mind-reading. Merely teaching the Dhamma is the miracle of instruction. Both of these are called Dhamma talk. With this, the Elder Sāriputta admonished. The variety of psychic powers is called the miracle of supernormal power. Instruction together with that is indeed Dhamma talk. With this, the Elder Moggallāna admonished.

“Thullaccayaṃ desāpehī”ti idaṃ bhedapurekkhārassa uposathādikaraṇe thullaccayassa uposathakkhandhakādīsu paṭhamameva paññattattā vuttaṃ, itarathā etesaṃ ādikammikattā anāpattiyeva siyā.

This statement, ‘Have him confess the grave offense,’ was said because for a monk intent on schism, in the matter of the Uposatha and so on, the grave offense had already been laid down from the very beginning in the Uposathakkhandhaka and other texts. Otherwise, because they would be first-time offenders, there would be no offense at all.

346. Sarasīti saro. Mahiṃ vikrubbatoti mahiṃ dantehi vilikhantassa. Idañca hatthīnaṃ sabhāvadassanaṃ. Nadīsūti saresu. Bhisaṃ ghasamānassāti yojanā. Jaggatoti yūthaṃ pālentassa.

346. ‘Sarasī’ means a lake. ‘Mahiṃ vikrubbato’ means of one scraping the earth with his tusks. And this shows the nature of elephants. ‘Nadīsu’ means in lakes. The connection is with ‘eating lotus stalks’ (`bhisaṃ ghasamānassa`). ‘Jaggato’ means of one protecting the herd.

347. Dūteyyaṃ [V 2.0242] gantunti dūtakammaṃ pattuṃ, dūtakammaṃ kātunti attho. Sahitāsahitassāti yuttāyuttassa, yaṃ vattuṃ, kātuñca yuttaṃ, tattha kusalo. Atha vā adhippetānādhippetassa vacanassa kusalo, byañjanamatte na tiṭṭhati, adhippetatthameva ārocetīti attho.

347. ‘To go as a messenger’ means to undertake the duty of a messenger, that is, to perform the duty of a messenger. ‘Of the suitable and unsuitable’ means of the fitting and the unfitting; he is skilled in what is fitting to say and to do. Or alternatively, he is skilled regarding the utterance of what is intended and not intended; he does not stand on the mere expression, but communicates only the intended meaning—this is the meaning.

350. Gāthāsu [M 2.0255] jātūti ekaṃsena. Mā udapajjatha mā hotūti attho. Pāpicchānaṃ yathāgatīti pāpicchānaṃ puggalānaṃ yādisī gati abhisamparāyo. Taṃ atthajātaṃ. Imināpi kāraṇena jānāthāti devadattassa “paṇḍito”tiādinā upari vakkhamānākāraṃ dasseti.

350. In the verses, `jātu` means certainly. The meaning is: ‘May it not arise, may it not be.’ `Pāpicchānaṃ yathāgati` means: whatever kind of future destination there is for persons of evil desires. You should know that matter by this reason also. Thus, it shows the manner of Devadatta which will be spoken of later with the verse beginning ‘paṇḍito,’ and so on.

Pamādaṃ anuciṇṇoti pamādaṃ āpanno. Āsīsāyanti avassaṃbhāvīatthasiddhiyaṃ. Sā hi idha āsīsāti adhippetā, na patthanā. Īdise anāgatatthe atītavacanaṃ saddavidū icchanti.

‘Indulging in heedlessness’ means one who has fallen into heedlessness. ‘By wish’ means for the certain attainment of the goal. Indeed, here ‘wish’ is intended to mean certainty, not a mere wish. In such a case, those who know grammar desire a past tense word in a future sense.

Dubbheti dubbheyya. Visakumbhenāti ekena visapuṇṇakumbhena. Soti so puggalo. Na padūseyya visamissaṃ kātuṃ na sakkotīti attho. Bhayānakoti vipulagambhīrabhāvena bhayānako. Tenāpi dūsetuṃ na sakkuṇeyyataṃ dasseti. Vādenāti dosakathanena. Upahiṃsatīti bādhati.

‘Dubbhe’ means ‘one might corrupt.’ ‘With a pot of poison’ means with one pot full of poison. ‘So’ means that person. ‘He could not corrupt’ means he is not able to make it mixed with poison; this is the meaning. ‘Bhayānako’ means terrifying because of its vast and deep nature. By that also, it shows the inability to corrupt it. ‘By speech’ means by speaking of faults. ‘Harasses’ means afflicts.

Saṅghabhedakakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse of the Schism-maker is finished.

Upālipañhākathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Questions of Upāli

351. Na pana ettāvatā saṅgho bhinno hotīti salākaggāhāpanamattena saṅghabhedānibbattito vuttaṃ. Uposathādisaṅghakamme kate eva hi saṅgho bhinno hoti. Tattha ca uposathapavāraṇāsu ñattiniṭṭhānena, sesakammesu apalokanādikammapariyosānena saṅghabhedo samatthoti daṭṭhabbo.

351. The statement, 'However, the Saṅgha is not split by this much,' is said because a schism of the Saṅgha is not accomplished merely by causing voting tickets to be taken. Indeed, the Saṅgha is split only when a formal act of the Saṅgha, such as the Uposatha, is performed. And among those acts, it should be understood that in the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā, the schism of the Saṅgha is completed by the completion of the motion; in the remaining acts, it is completed by the conclusion of the act beginning with the announcement.

“Abhabbatā na vuttā”ti idaṃ “bhikkhave, devadattena paṭhamaṃ ānantariyakammaṃ upacita”ntiādinā ānantariyattaṃ vadatā bhagavatā tassa abhabbatāsaṅkhātā pārājikatā na paññattā. Etena āpatti viya abhabbatāpi paññattianantarameva hoti, na tato pureti dasseti. Idha pana ādikammikassapi anāpattiyā avuttattā devadattādayopi na muttāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Regarding the statement, 'The state of being incapable was not spoken of': by the Blessed One, who, in speaking of the state of being an immediately effective kamma with the words, 'Monks, by Devadatta the first immediately effective kamma was accumulated,' and so on, the state of being pārājika, known as the 'state of being incapable,' was not laid down for him. By this, it is shown that, like an offense, the state of being incapable also occurs only immediately after the laying down of the rule, and not before that. Here, however, because the state of not being an offense was not spoken of even for the first perpetrator, it should be understood that Devadatta and others are not released.

Tayo satipaṭṭhānātiādīsu tayo eva satipaṭṭhānā, na tato paranti ekassa satipaṭṭhānassa [V 2.0243] paṭikkhepova idha adhammo, na pana tiṇṇaṃ satipaṭṭhānattavidhānaṃ [M 2.0256] tassa dhammattā. Evaṃ sesesupi hāpanakoṭṭhāsesu. Vaḍḍhanesu pana cha indriyānīti anindriyassapi ekassa indriyattavidhānameva adhammo. Evaṃ sesesupi. Na kevalañca eteva, “cattāro khandhā, terasāyatanānī”tiādinā yattha katthaci viparītato pakāsanaṃ sabbaṃ adhammo. Yāthāvato pakāsanañca sabbaṃ dhammoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Pakāsananti cettha tathā tathā kāyavacīpayogasamuṭṭhāpikā arūpakkhandhāva adhippetā, evamettha dasakusalakammapathādīsu anavajjaṭṭhena sarūpato dhammesu, akusalakammapathādīsu sāvajjaṭṭhena sarūpato adhammesu ca tadaññesu ca abyākatesu yassa kassaci koṭṭhāsassa bhagavatā paññattakkameneva pakāsanaṃ “dhammo”ti ca viparītato pakāsanaṃ “adhammo”ti ca dassitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kāmañcettha vinayādayopi yathābhūtato, ayathābhūtato ca pakāsanavasena dhammādhammesu eva pavisanti, vinayādināmena pana visesetvā visuṃ gahitattā tadavasesameva dhammādhammakoṭṭhāse pavisatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

In such cases as 'three foundations of mindfulness,' the rejection of one foundation of mindfulness, saying 'there are only three foundations of mindfulness, no more than that,' is here what is non-Dhamma. The establishing of three things as foundations of mindfulness, however, is not non-Dhamma, because that is Dhamma. Thus it is also in the remaining cases of diminution. In cases of addition, however, such as 'six faculties,' the establishing of one thing that is not a faculty as a faculty is itself non-Dhamma. Thus it is also in the remaining cases. And it is not only these; anywhere, any contrary explanation, such as 'four aggregates' or 'thirteen sense-bases,' is entirely non-Dhamma. And it should be understood that any explanation according to reality is entirely Dhamma. And here, by 'explanation,' it is only the immaterial aggregates that give rise to such and such bodily and verbal exertions that are intended. Thus, it should be understood that it has been shown that herein, regarding the ten wholesome courses of action and so on, which are Dhamma by their own nature on account of being blameless; and regarding the unwholesome courses of action and so on, which are non-Dhamma by their own nature on account of being blameworthy; and regarding other indeterminate things—the explanation of any portion whatsoever only in the sequence laid down by the Blessed One is 'Dhamma,' and the contrary explanation is 'non-Dhamma.' And although herein the Vinaya and so on also enter into the categories of Dhamma and non-Dhamma by way of being explained according to reality or not according to reality, it should be understood that because they are distinguished and taken separately by names such as 'Vinaya,' only the remaining dhammas enter into the Dhamma category.

Imaṃ adhammaṃ dhammoti karissāmātiādi dhammañca adhammañca yāthāvato ñatvāva pāpicchaṃ nissāya viparītato pakāsentasseva saṅghabhedo hoti, na pana tathāsaññāya pakāsentassāti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Esa nayo “avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpentī”tiādīsupi. Tattha niyyānikanti ukkaṭṭhanti attho. “Tathevā”ti iminā “evaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyakula”ntiādinā vuttamatthaṃ ākaḍḍhati.

The statement beginning, 'We will make this non-Dhamma into Dhamma,' is said in order to show that a schism of the Saṅgha occurs only for one who, having known both Dhamma and non-Dhamma as they really are, explains them contrarily while relying on evil desire, but not for one who explains them with that perception. This is the method also in cases such as, 'they explain non-Vinaya as Vinaya.' Therein, 'leading out' (niyyānika) means 'excellent.' By this word 'just so,' it draws in the meaning spoken of in the passage beginning, 'Thus is our teachers' lineage...'

Saṃvaro pahānaṃ paṭisaṅkhāti saṃvaravinayo, pahānavinayo, paṭisaṅkhāvinayo ca vutto. Tenāha “ayaṃ vinayo”ti. “Paññattaṃ apaññatta”nti dukaṃ “bhāsitaṃ abhāsita”nti dukena atthato samānameva, tathā duṭṭhulladukaṃ garukadukena. Teneva tesaṃ “cattāro satipaṭṭhānā…pe… idaṃ apaññattaṃ nāmā”tiādinā sadisaniddeso kato. Sāvasesāpattinti avasesasīlehi sahitāpattiṃ. Natthi etissaṃ āpannāyaṃ sīlāvasesāti anavasesāpatti.

Restraint, abandoning, and reflection are spoken of as the discipline of restraint, the discipline of abandoning, and the discipline of reflection. Therefore, he said, 'This is the discipline.' The pair 'prescribed and unprescribed' is the very same in meaning as the pair 'spoken and unspoken'; likewise, the pair of 'gross' is the same as the pair of 'grave.' For that very reason, a similar exposition of them was made with the words beginning, 'Four foundations of mindfulness... this is called "unprescribed".' 'An offense with a remainder' means an offense together with remaining moral precepts. Because for one who has fallen into this offense there is no remainder of moral precepts, it is an 'offense without a remainder'.

354. Pāḷiyaṃ samaggānañca anuggahoti yathā samaggānaṃ sāmaggī na bhijjati, evaṃ anuggahaṇaṃ anubalappadānaṃ.

354. In the Pāḷi, 'and support for the united' means support, the giving of successive strength, in such a way that the harmony of the united is not broken.

355. Siyā [M 2.0257] nu khoti sambhaveyya nu kho. Tasmiṃ adhammadiṭṭhīti attano “adhammaṃ dhammo”ti etasmiṃ dīpane ayuttadiṭṭhi. Bhede adhammadiṭṭhīti “adhammaṃ dhammo”ti dīpetvā anussāvanasalākaggāhāpanādinā attānaṃ muñcitvā catuvaggādikaṃ saṅghaṃ ekasīmāyameva ṭhitato [V 2.0244] catuvaggādisaṅghato viyojetvā ekakammādinipphādanavasena saṅghabhedakaraṇe adhammadiṭṭhiko hutvāti attho. Vinidhāya diṭṭhinti yā tasmiṃ “adhammaṃ dhammo”ti dīpane attano adhammadiṭṭhi uppajjati, taṃ vinidhāya paṭicchādetvā “dhammo evāya”nti viparītato pakāsetvāti attho. Evaṃ sabbattha attho veditabbo.

355. 'Siyā nu kho' means: could it be possible? 'Wrong view in that' means an unsuitable view regarding one's own explanation that 'non-Dhamma is Dhamma.' 'Wrong view in schism' means: having become one with a wrong view in the act of causing a schism of the Saṅgha by explaining 'non-Dhamma is Dhamma,' and then, by means of proclaiming the formal act, causing voting tickets to be taken, and so on, having freed oneself and separated a Saṅgha of a group of four or more from the Saṅgha of a group of four or more that is established within one and the same boundary, by way of accomplishing a single formal act, and so on. This is the meaning. 'Having concealed the view' means: whatever wrong view arises in oneself in that explanation that 'non-Dhamma is Dhamma,' having concealed and covered up that view, and having explained it contrarily as, 'This is indeed Dhamma.' This is the meaning. Thus the meaning should be known in all cases.

Bhede dhammadiṭṭhīti yathāvuttanayena saṅghabhedane doso natthīti laddhiko. Ayaṃ pana “adhammaṃ dhammo”ti dīpane adhammadiṭṭhiko hutvāpi taṃ diṭṭhiṃ vinidhāya karaṇena saṅghabhedako atekiccho jāto. Evaṃ bhede vematikoti imassa pana bhede vematikadiṭṭhiyā vinidhānampi atthi. Sesaṃ samameva. Tasmiṃ dhammadiṭṭhibhede adhammadiṭṭhīti ayaṃ pana bhede adhammadiṭṭhiṃ vinidhāya katattā saṅghabhedako atekiccho jāto. Sukkapakkhe pana sabbattha “adhammaṃ dhammo”tiādidīpane vā bhede vā dhammadiṭṭhitāya diṭṭhiṃ avinidhāyeva katattā saṅghabhedakopi satekiccho jāto. Tasmā “adhammaṃ dhammo”tiādidīpane vā saṅghabhede vā ubhosupi vā adhammadiṭṭhi vā vematiko vā hutvā taṃ diṭṭhiṃ, vimatiñca vinidhāya “dhammo”ti pakāsetvā vuttanayena saṅghabhedaṃ karontasseva ānantariyaṃ hotīti veditabbaṃ.

'Right view in schism' means one who has the view that 'there is no fault in causing a schism of the Saṅgha by the aforesaid method.' This one, however, although having a wrong view in explaining 'non-Dhamma is Dhamma,' by acting while concealing that view, has become an incurable schismatic. Similarly for one who is doubtful in schism; for this one, however, there is no concealment of the doubtful view in schism. The rest is the same. As for 'right view in that, wrong view in schism': this one, because of having acted while concealing a wrong view in schism, has become an incurable schismatic. In the bright faction, however, in all cases, whether in explaining 'non-Dhamma is Dhamma,' etc., or in schism, because of having a right view and having acted without concealing that view, even the schismatic has become curable. Therefore, it should be known that the immediately effective kamma occurs only for one who, whether in explaining 'non-Dhamma is Dhamma,' etc., or in causing a schism of the Saṅgha, or in both, having a wrong view or being doubtful, and then, having concealed that view and doubt, explains 'This is Dhamma' and causes a schism of the Saṅgha by the aforesaid method.

Upālipañhākathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Questions of Upāli is finished.

Saṅghabhedakakkhandhakavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The method of the commentary on the Chapter on Schism is finished.

8. Vattakkhandhako

8. The Chapter on Observances

Āgantukavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on Observances for Newcomers

357. Vattakkhandhake [M 2.0258][V 2.0245] pattharitabbanti ātape pattharitabbaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ abhivādāpetabboti vandanatthāya vassaṃ pucchanena navako sayameva vandatīti vuttaṃ. Nilloketabboti oloketabbo.

357. In the Chapter on Observances, 'it should be spread out' means it should be spread out in the sun. In the Pāḷi, 'he should be made to pay homage' means that for the purpose of paying homage, the junior monk himself pays homage by asking about the rains-residence; therefore, it is said. 'He should be looked at' means he should be looked at.

Āgantukavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on Observances for Newcomers is concluded.

Āvāsikavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on Observances for Resident Monks

359. “Yathābhāga”nti ṭhapitaṭṭhānaṃ anatikkamitvā mañcapīṭhādiṃ papphoṭetvā pattharitvā upari paccattharaṇaṃ datvā dānampi senāsanapaññāpanamevāti dassento āha “papphoṭetvā hi pattharituṃ pana vaṭṭatiyevā”ti.

359. 'According to the portion' means not transgressing the designated place, after shaking out the bed, bench, etc., spreading it, and placing a covering on top. To show that even the giving of this is indeed the preparing of a lodging, he said, 'Indeed, having shaken it out, it is permissible to spread it.'

Āvāsikavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on Observances for Resident Monks is concluded.

Anumodanavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on Observances for Anumodanā

362. Pañcame nisinneti anumodanatthāya nisinne. Na mahātherassa bhāro hotīti anumodakaṃ āgametuṃ na bhāro. Ajjhiṭṭhova āgametabboti attanā ajjhiṭṭhehi bhikkhūhi anumodanteyeva nisīditabbanti attho.

362. 'When seated in the fifth place' means when seated for the purpose of giving anumodanā. 'It is not a burden for the senior elder' means it is not a burden to await the one who gives anumodanā. 'He should be awaited only when requested' means that one should sit only when the monks requested by oneself are giving the anumodanā; this is the meaning.

Anumodanavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on Observances for Anumodanā is concluded.

Bhattaggavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on Observances in the Refectory

364. Manussānaṃ [V 2.0246] parivisanaṭṭhānanti yattha antovihārepi manussā saputtadārā āvasitvā bhikkhū netvā bhojenti. Āsanesu satīti nisīdanaṭṭhānesu [M 2.0259] santesu. Idaṃ, bhante, āsanaṃ uccanti āsanne samabhūmibhāge paññattaṃ therāsanena samakaṃ āsanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, therāsanato pana uccatare āpucchitvāpi nisīdituṃ na vaṭṭati. Yadi taṃ āsannampi nīcataraṃ hoti, anāpucchāpi nisīdituṃ vaṭṭati. Mahātherasseva āpattīti āsanena paṭibāhanāpattiyā āpatti. Avattharitvāti pārutasaṅghāṭiṃ avattharitvā, anukkhipitvāti attho.

364. 'The place where people serve' means a place where, even within the monastery, laypeople live with their sons and wives, and having brought the monks, they feed them. 'When seats are present' means when there are sitting places. The words 'Venerable sir, this seat is high' are said in reference to a seat, equal to the elder's seat, that is prepared on a level part of the ground that is nearby.
