Regarding the statement beginning, 'A legal issue of dispute, of the seven methods of settlement, how many does it partake of?', this is stated to show the prescribed methods of settlement when the four legal issues are appeased. Therein, 'how many methods of settlement does it partake of?' means: for its own appeasement, how many methods of settlement does it approach? By resorting to how many methods of settlement does it reach appeasement? This is the meaning. 'In how many methods of settlement is it included?' means: in order to appease itself, into how many settlements is it entered by virtue of being similar to them? 'By how many methods of settlement is it comprehended?' means: by those who are bringing about appeasement, by how many methods of settlement is it taken up in order to bring about that appeasement.

Bhajativāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Section on Partaking is concluded.

Khandhakapucchāvāro

The Section of Questions on the Khandhakas

Pucchāvissajjanāvaṇṇanā

Exposition of Questions and Answers

320. Upasampadakkhandhakanti [M 2.0284] pabbajjākhandhakaṃ (mahāva. 84). Saha niddesenāti saniddesaṃ. “Sanniddesa”nti vā pāṭho, so evattho. Nidānena ca niddesena ca saddhinti ettha paññattiṭṭhānapuggalādippakāsakaṃ nidānavacanaṃ nidānaṃ nāma, tannidānaṃ paṭicca niddiṭṭhasikkhāpadāni [V 2.0269] niddeso nāma, tehi avayavabhūtehi sahitaṃ taṃsamudāyabhūtaṃ khandhakaṃ pucchāmīti attho. Uttamāni padānīti āpattipaññāpakāni vacanāni adhippetāni. Tesaṃ…pe… kati āpattiyo hontīti tehi vacanehi paññattā kati āpattikkhandhā hontīti attho. Nanu āpattiyo nāma puggalānaññeva honti, na padānaṃ, kasmā pana “samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ kati āpattiyo”ti sāmivasena niddeso katoti āha “yena yena hi padenā”tiādi. Pāḷiyaṃ uposathantiādi uposathakkhandhakādīnaññeva (mahāva. 132 ādayo) gahaṇaṃ.

320. The Upasampadākkhandhaka (Mahāvagga 84) is the Pabbajjākkhandhaka. 'Together with the explanation' means it is 'saniddesaṃ'. Alternatively, the reading is 'sanniddesaṃ,' which has the very same meaning. In the phrase 'with the origin and with the explanation,' 'origin' (nidāna) is the name for the introductory words that indicate the place of promulgation, the person, and so on; 'explanation' (niddesa) is the name for the training rules pointed out in dependence on that origin. The meaning is: I ask about the Khandhaka, which is a collection of those and is comprised of those as its component parts. By 'the supreme terms,' the words that lay down the offenses are intended. 'Of them... how many offenses are there?': the meaning is, how many groups of offenses are laid down by those words? Is it not so that offenses belong only to persons, not to terms? Why then was the reference made by way of relation, as in 'of the excellent terms, how many offenses are there?' To this, he said the words beginning, 'For by whichever term...'. In the Pāḷi, by the words beginning 'Uposatha', the Uposathakkhandhaka and so on (Mahāvagga 132 ff.) are to be taken.

Pucchāvissajjanāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of Questions and Answers is concluded.

Ekuttarikanayaṃ

The Method of Increasing by One

Ekakavāravaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Single Section

321. Ekuttarikanaye [M 2.0285] pana ajānantena vītikkantāti paṇṇattiṃ vā vatthuṃ vā ajānantena vītikkantā pathavīkhaṇanasahaseyyādikā, sāpi pacchā āpannabhāvaṃ ñatvā paṭikammaṃ akarontassa antarāyikāva hoti.

321. In the Ekuttarika method, however, 'transgressed by one not knowing' refers to an offense such as digging the earth or sleeping together, which is transgressed by one not knowing either the rule or the basis. Even that offense, for one who, having later realized that it has been incurred, does not perform the remedy, becomes indeed an obstacle.

Pārivāsikādīhi pacchā āpannāti vattabhedesu dukkaṭāni sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tasmiṃ khaṇe āpajjitabbaantarāpattiyo sandhāyāti keci vadanti, tassa pubbāpattīnaṃantarāpatti-padeneva vakkhamānattā purimameva yuttataraṃ. Mūlavisuddhiyā antarāpattīti mūlāyapaṭikassanādīni akatvā sabbapaṭhamaṃ dinnaparivāsamānattavisuddhiyā caraṇakāle āpannaantarāpattisaṅkhātasaṅghādiseso. Agghavisuddhiyāti antarāpattiṃ āpannassa mūlāya paṭikassitvā odhānasamodhānavasena odhunitvā purimāpattiyā samodhāya tadagghavasena puna dinnaparivāsādisuddhiyā caraṇakāle puna āpannā antarāpatti.

The statement 'incurred later by those on probation, etc.' is said with reference to the dukkaṭa offenses in the breaking of duties. Some say it is said with reference to the intermediate offenses that should be incurred at that moment; however, because that will be stated by the very term 'intermediate offense of the previous offenses', the former statement is more suitable. 'An intermediate offense for the root-purification' is the Saṅghādisesa, called an intermediate offense, incurred during the time of observing the purification of probation and mānatta given first of all, without having performed such acts as returning to the root. 'Purification by value' is the intermediate offense incurred again at the time of observing the purification of probation, etc., given again, by one who, having incurred an intermediate offense, has been drawn back to the root, has been cleared by way of inclusion and consolidation, and has been combined with the former offense by way of the value of that offense.

Saussāhenevāti punapi taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitukāmatācittena, evaṃ desitāpi āpatti na vuṭṭhātīti adhippāyo. Dhuranikkhepaṃ akatvā āpajjane sikhāppattadosaṃ dassento āha “aṭṭhame vatthusmiṃ bhikkhuniyā pārājikamevā”ti. Na kevalañca bhikkhuniyā eva, bhikkhūnampi dhuranikkhepaṃ akatvā thokaṃ thokaṃ sappiādikaṃ theyyāya gaṇhantānaṃ pādagghanake puṇṇe pārājikameva. Keci pana “aṭṭhame vatthusmiṃ bhikkhuniyā pārājikameva [V 2.0270] hotīti vuttattā aṭṭhavatthukamevetaṃ sandhāya vutta”nti vadanti.

'With zeal itself' means with a mind desiring to incur that offense again; even though it has been confessed, one does not rise from the offense—this is the meaning. Wishing to show the fault of reaching the summit in incurring an offense without laying down the burden, he said, 'In the eighth basis, for a bhikkhunī it is a pārājika indeed.' And it is not only for a bhikkhunī; for bhikkhus also who, without laying down the burden, take little by little of ghee and so on by theft, when the value of a pāda is complete, it is a pārājika indeed. But some say: 'Because it was said, "In the eighth basis, for a bhikkhunī it is a pārājika indeed," this was said with reference only to the pārājika of the eight bases.'

Dhammikassa paṭissavassāti “idha vassaṃ vasissāmī”tiādinā gihīnaṃ sammukhā katassa dhammikassa paṭissavassa, adhammikassa pana “asukaṃ paharissāmī”tiādikassa paṭissavassa asaccāpanena āpatti natthi.

Regarding a righteous promise: in not making true a righteous promise made in the presence of laypeople, such as 'I will spend the rains-residence here,' there is an offense. However, by not making true an unrighteous promise, such as 'I will strike so-and-so,' there is no offense.

Tathā coditoti adhammena codito, sayaṃ sacce, akuppe ca aṭṭhatvā paṭicchādentopi adhammacuditako eva. Pañcānantariyaniyatamicchādiṭṭhiyeva micchattaniyatā nāma. Cattāro maggā sammattaniyatā nāma.

'Thus reproved' means reproved unrighteously. Even one who, not being established in truth and non-anger, conceals the matter, is indeed one who is unrighteously reproved. Only the five deeds with immediate result and fixed wrong view are called 'fixed in wrongness.' The four paths are called 'fixed in rightness.'

Ekakavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Single Section is concluded.

Dukavāravaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Section of Dyads

322. Dukesu [M 2.0286] sayameva sapuggaloti āha “mudupiṭṭhikassā”tiādi. Ādi-saddena aṅgajātacchedaattaghātādiāpattiyo saṅgahitā.

322. In the Dyads, oneself is indeed 'with a person'; therefore, he said, 'of one with a soft back,' and so forth. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), offenses such as cutting the sexual organ, killing oneself, and so on, are included.

Bhaṇḍāgārikacittakammāni vāti gahaṭṭhānaṃ bhaṇḍapaṭisāmanaṃ, itthipurisādipaṭibhānacittakammāni vā. “Cīvarādīni adento āpajjatī”ti idaṃ “upajjhāyena, bhikkhave, saddhivihāriko saṅgahetabbo anuggahetabbo…pe… patto dātabbo”tiādi (mahāva. 67) vacanato anādariyena āmisasaṅgahaṃ akarontassa dukkaṭaṃ, bhikkhuniyā pācittiyañca sandhāya vuttaṃ. Nissaṭṭhacīvarādīnaṃ adānaāpattipi ettheva saṅgahitā.

As for 'or the artistic works of a storekeeper,' it means either the storing of goods of householders or artistic works depicting figures of women, men, and so on. This statement, 'Not giving robes, etc., one falls into an offense,' was said in reference to the dukkaṭa offense for a preceptor who, through disrespect, does not provide material support—in accordance with the teaching, 'O bhikkhus, a co-resident should be taken care of and supported by the preceptor... a bowl should be given,' etc.—and the pācittiya offense for a bhikkhunī. The offense of not giving robes, etc., that have been forfeited is also included right here.

Pāḷiyaṃ desentoti sabhāgāpattiṃ, adesanāgāminiādiñca desento. Nidānuddese āpattiṃ anāvikaronto, na desento ca āpajjati nāma. Ovādaṃ agaṇhantoti bhikkhūhi bhikkhuniovādatthāya vuttaṃ vacanaṃ agaṇhanto bālagilānagamiyavivajjito. Attano paribhogatthaṃ dinnaṃ aññassa dāne, saṅghāṭiṃ apārupitvā santaruttarena gāmappavesanādīsu ca āpattiyopi aparibhogena āpajjitabbāpattiyova. Pamāṇanti saṅghabhedānantariyanipphattiyā lakkhaṇaṃ. Bālassāti nissayaggahaṇavidhiṃ ajānantassa lajjibālasseva. Lajjissāti byattassa nissayadāyakasabhāgataṃ [V 2.0271] parivīmaṃsantassa. Vinaye āgatā atthā venayikāti āha “dve atthā vinayasiddhā”ti.

In the Pāḷi, 'confessing' means confessing a common offense, an offense that is not confessable, and so on. During the recitation of the introduction, one who does not make an offense manifest and does not confess it is said to fall into an offense. 'Not accepting the exhortation' means not accepting the words spoken by the bhikkhus for the purpose of exhorting the bhikkhunīs, excluding one who is a fool, sick, or a traveler. In giving to another what was given for one's own use, and in entering a village, etc., with the lower and upper robes without wearing the double-layered robe, the offenses are indeed offenses to be fallen into through non-use. 'Measure' is the characteristic of the accomplishment of the immediately effective kamma of creating a schism in the Saṅgha. 'Of a fool' means of a conscientious fool who does not know the procedure for taking dependence. 'Of a conscientious one' means of a conscientious and competent person who investigates the suitability of a dependence-giver. The meanings that come in the Vinaya are 'Vinayic'; therefore, he said, 'Two meanings are established by the Vinaya.'

Pāḷiyaṃ appatto nissāraṇanti ettha pabbājanīyakammaṃ vihārato nissāraṇattā nissāraṇanti adhippetaṃ, tañca yasmā kuladūsakaṃ akaronto puggalo āpattibahulopi āveṇikalakkhaṇena appatto nāma hoti, tasmā appatto nissāraṇaṃ. Yasmā pana āpattādibahulassāpi “ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyyā”ti (cūḷava. 27) vuttaṃ, tasmā sunissārito, sabbathā pana suddho nirāpattiko dunnissāritoti daṭṭhabbo.

In the Pāḷi, regarding 'not liable for banishment,' here the act of banishment (pabbājanīyakamma) is intended as 'banishment' (nissāraṇa) because it is an expulsion from the monastery. Regarding this, because a person who is not a corrupter of families—even though having many offenses—is called 'not liable' by a distinct characteristic, therefore he is 'not liable for banishment.' But because it is said, 'If it wishes, the Saṅgha may carry out the act of banishment' even for one with many offenses and so forth, therefore he is 'well banished.' However, one who is in every way pure and without offense should be understood as 'badly banished.'

Appatto osāraṇantiādīsu upasampadākammaṃ ettha osāraṇaṃ adhippetaṃ, tañca hatthacchinnādiko ekacco paṭikkhittattā appattopi sosārito, paṇḍakādiko dosāritoti attho.

In texts such as 'not liable for inclusion,' the act of higher ordination (upasampadākamma) is intended here as 'inclusion' (osāraṇa). Regarding this, a certain person, such as one with a severed hand, although not eligible because of being rejected, is 'well included'; a paṇḍaka and others are 'badly included.' This is the meaning.

Dukavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section of Dyads is finished.

Tikavāravaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Section of Triads

323. Tikesu [M 2.0287] lohituppādāpattinti pārājikāpattiṃ. Āvusovādenāti “āvuso”ti ālapanena. Āpattinti dukkaṭāpattiṃ. Sesā rattiñceva divā cāti ettha aruṇuggamane āpajjitabbā paṭhamakathinādī (pārā. 459) sabbā āpattiyopi rattindivānaṃ vemajjheyeva āpajjitabbattā tatiyakoṭṭhāsaññeva paviṭṭhāti daṭṭhabbā. Atha vā uddhaste aruṇe āpajjitabbattā divā āpajjitabbesu eva paviṭṭhāti daṭṭhabbā, atthaṅgate sūriye bhikkhuniyo ovādanāpattiyo, pana rattandhakāre purisena saddhiṃ santiṭṭhanāpatti ca rattiyaññeva āpajjitabbā.

323. In the Triads, 'the offense of causing blood to arise' refers to a pārājika offense. 'By the address "āvuso"' means: because of addressing with the term 'āvuso.' 'An offense' refers to a dukkaṭa offense. Regarding 'the rest, both night and day': here, all offenses to be incurred at dawn, such as the first Kathina, should be understood as being included only in the third division, because they are to be incurred precisely in the middle of night and day. Alternatively, because they are to be incurred when dawn has risen, they should be understood as being included among those to be incurred during the day. However, offenses for admonishing bhikkhunīs after the sun has set, and the offense of standing together with a man in the darkness of night, are to be incurred only at night.

Purebhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamanaanatirittabhojanādīni divā eva āpajjitabbāni. Keci pana “bhojanapaṭisaṃyuttāni sekhiyāni, gaṇabhojanādīni ca divā eva āpajjitabbānī”ti vadanti. Tasmā īdisā āpattiyo muñcitvā sesāva tatiyakoṭṭhāsaṃ bhajantīti veditabbaṃ.

Offenses such as visiting families before the meal and concerning non-surplus food are to be incurred only during the day. Some teachers, however, say, 'The sekhiya rules connected with food, and offenses concerning group meals, etc., are to be incurred only during the day.' Therefore, it should be known that, having excluded such offenses, only the remaining ones are included in the third division.

Na ūnadasavassoti dasavassassa bālasseva paññattasikkhāpadattā vuttaṃ. Saddhivihārikaantevāsikesu [V 2.0272] asammāvattanāpattiṃ, alajjīnaṃ nissayadānādimpi dasavassova āpajjati, vuṭṭhāpiniṃ dve vassāni ananubandhādimpi ūnadasavassā āpajjanti. Abyākatacittoti supantassa bhavaṅgacittaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

'Not less than ten vassas' is said because it is a training rule laid down only for an ignorant monk of ten vassas. The offense of not behaving properly towards co-residents and pupils, and of giving dependence to the shameless, etc., is incurred only by a monk of ten vassas. The offense of not following a female preceptor for two years, etc., is incurred by a bhikkhunī of less than ten vassas. 'With an indeterminate mind' is said with reference to the life-continuum consciousness (bhavaṅga-citta) of one who is sleeping.

Appavārentoti anādariyena appavārento kenaci paccayena appavāretvā kāḷapakkhacātuddase saṅghe pavārente tattha anādariyena appavārento tameva āpattiṃ kāḷepi āpajjatīti juṇhe evāti niyamo na dissati, pacchimavassaṃvuttho pana pacchimakattikapuṇṇamiyameva pavāretuṃ labbhatīti tattha appavāraṇāpaccayā āpattiṃ āpajjamāno eva juṇhe āpajjatīti niyametabboti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Juṇhe kappatīti etthāpi eseva nayo.

Not performing pavāraṇā: one who does not perform pavāraṇā out of disrespect, or having not performed pavāraṇā for some reason. When the Saṅgha performs pavāraṇā on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one who does not perform pavāraṇā out of disrespect incurs that very offense even in the dark fortnight; thus, the restriction 'only in the bright fortnight' is not apparent. However, a monk who has completed the later rains-residence is allowed to perform pavāraṇā only on the full-moon day of the later Kattika. Therefore, it should be understood that only a monk who incurs an offense there on account of not performing pavāraṇā should be specified as 'incurs in the bright fortnight.' In 'it is allowable in the bright fortnight' also, this is the same method.

“Apaccuddharitvā hemante āpajjatī”ti iminā “vassānaṃ cātumāsaṃ adhiṭṭhātu”nti niyamavacaneneva apaccuddharantassa dukkaṭanti dasseti. Vassānupagamanaakaraṇīyena pakkamādayopi vasse eva āpajjati. Vatthikammādimpi gilāno eva. Adhotapādehi akkamanādīnipi anto eva āpajjati[M 2.0288]. Bhikkhuniyā anāpucchā ārāmappavesanādi ca antosīmāyameva. Nissayapaṭipannassa anāpucchādisāpakkamanādi ca bahisīmāyameva. Pātimokkhuddese santiyā āpattiyā anāvikaraṇāpattisamanubhāsanaūnavīsativassūpasampādanādisabbaadhammakammāpattiyopi saṅghe eva. Adhammena gaṇuposathādīsupi gaṇādimajjhe eva. Alajjissa santike nissayaggahaṇādipi puggalassa santike eva āpajjati.

By the phrase 'Having not withdrawn it, one incurs an offense in the winter season,' it shows that, precisely by the restrictive statement 'One should determine it for the four months of the rains,' there is a dukkaṭa offense for one who does not withdraw it. Not entering upon the rains-residence, departing without a legitimate reason, etc., are offenses one incurs only during the rains season. Applying a bandage, etc., is an offense incurred only by one who is sick. Treading with unwashed feet, etc., is an offense one incurs only inside. For a bhikkhunī, entering a monastery without asking permission, etc., is an offense incurred only within the boundary. For one practicing under dependence, departing to another region without asking permission, etc., is an offense incurred only outside the boundary. The offense of not revealing an existing offense during the recitation of the Pātimokkha; interrogation; giving ordination to one under twenty years; and all offenses of improper formal acts are incurred only in the Saṅgha. In performing a group Uposatha improperly, etc., one incurs an offense only in the midst of the group. Taking dependence from a shameless person, etc., is an offense incurred only in the presence of a single individual.

Tīṇi adhammikāni amūḷhavinayassa dānānīti yo ummattakopi vītikkamakāle, anummatto sañcicceva āpattiṃ āpajjitvā bhikkhūhi pacchā codito saramāno eva “na sarāmī”ti vadati, yo ca “supinaṃ viya sarāmī”ti vā musā vadati, yo ca ummattakakāle kataṃ sabbampi sabbesaṃ vaṭṭatīti vadati, imesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ dinnāni tīṇi amūḷhavinayassa dānāni adhammikāni.

The three improper grants of a verdict of not-insane are as follows: (1) Whoever, though now insane, was not insane at the time of the transgression, and having incurred the offense intentionally, when later accused by the monks, although remembering, says, 'I do not remember'; (2) and whoever falsely says, 'I remember it like a dream'; (3) and whoever says, 'Everything done during the time of insanity is allowable for all'—the three grants of a verdict of not-insane given to these three are improper.

Apakatattoti vinaye apakataññū. Tenāha “āpattānāpattiṃ na jānātī”ti (pari. 325). “Diṭṭhiñca anissajjantānaṃyeva kammaṃ kātabba”nti idaṃ bhikkhūhi ovadiyamānassa diṭṭhiyā anissajjanapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ, pācittiyampi vā avassameva sambhavatīti vuttaṃ.

'Unskilled' means one who is not knowledgeable in the Vinaya. Therefore, it is said, 'He does not know offense and non-offense.' Regarding the statement, 'A formal act should be carried out only against those who do not relinquish their view': this is said because for one who is being admonished by the monks, on account of not relinquishing the view, a dukkaṭa or even a pācittiya offense inevitably arises.

Mukhālambarakaraṇādibhedoti [V 2.0273] mukhabherīvādanādippabhedo. Upaghātetīti vināseti. Bījaniggāhādiketi cittaṃ bījaniṃ gāhetvā anumodanādikaraṇeti attho.

'The category of making a mouth-frame, etc.' means the category of playing a mouth-drum, etc. 'Destroys' means ruins. 'In the context of destroying seeds, etc.' means: in the act of taking a decorated fan and giving a blessing, etc.—this is the meaning.

Tikavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section of Triads is finished.

Catukkavāravaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Section of Tetrads

324. Catukkesu soti gihiparikkhāro. Avāpuraṇaṃ dātunti gabbhaṃ vivaritvā anto parikkhāraṭṭhapanatthāya vivaraṇakuñcikaṃ dātuṃ. Saṅghatthāya upanītaṃ sayameva anto paṭisāmitumpi vaṭṭati. Tenāha “anto ṭhapāpetuñca vaṭṭatī”ti.

324. In the Tetrads, 'so' is a layperson's requisite. 'Avāpuraṇaṃ dātuṃ' means to give the key for opening the chamber for the purpose of placing requisites inside. It is also permissible for oneself to store inside that which is brought for the sake of the Saṅgha. Therefore, it is said, 'It is also permissible to have it placed inside.'

Ādikammikesu paṭhamaṃ purisaliṅgaṃ uppajjatīti āha “paṭhamaṃ uppannavasenā”ti. Pāḷiyaṃ anāpatti vassacchedassāti vassacchedasambandhiniyā anāpattiyā [M 2.0289] evamattho. Mantabhāsāti mantāya paññāya kathanaṃ. “Navamabhikkhunito paṭṭhāyā”ti idaṃ “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhannaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ avasesānaṃ yathākatika”nti (cūḷava. 426) vacanato ādito aṭṭhannaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ paccuṭṭhātabbattā vuttaṃ.

Among those of the primal aeon, the male characteristic arises first; therefore, it is said, 'by way of having arisen first.' In the Pāḷi, as for anāpatti vassacchedassa, the meaning should be understood thus: by way of there being no offense connected with the interruption of the rains-residence. Mantabhāsā is speaking with wisdom (paññā). The phrase 'starting from the ninth bhikkhunī' is stated because, according to the text 'I allow, O bhikkhus, for eight bhikkhunīs according to seniority, and for the remaining according to agreement,' the first eight bhikkhunīs are to be risen up for.

“Idha na kappantīti vadantopi paccantimesu āpajjatī”tiādinā sañcicca kappiyaṃ akappiyanti vā akappiyaṃ kappiyanti vā kathentassa sabbattha dukkaṭanti dasseti.

By the text beginning, 'Here, even one who says, “It is not allowable,” commits an offense in the border regions,' it shows that for one who intentionally declares what is allowable as unallowable, or what is unallowable as allowable, there is a dukkaṭa offense everywhere.

Pubbakaraṇanti vuccatīti aṭṭhakathāsu vuttaṃ, tāni idha parivāre uddhaṭānīti adhippāyo. Idhādhippetāni pana dassento “chandapārisuddhī”tiādimāha.

That it is called 'preliminary action' is stated in the commentaries; the meaning is that these have been extracted here in the Parivāra. Now, showing what is intended here, he states the text beginning with 'purity of consent.'

Catukkavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Quadruple Section is concluded.

Pañcakavāravaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Fivefold Section

325. Pañcakesu āpucchitvā cārassa abhāvoti piṇḍapātikassa “nimantito sabhatto”ti imassa aṅgassa abhāvā tena sikkhāpadena tassa sabbathā anāpattīti adhippāyo[V 2.0274]. Susānaṃ netvā puna ānītakanti susāne petakiccaṃ katvā nikkhantehi nhatvā chaḍḍitāni nivatthapārutavatthāni evaṃ vuccanti.

325. In the pentads, apucchitvā cārassa abhāvo (the absence of going about without having asked permission) means that for an alms-round bhikkhu, due to the absence of this factor, namely 'being invited and partaking of a meal,' there is no offense whatsoever under that training rule; this is the meaning. Susānaṃ netvā puna ānītakaṃ (having been taken to the charnel ground and brought back again) refers to the lower and upper garments discarded after bathing by those who, having performed the funeral rites in the charnel ground, have departed.

Pāḷiyaṃ pañcahākārehīti pañcahi avahāraṅgehi. Vatthuto pana garukalahukabhedena pārājikathullaccayadukkaṭāni vuttāni. Itthipurisasaṃyogādikaṃ kilesasamudācārahetukaṃ paṭibhānacittakammaṃ nāma. Pañhāsahassaṃ pucchīti samathavipassanākammaṭṭhānesu pañhāsahassaṃ sammajjitvā ṭhitaṃ daharaṃ pucchi. Itaropi daharo attano gatamaggattā sabbaṃ vissajjesi, tena thero pasīdi. Vattaṃ paricchindīti vattaṃ niṭṭhāpesi. Kiṃ tvaṃ āvusotiādikaṃ thero khīṇāsavo sammajjanānisaṃsaṃ sabbesaṃ pākaṭaṃ kātuṃ avocāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

In the Pāḷi, pañcahākārehi means with the five factors of theft. However, according to the object, by the distinction of grave and light, pārājika, thullaccaya, and dukkaṭa offenses are stated. A spontaneous painting that is a cause for the arising of defilements, such as the union of a man and a woman, is called paṭibhānacittakamma. Pañhāsahassaṃ pucchi means he asked the junior bhikkhu, who was standing there after having swept, a thousand questions on the meditation subjects of serenity and insight. The other junior bhikkhu, because it was his own trodden path, answered everything, and thus the elder was pleased. Vattaṃ paricchindi means he completed the duty of sweeping. It should be understood that the elder, who was an Arahant, said the words beginning with 'What, friend...?' in order to make the benefits of sweeping evident to all.

“Jaṇṇukehi [M 2.0290] patiṭṭhāya padacetiya”nti pāṭhaseso. Codanaṃ kāressāmīti bhagavatā attānaṃ codāpessāmi, attānaṃ niggaṇhāpessāmīti attho.

'Having established oneself on one's knees near the footprint shrine'—this is the remainder of the text. Codanaṃ kāressāmi means: 'I will cause myself to be accused by the Blessed One; I will cause myself to be censured'; this is the meaning.

Ettakaṃ gayhūpaganti ettakaṃ adhikaraṇavūpasamatthāya gahetabbavacananti yathā sutvā viññātuṃ sakkoti, evaṃ anuggaṇhantoti yojanā. Ettha ca “attano bhāsapariyantaṃ anuggahetvā parassa bhāsapariyantaṃ anuggahetvā”ti ekaṃ, “adhammena karotī”ti ekaṃ, “appaṭiññāyā”ti ekañca katvā purimehi dvīhi pañcaṅgāni veditabbāni. Vatthunti methunādivītikkamaṃ. Kathānusandhivinicchayānulomasandhivasena vatthuṃ na jānātīti codakena vā cuditakena vā vuttakathānusandhinā tesaṃ vacanapaṭivacanānurūpena vadanto kathānusandhinā vatthuṃ na jānāti nāma, tañca suttavibhaṅge vinītavatthusaṅkhātena vinicchayānulomeneva vadanto vinicchayānulomasandhivasena vatthuṃ na jānāti nāma. Ñattikammaṃ nāma hotīti ñattikammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ nāma hotīti na jānātīti sambandho. Ñattiyā kammappattoti ñattiyā niṭṭhitāyapi kammappatto eva hoti. Anussāvanaṭṭhāne eva kammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ hotīti ñattikammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ nāma hoti, taṃ ñattiyā kāraṇaṃ na jānātīti attho.

Ettakaṃ gayhūpagaṃ means 'this much is a statement to be grasped for the settling of a legal issue.' The connection is: 'upholding it in such a way that one is able to understand it upon hearing.' Here, five factors should be understood by taking the following as single factors: 'not grasping the extent of one's own speech and not grasping the extent of another's speech'; 'acting contrary to the Dhamma'; and 'without acknowledgement,' together with the two preceding factors. 'The object' means a transgression such as sexual intercourse. 'One does not know the object by way of the connection of the discussion and the connection in accordance with the legal decision' is explained as follows: one who speaks according to the sequence of statements and counter-statements of the accuser or the accused is said not to know how to speak by way of the connection of the discussion. And one who speaks only in accordance with the legal decision—which in the Suttavibhaṅga is called a settled matter—is said not to know how to speak by way of the connection in accordance with the legal decision. The connection for ñattikammaṃ nāma hoti is that one does not know that the act by motion is considered complete. Ñattiyā kammappatto means that even when the motion is complete, one has only reached the formal act. The formal act is complete only at the point of the proclamation; thus the act by motion is considered complete. The meaning is that one does not know that reason concerning the motion.

Pāḷiyaṃ pañca visuddhiyoti āpattito visuddhihetuttā, visuddhehi kattabbato ca pātimokkhuddesā vuttā.

In the Pāḷi, the recitations of the Pātimokkha are called 'the five purifications' because they are a cause of purity from offenses and because they are to be performed by the purified.

Pañcakavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Fivefold Section is concluded.

Chakkavārādivaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Sixfold Section, etc.

326. Chakkādīsu [V 2.0275] pāḷiyaṃ cha agāravāti buddhadhammasaṅghasikkhāsu, appamāde, paṭisanthāre ca cha agāravā, tesu eva ca cha gāravā veditabbā. “Chabbassaparamatā dhāretabba”nti idaṃ vibhaṅge āgatassa paramassa dassanaṃ.

326. In the Pāḷi, regarding the sixes and so on, the six disrespects are: disrespect towards the Buddha, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha, and the training rules; and towards heedfulness; and towards friendly welcome. And in those very same things, the six respects are also to be understood. This phrase, 'The state of being for at most six years is to be maintained,' is an indication of the word 'highest' (parama) that appears in the Vibhaṅga.

328. Pāḷiyaṃ āgatehi sattahīti “pubbevassa hoti musā bhaṇissa”ntiādinā musāvādasikkhāpade (pāci. 4) āgatehi sattahi.

328. In the Pāḷi, the phrase 'by the seven that have come' refers to the seven factors that have come in the training rule on false speech, beginning with 'Even before, he has the thought, "I will speak falsely."

329. Taṃ [M 2.0291] kutettha labbhāti taṃ anatthassa acaraṇaṃ ettha etasmiṃ puggale, lokasannivāse vā kuto kena kāraṇena sakkā laddhunti āghātaṃ paṭivineti.

329. ‘How can that be obtained here?’ means that one dispels hatred by asking, ‘How, by what reason, can that non-practice of what is unbeneficial be obtained in this person or in the world’s assembly?’

330. Sassato lokotiādinā vasenāti “sassato loko, asassato loko. Antavā loko, anantavā loko. Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā. Hoti tathāgato parammaraṇā, na hoti tathāgato parammaraṇā. Hoti ca na hoti ca tathāgato parammaraṇā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato parammaraṇā”ti (ma. ni. 1.269) evaṃ āgatā dasa antaggāhikā diṭṭhiyo sandhāya vuttaṃ. Micchādiṭṭhiādayoti micchādiṭṭhimicchāsaṅkappādayo aṭṭhamicchāñāṇamicchāvimuttīhi saddhiṃ dasa micchattā. Tattha micchāñāṇanti micchādiṭṭhisampayutto moho. Avimuttasseva vimuttasaññitā micchāvimutti nāma.

330. By way of 'The world is eternal,' etc., means: it is said with reference to the ten views that grasp at extremes which are given as: 'The world is eternal, the world is not eternal. The world is finite, the world is infinite. That which is the life-principle is the body,' or 'The life-principle is one thing, the body is another.' 'A being exists after death, a being does not exist after death. A being both exists and does not exist after death, a being neither exists nor does not exist after death.' 'Wrong view and so on' means: the eight factors beginning with wrong view and wrong intention, together with wrong knowledge and wrong liberation, are the ten wrongnesses. Therein, 'wrong knowledge' is delusion associated with wrong view. 'Wrong liberation' is the name for the perception of being liberated on the part of one who is in fact not liberated.

Viparītāti sammādiṭṭhiādayo sammāñāṇasammāvimuttipariyosānā dasa. Tattha sammāvimutti arahattaphalaṃ, taṃsampayuttaṃ pana ñāṇaṃ vā paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ vā sammāñāṇanti veditabbaṃ.

'The opposite' refers to the ten qualities, beginning with right view and culminating in right knowledge and right liberation. Therein, right liberation is the fruit of arahantship, and the knowledge associated with it or the reviewing knowledge is to be understood as right knowledge.

Ekuttarikanayo niṭṭhito.

The method of numerical increase is concluded.

Uposathādipucchāvissajjanāvaṇṇanā

The explanation of questions and answers concerning the Uposatha and so on.

332. Uposathādipucchāsu [V 2.0276] pavāraṇagāthāti diṭṭhādīhi tīhi ṭhānehi pavāraṇāvācā eva. Evaṃ vuttānaṃ pana chandovicitilakkhaṇena vuttajātibhedā gāthā.

332. In the questions on the Uposatha and so on, the 'pavāraṇā verse' refers to just the speech of invitation (pavāraṇā) made on the three grounds beginning with 'what is seen'; it is so called. It is not, however, a verse (gāthā) that has divisions of type spoken of according to the characteristic of metrical analysis.

Chakkavārādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the sixfold sections, etc., is concluded.

Mahāvaggavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The method of the commentary on the Mahāvagga is completed.

Paññattivaggo

Chapter on Regulations

Paṭhamagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

The First Verse Collection

Sattanagaresu paññattasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

The explanation of the training rules established in the seven towns.

335. Aḍḍhuḍḍhasatānīti [V 2.0277][M 2.0292] paññāsādhikāni tīṇi satāni. Viggahapadena manussaviggahaṃ vuttaṃ.

335. As for `aḍḍhuḍḍhasatāni`: three hundred with an excess of fifty. By the term `viggaha`, the training rule on `manussaviggaha` (human form) is stated.

Atirekanti paṭhamakathinaṃ. Kāḷakanti suddhakāḷakaṃ. Bhūtanti bhūtārocanaṃ. Bhikkhunīsu ca akkosoti “yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuṃ akkoseyyā”ti (pāci. 1029) vuttaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ.

As for `atireka`: it is the first `kathina` training rule. As for `kāḷaka`: it is the `suddhakāḷaka` (pure black) training rule. As for `bhūta`: it is the `bhūtārocana` (informing about a fact) training rule. As for `bhikkhunīsu ca akkoso`: it is the training rule stated as, 'Whatever bhikkhunī should revile a bhikkhu...'

Dvepi ca bhedāti dve saṅghabhedasikkhāpadāni. Antaravāsakanāmena aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā hatthato cīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ vuttaṃ. Suttanti suttaṃ viññāpetvā vāyāpanaṃ. Vikāleti vikālabhojanaṃ. Cārittanti purebhattaṃ pacchābhattaṃ cārittaṃ. Nahānanti orenaddhamāsanahānaṃ.

As for `dvepi ca bhedā`: the two training rules on schism in the Saṅgha. By the name `antaravāsaka`: the acceptance of a robe from the hand of a non-relative bhikkhunī is stated. As for `sutta`: having requested thread, causing it to be woven. As for `vikāle`: eating at the wrong time. As for `cāritta`: the custom of going before the meal and after the meal. As for `nahāna`: the training rule on bathing within half a month.

Cīvaraṃ datvāti samaggena saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā khiyyanaṃ. Giragganti naccagītaṃ. Cariyāti antovassaṃ cārikacaraṇaṃ. Tatthevāti vassaṃvutthāya cārikaṃ apakkamitvā tattheva nivāsanaṃ paṭicca paññattasikkhāpadaṃ. Chandadānenāti pārivāsikena chandadānena.

As for `cīvaraṃ datvā`: having given a robe by the united Saṅgha, then disparaging it. As for `giragga`: the training rule on dancing and singing. As for `cariyā`: wandering on tour during the rains-residence. As for `tattheva`: the training rule promulgated on account of a bhikkhunī, after having completed the rains-residence, dwelling in that very place without departing on tour. As for `chandadānena`: by the giving of consent by one on probation.

Pārājikāni cattārīti bhikkhunīnaṃ asādhāraṇāni. Soḷasāti ādito pañca sikkhāpadāni, kuladūsanañcāti cha, bhikkhunīnaṃ asādhāraṇāni dasa nissaggiyāni.

As for the four `pārājikas`: they are those unique to the bhikkhunīs. As for the sixteen: the five training rules from the beginning and the `kuladūsana` (corrupting families) training rule—thus six—and the ten `nissaggiya` rules that are unique to the bhikkhunīs.

Catuttiṃsāti paṭhamakathinasuddhakāḷakacīvarapaṭiggahaṇarūpiyacīvaravāyāpanakoseyyamissakaeḷakalomadhovāpanadutiyapattavajjitāni [V 2.0278] bhikkhuvibhaṅge dvāvīsati, bhikkhunīnaṃ asādhāraṇāni dvādasa cāti catuttiṃsa. Chapaññāsasatanti vesāliyādīsu paññattāni dvattiṃsasikkhāpadāni ṭhapetvā sesā chapaññāsasataṃ.

As for the thirty-four: excluding the rules on the first `kathina`, pure black, robe acceptance, silver, having a robe woven, mixed with silk, having goat's wool washed, and the second bowl, there are twenty-two in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, and twelve that are unique to bhikkhunīs; thus, thirty-four. As for the one hundred and fifty-six: setting aside the thirty-two training rules promulgated in Vesālī and other places, the remainder is one hundred and fifty-six.

Dasa [M 2.0293] gārayhāti vosāsaappaṭisaṃ viditasikkhāpadadvayañca ṭhapetvā sesāni dasa pāṭidesanīyāni. Dve sattati sekhiyāni surusurukārakasāmisenahatthenapānīyathālakapaṭiggahaṇasasitthakapattadhovanāni tīṇi ṭhapetvā sesāni sekhiyāni.

As for the ten blameworthy rules: setting aside the two training rules of `vosāsa` and `appaṭisaṃvidita`, the remainder are the ten `pāṭidesanīya` rules. As for the seventy-two `sekhiya` rules: setting aside the three rules on making a slurping sound, accepting a water-pot with a hand soiled by food, and washing a bowl with leftovers, the remainder are the `sekhiya` rules.

Seyyāti anupasampannena sahaseyyasikkhāpadaṃ. Khaṇaneti pathavīkhaṇanaṃ. Gaccha devateti bhūtagāmasikkhāpadaṃ vuttaṃ. Sappāṇakaṃ siñcanti sappāṇodakasiñcanaṃ. Mahāvihāroti mahallakavihāro.

As for `seyyā`: the training rule on lying down together with one who is not fully ordained. As for `khaṇane`: digging the earth. As for `gaccha devate`: the training rule on `bhūtagāma` (plant life) is stated. As for `sappāṇakaṃ siñcaṃ`: sprinkling water containing living beings. As for `mahāvihāro`: a large monastery.

Aññanti aññavādakaṃ. Dvāranti yāva dvārakosā aggaḷaṭṭhapanaṃ. Sahadhammoti sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno. Payopānanti surusurukārakasikkhāpadaṃ.

As for `añña`: the `aññavādaka` (speaking otherwise) training rule. As for `dvāra`: placing a bolt as far as the door-post. As for `sahadhamme`: the `sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno` (being spoken to in accordance with the Dhamma) training rule. As for `payopāna`: the training rule on making a slurping sound.

Eḷakalomoti eḷakalomadhovāpanaṃ. Patto cāti dutiyapatto. Ovādoti bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ovādo. Bhesajjanti catumāsapaccayapavāraṇāsikkhāpadaṃ. Āraññikoti catutthapāṭidesanīyaṃ. Ovādoti ovādāya vā saṃvāsāya vā agamanaṃ.

As for `eḷakalomā`: the training rule on having goat's wool washed. As for `patto ca`: the second bowl training rule. As for `ovādo`: the training rule on exhortation after having approached the bhikkhunīs' residence. As for `bhesajja`: the training rule on the four-month invitation for requisites. As for `āraññiko`: the fourth `pāṭidesanīya` training rule. As for `ovādo` [the second instance]: the training rule on not going for exhortation or for communion.

337. “Ye ca yāvatatiyakā”ti pañhassa “ime kho yāvatatiyakā”ti vissajjanaṃ vatvā tadanantaraṃ “sādhāraṇaṃ asādhāraṇa”ntiādipañhānaṃ vissajjane vattabbe yasmā taṃ avatvā “kati chedanakānī”tiādike aṭṭha pañhe antarā vissajjetvā tesaṃ anantarā “vīsaṃ dve satāni bhikkhūnaṃ…pe… chacattārīsā bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhunīhi asādhāraṇā”tiādinā ukkameneva sādhāraṇādipañhā vissajjitā, tasmā taṃ ukkamavissajjanakāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ “yasmā pana ye ca yāvatatiyakāti ayaṃ pañho”tiādimāha.

337. To the question, “And those which are `yāvatatiyaka`?” having given the answer, “These, indeed, are the `yāvatatiyaka`,” and immediately after that, when the answer to the questions on `sādhāraṇa` (shared) and `asādhāraṇa` (unshared), etc., should have been given, because, without giving that answer, eight questions such as, “How many are `chedanaka`?” were answered in between, and immediately after those, the questions on `sādhāraṇa`, etc., were answered out of sequence with the passage beginning, “Two hundred and twenty for the bhikkhus… forty-six for the bhikkhus, unshared by the bhikkhunīs…,” therefore, to show the reason for that out-of-sequence answer, he said the passage beginning, “Because this question, ‘And those which are `yāvatatiyaka`?’”

338. Dhovanañca paṭiggahotiādigāthā aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ gāthāva. Chabbassāni nisīdananti dve sikkhāpadāni. Dve lomāti tiyojanātikkamadhovāpanavasena dve eḷakalomasikkhāpadāni. Vassikā āraññakena cāti vassikasāṭikā pariyesanaaraññakesu senāsanesu viharaṇasikkhāpadena saha.

338. The verse beginning `dhovanañca paṭiggaho` is a verse of the commentary masters. By `chabbassāni nisīdana` (a sitting-cloth for six years), two training rules are taken. As for `dve lomā` (two wools): the two `eḷakalomā` training rules, by way of having it washed beyond three yojanas. As for `vassikā āraññakena ca`: together with the training rule on seeking a rains-cloth and the training rule on dwelling in forest lodgings.

Paṇītanti [V 2.0279] paṇītabhojanaviññāpanaṃ. Ūnanti ūnavīsativassūpasampādanaṃ. Mātugāmena saddhinti saṃvidhāya gamanaṃ vuttaṃ. Yā sikkhāti yaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ. Nisīdane [M 2.0294] ca yā sikkhāti pamāṇātikkantanisīdanakārāpane yaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ. Tathā vassikā yā ca sāṭikāti etthāpi.

As for `paṇīta`: the training rule on requesting fine food. As for `ūna`: ordaining one who is less than twenty years old. As for `mātugāmena saddhiṃ`: going by appointment is stated. As for `yā sikkhā`: it means 'whatever training rule'. As for `nisīdane ca yā sikkhā`: 'whatever training rule' there is regarding the making of a sitting-cloth that exceeds the standard measurement. Likewise also in the phrase `vassikā yā ca sāṭikā`.

Pāḷiyaṃ sataṃ sattati chaccevime honti ubhinnaṃ asādhāraṇāti bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīhi asādhāraṇā chacattārīsa, bhikkhunīnaṃ bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇā tiṃsādhikaṃ satañcāti evaṃ ubhinnaṃ asādhāraṇā ca chasattatiadhikaṃ sataṃ sikkhāpadānīti attho. Sataṃ sattati cattārīti ubhinnaṃ sādhāraṇasikkhānaṃ gaṇanā catusattatiadhikaṃ sataṃ sikkhāpadānīti attho.

In the Pāḷi, as for `sataṃ sattati chaccevime honti ubhinnaṃ asādhāraṇā`: the meaning is that the forty-six training rules of the bhikkhus, not shared with the bhikkhunīs, and the one hundred and thirty training rules of the bhikkhunīs, not shared with the bhikkhus—thus the training rules unshared by both are one hundred and seventy-six. As for `sataṃ sattati cattāri`: this is the count of the training rules shared by both; the meaning is that there are one hundred and seventy-four such training rules.

Vibhattiyoti āpattikkhandhā ceva uposathapavāraṇādayo ca adhippetā. Te hi pārājikādibhedena, bhikkhuuposathādibhedena ca vibhajīyanti. Tenāha “vibhattiyo”tiādi. Tesanti aṭṭhannaṃ pārājikādīnaṃ. Dvīhītiādi vivādādhikaraṇādīnaṃ samathehi vūpasamadassanaṃ.

By `vibhattiyo`, both the aggregates of offenses and observances such as the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā are intended. For they are divided by distinctions such as `pārājika`, etc., and by distinctions such as the bhikkhu Uposatha, etc. Therefore, it is said, `vibhattiyo`, etc. As for `tesaṃ`: of the eight, `pārājika`, etc. The phrase `dvīhi`, etc., is for showing the settlement of legal questions concerning disputes, etc., by means of the settlement procedures.

Sattanagaresu paññattasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rules promulgated in the seven cities is concluded.

Pārājikādiāpattivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of Offenses Beginning with Pārājika.

339. Idanti “pārājikanti yaṃ vutta”ntiādinā vuttaṃ vacanaṃ sandhāya vadati. Idañhi heṭṭhā “garuka lahuka”ntiādinā uddhaṭapañhesu anāgatampi “sabbānipetāni viyākarohi, handa vākyaṃ suṇoma te”ti ettha yathāvuttāni aññānipi “sabbānipetāni viyākarohi, handa vākyaṃ suṇomā”ti evaṃ gahitamevāti dassento “iminā pana āyācanavacanena saṅgahitassā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

339. The word `idaṃ` is spoken with reference to the statement beginning with `pārājikanti yaṃ vuttaṃ`. Indeed, wishing to show that although this did not appear below in the questions raised beginning with `garukaṃ lahukaṃ`, in the phrase `sabbānipetāni viyākarohi, handa vākyaṃ suṇoma te`, it is taken to mean 'Explain all these things—both those already mentioned and others—come, let us hear your words,' the passage beginning with `iminā pana āyācanavacanena saṅgahitassā` was spoken.

Ativassatīti ovassati, vassodakaṃ pavisatīti attho. Dhammānanti yathā catupaccaye dhārayatīti dhammo, tesaṃ. Tenāha “saṅkhatadhammāna”nti. Gāthāsaṅgaṇikanti gāthāsaṅgaho, te te atthā gāthāhi saṅgahetvā gaṇīyanti kathīyanti etthāti hi gāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ.

“Ativassati” means it pours down; the meaning is that rainwater enters. As for “dhammānaṃ,” because it sustains the four requisites, it is called a “dhamma”; “dhammānaṃ” means “of these.” Therefore, he said, “saṅkhatadhammānaṃ” (of conditioned phenomena). As for “gāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ,” it is a collection of verses. Indeed, because in this statement those various meanings are collected by means of verses and are enumerated and spoken, it is called “gāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ.”

Pārājikādiāpattivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of Offenses Beginning with Pārājika is Concluded.

Paṭhamagāthāsaṅgaṇikavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The Method of Explanation for the First Collection of Verses is Concluded.

Adhikaraṇabhedaṃ

The Division of Legal Issues

Ukkoṭanabhedādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discussion on the Division of Re-opening a Case and Other Matters

341. “Alaṃ [M 2.0295][V 2.0280] āvuso”ti attapaccatthike saññāpetvāti pattacīvarādiatthāya alaṃ bhaṇḍanādikaraṇanti vivādādīsu dosadassanamattena saññāpetvā aññamaññaṃ khamāpetvā vūpasamenti, na pana aññamaññaṃ āpattānāpattidassanavasenāti adhippāyo. Tenāha “pāḷimuttakavinicchayenevā”ti.

The phrase `alaṃ āvuso’ti attapaccatthike saññāpetvā` means: having made the opposing parties understand, 'Friends, it is not proper to engage in quarreling and so forth for the sake of bowls, robes, and other requisites.' Thus, in disputes and the like, they bring about a settlement by merely pointing out the fault and having them ask forgiveness from one another, but not by way of demonstrating to one another what is an offense and what is not an offense. This is the intention. Therefore, he said, `pāḷimuttakavinicchayenevā` (by a decision independent of the Pāḷi text alone).

Visamāni kāyakammādīni nissito bhikkhu visamanissito nāma, micchādiṭṭhinissito gahananissito, balavante purise nissito balavanissito nāmāti dassento “eko visamānī”tiādimāha.

A bhikkhu who relies on uneven bodily actions and so forth is called 'one who relies on the uneven'; one who relies on wrong view is called 'one who relies on the thicket'; one who relies on powerful persons is called 'one who relies on the powerful.' Wishing to show this, he said the passage beginning with `eko visamāni`.

Ukkoṭanabhedādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

341. The Explanation of the Discussion on the Division of Re-opening a Case and Other Matters is Concluded.

Adhikaraṇanidānādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Origin of Legal Issues and Other Matters.

342. Āpattiṃ nissāya uppajjanakaāpattivasenāti paresaṃ, attano ca āpattiṃ paṭicchādentānaṃ vajjapaṭicchādīnaṃ pārājikādiāpattimeva sandhāya vuttaṃ, na sabbāpattiyo. Kiccaṃ nissāya uppajjanakakiccānanti ukkhepanīyādikammaṃ nissāya uppajjanakānaṃ tadanuvattikāya bhikkhuniyā yāvatatiyānussāvanānaṃ kiccānaṃ vasena, na sabbesaṃ kiccānaṃ vasenāti.

The phrase `āpattiṃ nissāya uppajjanakaāpattivasena` is spoken with reference only to the offenses beginning with pārājika of the `vajjapaṭicchādī` bhikkhunīs who conceal the offenses of others and of themselves; it is not spoken with reference to all offenses. The phrase `kiccaṃ nissāya uppajjanakakiccānaṃ` means that an issue arises by way of duties that arise depending on a formal act such as suspension (`ukkhepanīya`), namely the duties of admonishing up to the third time a bhikkhunī who is a follower of the suspended one; it does not arise by way of all duties.

344. Pāḷiyaṃ “katihi adhikaraṇehī”ti pucchāya “ekena adhikaraṇena kiccādhikaraṇenā”ti vuttaṃ. “Katisu ṭhānesū”ti pucchāya “tīsu ṭhānesu saṅghamajjhe, gaṇamajjhe, puggalassa santike”ti vuttaṃ. “Katihi samathehī”ti pucchāya “tīhi samathehī”ti vuttaṃ. Tīhipi etehi eko vūpasamanappakārova pucchito, vissajjito cāti veditabbo.

In the Pāḷi, to the question, “By how many legal issues?” the answer given is, “By one legal issue, a procedural issue.” To the question, “In how many places?” the answer given is, “In three places: in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, and in the presence of an individual.” To the question, “By how many settlements?” the answer given is, “By three settlements.” It should be understood that by all three of these questions and answers, only one mode of settlement is both asked about and answered.

348. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ [V 2.0281] hoti anuvādādhikaraṇantiādīsu vivādādhikaraṇameva anuvādādhikaraṇādipi hotīti pucchāya vivādādhikaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇameva hoti, anuvādādayo na hotīti vissajjanaṃ.

342. In passages beginning with `vivādādhikaraṇaṃ hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ`, to the question, “Is a legal issue of dispute also a legal issue of accusation and so forth?” the answer is that a legal issue of dispute is only a legal issue of dispute; legal issues of accusation and so forth do not arise.

Adhikaraṇanidānādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

344. The Explanation of the Origin of Legal Issues and Other Matters is Concluded.

Sattasamathanānātthādivaṇṇanā

348. The Explanation of the Seven Appeasements, Various Meanings, and So Forth.

354. Adhikaraṇapucchāvissajjane [M 2.0296] pāḷiyaṃ vipaccayatāya vohāroti virūpavipākāya aññamaññaṃ dukkhuppādanāya kāyavacīvohāro. Medhaganti vuddhippatto kalaho.

In the Pāḷi, in the answer to the question on legal issues, the term `vohāra` in the sense of `vipaccayatā` (adversity) is bodily and verbal disputing for the purpose of an adverse result, for causing suffering to one another. `Medhaga` means a quarrel that has reached maturity.

Anusampavaṅkatāti vipatticodanāya anu anu saṃyujjanavasena ninnatā.

`Anusampavaṅkatā` means an inclination by way of being repeatedly connected to an accusation of transgression.

Abbhussahanatāti ativiya sañjātussāhatā. Anubalappadānanti codakānampi upatthambhakaraṇaṃ. Kammasaṅgahābhāvenāti saṅghasammukhatādimattassa sammukhāvinayassa saṅghādīhi kattabbakiccesu saṅgahābhāvā.

354. `Abbhussahanatā` means being exceedingly enthusiastic. `Anubalappadāna` means giving support even to the accusers. `Kammasaṅgahābhāvena` means due to the absence of inclusion of the `sammukhāvinaya`—which is merely the presence of the Saṅgha and so forth—in the duties to be performed by the Saṅgha and others.

Sattasamathanānātthādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Seven Appeasements, Various Meanings, and So Forth is concluded.

Adhikaraṇabhedavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The Method of Explaining the Divisions of Legal Issues is concluded.

Dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

The Second Collection of Verses

Codanādipucchāvissajjanāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of Questions and Answers Beginning with Accusation

359. Dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikāya [M 2.0297] “codanā kimatthāyā”tiādikā pucchā upālittherena katā. “Codanā sāraṇatthāyā”tiādivissajjanaṃ bhagavatā vuttaṃ. Upālitthero sayameva pucchitvā vissajjanaṃ akāsītipi vadanti.

In the Second Collection of Verses, the question beginning, “For what purpose is accusation?” was asked by the Elder Upāli. The answer beginning, “Accusation is for the purpose of reminding,” was spoken by the Blessed One. Some also say that the Elder Upāli himself asked the question and gave the answer.

Mantaggahaṇanti tesaṃ vicāraṇāgahaṇaṃ, suttantikattherānaṃ, vinayadharattherānañca adhippāyagahaṇanti [V 2.0282] attho. Pāṭekkaṃ vinicchayasanniṭṭhāpanatthanti tesaṃ paccekaṃ adhippāyaṃ ñatvā tehi samuṭṭhāpitanayampi gahetvā vinicchayapariyosāpanatthanti adhippāyo.

`Mantaggahaṇa` means the grasping of their deliberation; the meaning is that it is the grasping of the intention of the Suttanta-reciting elders and the Vinaya-holding elders. `Pāṭekkaṃ vinicchayasanniṭṭhāpanatthaṃ` (for the purpose of settling each individual decision) means: for the purpose of concluding the decision, having known their individual intentions and also having taken the method established by them—this is the intention.

“Mā kho turito abhaṇī”tiādinā abhimukhe ṭhitaṃ kañci anuvijjakaṃ ovadantena viya therena anuvijjakavattaṃ kathitaṃ.

359. By means of the phrase, “Do not speak hastily,” and so forth, the duties of an investigator were spoken by the Elder as if he were advising a certain investigator standing before him.

Anuyuñjanavattanti anuyujjanakkamaṃ, taṃ pana yasmā sabbasikkhāpadavītikkamavisayepi taṃtaṃsikkhāpadānulomena kattabbaṃ, tasmā “sikkhāpadānulomika”nti vuttaṃ. Attano gatiṃ nāsetīti attano sugatigamanaṃ vināseti.

`Anuyuñjanavatta` means the procedure of questioning. Since that procedure should be carried out in accordance with the respective training rule even in a matter of transgressing any training rule, it is therefore called `sikkhāpadānulomika` (in accordance with the training rules). `Attano gatiṃ nāseti` (destroys one's own destination) means one destroys one's own going to a good destination.

Anusandhita-saddo bhāvasādhanoti āha “anusandhitanti kathānusandhī”ti. Vattānusandhitenāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Vattānusandhitenāti ācārānusandhinā, ācārena saddhiṃ samentiyā paṭiññāyāti attho. Tenāha “yā assa vattenā”tiādi.

The word `anusandhita` is a noun of state (`bhāvasādhana`); therefore, it is said, “`Anusandhita` means continuity of speech (`kathānusandhi`).” In the word `vattānusandhitena` also, this is the same method. `Vattānusandhitena` means by continuity of conduct (`ācārānusandhinā`); the meaning is by a pledge that accords with one's conduct. Therefore, it is said, “Whatever by his conduct,” and so forth.

Pāḷiyaṃ sañcicca āpattintiādi alajjilajjilakkhaṇaṃ bhikkhubhikkhunīnaṃ vasena vuttaṃ tesaññeva sabbappakārato sikkhāpadādhikārattā. Sāmaṇerādīnampi sādhāraṇavasena pana sañcicca yathāsakaṃ sikkhāpadavītikkamanādikaṃ alajjilajjilakkhaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ.

In the Pāḷi, the characteristic of the shameless and the shameful, beginning with “an intentional offense,” is spoken with reference to monks and nuns, because the training rules are their domain in every respect. However, with regard to novices and others, by way of what is common, intentionally transgressing their own respective training rules, and so forth, should be understood as the characteristic of the shameless and the shameful.

Kathānusandhivacananti cuditakaanuvijjakānaṃ kathāya anusandhiyuttaṃ vacanaṃ na jānāti, tehi ekasmiṃ kāraṇe vutte sayaṃ taṃ asallakkhetvā attano abhirucitameva asambandhitatthanti attho. Vinicchayānusandhivacanañcāti anuvijjakena katassa āpattānāpattivinicchayassa anuguṇaṃ, sambandhavacanañca.

`Kathānusandhivacana` means: one does not know the speech that is connected with the talk of the accused and the investigator. When a certain point is spoken by them, one, not having noted that point, understands only an unconnected matter that is pleasing to oneself—this is the meaning. And `vinicchayānusandhivacana` is speech that is in accordance with the decision on offense and non-offense made by the investigator, and it is connected speech.

Codanādipucchāvissajjanāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of Questions and Answers Beginning with Accusation is concluded.

Codanākaṇḍaṃ

The Chapter on Accusation.

Anuvijjakakiccavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Duties of the Investigator.

360. Pāḷiyaṃ [M 2.0298][V 2.0283] yaṃ kho tvantiādīsu tvaṃ, āvuso, yaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ codesi, taṃ kimhi dose codesi, katarāya vipattiyā codesīti attho. Evaṃ sabbattha.

360. In the Pāḷi, in passages such as `yaṃ kho tvaṃ...`, the meaning is: 'Friend, regarding the matter for which you accuse this bhikkhu, for what fault do you accuse him? By what kind of transgression do you accuse him?' This is so everywhere.

361. Asuddhaparisaṅkitoti asuddhāya aṭṭhāne uppannāya parisaṅkāya parisaṅkito. Tenāha “amūlakaparisaṅkito”ti.

361. `Asuddhaparisaṅkito` (suspected of impurity) means: one is suspected due to a suspicion of impurity that has arisen in an inappropriate instance. Therefore, it is said, `amūlakaparisaṅkito` (suspected without basis).

364. Pāḷiyaṃ uposatho sāmaggatthāyāti visuddhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ aññoññanirapekkho ahutvā uposatho uposathaṭṭhānaṃ sannipatitvā “pārisuddhiṃ āyasmanto ārocetha, parisuddhetthāyasmanto, parisuddho ahaṃ āvuso”tiādinā aññamaññaṃ parisuddhivīmaṃsanārocanavasena ayutte vivajjetvā yutteheva kāyacittasāmaggīkaraṇatthāya.

364. In the Pāḷi, `uposatho sāmaggatthāya` means: for purified bhikkhus, not being unconcerned with one another, the Uposatha is for the purpose of creating unity of body and mind with only suitable persons, having assembled at the Uposatha place and, by means of mutual examination and declaration of purity with such words as, ‘Venerable sirs, declare your purity; the venerable sirs here are pure; I am pure, friends,’ having avoided unsuitable persons.

Visuddhāya pavāraṇāti diṭṭhasutādīhi aññamaññaṃ kathāpetvā visuddhisampādanatthāyāti attho. Ubho eteti āmisapuggalanissayane ete ubho.

`Visuddhāya pavāraṇā` means for the purpose of accomplishing purity by having one another speak about what was seen, heard, and so on. `Ubho ete` refers to these two: reliance on material things and reliance on persons.

Anuvijjakakiccavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Duties of the Investigator is concluded.

Cūḷasaṅgāmaṃ

The Minor Confrontation.

Anuvijjakassa paṭipattivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Practice of the Investigator.

365. Tatra [M 2.0299] hīti tasmiṃ sannipāte. Attapaccatthikāti lajjipesalassa codakapāpagarahīpuggalassa anatthakāmā verīpuggalā. Sāsanapaccatthikāti attano anācārānuguṇaṃ buddhavacanaṃ pakāsento taṇhāgatikā, diṭṭhigatikā ca. Ajjhogāhetvāti alajjiabhibhavanavasena [V 2.0284] saṅghamajjhaṃ pavisitvā. So saṅgāmāvacaroti so codako saṅgāmāvacaro nāma. Diṭṭhasutamutampi rājakathādikanti diṭṭhasutavaseneva rājacorādikathaṃ, mutavasenapi annādikathañca akathentenāti yojetabbaṃ. Kappiyākappiyanissitā vātiādīsu rūpārūpapaṭicchedapadena sakalaabhidhammatthapiṭakattaṃ dasseti. Samathācārādīhi paṭisaṃyuttanti sakalasuttantapiṭakattaṃ. Tattha samathācāro nāma samathabhāvanākkamo. Tathā vipassanācāro. Ṭhānanisajjavattādinissitāti saṅghamajjhādīsu garucittīkāraṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā ṭhānādikkamanissitā ceva cuddasamahāvattādivattanissitā ca, ādi-saddena appicchatādinissitā cāti attho. Pañhe uppanneti kenaci uppanne pañhe pucchite. Idañca upalakkhaṇamattaṃ, yaṃ kiñci upaṭṭhitaṃ dhammaṃ bhāsassūti adhippāyo.

365. `Tatra hi` means in that assembly. `Attapaccatthikā` means hostile persons who desire the disadvantage of the accuser, a person who is modest, virtuous, and censures evil. `Sāsanapaccatthikā` means those who follow after craving and those who follow after wrong views, who proclaim the Buddha's word in accordance with their own misconduct. `Ajjhogāhetvā` means having entered the midst of the Saṅgha by means of overpowering the shameless one. `So saṅgāmāvacaro` means that accuser is called a `saṅgāmāvacara` (one who frequents battlefields). `Diṭṭhasutamutampi rājakathādikaṃ` should be construed as: by not speaking of talk of kings, thieves, and so on, based only on what is seen or heard, and talk without beginning based on what is cognized. In passages such as `kappiyākappiyanissitā vā`, by the term `rūpārūpapariccheda` (distinction of form and formless), it indicates the meaning of the entire Abhidhamma Piṭaka. By the passage `samathācārādīhi paṭisaṃyuttaṃ`, it indicates the meaning of the entire Suttanta Piṭaka. Therein, `samathācāra` (the conduct of tranquility) is the sequence of developing tranquility; similarly for `vipassanācāra` (the conduct of insight). `Ṭhānanisajjavattādinissitā` means: having established respect and reverence in the midst of the Saṅgha and so on, one relies on the transgression of standing, and on the observances such as the fourteen great observances; by the word `ādi` (etc.), the meaning is that one also relies on having few desires and so on. `Pañhe uppanne` means when a question is made to arise, when it is asked by someone. And this is merely an illustration; the intention is: ‘You should speak on whatever Dhamma presents itself.’

Kulapadeso nāma khattiyādijātiyampi kāsikarājakulādikulaviseso. Etamevāha “kulapadeso khattiyakulādivaseneva veditabbo”ti. Sannipātamaṇḍaleti attano anuvijjamānappakāraṃ saṅghassa ñāpanatthaṃ uṭṭhāya saṅghasannipātamajjhe ito cito ca paresaṃ mukhaṃ olokentena na caritabbaṃ. Yathānisinneneva dhammavinayānuguṇaṃ vinicchayaṃ yathā sabbe suṇanti, tathā vattabbanti attho.

`Kulapadeso` (a specific family) means, even among castes such as the Khattiya, a specific kind of family, such as the Kāsika royal family. For this reason, it is said: ‘A specific family should be understood in terms of Khattiya families and the like.’ `Sannipātamaṇḍale` (in the assembly circle) means: for the purpose of making known to the Saṅgha one's manner of investigation, one should not stand up in the middle of the Saṅgha assembly and wander about looking at the faces of others here and there. The meaning is that, remaining seated as one is, one should state the decision in accordance with the Dhamma and Vinaya in such a way that all may hear.

Pāḷiyaṃ acaṇḍikatenāti akatacaṇḍabhāvena, apharusenāti attho. “Hitānukampinā”ti etena mettāpubbabhāgo vutto. “Kāruṇikena bhavitabba”nti iminā appanāppattakaruṇā vuttā. “Hitaparisakkinā”ti iminā karuṇāpubbabhāgo. Tenāha “karuṇā ca karuṇāpubbabhāgo ca upaṭṭhāpetabboti ayaṃ padadvayepi adhippāyo”ti. Lajjiyāti lajjinī.

In the Pāḷi, `acaṇḍikatena` means by not adopting a fierce nature; the meaning is `apharusena` (not roughly). By the term `hitānukampinā` (sympathetic to their welfare), the preliminary stage of loving-kindness is stated. By the phrase `kāruṇikena bhavitabba` (one should be compassionate), compassion that has reached absorption is stated. By the term `hitaparisakkinā` (seeking their welfare), the preliminary stage of compassion is stated. Therefore, it is said: ‘Both compassion and the preliminary stage of compassion should be established’—this is the intention in both terms. `Lajjiyā` means for the conscientious one.

Anuyogavattaṃ [M 2.0300] kathāpetvāti “kālena vakkhāmī”tiādinā (pari. 362) vuttavattaṃ. Anuyuñjanācārakkameneva anuyuñjanaṃ anuyogavattaṃ nāma, taṃ kathāpetvā teneva kamena anuyuñjāpetvāti attho. Ujumaddavenāti ettha ajjhāharitabbapadaṃ dasseti “upacaritabbo”ti. “Dhammesu ca puggalesu cā”ti idaṃ “majjhattena bhavitabba”nti pakatena sambandhitabbanti āha “dhammesu ca puggalesu ca…pe… majjhattoti veditabbo”ti. Yañhi yattha katthaci kattabbaṃ, taṃ tattha atikkamanto majjhatto nāma na hoti, dhammesu ca gāravo kattabbo. Puggalesu pana mettābhāvena pakkhapātagāravo. Tasmā imaṃ vidhiṃ anatikkantova tesu majjhattoti veditabbo.

`Anuyogavattaṃ kathāpetvā` refers to the duty stated with the words, ‘I will speak at the proper time,’ and so on. The interrogation itself, following the procedure of the conduct of interrogation, is called the `anuyogavatta` (duty of interrogation). The meaning is: having caused that to be stated, and having caused the interrogation to proceed according to that same procedure. In the phrase `ujumaddavena` (with uprightness and gentleness), it shows that the word to be supplied is `upacaritabbo` (one should be treated). The phrase `dhammesu ca puggalesu ca` (in regard to both the Dhamma and individuals) should be connected with the preceding phrase, `majjhattena bhavitabba` (one should be impartial). Therefore, it is said: ‘In regard to both the Dhamma and individuals… one should be understood as impartial.’ For, one who transgresses what should be done in any given situation is not called ‘impartial.’ And respect should be shown towards the Dhamma. However, with regard to individuals, respect due to partiality arises through the state of loving-kindness. Therefore, one should be understood as being impartial towards them only when not transgressing this rule.

366. Saṃsandanatthanti āpatti vā anāpatti vāti saṃsaye jāte saṃsanditvā nicchayakaraṇatthaṃ [V 2.0285] vuttanti adhippāyo. Atthadassanāyāti sādhetabbassa āpattādiupameyyatthassa codakacuditake attano paṭiññāya eva sarūpavibhāvanatthaṃ. Attho jānāpanatthāyāti evaṃ vibhāvito attho codakacuditakasaṅghānaṃ ñāpanatthāya nijjhāpanatthāya, sampaṭicchāpanatthāyāti attho. Puggalassa ṭhapanatthāyāti codakacuditake attano paṭiññāya eva āpattiyaṃ, anāpattiyaṃ vā patiṭṭhāpanatthāya. Sāraṇatthāyāti pamuṭṭhasarāpanatthāya. Savacanīyakaraṇatthāyāti dose sāritepi sampaṭicchitvā paṭikammaṃ akarontassa savacanīyakaraṇatthāya. “Na te apasādetabbā”ti idaṃ adhippetatthadassanaṃ. Tattha avisaṃvādakaṭṭhāne ṭhitā eva na apasādetabbā, na itareti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

366. ‘For the purpose of collation’—the intention is that this is said for the purpose of making a decision by collating, when a doubt has arisen as to whether it is an offense or not an offense. ‘For the sake of showing the meaning’ means for the purpose of revealing the true nature of the meaning to be proven—the thing to be compared, such as the offense—to the accuser and the accused, by means of one's own declaration. ‘For the purpose of making the meaning known’—the meaning is that the meaning thus revealed is for the purpose of making it known to the accuser, the accused, and the Saṅgha, for the purpose of making them reflect, and for the purpose of making them accept it. ‘For the purpose of establishing the person’ means for the purpose of establishing the accuser and the accused in an offense or no offense, by means of one's own declaration. ‘For the purpose of reminding’ means for the purpose of causing one who has forgotten to remember. ‘For the purpose of making one answerable’ means for the purpose of making a person answerable who, even when reminded of the fault and having accepted it, does not undertake the remedy. ‘They are not to be rebuked’—this shows the intended meaning. Herein, it should be understood that only those who stand in a position of non-contradiction are not to be rebuked; it is not that others are not to be rebuked.

Appaccayaparinibbānatthāyāti āyatiṃ paṭisandhiyā akāraṇabhūtaparinibbānatthāya. Parinibbānañhi nāma khīṇāsavānaṃ sabbapacchimā cuticittakammajarūpasaṅkhātā khandhā, te ca sabbākārato samucchinnānusayatāya punabbhavāya anantarādipaccayā na honti aññehi ca taṇhādipaccayehi virahitattā. Tasmā “appaccayaparinibbāna”nti vuccati. Tanti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ. Tenevāha “tasmi”nti. Vinayamantanāti vinayavinicchayo. Sotāvadhānanti sotassa odahanaṃ, savananti attho. Tenāha “yaṃ uppajjati ñāṇa”nti. Yathāvuttāya vinayasaṃvarādikāraṇaparamparāya vimuttiyā eva padhānattā sā puna cittassa vimokkhoti uddhaṭoti āha “arahattaphalasaṅkhāto vimokkho”ti. Atha vā yo yaṃ kiñci dhammaṃ anupādiyitvā [M 2.0301] parinibbānavasena cittassa cittasantatiyā, tappaṭibaddhakammajarūpasantatiyā ca vimokkho vimuccanaṃ apunappavattivasena vigamo, etadatthāya etassa vigamassatthāya evāti evaṃ nigamanavasenapettha attho veditabbo.

‘For the sake of the final passing away without a resultant cause’ means for the sake of the final passing away which is not a cause for future rebirth-linking. Indeed, what is called ‘final passing away’ are the very last aggregates of those whose taints are destroyed, designated as the death-consciousness and kamma-born matter. And those aggregates, because their latent tendencies are cut off in every way, are not proximity conditions and so forth for renewed existence, and because they are devoid of other conditions such as craving. Therefore, it is called ‘the final passing away without a resultant cause.’ ‘That’ is the knowledge and vision of liberation. For that reason, he said ‘in that.’ ‘Deliberation on the Vinaya’ is the decision on the Vinaya. ‘Attentive listening’ is the applying of the ear; the meaning is ‘hearing.’ Therefore, he said, ‘whatever knowledge arises.’ Because liberation alone is primary through the succession of causes such as the restraint of the discipline as stated, that liberation is again extracted as ‘the liberation of the mind’; therefore, he said, ‘the liberation designated as the fruit of Arahantship.’ Alternatively, the meaning here should also be understood by way of conclusion thus: whatever liberation of the mind there is—a release from the continuity of mind and from the continuity of kamma-born matter connected with it, by not clinging to any phenomenon whatsoever by way of final passing away, which is the cessation by way of non-recurrence—is for the sake of this, for the sake of this very cessation.

367. Anuyogavattagāthāsu kusalena buddhimatāti sammāsambuddhena. Katanti nibbattitaṃ, pakāsitanti attho. Tenevātiādīsu teneva katākatassa ajānaneva pubbāparaṃ ajānanassa, aññassapi bhikkhuno yaṃ katākataṃ hoti, tampi na jānātīti attho. Attano sadisāyāti yathāvuttehi dosehi yuttatāya attanā sadisāya.

367. In the verses on the practice of inquiry, ‘by the skillful, the intelligent one’ means by the Perfectly Enlightened One. ‘Done’ means produced, declared; this is the meaning. In texts such as ‘by that very one,’ the meaning is: by that very fact of not knowing what was done and not done, of not knowing what comes before and after, he also does not know what duty is to be done by another bhikkhu. ‘Similar to oneself’ means similar to oneself because of being endowed with the faults as stated.

Anuvijjakassa paṭipattivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Practice of the Investigator is concluded.

Mahāsaṅgāmaṃ

The Great Battle

Voharantena jānitabbādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of ‘What Should Be Known by One Transacting,’ and So Forth

368-374. Mahāsaṅgāme [M 2.0302][V 2.0286] pāḷiyaṃ saṅgāmāvacarenāti anuvijjakaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vatthūti methunādivītikkamo. Nidānanti vesāliādipaññattiṭṭhānaṃ. Puggalo akārako jānitabboti ettha saṅghe vā gaṇe vā pariṇāyakabhūto puggaloti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

In the Pāḷi of the Mahāsaṅgāma, ‘by one who frequents battles’ is said with reference to an investigator. ‘Basis’ is the transgression of sexual intercourse, and so forth. ‘Origin’ is the place of promulgation, such as Vesālī. Here, in ‘the person should be known as a non-doer,’ it should be understood as a person who has become a leader in the Saṅgha or in a group.

375. Vissaṭṭhisikkhāpadanti nīlādidasannaṃ sukkānaṃ mocanavasena vuttaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhisikkhāpadaṃ. Tañhi telādimandavaṇṇānaṃ nīlādipacuravaṇṇānaṃ vasena “vaṇṇāvaṇṇā”ti vuttaṃ. Pacuratthe hi idha avaṇṇoti a-kāro.

375. ‘The training rule on emission’ is the training rule on the emission of semen, spoken by way of the emission of the ten kinds of semen, beginning with blue. For it is called ‘of color and of abundant color’ by way of faint colors such as oil and abundant colors such as blue. Indeed, here in the word ‘avaṇṇa,’ the letter ‘a’ occurs in the sense of ‘abundance’.

379. Yāva akaniṭṭhabrahmāno dvidhā hontīti ettha avihādisuddhāvāsikā aññabhūmīsu ariyā dhammavādīpakkhaṃ eva bhajanti, itare duvidhampīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

379. Here, in ‘up to the Akaniṭṭha brahmās, they become twofold,’ it should be understood thus: the noble ones who are inhabitants of the Pure Abodes, beginning with Avihā, and the noble ones in other planes, associate only with the faction of the Dhamma-speakers. The others associate with both factions.

Voharantena jānitabbādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of ‘What Should Be Known by One Transacting,’ and So Forth, is concluded.

Kathinabhedaṃ

The Section on the Kathina

Kathinaatthatādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Spreading of the Kathina, and So Forth

404. Kathine [M 2.0303] anāgatavasenāti udakāharaṇādipayoge uppanne pacchā dhovanādipubbakaraṇassa uppattito tappayogassa anāgatavaseneva anantarapaccayo. Paccayattañcassa kāriyabhūtassa yasmā nipphādetabbataṃ nissāya paccayā pavattā, na vinā tena, tasmā tena pariyāyena vuttaṃ, na sabhāvato sabbattha. Tenāha “payogassa hī”tiādi. Tattha payogassa sattavidhampi pubbakaraṇaṃ paccayo hotīti sambandho. Kāraṇamāha “yasmā”tiādi. Pubbakaraṇassatthāyāti pubbakaraṇassa nipphādanatthāya. Purejātapaccayeti purejātapaccayassa [V 2.0287] visaye. Esāti payogo. Dhovanādidhammesu ekampi attano purejātapaccayabhūtaṃ dhammaṃ na labhati, attano uppattito purejātassa pubbakaraṇassa abhāvāti attho. Labhatīti pacchājātapaccayaṃ pubbakaraṇaṃ labhati, pacchājātapaccayo hotīti attho.

404. Regarding the Kathina, the phrase 'by way of the future' is explained: when an application such as fetching water has arisen, and subsequently, due to the arising of a preliminary act such as washing, for that application the immediate condition is solely by way of the future. And as for its conditionality, which is an effect, because the conditions proceed relying on that which is to be accomplished, and not without it, it is therefore stated in that manner, not inherently in all cases. For that reason, he said, 'For the application...' and so forth. Therein, the connection is that the sevenfold preliminary act is a condition for the application. He states the reason with 'because...' and so forth. 'For the sake of the preliminary act' means for the accomplishment of the preliminary act. 'In the pre-nascent condition' means in the sphere of the pre-nascent condition. 'This' refers to the application. Among phenomena such as washing, it does not obtain even one phenomenon that has become its own pre-nascent condition; the meaning is, because of the absence of a preliminary act that arose prior to its own arising. 'It obtains' means: the preliminary act obtains the state of being a post-nascent condition; it becomes a post-nascent condition—this is the meaning.

Pāḷiyaṃ pannarasa dhammā sahajātapaccayena paccayoti ettha pubbakaraṇassāti vā payogassāti vā aññassa kassaci paccayuppannassa aparāmaṭṭhattā pannarasa dhammā sayaṃ aññamaññasahajātapaccayena paccayoti evamattho gahetabbo, tehi saha uppajjanakassa aññassa abhāvā. Evaṃ upari sabbattha. Tenāha “sahajātapaccayaṃ panā”tiādi. Mātikā ca palibodhā cāti ettha ca-saddena pañcānisaṃsāni gahitānīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ mātikānañca palibodhānañcāti etthāpi. Tehipi attho anantarameva mātikādīhi saha jāyanti. Teneva “pannarasa dhammā sahajātapaccayena paccayo”ti vuttā. Āsāti cīvarāsā. Vatthūti āsāya nimittabhūtaṃ anuppannacīvaraṃ. “Dassāma karissāmā”ti hi dāyakehi paṭiññātacīvaraṃ nissāya anantaraṃ uppajjamānā cīvarāsā anantarapaccayādibhāvena vuttā. Āsānañca anāsānañcāti labbhamānakacīvare uppajjanakacīvarāsānañceva alabbhamāne cīvare uppajjanakaanāsānañca, āsānaṃ, tabbigamānañcāti attho. Khaṇe khaṇe uppattibhedaṃ sandhāya “āsāna”nti bahuvacanaṃ kataṃ, āsāya[M 2.0304], anāsāya cāti attho. Tenāha “āsā ca anāsā cā”ti.

In the Pāḷi, regarding 'fifteen phenomena are a condition by way of the conascence condition,' here, because no other conditioned phenomenon whatsoever, such as 'of the preliminary act' or 'of the application,' is referred to, the meaning to be understood is that the fifteen phenomena are themselves mutually a condition by way of the conascence condition, as there is no other that arises together with them. Thus it is in all instances above. For that reason, he said, 'But the conascence condition...' and so forth. Regarding 'the matrix and the obstructions,' here it should be understood that the five benefits are included by the word 'ca.' Similarly, also regarding 'of the matrices and of the obstructions.' For they too arise immediately together with the matrix and so forth. For that very reason, it is said, 'fifteen phenomena are a condition by way of the conascence condition.' 'Hope' refers to the hope for a robe. 'Object' refers to the unarisen robe that serves as the basis for that hope. For the hope for a robe that arises immediately, relying on a robe promised by donors saying, 'We will give, we will make,' is stated as being in the manner of an immediate condition, and so forth. 'Of hopes and of lack of hope' means: of the hopes for a robe arising when a robe is obtainable, and of the lack of hope arising when a robe is unobtainable, and of desires, and of their passing away—this is the meaning. With reference to the difference in arising from moment to moment, the plural 'āsānaṃ' is used; the meaning is of hope and of lack of hope. Therefore, he said, 'hope and lack of hope.'

Kathinaatthatādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Spreading of the Kathina, and so forth, is concluded.

Pubbakaraṇanidānādivibhāgavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Division of Preparatory Actions, Origins, and So Forth

406-7. Cha cīvarānīti khomādīsu chasu aññataraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sabbasaṅgāhikavasena pana “cīvarānī”ti bahuvacanaṃ kataṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ panettha vatthu, āsā ca anāsā cātiādīsu atthate kathine ānisaṃsavasena uppajjanakapaccāsācīvaraṃ “vatthū”ti vuttaṃ. Kathinacīvaraṃ hetupaccaya-saddehi vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

'Six robes' is stated with reference to any one of the six types, such as linen, and so forth. However, the plural 'robes' is used by way of comprehensive inclusion. In the Pāḷi here, in phrases such as 'object,' 'hope and lack of hope,' and so forth, regarding the Kathina that has been spread, the robe anticipated as arising by way of the benefits is called 'object.' It should be understood that the Kathina robe is spoken of by terms such as 'cause' and 'condition'.

408. Paccuddhāro tīhi dhammehītiādi kathinatthāratthāya ticīvarato aññaṃ vassikasāṭikādiṃ paccuddharituṃ, adhiṭṭhahitvā attharituñca na vaṭṭatīti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. “Vacībhedenā”ti etena kevalaṃ kāyena kathinatthāro na ruhatīti dasseti.

408. 'Withdrawal is by three factors,' and so forth, is stated to show that for the purpose of spreading the Kathina, it is not permissible to withdraw, nor to determine and spread, a rains-cloth or the like that is other than the three robes. By this, 'by verbal declaration' indicates that the spreading of the Kathina does not succeed merely by physical action.

Pubbakaraṇanidānādivibhāgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Division of Preparatory Actions, Origins, and So Forth, is concluded.

Kathinādijānitabbavibhāgavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Division of Things to be Known Regarding the Kathina, etc.

412. Yesu [V 2.0288] rūpādidhammesūti “purimavassaṃvutthā bhikkhū, pañcahi anūno saṅgho, cīvaramāso, dhammena samena samuppannaṃ cīvara”nti evamādīsu yesu rūpārūpadhammesu. Satīti santesu. Missībhāvoti saṃsaggatā samūhapaññattimattaṃ. Tenāha “na paramatthato eko dhammo atthī”ti.

412. ‘In which material and so forth phenomena’—that is, in these material and immaterial phenomena, such as ‘monks who have completed the first rains-residence,’ ‘a Saṅgha of not less than five,’ ‘the robe-month,’ ‘a robe obtained righteously and properly,’ and so forth. ‘When present’ means when they exist. ‘State of mixture’ refers to association, a mere collective designation. Therefore, he said, ‘In the ultimate sense, there is not one single phenomenon.’

416. Ekato uppajjantīti kathinuddhārena saha uppajjamānārahā hontīti attho. Kathinatthārato hi pabhuti sabbe kathinuddhārā taṃ taṃ kāraṇantaramāgamma uppajjanti, tasmā sabbe ekuppādā nāma jātā. Tesu antarubbhārasahubbhārā dve eva taṃ vihāraṃ anatthatakathinavihārasadisaṃ karontā sayaṃ sakalena kathinatthārena saha nirujjhanti uddhārabhāvaṃ pāpuṇanti[M 2.0305]. Avasesā pana taṃ taṃ pāṭipuggalikameva kathinatthāraṃ dvinnaṃ palibodhānaṃ upacchindanavasena nirodhentā sayaṃ uddhārabhāvaṃ pāpuṇanti, na sakalaṃ kathinatthāraṃ. Kathinuddhārānañca nirodho nāma taṃ taṃ kāraṇamāgamma uddhārabhāvappatti, evañca uppatti nāma kathinuddhāro eva. Tenāha “sabbepi atthārena saddhiṃ ekato uppajjantī”tiādi. Tattha purimā dveti “ekuppādā ekanirodhā”ti pāḷiyaṃ paṭhamaṃ vuttā antarubbhārasahubbhārā dve. Tesūti pakkamanantikādīsu. Uddhārabhāvaṃ pattesūti uddhārabhāvappattisaṅkhātanirodhaṃ pattesūti attho. Atthāro tiṭṭhatīti katacīvaraṃ ādāya pakkantādipuggalaṃ ṭhapetvā tadavasesānaṃ palibodhasabbhāvato kathinatthāro tiṭṭhati.

416. ‘Arising together’ means they are fit to arise together with the spreading of the Kathina. For, from the spreading of the Kathina onwards, all Kathina revocations arise depending on this or that subsequent cause; therefore, they are all called 'of single arising'. Among these, only the two—disappearance and coincident revocation—render that monastery similar to one where the Kathina has not been spread, and they themselves cease together with the entire spreading of the Kathina, attaining the state of revocation.
