The remaining revocations, however, by way of cutting off the two hindrances for each individual, cause that individual's spreading of the Kathina to cease, and they themselves attain the state of revocation; they do not cause the entire spreading of the Kathina to cease. And the cessation of the Kathina spreadings is the attainment of the state of revocation, depending on this or that cause. And so, what is called 'arising' is the spreading of the Kathina itself. Therefore, he said, ‘All arise together with the spreading,’ and so forth. Therein, 'the first two' refers to the two—disappearance and coincident revocation—which are mentioned first in the Pāḷi as ‘of single arising, of single cessation.’ ‘Among them’ refers to those beginning with the revocation on departure. ‘Having reached the state of revocation’ means having reached the cessation which is designated as the attainment of the state of revocation. ‘The spreading remains’ means that, setting aside the individual who has departed after taking the completed robe, the spreading of the Kathina remains for the others due to the existence of the hindrances.

Kathinādijānitabbavibhāgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Division of Things to be Known Regarding the Kathina, etc., is concluded.

Paññattivaggavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The Method of Explaining the Chapter on Designations is concluded.

Saṅgahavaggo

The Chapter on Inclusion

Upālipañcakaṃ

The Upāli Pentad

Nappaṭippassambhanavaggavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Chapter on Non-Calming

421. Samaggehi [M 2.0306][V 2.0289] karaṇīyānīti vivādādhikaraṇehi pubbe asamaggā hutvā pacchā sāmaggiṃ upagatehi kattabbāni. Kiṃ pana asaññatamissaparisāya saddhiṃ lajjino sāmaggiṃ karontīti āha “uposathapavāraṇādīsu hī”tiādi. Tattha ṭhitāsūti uposathapavāraṇāsu appavattīsu. Upatthambho na dātabboti uparūpari appavattanatthāya mayampi uposathaṃ na karissāmātiādinā kalahassa upatthambho na dātabbo, dhammena vinayena sāmaggiṃ katvā samaggeheva asaññatā bhikkhū vinetabbāti adhippāyo. Tenāha “sace saṅgho accayaṃ desāpetvā”tiādi. Bhikkhuno nakkhamatīti kesuci puggalesu appamattakadosadassanena na ruccati. Diṭṭhāvikammampi katvāti “na metaṃ khamatī”ti sabhāgassa bhikkhuno attano diṭṭhiṃ āvikatvā. Upetabbāti sāsanahāniyā abhāvā sāmaggiṃ akopetvā kāyasāmaggī dātabbā, īdise ṭhāne alajjiparibhogo āpattikaro na hoti, vaṭṭatiyeva. Ye pana sāsanavināsāya paṭipannā, tehi saha na vattati, āpatti eva hoti sāsanavināso ca. Tenāha “yatra pana uddhamma”ntiādi. “Diṭṭhāvikammaṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti iminā diṭṭhiyā āvikatāyapi āpattiṃ dasseti.

421. ‘Acts to be done by those in unity’ means: the acts to be done by those monks who, having previously been disunited due to disputes and legal issues, later attained unity. But how can conscientious monks achieve unity with an assembly mixed with the unrestrained? For this reason, it is said, ‘In Uposatha, Pavāraṇā, etc.’ Therein, ‘when they are established’ means when Uposatha and Pavāraṇā are not proceeding. ‘Support should not be given’ means: for the sake of preventing it from repeatedly not proceeding, support for a quarrel should not be given by saying, “We too will not perform the Uposatha.” The intention is that the unrestrained monks should be disciplined only by those who are united, having established unity in accordance with the Dhamma and Vinaya. Therefore, he said, ‘If the Saṅgha, having had the transgression confessed…’ ‘It is not agreeable to the monk’ means: he is not pleased due to seeing a minor fault in certain individuals. ‘Having even made his view known’ means: having made his own view apparent to a monk of like mind by saying, “This is not agreeable to me.” ‘It should be undertaken’ means: because there is no decline of the Teaching, unity should not be disrupted, and bodily unity should be given. In such a situation, association with the shameless does not entail an offense; it is indeed permissible. But as for those who are practicing for the destruction of the Teaching, association with them is not permissible; there is indeed an offense, and there is destruction of the Teaching. Therefore, he said, ‘But where there is a perversion of the Dhamma…’ By this statement, ‘Making one’s view known is not permissible,’ he shows that there is an offense even when the view has been made apparent.

422. Kaṇhavācoti rāgadosādīhi kiliṭṭhavacano. Anatthakavacanassa dīpanaṃ pakāsanaṃ assāti anatthakadīpano. Mānaṃ nissāyāti vinicchayakaraṇaṃ tava bhāroti saṅghena bhāre akatepi “ahamevettha voharituṃ araharūpo”ti mānaṃ nissāya. Yathādiṭṭhiyāti anurūpaladdhiyā. Yassa hi atthassa yādisī diṭṭhi anurūpā, taṃ gahetvā na byākatāti attho[V 2.0290].Assa attanoti adhammādiatthaṃ sandhāya vadati, na puggalaṃ, assa adhammādiatthasaṅkhātassa attano sarūpassa yā anurūpā diṭṭhīti [M 2.0307] attho. Laddhiṃ nikkhipitvāti anurūpaladdhiṃ chaḍḍetvā, aggahetvāti attho. Tenāha “adhammādīsu dhammādiladdhiko hutvā”ti. Atha vā attano laddhiṃ nigūhitvā puggalānuguṇaṃ tathā byākaronto na yathādiṭṭhiyā byākatā nāma. Imasmiṃ pakkhe adhammādīsu dhammādiladdhiko hutvāti ettha adhammādīsu dhammādiladdhiko viya hutvāti attho gahetabbo.

422. ‘One of dark speech’ means one whose speech is defiled by lust, hatred, and so on. ‘One who illuminates the unbeneficial’ is so called because for this person there is the illumination and clarification of unbeneficial speech. ‘Relying on conceit’ means: even when the responsibility has not been given by the Saṅgha, relying on the conceit that, “I alone am fit to decide here.” ‘According to his view’ means according to a suitable view. The meaning is that for whatever matter, whatever view is suitable, he does not declare it, having grasped that view. ‘Of his own’ means: he speaks with reference to the meaning of non-Dhamma, etc., not with reference to a person. The meaning is: the view that is suitable for his own nature, which is designated as the meaning of non-Dhamma, etc. ‘Having set aside the view’ means having abandoned the suitable view, not having grasped it—this is the meaning. Therefore, he said, ‘having become one with a Dhamma-view in matters of non-Dhamma, etc.’ Alternatively, one who, having concealed his own view, declares in such a way according to the person, is not one who has declared according to his view. In this alternative, here in the phrase ‘having become one with a Dhamma-view in matters of non-Dhamma, etc.,’ the meaning should be taken as: ‘having become as if one with a Dhamma-view in matters of non-Dhamma, etc.’

Nappaṭippassambhanavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter on Non-Calming is concluded.

Vohāravaggādivaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Section on Transactions, etc.

424. Kammañattīti kammabhūtā ñatti. Anussāvananirapekkhā ñattikammabhūtā ñattīti attho. Kammapādañatti nāma ñattidutiyakammādīsu anussāvanakammassa pādabhūtā adhiṭṭhānabhūtā ñatti. Navasu ṭhānesūti osāraṇādīsu navasu ṭhānesu. Dvīsu ṭhānesūti ñattidutiyañatticatutthakammesu.

424. `Kammañatti` means a motion that is the act itself. The meaning is: it is a motion that is a formal act by motion, independent of a proclamation. What is called `kammapādañatti` is a motion that serves as the basis or foundation for the act of proclamation in procedures such as those requiring a motion followed by one proclamation. `In nine instances` means in the nine instances such as reinstatement. `In two instances` means in procedures requiring a motion followed by one proclamation and those requiring a motion followed by three proclamations.

Suttānulomanti ubhatovibhaṅge suttānulomabhūte mahāpadese sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vinayānulomanti khandhakaparivārānulomabhūte mahāpadese. Suttantike cattāro mahāpadeseti suttābhidhammapiṭakesu anuññātapaṭikkhittasuttānulomavasena nayato gahetabbe cattāro atthe.

`Suttānuloma` is said in reference to the great authorities in both Vibhaṅgas that are in conformity with the Suttas. `Vinayānuloma` is said in reference to the great authorities that are in conformity with the Khandhakas and Parivāra. `The four great authorities in the Suttanta` is said in reference to the four meanings to be understood by method from the Sutta and Abhidhamma Piṭakas, by way of what is permitted and prohibited in conformity with the Suttas.

425. Diṭṭhīnaṃ āvikammānīti āpattiladdhīnaṃ pakāsanāni, āpattidesanākammānīti attho.

425. `Diṭṭhīnaṃ āvikammāni` means the declarations of views that are offenses; the meaning is, they are the acts of confessing offenses.

Yathā catūhi pañcahi diṭṭhi āvikatā hotīti yathā āvikate catūhi pañcahi ekībhūtehi ekassa puggalassa santike āpatti desitā nāma hoti, evaṃ desetīti attho. Evaṃ desento ca attanā saddhiṃ tayo vā cattāro vā bhikkhū gahetvā ekassa santike deseti. Evaṃ desetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Desitā ca āpatti na vuṭṭhāti, desanāpaccayā dukkaṭañca hoti. Dvinnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ pana ekato desetuṃ vaṭṭati.

`Just as a view is made manifest by four or five` means: in the manner that an offense is considered confessed in the presence of one person when it is made manifest by four or five monks who are united, so does one confess. This is the meaning. A monk confessing in this way takes three or four monks with him and confesses in the presence of one monk. It is not proper to confess in this way. And even if confessed, the offense is not lifted; and because of the confession, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred by him. However, it is proper for two or three to confess together.

444. Adassanenāti imassa akappiyaṃ parivajjentānaṃ vinayadharānaṃ paṭipattiyā adassanena[V 2.0291], tesaṃ diṭṭhānugatiṃ anāpajjanenātipi attho gahetabbo. Akappiye kappiyasaañatāyāti rajatādiakappiye tipuādisaññitāya[M 2.0308]. Pucchitvā vā aññesaṃ vā vuccamānaṃ asuṇanto āpajjatīti ettha pucchitvā asuṇanto vā pucchiyamānaṃ asuṇanto vāti paccekaṃ yojetabbaṃ. Ekarattātikkamādivasenāti adhiṭṭhitacīvarena vippavasitvā ekarattātikkamena pācittiyaṃ āpajjati. Ādi-saddena charattātikkamādīnaṃ saṅgaho.

444. `By not seeing` means: by not seeing the practice of the Vinaya-holders who avoid what is improper for this monk; this meaning should also be taken: by not following the example of what they have seen. `By perceiving the improper as proper` means: in the case of what is improper, such as silver, having the perception that it is tin, etc. Here, in the phrase `he commits an offense by not listening when asked or when it is being said by others`, it should be construed separately thus: `not listening after having asked` or `not listening when being asked`. `By way of exceeding one night, etc.` means: one falls into a pācittiya offense by being separated from a determined robe and exceeding one night. By the word `ādi`, exceeding six nights, etc., is included.

450. Anatthaṃ kalisāsananti anatthāvahaṃ kodhavacanaṃ āropento dosaṃ āropento upaddavāya parisakkatīti attho.

450. `Anatthaṃ kalisāsanaṃ` means: imputing words of anger that bring harm, imputing fault, one strives for trouble to arise. This is the meaning.

454. Vohāraniruttiyanti tassa tassa atthassa vācakasadde pabhedagatañāṇappatto na hotīti attho.

454. `In conventional terminology` means: one has not attained the knowledge of the distinctions in the words that express each particular meaning. This is the meaning.

455. Parimaṇḍalabyañjanāropane kusalo na hotīti parimaṇḍalena padabyañjanena vatthuṃ, parehi vuttaṃ jānituñca asamatthoti attho.

455. `Is not skilled in the application of well-rounded phrases` means: one is incapable of speaking with complete words and phrases, and of knowing what is said by others. This is the meaning.

458. Anussāvanenāti anu anu kathanena. Tenāha “nanu tumhe”tiādi, yaṃ avocumha, svāyaṃ pakāsitoti sambandho. Tattha yanti idaṃ yasmā vacanāpekkhaṃ na hoti, vacanatthāpekkhameva, tasmā tena vacanena nānākaraṇābhāvaṃ pakāsayissāmāti yamatthaṃ avocumhāti attho gahetabbo. Teneva “svāya”nti pulliṅgavasena paṭiniddeso kato, tassa so ayaṃ nānākaraṇābhāvoti attho.

458. `By proclamation` means by speaking again and again. Therefore, he said, `Is it not that you...` and so forth. The connection is: `The meaning which we have spoken, that very one has been made clear.` Therein, since this word `yaṃ` does not refer to the word but only to the meaning of the word, the meaning should be taken thus: `With that word, I will make clear the absence of difference, which is the meaning we have spoken.` For that very reason, the reference back with `svāyaṃ` is made in the masculine gender. Of that, the meaning is: `that very absence of difference`.

467. Mañcapadādīsupi naḷāṭaṃ paṭihaññeyyāti andhakāre cammakhaṇḍaṃ paññapetvā vandituṃ onamantassa naḷāṭaṃ vā akkhi vā mañcādīsu paṭihaññati. Etena vandatopi āpattiabhāvaṃ vatvā vandanāya sabbathā paṭikkhepābhāvañca dīpeti. Evaṃ sabbattha suttantarehi appaṭikkhittesu. Naggādīsu pana vandituṃ na vaṭṭatīti. Ekato āvaṭṭoti ekasmiṃ dosāgatipakkhe parivatto paviṭṭhoti attho. Tenāha “sapattapakkhe ṭhito”ti. Vandiyamānoti onamitvā vandiyamāno. Vanditabbesu uddesācariyo, nissayācariyo ca yasmā navakāpi honti, tasmā te vuḍḍhā eva vandiyāti veditabbā.

467. `One might strike one's forehead even on the legs of a bed, etc.` means: for a monk who, having spread a piece of leather in the dark, bows down to pay homage, his forehead or eye strikes a bed, etc. By this, having stated the absence of an offense even for one who pays homage, it also shows the absence of a prohibition in every way for paying homage. Thus it is in all cases regarding those who are not prohibited by other texts. However, it is not proper to pay homage to the naked, etc. `Ekato āvaṭṭo` means: one has entered a faction of wrong course due to hatred. This is the meaning. Therefore, it is said, `standing in the rival faction`. `Vandiyamāno` means being paid homage to while bowing down. Among those who should be paid homage to, since the recitation teacher and the dependence teacher may also be junior, therefore, it should be known that they are to be paid homage to only if they are elders.

470. Pubbe [V 2.0292] vuttamevāti sahaseyyādipaṇṇattivajjaṃ. Itaranti sacittakaṃ.

470. `As previously stated` means the prescribed offense of sharing a bed, etc. `The other` means that which is intentional.

Vohāravaggādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section on Transactions, etc., is concluded.

Aparadutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

The Collection Connected with the Other Second Verse

Kāyikādiāpattivaṇṇanā

Commentary on Offenses Pertaining to the Body, and so forth

474. “Kati [M 2.0309] āpattiyo”tiādinā upālittherena vinayassa pāṭavatthaṃ sayameva pucchitvā vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Bhikkhunīnaṃyeva…pe… aṭṭhavatthukā nāmāti bhikkhunīnaṃ paññattā ekā eva āpatti aṭṭhavatthukā nāmāti attho.

474. By the words beginning with 'How many offenses?', for the sake of proficiency in the Vinaya, the Elder Upāli himself asked and gave the answer. As for 'For the bhikkhunīs...pe...is called the eight-factored': this means that for the bhikkhunīs, only one offense that was laid down is called the eight-factored. This is the meaning.

475. Kammañca kammapādakā cāti ettha yasmā ñattikammesu ñatti sayameva kammaṃ hoti, ñattidutiyañatticatutthesu kammesu anussāvanasaṅkhātassa kammassa ñattipādakabhāvena tiṭṭhati, tasmā imāni dve “ñattikiccānī”ti vuttāni.

475. In the phrase 'the act and the bases of the act': because in acts by motion, the motion itself is the act, and in acts which are motion-second and motion-fourth, the motion stands as the basis for the act which is called the proclamation, therefore these two are called 'the functions of the motion'.

Pācittiyena saddhiṃ dukkaṭā katāti dasasupi sikkhāpadesu ekatoupasampannāya vasena vuttadukkaṭaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Paṭhamasikkhāpadamhīti bhikkhunovādavaggassa paṭhamasikkhāpadavibhaṅge (pāci. 144 ādayo). Adhammakammeti bhikkhunovādakasammutikamme adhammakamme jāte āpajjitabbā dve āpattinavakā, dhammakamme dve āpattinavakāti cattāro navakā vuttā. Āmakadhaññaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā viññāpanādipubbapayoge dukkaṭaṃ, ajjhohāre pācittiyaṃ. Pācittiyena saddhiṃ dukkaṭā katāyevāti vuttaṃ.

The statement 'A dukkaṭa is done together with a pācittiya' is said in reference to the dukkaṭa mentioned in the ten training rules by way of a bhikkhunī ordained on one side. 'In the first training rule' means in the analysis of the first training rule of the Bhikkhunovādaka chapter. As for 'in an unlawful act': in the formal act of appointing a bhikkhunī-admonisher, when it becomes an unlawful act, there are two sets of nine offenses to be incurred, and when it is a lawful act, two sets of nine offenses; thus four sets of nine are stated. For a bhikkhunī who, having requested raw grain, eats it: there is a dukkaṭa in the preliminary effort of requesting, etc., and a pācittiya in swallowing. It is said, 'A dukkaṭa is indeed done together with a pācittiya'.

Vijahantī tiṭṭhatītiādīsu yadā bhikkhuniyā ekena pādena hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā ṭhatvā kiñci kammaṃ katvā tato aparena pādena vijahitvā ṭhātukāmatā uppajjati, tadā sā yathākkamaṃ “vijahantī tiṭṭhati, vijahitvā tiṭṭhatī”ti imaṃ vohāraṃ labhati. Aññathā hissā gāmūpacāramokkantiyā viseso na siyā hatthapāsavijahanassāpi gamanattā. Nisīdati vā nipajjati vāti etthāpi yathāvuttādhippāyena addhāsanena hatthapāsaṃ vijahantī nisīdati, sakalena [V 2.0293] vā āsanena vijahitvā nisīdati, addhasarīrena vijahantī nipajjati, sakalena sarīrena vijahitvā nipajjatīti yojetabbaṃ.

In the texts beginning with 'Leaving, she stands': when for a bhikkhunī, having left arm's reach with one foot and stood, and having done some deed, the desire to stand having left with the other foot arises, then that bhikkhunī, in sequence, obtains this designation: 'leaving, she stands,' and 'having left, she stands.' Indeed, otherwise there would be no difference for her from one who has entered the village precincts, because leaving arm's reach is also a form of going. Also in the phrase 'she sits or she lies down,' it should be connected with the aforesaid meaning: leaving arm's reach with half the seat, she sits; or having left with the whole seat, she sits; with half the body leaving, she lies down; having left with the whole body, she lies down.

Kāyikādiāpattivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on Offenses Pertaining to the Body, and so forth, is concluded.

Pācittiyavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Pācittiya

476. Sabbāni [M 2.0310] nānāvatthukānīti sappinavanītādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ vatthūnaṃ bhedena pācittiyāni pañca nānāvatthukāni. Esa nayo paṇītabhojanavisaye nava pācittiyānītiādīsupi. Etena bhesajjapaṇītabhojanasikkhāpadāni ekekasikkhāpadavasena paññattānipi vatthubhedena paccekaṃ pañcasikkhāpadanavasikkhāpadasadisāni bhikkhunīnaṃ pāṭidesanīyāpattiyo viyāti dasseti. Teneva “nānāvatthukānī”ti vuttaṃ. Sappiṃ eva paṭiggahetvā anekabhājanesu ṭhapetvā sattāhaṃ atikkāmentassa bhājanagaṇanāya sambhavantiyo bahukāpi āpattiyo ekavatthukā eva honti, evaṃ sappibhojanameva bahūsu ṭhānesu viññāpetvā ekato vā visuṃ visumeva vā bhuñjantassa āpattiyo ekavatthukā evāti daṭṭhabbā.

476. Regarding 'Sabbāni nānāvatthukāni' (All have different substances): by the distinction of the five substances—ghee, fresh butter, and so forth—the five pācittiyas have different substances. This same method applies also in the case of choice foods, in passages such as 'nava pācittiyāni' (nine pācittiyas). By this, it is shown that the training rules on medicines and choice foods, though established by way of single training rules, are, due to the distinction of substance, individually similar to five training rules and nine training rules respectively, just like the pāṭidesanīya offenses for bhikkhunīs. For that very reason, it is said, 'nānāvatthukāni' (having different substances). For a monk who, having accepted only ghee, places it in many containers and lets seven days pass, the many offenses that arise according to the count of the containers are indeed of a single substance. Similarly, for a monk who, having requested food with ghee in many places, eats it either all together or separately, the offenses should be understood as being of a single substance.

Pāḷiyaṃ ekavācāya deseyya, vuttā ādiccabandhunāti ettha “deseyyāti vuttā”ti iti-saddaṃ ajjhāharitvā yojetabbaṃ. Evaṃ sesesupi.

In the Pāḷi, regarding the phrase 'ekavācāya deseyya, vuttā ādiccabandhunā' (one should confess in a single statement; spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun), it should be connected by supplying the word 'iti' as follows: 'deseyya, iti vuttā' (one should confess; thus it was spoken). It is the same in the remaining cases as well.

Bhedānuvattakānanti ettha ādi-saddo luttaniddiṭṭho. Yāvatatiyakā ca sabbe ubhatovibhaṅge āgatā, saṅghādisesasāmaññena ekaṃ, pācittiyasāmaññena ca ekaṃ katvā “yāvatatiyake tisso”ti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ettha ca ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ, dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayāpi santi eva. Tāni mātikāya na āgatāni. Mātikāgatavasena hettha “tisso”ti vuttaṃ.

Regarding 'Bhedānuvattakānaṃ,' here the word 'ādi' is indicated as elided. And as for all the 'yāvatatiyakā' (offenses repeated up to the third time) that appear in the Ubhatovibhaṅga, it should be understood that it is said, 'in the yāvatatiyaka, there are three,' by making one group based on the commonality of Saṅghādisesa, and one group based on the commonality of Pācittiya. And here, there is indeed a dukkaṭa offense for the motion (ñatti), and there are also thullaccaya offenses for the two formal acts. These do not appear in the mātikā. Indeed, it is said 'three' here by way of what appears in the mātikā.

Saṅghādīhīti saṅghagaṇapuggalehi kāraṇabhūtehi. Abbhuṇhasīloti parisuddhabhāvūpagamanena abhinavuppannasīlo. Abhinavuppannañhi “abbhuṇha”nti vuccati, parisuddhasīloti attho. Tenāha “pākatiko”ti.

Regarding 'Saṅghādīhi': by the Sangha, the group, and individuals, who have become the cause. Regarding 'Abbhuṇhasīlo': one who has newly arisen virtue by having reached a state of purity. Indeed, what has newly arisen is called 'abbhuṇha'; the meaning is 'one of purified virtue.' Therefore, it is said, 'pākatiko'.

“Kosambakakkhandhake vuttānisaṃse”ti idaṃ kosambakakkhandhake “sace maṃ ime bhikkhū āpattiyā adassane ukkhipissanti, na mayā saddhiṃ uposathaṃ karissantī”tiādinā āpattiyā [V 2.0294] adassane ādīnavaṃ dassetvā paresampi saddhāya āpattidesanāvidhānamukhena sāmatthiyato pakāsito. Ekato uposathakaraṇa, pavāraṇākaraṇa, saṅghakammakaraṇa, āsanenisīdana, yāgupānenisīdana, bhattaggenisīdana, ekacchannesayana, yathāvuḍḍhaabhivādanādikaraṇasaṅkhāte aṭṭhānisaṃse sandhāya vuttaṃ.

This phrase, 'the benefits stated in the Kosambakakkhandhaka,' refers to the benefits that are revealed by implication in the Kosambakakkhandhaka. There, by means of the passage beginning, 'If these monks suspend me for not seeing an offense, they will not perform the Uposatha with me,' the danger in not seeing an offense is shown; and with reference to others also, through the method of confessing an offense, these benefits are revealed. It is stated with reference to the eight benefits, which are designated as: performing the Uposatha together, performing the Pavāraṇā together, performing Sangha acts together, sitting on seats together, sitting together for rice-gruel, sitting together in the refectory, dwelling together in the same lodging, and performing acts such as paying respects according to seniority.

Catunnanti [M 2.0311] vinayapiṭake āgatānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Katamā pana sāti sā catubbidhā accayadesanā katamāti attho. Abhimārānanti māraṇatthāya payojitadhanuggahānaṃ. Upaṭṭhāyikāyāti sahaseyyasikkhāpadavatthusmiṃ āgatāya.

Regarding 'Catunnaṃ': it is stated by way of the persons who appear in the Vinayapiṭaka. 'Katamā pana sā?' The meaning is: 'What is that fourfold confession of transgression?' Regarding 'Abhimārānaṃ': of the archers dispatched for the purpose of killing. Regarding 'Upaṭṭhāyikāya': of the woman who appears in the story of the training rule on lying down together.

Aṭṭhannaṃ bhikkhunīnanti therāsanato paṭṭhāya aṭṭhahi bhikkhunīhi itarāya āgatāya vuḍḍhāya bhikkhuniyā āsanaṃ dātabbaṃ. Aṭṭhannaṃ pana bhikkhunīnaṃ navakāya āgatāya adātumpi vaṭṭati. Tāya pana saṅghanavakāsane laddhokāse nisīditabbaṃ. Atha vā aṭṭhannaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ itarāya navakatarāya āsanaṃ dātabbaṃ. Kammāni navāti osāraṇādīni nava eva.

Regarding 'Aṭṭhannaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ': starting from the elder's seat, a seat should be given by the eight bhikkhunīs to another elder bhikkhunī who has arrived. However, for the eight bhikkhunīs, it is permissible not to give a seat to a junior who has arrived. But that junior bhikkhunī should sit in the space obtained in the place of the junior-most of the Sangha. Alternatively, a seat should be given by another, more junior bhikkhunī to the eight elder bhikkhunīs. Regarding 'Kammāni nava': they are just the nine beginning with reinstatement.

Pācittiyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Pācittiya is concluded.

Avandanīyapuggalādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of Persons Not to Be Venerated, and so forth

477. Dasa janāti “dasa ime, bhikkhave, avandiyā”tiādinā (pari. 330) vuttā navakaanupasampannanānāsaṃvāsakamātugāmapaṇḍakā pañca, pārivāsikādayo ca pañcāti dasa janā.

477. 'Ten persons' refers to the ten persons stated in the text beginning, 'Monks, these ten are not to be venerated,' namely: the five—a junior monk, one not fully ordained, one of a different communion, a woman, and a eunuch; and the five beginning with one on probation. Thus, ten persons.

Dvādasa kammadosāti dosayuttakammāni dvādasāti attho. Kammasampattiyoti sampannakammāni, visuddhakammānīti attho. Etadevāti dhammena samaggameva.

'Twelve faults of action' means twelve actions connected with faults. 'Accomplishment of action' means accomplished actions, purified actions. The phrase refers to what is indeed a lawful, unified act.

Anantaṃ nibbānaṃ ajini jinitvā paṭilabhatīti anantajinoti āha “pariyanta”iccādi. Svevāti so eva bhagavā.

Because he conquered the endless Nibbāna, and having conquered it, he attains it, he is called the 'Conqueror of the Endless'; therefore, he spoke the words beginning with 'pariyanta'. 'Sveva' means that very Blessed One.

“Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te”tiādinā upālitthereneva ekaṃ vinayadharaṃ sammukhe [V 2.0295] ṭhitaṃ pucchantena viya pucchitvā tena vissajjitaṃ viya vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Tattha vinayaṃ paṭijānantassāti vinayaṃ jānāmīti paṭijānantassa. Vinayānīti vinaye tayā vuccamāne suṇoma.

By the text beginning, 'We shall listen to the points of Vinaya from you who profess the Vinaya,' the Elder Upāli himself asked as if questioning a certain Vinaya expert standing before him, and gave the answer as if it were answered by that expert. Therein, 'of one who professes the Vinaya' means of one who professes, 'I know the Vinaya.' 'We shall listen to the points of Vinaya' means 'We shall listen when the Vinaya is spoken by you.'

478. Pāḷiyaṃ pārājikātiādi ubhatovibhaṅgesu āgatesu aggahitaggahaṇavasena vuttaṃ.

478. In the Pāḷi text, the words beginning with 'pārājika', which occur in the two Vibhaṅgas, are stated by way of taking up what has not yet been taken up.

Avandanīyapuggalādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of Persons Not to Be Venerated, and so forth, is concluded.

Sedamocanagāthā

The Verses for Dispelling Doubts

Avippavāsapañhāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Question on Non-separation

479. Sedamocanagāthāsu [M 2.0312] akappiyasambhogoti anupasampannehi saddhiṃ kātuṃ paṭikkhitto uposathādisaṃvāso eva vutto. Pañhā mesāti ettha ma-kāro padasandhikaro. Esāti ca liṅgavipallāsavasena vuttaṃ, pañho esoti attho. Pañha-saddo vā dviliṅgo daṭṭhabbo. Tenāha “esā pañhā”tiādi.

479. In the Verses for Dispelling Doubts, 'improper communion' refers only to communion such as the Uposatha, which is forbidden to be done with those not fully ordained. In 'Pañhā mesā', the letter 'ma' serves for euphonic conjunction. And 'esā' is stated by way of gender inversion; the meaning is 'eso pañho'. Alternatively, the word 'pañha' should be seen as having two genders. Therefore, he said, 'esā pañhā,' and so forth.

Garubhaṇḍaṃ sandhāyāti garubhaṇḍena garubhaṇḍaparivattanaṃ sandhāya. Dasāti dasa avandiyapuggale. Ekādaseti abhabbapuggale. Sikkhāya asādhāraṇoti khurabhaṇḍaṃ dhāretuṃ anuññātasikkhāpadena bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇasikkhāpadoti attho.

'With reference to heavy goods' means with reference to the exchange of heavy goods with heavy goods. 'Ten' refers to the ten persons not to be venerated. 'Eleven' refers to the incapable persons. 'Not common in the training' means that by the training rule that permits the carrying of a razor case, it is a training rule not held in common by bhikkhus with others; this is the meaning.

Ubbhakkhake na vadāmīti akkhato uddhaṃ sīse ṭhitamukhamaggepi pārājikaṃ sandhāya na vadāmi. Adhonābhinti nābhito heṭṭhā ṭhitavaccapassāvamaggepi vivajjiya aññasmiṃ sarīrappadese methunadhammapaccayā kathaṃ pārājiko siyāti attho.

'I do not speak of the upper cavity' means: I do not speak with reference to a pārājika offense even in the passage of the mouth situated on the head above the collarbone. 'Below the navel' means: having excluded the passages for feces and urine situated below the navel, how could one become subject to a pārājika offense on account of sexual intercourse in another part of the body? This is the meaning.

Chejjavatthunti pārājikaṃ.

'A ground for expulsion' means a pārājika offense.

Avippavāsapañhāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Question on Non-separation is concluded.

Pārājikādipañhāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Questions Regarding Pārājika, etc.

480. Dussakuṭiādīnīti [V 2.0296] ādi-saddena acchataratipupaṭṭādīhi, tiṇapaṇṇādīhi ca paṭicchannakuṭiyo saṅgaṇhāti. Tādisāya hi kuṭiyā bahi ṭhatvā anto ṭhitāya itthiyā magge dussādinā santhataṃ katvā pavesentopi pārājiko siyā. Liṅgaparivattaṃ sandhāya vuttāti liṅge parivatte paṭiggahaṇassa vijahanato puna appaṭiggahetvā paribhuñjanāpattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

480. In the phrase 'huts of cloth, etc.', by the word 'etc.', it includes huts covered with very thin reed mats, etc., and with grass, leaves, etc. Indeed, in such a hut, having stood outside, even a monk who inserts into the passage of a woman standing inside, after having lined it with a cloth or the like, would be subject to Pārājika. As for 'stated with reference to the change of gender', it is said with reference to the offense of consuming without re-accepting, due to the relinquishing of the acceptance when the gender has changed.

Pāḷiyaṃ bhikkhū siyā vīsatiyā samāgatāti vīsatiyā saṅkhātāya bhikkhū samāgatā, etena sabbakammārahataṃ saṅghassa dasseti.

In the Pāḷi, 'bhikkhū siyā vīsatiyā samāgatā' means that monks are assembled, counted as twenty; by this, it shows the Saṅgha's worthiness for all formal acts.

Nivatthoti [M 2.0313] gāthāya antaravāsakena nivattho uttarāsaṅgena diguṇaṃ katvā pārutasaṅghāṭiyo. Iti tāni tīṇipi cīvarāni kāye gatāneva bhikkhuniyā bindumattaṃ kāḷakaṃ udakena dhovitamatte nissaggiyāni hontīti attho.

In the verse beginning with 'Clothed': clothed with the inner robe, having folded the upper robe in two, and wearing the outer robe. Thus, the meaning is that those three robes, while on the bhikkhunī’s body, become subject to forfeiture merely upon a spot of dark substance the size of a drop being washed with water.

Itthiṃ haneti gāthāya na mātubhūtaṃ itthiṃ haneyya, na pitubhūtaṃ purisaṃ haneyya. Anariyanti tañca anarahantameva haneyya, etena arahantaghātakopi na hotīti dasseti. Anantaraṃ phuseti ānantariyaṃ phusatīti attho.

In the verse beginning 'Kill a woman': one should not kill a woman who is one's mother; one should not kill a man who is one's father. As for 'a non-noble', one should kill only that one who is not an Arahant; by this, it shows that one is not a killer of an Arahant. As for 'touches the immediate', the meaning is: one attains an act with immediate consequence.

481. Suppatiṭṭhita-nigrodhasadisanti yojanavitthataṃ rukkhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

481. 'Like a well-established banyan tree' is said with reference to a tree a yojana in breadth.

Sattarasakesūti bhikkhunīnaṃ paññattasattarasasaṅghādisesesu.

'Among the seventeen' means among the seventeen Saṅghādisesa rules laid down for bhikkhunīs.

Pārājikādipañhāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Questions Regarding Pārājika, etc., is concluded.

Pañcavaggo

The Fifth Chapter

Kammavaggavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Chapter on Formal Acts

483. Kammavagge [M 2.0314][V 2.0297] ṭhapitauposathapavāraṇānaṃ kattikamāse sāmaggiyā katāya sāmaggīpavāraṇaṃ muñcitvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti āha “ṭhapetvā kattikamāsa”nti. Sace pana tesaṃ nānāsīmāsu mahāpavāraṇāya visuṃ pavāritānaṃ kattikamāsabbhantare sāmaggī hoti, sāmaggīuposatho eva tehi kattabbo, na pavāraṇā. Ekasmiṃ vasse katapavāraṇānaṃ puna pavāraṇāya avihitattā. Sāmaggīdivasoti anuposathadivase sāmaggīkaraṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sace pana cātuddasiyaṃ, pannarasiyaṃ vā saṅgho sāmaggiṃ karoti, tadā sāmaggīuposathadivaso na hoti, cātuddasīpannarasīuposathova hoti. Upari pavāraṇāyapi eseva nayo.

483. In the Chapter on Formal Acts, for those whose Uposatha and Pavāraṇā have been postponed, if unity is achieved in the month of Kattika, it is not proper to perform the Uposatha after abandoning the Pavāraṇā of unity. Therefore, he said, 'except for the month of Kattika.' However, if unity occurs within the month of Kattika for those who have performed the Great Pavāraṇā separately in various boundaries, only the Uposatha of unity should be performed by them, not the Pavāraṇā. This is because for those who have already performed Pavāraṇā in one year, performing Pavāraṇā again is not prescribed. The term 'day of unity' is said with reference to making unity on a non-Uposatha day. But if the Saṅgha makes unity on the fourteenth or fifteenth day, then it is not a 'day of unity Uposatha'; it is just the fourteenth or fifteenth Uposatha. This is the same method for the Pavāraṇā above as well.

Paccukkaḍḍhitvā ṭhapitadivasoti bhaṇḍanakārakehi upaddutā vā kenacideva karaṇīyena pavāraṇāsaṅgahaṃ vā katvā ṭhapito kāḷapakkhacātuddasīdivasova. Dve ca puṇṇamāsiyoti pubba-kattikapuṇṇamā, pacchimakattikapuṇṇamā cāti dve puṇṇamāsiyo. Evaṃ catubbidhampīti puṇṇamāsīdvayena saddhiṃ sāmaggīpavāraṇaṃ, cātuddasīpavāraṇañca sampiṇḍetvā vuttaṃ. Idañca pakaticārittavasena vuttaṃ. Tathārūpapaccaye pana sati ubhinnaṃ puṇṇamāsīnaṃ purimā dve cātuddasiyopi kāḷapakkhacātuddasiyā anantarā pannarasīpīti imepi tayo divasā pavāraṇādivasā evāti imaṃ sattavidhampi pavāraṇādivasaṃ ṭhapetvā aññasmiṃ divase pavāretuṃ na vaṭṭati.

As for 'the day postponed and set aside,' it is the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, set aside either due to being harassed by quarrel-makers, or due to some duty, or after having made a Pavāraṇā compact. As for 'and two full moon days,' these are the earlier Kattika full moon and the later Kattika full moon. As for 'thus fourfold,' this is said by combining the Pavāraṇā of unity and the fourteenth-day Pavāraṇā together with the pair of full moon days. And this is said according to normal custom. However, when such a condition exists, the two fourteenth days preceding the two full moon days, and the fifteenth day immediately following the fourteenth of the dark fortnight—these three days are also Pavāraṇā days. Thus, setting aside these seven kinds of Pavāraṇā days, it is not proper to perform Pavāraṇā on another day.

484. Anussāvanakammaṃ katvāti paṭhamaṃ anussāvanaṃ sāvetvā “esā ñattī”ti anussāvanānantarameva sakalaṃ ñattiṃ vatvā, pariyosāne “esā ñattī”ti vatvāti adhippāyo.

484. As for 'having performed the act of announcement,' the meaning is this: first, having made the announcement heard, then immediately after the announcement, having stated the entire motion, and at the end, having said, 'This is the motion.'

485. Yvāyanti [V 2.0298] byañjanappabhedo adhippeto. Dasadhā byañjanabuddhiyā pabhedoti ettha dasadhā dasavidhena byañjanānaṃ pabhedoti yojetabbaṃ. Kenāyaṃ pabhedoti āha “byañjanabuddhiyā”ti. Yathādhippetatthabyañjanato byañjanasaṅkhātānaṃ akkharānaṃ janikā buddhi byañjanabuddhi, tāya byañjanabuddhiyā[M 2.0315], akkharasamuṭṭhāpakacittabhedenevāti attho. Yaṃ vā saṃyogaparaṃ katvā vuccati, idampi garukanti yojanā.

485. By 'yvāyaṃ' is meant a variety of consonants. Here, in 'a tenfold variety through cognition of consonants,' it should be construed as 'a variety of consonants in ten ways.' To the question, 'By what is this variety made?' he said, 'through cognition of consonants.' The cognition that produces the letters designated as consonants which express the intended meaning is 'cognition of consonants'; by that cognition of consonants, the meaning is 'by the very difference in the mind that produces the letters.' Or, the connection is: what is said by making it followed by a conjunct consonant, this too is a heavy syllable.

Tattha āyasmatotiādīsu yāni anantaritāni sa-kārama-kārādibyañjanāni “saṃyogo”ti vuccanti, so saṃyogo paro yassa a-kārādino, so saṃyogaparo nāma. Rassanti akārādibyañjanarahitaṃ saraṃ. Asaṃyogaparanti “yassa nakkhamatī”tiādīsu ya-kāra na-kārādibyañjanasahitasaraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ta-kārassa tha-kāraṃ akatvā vaggantare sithilameva katvā “suṇāṭu me”tiādiṃ vadantopi duruttaṃ karotiyeva ṭhapetvā anurūpaṃ ādesaṃ. Yañhi “saccikatthaparamatthenā”ti vattabbe “saccikaṭṭhaparamaṭṭhenā”ti ca “atthakathā”ti vattabbe “aṭṭhakathā”ti ca tattha tattha vuccati, tādisaṃ pāḷiaṭṭhakathāsu diṭṭhapayogaṃ, tadanurūpañca vattuṃ vaṭṭati, tato aññaṃ na vaṭṭati. Tenāha “anukkamāgataṃ paveṇiṃ avināsentenā”tiādi.

There, in phrases like 'āyasmato,' the immediately following consonants such as the letter 's,' the letter 'm,' and so forth, are called a 'conjunct consonant.' A vowel, such as 'a,' which is followed by that conjunct consonant, is called 'one followed by a conjunct consonant.' 'Short' is said with reference to a vowel, such as 'a,' that is without a consonant. 'Not followed by a conjunct consonant' is said with reference to a vowel together with a consonant such as the letter 'y,' the letter 'n,' and so forth, as in 'yassa nakkhamatī.' Even one who, without changing the letter 't' to 'th,' makes it just a soft consonant in another consonant-group and says 'suṇāṭu me,' etc., certainly makes a mispronunciation, except for a suitable substitution. Indeed, where one should say 'saccikatthaparamatthenā,' it is also said in various places as 'saccikaṭṭhaparamaṭṭhenā,' and where one should say 'atthakathā,' it is said as 'aṭṭhakathā.' It is proper to speak such usage seen in the Pāḷi and commentaries, and what is in accordance with that. Other than that is not proper. Therefore, he said: 'Without destroying the tradition that has come down in succession,' etc.

Dīghe vattabbe rassantiādīsu “bhikkhūna”nti vattabbe “bhikkhuna”nti vā “bahūsū”ti vattabbe “bahusū”ti vā “nakkhamatī”ti vattabbe “na khamatī”ti vā “upasampadāpekkho”ti vattabbe “upasampadāpekho”ti vā evaṃ anurūpaṭṭhānesu eva dīgharassādi rassadīghādivasena parivattetuṃ vaṭṭati, na pana “nāgo”ti vattabbe “nago”ti vā “saṅgho”ti vattabbe “sagho”ti vā “tisso”ti vattabbe “tiso”ti vā “yācatī”ti vattabbe “yācantī”ti vā evaṃ ananurūpaṭṭhānesu vattuṃ. Sambandhaṃ, pana vavatthānañca sabbathāpi vaṭṭatīti gahetabbaṃ.

In such cases as when a short vowel is used where a long one should be spoken: when 'bhikkhūnaṃ' should be said, it is permissible to say 'bhikkhunaṃ'; or when 'bahūsū' should be said, it is permissible to say 'bahusū'; or when 'nakkhamati' should be said, it is permissible to say 'na khamati'; or when 'upasampadāpekkho' should be said, it is permissible to say 'upasampadāpekho'. Thus, only in appropriate places is it permissible to change long and short vowels, and so forth, by way of short and long vowels, and so forth. However, it is not permissible to say 'nago' when 'nāgo' should be said, or 'sagho' when 'saṅgho' should be said, or 'tiso' when 'tisso' should be said, or 'yācantī' when 'yācatī' should be said; thus, it is not permissible to speak in such inappropriate places. However, it should be understood that connection and separation are permissible in every way.

486. Sesasīmāsupīti atimahatīādīsu dasasupi.

486. The phrase 'also in the remaining boundaries' refers to: also in the ten boundaries, such as the excessively large one and so forth.

488. Catuvaggakaraṇeti catuvaggena saṅghena kattabbe. Anissāritāti uposathaṭṭhapanādinā vā laddhinānāsaṃvāsakabhāvena vā na bahikatā. Aṭṭhakathāyañhi “apakatattassāti ukkhittakassa vā, yassa vā uposathapavāraṇā ṭhapitā hontī”ti (pari. aṭṭha. 425) vuttattā ṭhapitauposathapavāraṇo bhikkhu apakatatto evāti gahetabbaṃ. Parisuddhasīlāti pārājikaṃ anāpannā adhippetā. Parivāsādikammesu pana garukaṭṭhāpi apakatattā evāti gahetabbaṃ[V 2.0299]. Avasesā…pe… chandārahāva hontīti saṅghato [M 2.0316] hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā ṭhite sandhāya vuttaṃ. Avijahitvā ṭhitā pana chandārahā na honti, tepi catuvaggādito adhikā hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvāva chandārahā honti. Tasmā saṅghato hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā ṭhiteneva chando vā pārisuddhi vā dātabbā.

488. As for 'in an act to be performed by a group of four': it means in an act to be performed by a Saṅgha of four. As for 'not excluded': it means not being made external by means of suspending the Uposatha and so forth, or by being of a different communion. Indeed, since it is said in the commentary: 'As for "one who is not a normal participant": it means one who has been suspended, or one whose Uposatha and Pavāraṇā have been suspended,' a bhikkhu whose Uposatha and Pavāraṇā have been suspended is to be understood as not being a normal participant. By 'of pure virtue,' it is intended that they have not fallen into a pārājika offense. In acts such as probation, however, even those who are undergoing penalty for a grave Saṅghādisesa offense are to be understood as not being normal participants. The statement 'The rest... are worthy of consent' is said in reference to those standing having left the hand's reach from the Saṅgha. However, those standing without having left are not worthy of consent; even they, being more than a group of four, are worthy of consent only after having left the hand's reach. Therefore, consent or a declaration of purity should be given only by one standing having left the hand's reach from the Saṅgha.

Kammavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Chapter on Formal Acts is concluded.

Apalokanakammakathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Discourse on the Act of Announcement

496. Etarahi sacepi sāmaṇerotiādīsu buddhādīnaṃ avaṇṇabhāsanampi akappiyādiṃ kappiyādibhāvena dīpanampi diṭṭhivipattiyaññeva pavisati. Teneva vakkhati “taṃ laddhiṃ nissajjāpetabbo”ti. Bhikkhūnampi eseva nayo. Micchādiṭṭhikoti buddhavacanādhippāyaṃ viparītato gaṇhanto, so eva antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgatoti ca vutto. Keci pana “sassatucchedānaṃ aññataradiṭṭhiyā samannāgato”ti vadanti, taṃ na yuttaṃ, sassatucchedaggāhassa sāmaṇerānaṃ liṅganāsanāya kāraṇattena heṭṭhā aṭṭhakathāyameva (mahāva. aṭṭha. 108) vuttattā, idha ca daṇḍakammanāsanāya eva adhippetattā.

496. In such cases as 'Now, if a novice...': speaking dispraise of the Buddha and others, and presenting what is improper, etc., as proper, etc., enters into wrong view itself. For that very reason, it will be said: 'He should be made to relinquish that doctrine.' This same method applies to bhikkhus as well. As for 'one of wrong view': it is one who grasps the meaning of the Buddha's words perversely; he is also said to be one endowed with a view that adheres to extremes. Some, however, say: 'He is one endowed with either of the views of eternalism or annihilationism.' That statement is not correct, because it was stated below in the commentary itself that holding the view of eternalism or annihilationism is a reason for the removal of the sign for novices, and because here, only the removal by a penal act is intended.

Tassāpi dātabboti vijjamānaṃ mukharādibhāvaṃ nissāya appaṭipucchitvāpi paṭiññaṃ aggahetvāpi āpattiṃ anāropetvāpi desitāyapi āpattiyā khuṃsanādito anoramantassa dātabbova. Oramantassa pana khamāpentassa na dātabbo.

As for 'It should be given even to him': on account of his manifest foul-mouthedness and so forth, it should indeed be given to one who does not desist from reviling and so forth, even without questioning him, without obtaining his admission, without charging him with an offense, and even when an offense has been confessed. However, for one who desists and asks for forgiveness, it should not be given.

Brahmadaṇḍassa dānanti kharadaṇḍassa ukkaṭṭhadaṇḍassa dānaṃ. Tajjanīyādikamme hi kate ovādānusāsanippadānapaṭikkhepo natthi. Dinnabrahmadaṇḍe pana tasmiṃ saddhiṃ tajjanīyādikammakatehi paṭikkhittampi kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, “neva vattabbo”tiādinā ālāpasallāpādimattassāpi nakārena paṭikkhittattā. Tañhi disvā bhikkhū gīvaṃ parivattetvā olokanamattampi na karonti, evaṃ vivajjetabbaṃ nimmadanakaraṇatthameva tassa daṇḍassa anuññātattā. Teneva channattheropi ukkhepanīyādikammakatopi abhāyitvā brahmadaṇḍe dinne “saṅghenāhaṃ sabbathā vivajjito”ti mucchito papati. Yo pana brahmadaṇḍakatena saddhiṃ ñatvā saṃsaṭṭho avivajjetvā viharati, tassa dukkaṭamevāti gahetabbaṃ aññathā brahmadaṇḍavidhānassa [M 2.0317] niratthakatāpasaṅgato. Tenāti brahmadaṇḍakatena. Yathā tajjanīyādikammakatehi, evameva tato adhikampi [V 2.0300] saṅghaṃārādhentena sammāvattitabbaṃ. Tañca “sorato nivātavuttī”tiādinā sarūpato dassitameva. Tenāha “sammāvattitvā khamāpentassa brahmadaṇḍo paṭippassambhetabbo”ti.

The giving of the 'higher punishment' (brahmadaṇḍa) is the giving of a harsh punishment, a severe punishment. Indeed, when an act such as censure (tajjanīya) is performed, there is no rejection of giving admonition and instruction. However, with one to whom the higher punishment has been given, it is not proper to do even that, nor that which is forbidden for those subjected to acts such as censure, because even mere conversation and talk is rejected by the letter 'na' in the phrase 'he should not be spoken to' (neva vattabbo), and so on. Indeed, seeing him, the bhikkhus do not even so much as turn their necks to look, because that punishment was permitted for the very purpose of crushing his pride by avoiding him thus. For that very reason, the Elder Channa, though he had been subjected to acts such as suspension and was not afraid, when the higher punishment was given, fainted and fell, thinking, 'I have been completely shunned by the Saṅgha!' But as for whichever bhikkhu, knowing, lives associating and not avoiding one upon whom the higher punishment has been imposed, for him there is a dukkaṭa offense; thus it should be understood. Otherwise, the ordinance of the higher punishment would be rendered meaningless. By 'by him' (tena) is meant: by the one upon whom the higher punishment has been imposed. Just as it should be practiced by those upon whom acts such as censure have been performed, in that same way and even more so, he should practice properly, pleasing the Saṅgha. And that practice has been shown in its nature by the phrase 'gentle, of humble conduct,' and so on. Therefore, it is said: 'For one who behaves properly and asks for forgiveness, the higher punishment should be revoked.'

Yaṃ taṃ bhagavatā avandiyakammaṃ anuññātanti sambandho. “Tassa bhikkhuno daṇḍakammaṃ kātu”nti sāmaññato anuññātappakāraṃ dassetvā puna visesato anuññātappakāraṃ dassetuṃ “atha kho”tiādipāḷi uddhaṭāti veditabbaṃ. Imassa apalokanakammassa ṭhānaṃ hotīti apalokanakammassa sāmaññassa pavattiṭṭhānaṃ hotīti. Visesabyatirekena avijjamānampi tadaññattha appavattiṃ dassetuṃ visesanissitaṃ viya voharīyati. “Kammaññeva lakkhaṇa”nti iminā osāraṇādivasena gahitāvasesānaṃ sabbesaṃ apalokanakammassa sāmaññalakkhaṇavasena gahitattā kammaññeva lakkhaṇamassāti kammalakkhaṇanti nibbacanaṃ dasseti. Idañca vuttāvasesānaṃ kammānaṃ niṭṭhānaṭṭhānaṃ, saṅkhārakkhandhadhammāyatanāni viya vuttāvasesakhandhāyatanānanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Teneva vakkhati “ayaṃ panettha pāḷimuttakopi kammalakkhaṇavinicchayo”tiādi (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496). Yathā cettha, evaṃ upari ñattikammādīsupi kammalakkhaṇaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tassa karaṇanti avandiyakammassa karaṇavidhānaṃ.

The Blessed One allowed that act of making one unworthy of homage; this is the connection. Having shown in a general way the manner of permission, saying, 'To perform a disciplinary act for that bhikkhu,' then, in order to show the manner of permission in a specific way, the Pāḷi beginning with 'atha kho' was extracted; thus it should be understood. The statement 'This is the occasion for this act by announcement' means it is the occasion for the proceeding of a general act by announcement. Although it does not exist without a specific distinction, in order to show its non-occurrence elsewhere than in that act of making one unworthy of homage, it is spoken of as if it were dependent on a specific distinction. By this phrase 'The act itself is the characteristic,' because all remaining acts by announcement, which are the remainder of those taken by way of rehabilitation and so on, are included by way of the general characteristic, it shows the derivation: 'For this act, the act itself is the characteristic, therefore it is called "act-characteristic".' And this is the place of completion for the remaining acts that have been mentioned, just like the aggregate of formations and the mind-object base are the place of completion for the remaining aggregates and bases that have been mentioned; thus it should be seen. For that very reason, it will be said: 'Moreover, this analysis of the act-characteristic here is even outside the Pāḷi Canon,' and so on. Just as it is stated here in the case of the act by announcement, so too, it should be understood that the act-characteristic is stated above in the cases of the act by motion, and so on. 'Its performance' means the procedure for performing the act of making one unworthy of homage.

“Na vanditabbo”ti iminā vandantiyā dukkaṭanti dassetīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Saṅghena kataṃ katikaṃ ñatvā maddanaṃ viya hi saṅghasammutiṃ anādarena atikkamantassa āpatti eva hoti.

By this phrase 'He is not to be paid homage to,' it shows that for a bhikkhunī who pays homage, there is a dukkaṭa offense; thus it should be understood. Indeed, for one who, knowing the agreement made by the Saṅgha, transgresses the Saṅgha's resolution with disrespect, as if trampling upon it, there is certainly an offense.

Bhikkhusaṅghassāpi panetaṃ labbhatiyevāti avandiyakammassa upalakkhaṇamattena gahitattā bhikkhusaṅghassāpi kammalakkhaṇaṃ labbhati eva.

The statement 'Moreover, this is certainly obtainable for the Saṅgha of bhikkhus' means that because the act of making one unworthy of homage is taken merely as an illustrative example, the act-characteristic is certainly obtainable for the Saṅgha of bhikkhus as well.

Salākadānaṭṭhānaṃ salākaggaṃ nāma. Yāgubhattānaṃ bhājanaṭṭhānāni yāgaggabhattaggāni nāma. Etesupi hi ṭhānesu sabbo saṅgho uposathe viya sannipatito, kammañca vaggakammaṃ na hoti, “mayametaṃ na jānimhā”ti pacchā khiyyantāpi na honti. Khaṇḍasīmāya pana kate khiyyanti. Saṅghikapaccayañhi acchinnacīvarādīnaṃ dātuṃ apalokentehi upacārasīmaṭṭhānaṃ sabbesaṃ [M 2.0318] anumatiṃ gahetvāva kātabbaṃ. Yo pana visabhāgapuggalo dhammikaṃ apalokanaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ upāyena bahiupacārasīmāgataṃ vā katvā khaṇḍasīmaṃ vā pavisitvā kātuṃ vaṭṭati.

The place for giving out tickets is called the ticket-distribution place. The places for apportioning rice-gruel and meals are called the gruel-distribution place and the meal-distribution place. For in these places too, the entire Saṅgha is assembled as on an Uposatha day, and the act is not a divided act, and there are none who complain afterwards, saying, 'We did not know of this.' But if it is done in a partial boundary, they do complain. For, in order to give a Saṅgha requisite to those such as a bhikkhu whose robe has been stolen, those making the announcement must do so only after having obtained the consent of all those standing in the vicinity of the boundary. But as for any dissenting person who obstructs a lawful announcement, it is allowable to perform the act by making him go outside the vicinity of the boundary by some means, or by entering a partial boundary.

Yaṃ sandhāya “apalokanakammaṃ karotī”ti sāmaññato dasseti, taṃ apalokanakammaṃ sarūpato [V 2.0301] dassetumāha “acchinnacīvaraṃ”iccādi. Yadi apaloketvāva cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ, kiṃ pana appamattakavissajjakasammutiyāti āha “appamattakavissajjanakena panā”tiādi. Nāḷi vā upaḍḍhanāḷi vāti divase divase apaloketvā dātabbassa pamāṇadassanaṃ. Tena yāpanamattameva apaloketabbaṃ, na adhikanti dasseti. Ekadivasaṃyeva vātiādi dasavīsatidivasānaṃ ekasmiṃ divaseyeva dātabbaparicchedadassanaṃ, tena yāva jīvanti vā yāva rogā vuṭṭhahatīti vā evaṃ apaloketuṃ na vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Iṇapalibodhanti iṇavatthuṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Tañca iṇāyikehi palibuddhassa lajjipesalassa sāsanupakārakassa pamāṇayuttameva kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ niyametvā apaloketvā dātabbaṃ, na pana sahassaṃ vā satasahassaṃ vā mahāiṇaṃ. Tādisañhi bhikkhācariyavattena sabbehi bhikkhūhi tādisassa bhikkhuno pariyesitvā dātabbaṃ.

With reference to which act by announcement it is shown generally, 'he performs an act by announcement,' in order to show that act by announcement in its own nature, he said, 'a robe that has been stolen,' and so on. Due to the objection, 'If a robe is to be given only after making an announcement, then what is the use of the authorization for a distributor of minor things?' he said, 'But by a distributor of minor things,' and so on. The phrase 'a nāḷi or half a nāḷi' is to show the measure of the item to be given each day after making an announcement. By that, it shows that only what is sufficient for sustenance should be announced for, not more. The phrase beginning with 'or on a single day only' is to show the defined limit of what is to be given for ten or twenty days on one single day; by that, it shows that it is not allowable to make an announcement thus: 'for as long as he lives' or 'until he recovers from the illness.' 'Hindered by debt' shows that it is allowable to give an item for a debt; this is the connection. And that: for a bhikkhu who is harassed by creditors, who is conscientious and amiable, and a benefactor to the Teaching, an allowable item that is only of a suitable amount should be given, after having determined it and made an announcement; but a large debt of a thousand or a hundred thousand should not be given. For such a debt should be sought for and given to such a bhikkhu by all the bhikkhus through the practice of going on alms-round.

Upanikkhepatoti cetiyapaṭijagganatthāya vaḍḍhiyā payojetvā kappiyakārakehi ṭhapitavatthuto. Saṅghikenapīti na kevalañca tatruppādato paccayadāyakehi catupaccayatthāya saṅghassa dinnavatthunāpīti attho.

'From a deposit' means: from an item placed by those who make things allowable, having invested it for interest for the purpose of maintaining a cetiya. 'And by what belongs to the Saṅgha' means: not only from what is produced there, but also by an item given to the Saṅgha by donors of requisites for the sake of the four requisites; this is the meaning.

Saṅghabhattaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti mahādānaṃ dentehipi kariyamānaṃ saṅghabhattaṃ viya kāretuṃ na vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo.

'It is not allowable to prepare a Saṅgha meal' means: it is not allowable to have a Saṅgha meal prepared in the manner of one being prepared even by those giving a great donation. This is the intention.

“Yathāsukhaṃ paribhuñjituṃ ruccatī”ti vuttattā attano paribhogappahonakaṃ appaṃ vā bahuṃ vā gahetabbaṃ, adhikaṃ pana gahetuṃ na labhati. Uposathadivaseti nidassanamattaṃ, yasmiṃ kismiñci divasepi kataṃ sukatameva hoti. Karontena “yaṃ imasmiṃ vihāre antosīmāya saṅghasantakaṃ…pe… yathāsukhaṃ paribhuñjituṃ mayhaṃ ruccatī”ti evaṃ katikā kātabbā, tathā dvīhi tīhipi “āyasmantānaṃ ruccatī”ti vacanameva hettha viseso. Tesampīti rukkhānaṃ. Sā eva katikāti visuṃ katikā na kātabbāti attho.

Because it is said, 'It is agreeable to use it as one pleases,' a small or large amount sufficient for one's own use should be taken, but one is not allowed to take more. The phrase 'on the Uposatha day' is merely an illustration; if it is done on any day whatsoever, it is indeed well done. The one performing it should make an agreement thus: 'Whatever belonging to the Saṅgha is within the boundary in this monastery... it is agreeable to me to use it as I please.' Two or three bhikkhus should also do so in the same way; indeed, the only difference here is the wording, 'Is it agreeable to the venerable ones?' 'For them also' refers to the trees. 'That same agreement' means a separate agreement should not be made; this is the meaning.

Tesanti [M 2.0319] rukkhānaṃ. Saṅgho sāmīti sambandho. Purimavihāreti purime yathāsukhaṃ paribhogatthāya katakatike vihāre. Pariveṇāni katvā jaggantīti yattha arakkhiyamāne phalāphalāni, rukkhā ca vinassanti, tādisaṃ ṭhānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, tattha saṅghassa katikā na pavattīti adhippāyo. Ye pana rukkhā bījāni ropetvā ādito paṭṭhāya paṭijaggitā, tepi dasamabhāgaṃ datvā ropakeheva paribhuñjitabbā. Tehīti jaggakehi.

'Of them' means of the trees. The Saṅgha is the owner; this is the connection. 'In the former monastery' means: in a monastery where an agreement was formerly made for use as one pleases. The phrase 'having made enclosures, they look after them' was said with reference to such a place where, if left unguarded, both fruits great and small and the trees are destroyed; the intention is that the Saṅgha's agreement does not apply there. As for those trees that were tended from the very beginning after planting the seeds, they too should be enjoyed by the planters themselves after giving a tenth share. 'By them' means by those who tend them.

Tatthāti [V 2.0302] tasmiṃ vihāre. Mūleti ādikāle, pubbeti attho. Dīghā katikāti aparicchinnakālā yathāsukhaṃ paribhogatthāya katikā. Nikkukkuccenāti “abhājitamida”nti kukkuccaṃ akatvāti attho. Khiyyanamattamevetanti tena khiyyanena bahuṃ khādantānaṃ doso natthi attano paribhogappamāṇasseva gahitattā, khiyyantepi attano pahonakaṃ gahetvā khāditabbanti adhippāyo.

By 'there' is meant 'in that monastery.' By 'at the root' is meant 'at the beginning,' meaning 'at first.' By 'a long-term agreement' is meant an agreement for an unlimited time, for the purpose of using as one pleases. By 'without scruples' is meant 'without creating scruples thinking, "This has not been shared out"'—that is the meaning. By 'this is merely a reproach' is meant that by that reproach, there is no fault for those eating a lot, because only their own proper amount for consumption has been taken; the intention is that even the one who complains should take and eat what is sufficient for themselves.

Gaṇhathāti na vattabbāti tathāvutte teneva bhikkhunā dinnaṃ viya maññeyyuṃ, taṃ nissāya micchājīvasambhavo hotīti vuttaṃ. Tenāha “anuvicaritvā”tiādi. Upaḍḍhabhāgoti ekabhikkhuno paṭivīsato upaḍḍhabhāgo. Dentena ca “ettakaṃ dātuṃ saṅgho anuññāsī”ti evaṃ attānaṃ parimocetvā yathā te saṅghe eva pasīdanti, evaṃ vatvā dātabbaṃ.

'It should not be said, "Take it."' When this is said, they might think it is as if given by that bhikkhu himself. Depending on that, wrong livelihood arises—thus it is said. Therefore, he said, 'Having gone around,' etc. 'Half a share' means half a share from one bhikkhu's portion. And when giving, having freed oneself by saying, 'The Saṅgha has allowed this much to be given,' it should be given by speaking in such a way that they have confidence in the Saṅgha alone.

Apaccāsīsantenāti gilānagamikissarādīnaṃ anuññātapuggalānampi attano santakaṃ dentena apaccāsīsanteneva dātabbaṃ, ananuññātapuggalānaṃ pana apaccāsīsantenāpi dātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti. Saṅghikameva yathākatitāya dāpetabbaṃ. Attano santakampi paccayadāyakādī sayameva vissāsena gaṇhanti, na vāretabbā, laddhakappiyanti tuṇhī bhavitabbaṃ. Pubbe vuttamevāti “kuddho hi so rukkhepi chindeyyā”tiādinā tuṇhībhāve kāraṇaṃ pubbe vuttameva. Tehi kataanatthābhāvepi kāruññena tuṇhī bhavituṃ vaṭṭati, “gaṇhathā”tiādi pana vattuṃ na vaṭṭati.

By 'without expecting anything in return' is meant that when giving one's own property even to permitted individuals such as the sick, travelers, those in authority, and so forth, it should be given only without expecting anything in return. But to unpermitted individuals, it is not proper to give even without expecting anything in return. What belongs to the Saṅgha should be caused to be given according to the agreement. Even one's own property, if supporters of requisites and so forth take it of their own accord with familiarity, they should not be prevented; one should be silent, thinking, 'It has become allowable.' 'It has been stated previously' means: the reason for being silent has already been stated previously with the words, 'For an angry person might even cut down a tree,' etc. Even if no harm has been done by them, it is proper to be silent out of compassion; but it is not proper to say, 'Take it,' etc.

Garubhaṇḍattā…pe… na dātabbanti jīvarukkhānaṃ ārāmaṭṭhānīyattā, dārūnañca gehasambhārānupagatattā “sabbaṃ tvameva gaṇhā”ti dātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti vuttaṃ. Akatāvāsaṃ vā katvāti pubbe avijjamānaṃ senāsanaṃ katvā jaggitakāle phalavāre sampatte.

'Due to being heavy goods…pe…it should not be given' is said because, due to living trees being in the position of a monastery park and timber having become building material for a house, it is not proper to give, saying, 'Take all of it.' 'Or, having made an unmade dwelling' means having made a lodging that did not previously exist. 'At the time of tending' means when the turn for the fruit arrives.

Apalokanakammakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourse on the Act of Announcement is finished.

Atthavasavaggādivaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Chapter on the Power of the Meaning, etc.

498. Vipākadukkhasaṅkhātānaṃ [M 2.0320] samparāyikaverānanti ettha pāṇātipātādiverena nibbattattā, verappattiyā hetuttā ca “vipākadukkhavedanā”ti vuttā. Pāṇātipātādipañcaveravinimuttānampi akusalānaṃ verehi saha ekato saṅgaṇhanatthaṃ “dasaakusalakammapathappabhedāna”nti puna vuttaṃ.

498. Regarding the phrase 'of future enmities which are reckoned as the suffering of result': because they arise from enmity such as the destruction of life, and because they are a cause for the arising of enmity, they are called 'painful feeling that is the result'. For the purpose of including even the unwholesome actions that are free from the five enmities beginning with the destruction of life together with the enmities, it is again stated: 'of the divisions of the ten unwholesome courses of action'.

499-500. Taṃ [V 2.0303] kammanti tajjanīyādikammameva, sattā āpattikkhandhā paññattaṃ nāmāti sambandho. Antarā kenaci apaññatte sikkhāpadeti imasmiṃ kappe ādito paṭṭhāya yāva amhākaṃ bhagavato abhisambodhi, tāva antarākāle kakusandhādiṃ ṭhapetvā kenaci apaññatte sikkhāpadeti attho. Vinītakathā sikkhāpadanti vinītavatthūni eva. Tāni hi taṃtaṃsikkhākoṭṭhāsānaṃ pakāsanato “sikkhāpada”nti ca āpattianāpattīnaṃ anupaññāpanato “anupaññatta”nti ca vuccanti.

As for 'that act', it is only an act such as rebuke. The seven groups of offenses are what is called 'prescribed'; this is the connection. As for 'in a training rule not prescribed by anyone in the interim', the meaning is this: in this aeon, from the beginning up to the full enlightenment of our Blessed One, in that intervening period, setting aside Kakusandha and others, 'in a training rule not prescribed by anyone'. As for 'the training rule that is the discussion on settled matters', it is just the settled matters. Indeed, because they make known the various sections of the training, they are called 'training rules'; and because they make known again and again the offenses and non-offenses, they are called 'additionally prescribed'.

Atthavasavaggādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Chapter on the Power of the Meaning, etc., is finished.

Saṅgahavaggavaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The exposition of the commentary on the Chapter of the Summary is finished.

Iti mahāvaggo, paññattivaggo, saṅgahavaggoti tīhi mahāvaggehi paṭimaṇḍito parivāroti veditabbo.

Thus, it should be known that the Parivāra is adorned with the three great chapters: the Mahāvagga, the Paññattivagga, and the Saṅgahavagga.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya vimativinodaniyaṃ

Thus, in the Vimativinodanī, a sub-commentary on the Samantapāsādikā, the commentary on the Vinaya.

Parivāravaṇṇanānayo niṭṭhito.

The exposition of the commentary on the Parivāra is finished.

Nigamanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Concluding Discourse

Avasānagāthāsu [M 2.0321] ubhatovibhaṅga-khandhaka-parivārehi vibhattattā vibhāgapaṭidesanā yasmiṃ vinayapiṭake. So ubhatovibhaṅga-khandhaka-parivāravibhattadesano āhāti yojanā. Tassāti vinayapiṭakassa.

In the concluding verses: In whichever Vinaya Piṭaka there is a teaching divided by the two Vibhaṅgas, the Khandhakas, and the Parivāra; therefore, that Vinaya is called 'one whose teaching is divided by the two Vibhaṅgas, the Khandhakas, and the Parivāra'. It speaks of that. This is the construction. As for 'of that', it means 'of the Vinaya Piṭaka'.

Satthu mahābodhīti dakkhiṇasākhaṃ sandhāya vadati. Yaṃ padhānagharaṃ nāma pariveṇaṃ, tattha cārupākārena sañcitaṃ parikkhittaṃ yaṃ pāsādaṃ kārayi, tatra tasmiṃ mahānigamasāmino pāsāde vasatāti yojetabbā.

As for 'the Teacher's great Bodhi', this is said in reference to the southern branch. The connection should be made thus: (this commentary was written by me) residing in that mansion which the lord Mahānigamasāmi caused to be built in the monastic college named Padhānaghara, a mansion built up and enclosed by a beautiful wall.

Buddhasiriṃ uddisitvā nissāya, tassa vā ajjhesanampi paṭicca yā iddhā paripuṇṇavinicchayatāya samiddhā vinayasaṃvaṇṇanā āraddhāti yojanā.

The construction is as follows: this Vinaya commentary—which is prosperous and accomplished due to its complete discernment—was undertaken in reference to and reliance upon the elder Buddhasiri, or on account of his request.

Sirinivāsassāti siriyā nivāsanaṭṭhānabhūtassa siripālanāmakassa rañño. Jayasaṃvacchareti vijayayutte saṃvacchare. Āraddhakāladassanatthaṃ puna “jayasaṃvacchare ayaṃ āraddhā”ti vuttaṃ.

As for 'of Sirinivāsa', it means of the king named Siripāla, who has become the abode of fortune. As for 'in the Jayasaṃvacchara', it means in the year associated with victory. To show the time of commencement, it is again stated: 'This was undertaken in the Jayasaṃvacchara'.

Kāle [V 2.0304] vassanti yuttakāle vassanasīlo. Devoti megho.

As for 'rains in season', it means one who is accustomed to raining at the proper time. As for 'deva', it means the cloud.

Nigamanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Concluding Discourse is finished.

Nigamanakathā

Concluding Remarks

Ettāvatā [M 2.0322] ca āraddhā, vinayaṭṭhakathāya yā;

Vaṇṇanā nātivitthiṇṇā, paripuṇṇavinicchayā.

And by this much, the commentary on the Vinaya Aṭṭhakathā which was undertaken is not too extensive and has complete judgments.

Paññāsabhāṇavārāya, tantiyā parimāṇato;

Samijjhaniṭṭhiparamā, yā vimativinodanī.

That which is named Vimativinodanī, having fifty recitations by measure of the text, has perfect completion as its final state.

Anantarāyena katā, ayaṃ niṭṭhamupāgatā;

Yaṃ taṃ niṭṭhaṃ tathā sabbe, pāṇino samanorathā.

This treatise, composed without hindrance, has reached completion. Just as it has reached completion, so may all the heart's desires of beings reach completion.

Therehi vinayaññūhi, sucisallekhavuttihi;

Avissatthātivitthiṇṇa-ganthabhīrū hipatthitaṃ.

Desired by the elders who know the Vinaya, who are of pure and effacing conduct, and who, not being bold, are fearful of overly extensive texts.

Karontena mayā evaṃ, vinayaatthavaṇṇanaṃ;

Yaṃ pattaṃ kusalaṃ tena, patvā sambodhimuttamaṃ.

Through whatever merit has been attained by me, who am thus composing the commentary on the meaning of the Vinaya, having reached supreme enlightenment,

Vinayatthaṃ pakāsetvā, yo sopāyena lakkhaṇaṃ;

Sopāyaṃ vimaticcheda-ñāṇacakkhupadāyakaṃ.

Having explained the meaning of the Vinaya with its method and characteristics, this work is endowed with means and gives the eye of wisdom that cuts through doubt.

Viraddhatthavipallāsa-ganthavitthārahāniyā;

Visuddhiṃ pāpayissāmi, satte saṃsāradukkhato.

for the sake of abandoning erroneous, perverted, knotty, and overly extensive meanings, may I lead beings from the suffering of saṃsāra to purity.

Lokiyehi ca bhogehi, guṇehi nikhilā pajā;

Sabbehi sahitā hontu, ratā sambuddhasāsaneti.

May all beings be endowed with worldly wealth and all supramundane virtues, and may they delight in the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Vimativinodanīṭīkā niṭṭhitā.

The Vimativinodanīṭīkā is concluded.
